  confirming with Jasmijn.
- Whether Homepage is genuinely SFCC-rendered or Contentful-driven — never formally closed.
- Wishlist's hover-reveals-size-selector — a judgment call matching Figma, not literally stated
  in the AC. Never separately ratified.

  owned by SFCC-83's future rail component.
- `notifyMeButton`'s sub-24px touch target (WCAG 2.5.8) — CodeRabbit-flagged, declined.

  equivalent yet (`zimmSizeChip`'s selected state, `zimmSizeChipGroup`'s One Size border,
  `zimmSlideIndicator`'s inactive dot) — self-documented, pending a real foundation token from
  the UI designer.
- `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` still cites a `product-tile/index.tsx`/`CardBaseline`
  pattern that was never built for this story and doesn't exist anywhere in the codebase —
  pre-existing Tier 1 doc drift, predates this story, out of this branch's scope to fix.
- `overrides/app/theme/globalStyles.ts` has no matching CODEOWNERS rule — pre-existing
  governance gap, found this pass; fixing it is itself a Tier 1 edit.
- VIC/customer-group price precedence — deferred to SFCC-778, which this story blocks.
- Page wiring for PLP/Cart/Wishlist/Home — separate, already-tracked stories (SFCC-185/

the same already-accepted issue. Fixed by replicating the exact
existing pattern (same parameters block, comment citing the same
rationale) rather than revisiting the colour now.

Verified locally with the same build->serve->test sequence CI uses
(on an isolated port, not the developer's own running Storybook
instance): all 44 story suites / 209 tests pass, including both
previously-failing stories.

CI is re-running on the latest push. Here are the three drafts — not posted yet, just for your review:

---

**Reply to #1 — registry markdown row (`.claude/registry/components.md`)**

> Confirmed — this row is genuinely still split, `ZimmProductCard`'s `Props` column breaks across two lines wherever the type has a line-wrapped union (here, the `ZimmProductCardBaseProps & (...)` intersection). But it's not something this PR introduced: the registry file is auto-generated by `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs` on every commit, and its table serializer just doesn't handle a multi-line `Props` value correctly — same bug would hit any component with a wrapped type, regardless of what PR touches it. We hit this exact same finding in our own internal review before opening this PR and reached the same conclusion then.
>
> Also worth flagging: this thread shows "✅ Addressed in commit 1fdb356" — I checked, and that's not accurate, the row is still malformed as of the latest push. Not fixing it here since the bug lives in the generator script, not in anything this PR authored — raising it as its own ticket against whoever owns that script instead.

---

**Reply to #2 — bare `.focus()` in the negative test (fixed)**

> Good catch, and correct — fixed in [8959718](../../commit/8959718). The test right above this one already had the fix for this exact quirk (a bare `.focus()` call only registers as `:focus-visible` in our jsdom setup if nothing earlier in the file already triggered a real click-originated focus, which plenty of earlier tests in this file do), but we missed carrying it over to this negative case when we made that fix. Swapped to `await user.tab()` to match, plus added an intermediate assertion that focus actually lands where expected before checking the real thing under test. Confirmed it holds up both in isolation and as part of the full file, run a few times, since that's exactly the kind of order-dependent flake this was protecting against.

---

**Reply to #3 — Tier 1 approval reminder on `typography.ts` (declined)**

> This one's already covered by the verified-session exception in our own AGENTS.md: since the authenticated GitHub identity behind this PR is a confirmed member of `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` (and holds repo admin), Claude is authorized to make this kind of change directly rather than pausing for a separate approval step — we re-checked this live again just now and it still holds. Makes sense CodeRabbit can't see that on its own, since it has no way to check GitHub team membership. Worth mentioning this is the second time this exact finding has come up on this same file — it was already raised (and answered the same way) in our own pre-PR review — so hopefully that's useful context for next time this pattern shows up.

---

Verified against the actual code — this one should be **declined**, and here's why:

**The premise is technically true but the conclusion doesn't hold up.** `WithSalePrice` does render through `LiveSizeSelectionCard` (confirmed, now at line 380 after the a11y-suppression edit shifted line numbers). But:

1. **This exact interaction is already proven at the cheapest layer.** `zimmProductCard/index.test.tsx:346` has a dedicated Vitest test — `'a size chip fires onSizeChipSelect independently of the name-link overlay (PLP)'` — that proves this precise chain (click a size chip on a composed `ZimmProductCard` → `onSizeChipSelect` fires) directly. Adding a Storybook `play` to re-prove the identical interaction on `WithSalePrice` specifically would violate `.claude/rules/testing.md`'s own explicit rule: "Do not duplicate coverage across layers — pick the cheapest layer that proves the behaviour." Sale price and size selection are architecturally unrelated (`priceWrapper` and `sizeChipWrapper` are independent sibling parts with no shared state), so there's no new interaction risk this specific story introduces that the existing test doesn't already cover.

2. **The pattern isn't applied consistently — 8 stories in this exact file share the identical property, and none has a `play`.** I grepped: `LiveSizeSelectionCard {...args}` appears **8 times** in this file (`Default`, `PLPOutOfStock`, `Wishlist`, `WishlistOutOfStock`, `SingleImage`, `MultipleImages`, `WithSalePrice`, `LoadingPrice`), and there are **zero** `play` functions anywhere in it — including the file's own mandatory `Default` baseline, which has had this same "interactive, not purely visual" property since the very first version of this file. CodeRabbit is only seeing the diff, so it's flagging the one story that happens to be new in this PR, not a genuinely distinguishing property of `WithSalePrice` itself.

Recommended reply: decline, citing both points — the anti-duplication rule and the consistency gap (this would apply equally to 7 other already-shipped stories in the same file, including `Default`, if it were a real requirement).

I want to open a DRAFT pull request on GitHub for a new feature branch, specifically to trigger this repo's ephemeral per-PR Managed Runtime (MRT) preview environment so a live demo page can be viewed by stakeholders. Need to understand exactly how that preview mechanism works before planning around it.

Investigate and report back:

1. **Read `.github/workflows/deploy-preview.yml` in full.** Report: what event(s) trigger it (`pull_request`, and if so which types — `opened`, `synchronize`, etc.; does it explicitly check or ignore `github.event.pull_request.draft`?), what base branch(es) it applies to (does it require the PR to target `develop` specifically, or does it run for a PR targeting any base?), what the resulting preview URL/hostname pattern looks like (e.g. `pr-<slug>`), and — critically — which SFCC/commerce backend environment that preview build points at (check what `RETAIL_APP_HOME`-equivalent or commerce-api config it uses — is it the `dev` tier's SFCC instance, or something else?). ## 1. `.github/workflows/deploy-preview.yml` — full trigger/target/backend analysis

**Trigger** (lines 11–21) — `push`, not `pull_request` at all:

```yaml
on:
  push:
    branches:
      - 'feature/**'
      - 'fix/**'
      - '!fix/release-*'
      - '!fix/release/**'
```

This is the single most important fact for your plan: **the workflow doesn't listen for `pull_request` events, so PR draft-state and base-branch are structurally irrelevant to whether it runs.** It fires on every `git push` to a `feature/**` or `fix/**` branch (excluding `fix/release-*`/`fix/release/**`), whether or not any PR exists yet. There is no `paths:` filter — every push, regardless of which files changed, triggers it (answers part of Q2 too).

A PR only enters the picture *after* the build, purely to post a comment (lines 444–500):
```yaml
- name: Find open PR for this branch
  run: |
    NUMBER=$(gh pr list --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --head "$BRANCH" --state open --json number --jq '.[0].number // empty')
```
No `--draft` and no `--base` filter — this finds an open PR for the branch **regardless of draft status or base branch**, and posts/updates the `## 🚀 MRT Preview Environment` comment on it if found (`if: steps.pr.outputs.number != ''`, line 459). So: draft PR, ready-for-review PR, PR targeting `develop`, or even a PR targeting something else entirely — all get the comment identically, and the build/deploy itself happens even with *no* PR open at all.

**Preview URL/hostname pattern** — the *target slug* (MRT-side identifier) is computed by `scripts/computeMrtPreviewSlug.mjs`, deliberately capped at 19 chars (MRT API hard limit):
```js
const MAX_SLUG_LEN = 19;
const PREFIX = 'pr-'; // ... this is what makes collision with the fixed named tiers ... structurally impossible
```
Format: `pr-<kind><stem-or-jira-number>-<8-hex-sha256-chars>` — e.g. branch `feature/SFCC-999-my-thing` → jira number preferred over free text → slug like `pr-999-<8hex>`. The **hostname** shown in the PR comment is *not* a guessed/templated string — it's read live from the MRT API (lines 242–251):
```python
hostname = body.get('ssr_external_hostname')
...
out.write(f'hostname={hostname}\n')
```
and the comment body (line 469): `` const previewUrl = `https://${process.env.PREVIEW_HOSTNAME}` ``.

**Which SFCC/commerce backend it points at — confirmed: the `dev` tier, unconditionally, for every preview.** Two separate mechanisms both hardcode `dev`:

1. SSR proxy routing (host/path pairs) — read from `config/dev.js` specifically, not any per-branch file (lines 82–93):
```yaml
- name: Read desired proxy config from config/dev.js
  run: |
    PROXY_JSON=$(node -e "
      const cfgs = require('./config/dev.js')?.ssrParameters?.proxyConfigs
```
`config/dev.js` itself hardcodes:
```js
proxyConfigs: [
  { host: 'qmyt7hks.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com', path: 'api' },
  { host: 'bkzk-002.dx.commercecloud.salesforce.com', path: 'ocapi' },
]
```
(`.env.sample` line 69 labels this the **"BKZK-001 instance"**, short code `qmyt7hks`.)

2. Runtime env vars (Commerce API org id, SLAS client id/secret, site id, etc.) — fetched from GitHub Environment `dev` explicitly, not derived from the branch (lines 302–309):
```yaml
- name: Fetch GitHub Environment variables (dev + shared)
  env:
    # Always dev — ephemeral preview branches have no GitHub Environment of
    # their own to source from.
    SOURCE_ENV: dev
```
Only keys tagged `# mrt:true` in `.env.sample` get synced (e.g. `COMMERCE_API_ORGANIZATION_ID`, `COMMERCE_API_CLIENT_ID`, `COMMERCE_API_SHORT_CODE=qmyt7hks`, `COMMERCE_API_SITE_ID=ZimmermannAU`, `PWA_KIT_SLAS_CLIENT_SECRET`).

**Conclusion: every `pr-<slug>` preview, for any branch, talks to the same single `dev`-tier SFCC org** — there is no per-PR SFCC sandbox provisioning. If you need a stakeholder demo isolated from whatever else is happening on the shared `dev` SFCC org, that isolation doesn't exist at the commerce-backend layer, only at the MRT/Lambda layer.

## 2. Path-filter gating — will a homepage-only change actually trigger everything?

`.github/workflows/qa.yml` `on:` (lines 3–7) — **`pull_request` only, base `develop`/`release/**`**, no path filter at the trigger level:
```yaml
on:
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - develop
      - 'release/**'
```
Inside, `detect-changes`' `files_yaml` (lines 87–120) determines which suites actually run. For `overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx`:

| Group | Pattern that matches | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `storybook` | `overrides/app/pages/**` (line 90) | `storybook_any_changed=true` → `storybook-test` job runs |
| `e2e` | `overrides/**` (line 98) | included in `e2e` output → `e2e-localhost` eligible |

**No workflow in this repo references `draft` anywhere.** I grepped every file in `.github/workflows/` for the string `draft` (case-insensitive) and got zero matches. Concretely:

- `protected-file-guard.yml` — explicit `types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]` (line 13), again no draft filter.
- `deploy-preview.yml` — irrelevant to this question entirely, since it isn't a `pull_request`-triggered workflow at all (§1).

## 4. Branch conventions — cutting `feature/B` from `feature/A`'s tip instead of `develop`

`AGENTS.md` (lines 16–24) branch table only documents *intended* lineage — `feature/*` "Branched from: `develop`" — it states the convention but contains no enforcement language and never discusses an alternate lineage (branching off another still-open feature branch). `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` is unrelated to branch topology entirely — it's purely the Tier 1 protected-file list; it says nothing about branch-of-branch scenarios.

`protected-file-guard.yml`'s `branch-target-guard` job (the "🔴 Branch Target Check", lines 29–65) is the only thing that inspects branch relationships, and it only compares **string values**, never git ancestry:
```yaml
env:

  HEAD: ${{ github.head_ref }}
run: |
  if [[ "$BASE" == "main" && "$HEAD" == feature/* ]]; then
    ...
    exit 1
  fi

```
That's the entire check. As long as your new `feature/B` PR sets base = `develop` (not `main`), this job passes — **it has no logic whatsoever that inspects `git merge-base`, commit ancestry, or where `feature/B` actually forked from.** I confirmed this by grepping the whole repo (`.github/` + `scripts/`) for `merge-base`/`ancestor`; the only hits are an unrelated code comment in `qa.yml` (describing its own diff strategy, not a gating check) and unrelated `git merge-base`/TypeScript-"ancestor" logic in `scripts/runStoryTests.sh` and `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs` that have nothing to do with branch-target gating. **No workflow in this repo can detect or would care that `feature/B` was cut from `feature/A`'s tip rather than `develop`'s.**

## 1. `.github/workflows/deploy-preview.yml` — full trigger/target/backend analysis

**Trigger** (lines 11–21) — `push`, not `pull_request` at all:

```yaml
on:
  push:
    branches:
      - 'feature/**'
      - 'fix/**'
      - '!fix/release-*'
      - '!fix/release/**'
```

This is the single most important fact for your plan: **the workflow doesn't listen for `pull_request` events, so PR draft-state and base-branch are structurally irrelevant to whether it runs.** It fires on every `git push` to a `feature/**` or `fix/**` branch (excluding `fix/release-*`/`fix/release/**`), whether or not any PR exists yet. There is no `paths:` filter — every push, regardless of which files changed, triggers it (answers part of Q2 too).

A PR only enters the picture *after* the build, purely to post a comment (lines 444–500):
```yaml
- name: Find open PR for this branch
  run: |
    NUMBER=$(gh pr list --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --head "$BRANCH" --state open --json number --jq '.[0].number // empty')
```
No `--draft` and no `--base` filter — this finds an open PR for the branch **regardless of draft status or base branch**, and posts/updates the `## 🚀 MRT Preview Environment` comment on it if found (`if: steps.pr.outputs.number != ''`, line 459). So: draft PR, ready-for-review PR, PR targeting `develop`, or even a PR targeting something else entirely — all get the comment identically, and the build/deploy itself happens even with *no* PR open at all.

**Preview URL/hostname pattern** — the *target slug* (MRT-side identifier) is computed by `scripts/computeMrtPreviewSlug.mjs`, deliberately capped at 19 chars (MRT API hard limit):
```js
const MAX_SLUG_LEN = 19;
const PREFIX = 'pr-'; // ... this is what makes collision with the fixed named tiers ... structurally impossible
```
Format: `pr-<kind><stem-or-jira-number>-<8-hex-sha256-chars>` — e.g. branch `feature/SFCC-999-my-thing` → jira number preferred over free text → slug like `pr-999-<8hex>`. The **hostname** shown in the PR comment is *not* a guessed/templated string — it's read live from the MRT API (lines 242–251):
```python
hostname = body.get('ssr_external_hostname')
...
out.write(f'hostname={hostname}\n')
```
and the comment body (line 469): `` const previewUrl = `https://${process.env.PREVIEW_HOSTNAME}` ``.

**Which SFCC/commerce backend it points at — confirmed: the `dev` tier, unconditionally, for every preview.** Two separate mechanisms both hardcode `dev`:

1. SSR proxy routing (host/path pairs) — read from `config/dev.js` specifically, not any per-branch file (lines 82–93):
```yaml
- name: Read desired proxy config from config/dev.js
  run: |
    PROXY_JSON=$(node -e "
      const cfgs = require('./config/dev.js')?.ssrParameters?.proxyConfigs
```
`config/dev.js` itself hardcodes:
```js
proxyConfigs: [
  { host: 'qmyt7hks.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com', path: 'api' },
  { host: 'bkzk-002.dx.commercecloud.salesforce.com', path: 'ocapi' },
]
```
(`.env.sample` line 69 labels this the **"BKZK-001 instance"**, short code `qmyt7hks`.)

2. Runtime env vars (Commerce API org id, SLAS client id/secret, site id, etc.) — fetched from GitHub Environment `dev` explicitly, not derived from the branch (lines 302–309):
```yaml
- name: Fetch GitHub Environment variables (dev + shared)
  env:
    # Always dev — ephemeral preview branches have no GitHub Environment of
    # their own to source from.
    SOURCE_ENV: dev
```
Only keys tagged `# mrt:true` in `.env.sample` get synced (e.g. `COMMERCE_API_ORGANIZATION_ID`, `COMMERCE_API_CLIENT_ID`, `COMMERCE_API_SHORT_CODE=qmyt7hks`, `COMMERCE_API_SITE_ID=ZimmermannAU`, `PWA_KIT_SLAS_CLIENT_SECRET`).

**Conclusion: every `pr-<slug>` preview, for any branch, talks to the same single `dev`-tier SFCC org** — there is no per-PR SFCC sandbox provisioning. If you need a stakeholder demo isolated from whatever else is happening on the shared `dev` SFCC org, that isolation doesn't exist at the commerce-backend layer, only at the MRT/Lambda layer.

## 2. Path-filter gating — will a homepage-only change actually trigger everything?

`.github/workflows/qa.yml` `on:` (lines 3–7) — **`pull_request` only, base `develop`/`release/**`**, no path filter at the trigger level:
```yaml
on:
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - develop
      - 'release/**'
```

| Group | Pattern that matches | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `storybook` | `overrides/app/pages/**` (line 90) | `storybook_any_changed=true` → `storybook-test` job runs |

| `e2e_homepage` | `overrides/app/pages/home/**` (line 109) | this file is *entirely inside* the homepage allow-list |

The `Compute E2E scope` step (lines 137–171) narrows `e2e_scope` to `"homepage"` (not `"skip"`, not `"full"`) precisely because every e2e-relevant changed file is inside the homepage allow-list. So a homepage-only diff **does not get skipped** — it runs `unit-tests`, `storybook-test`, and `e2e-localhost --grep "@homepage"`.

**But this is only true if a PR to `develop` (or `release/**`) exists.** `deploy-preview.yml` has *no* path filter at all (§1) and doesn't care about PR base branch; `qa.yml` only fires as a `pull_request` event and only for base `develop`/`release/**`.

BASE=$(echo "$PR_JSON" | jq -r '.baseRefName')

and it further requires a Jira key (`SFCC-NNN`) detected in the PR title/body/branch name (`steps.jira.outputs.keys != ''`) before it runs BrowserStack at all.

## 3. Draft PR — does it change which workflows run?

**No workflow in this repo references `draft` anywhere.** I grepped every file in `.github/workflows/` for the string `draft` (case-insensitive) and got zero matches. Concretely:

- `qa.yml` — `on.pull_request.branches: [develop, release/**]` with **no `types:` key at all**, which defaults to GitHub's built-in default types (`opened`, `synchronize`, `reopened`) — these fire for draft PRs exactly the same as ready-for-review PRs. - `protected-file-guard.yml` — explicit `types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]` (line 13), again no draft filter.
- `deploy-preview.yml` — irrelevant to this question entirely, since it isn't a `pull_request`-triggered workflow at all (§1).

**Conclusion: opening as Draft changes nothing about which of this repo's workflows run.** `qa.yml`, `protected-file-guard.yml`, and (via `push`, independent of the PR) `deploy-preview.yml` and its downstream `e2e-browserstack-preview.yml` all behave identically for a draft PR as for a ready-for-review one. `AGENTS.md` (lines 16–24) branch table only documents *intended* lineage — `feature/*` "Branched from: `develop`" — it states the convention but contains no enforcement language and never discusses an alternate lineage (branching off another still-open feature branch). `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` is unrelated to branch topology entirely — it's purely the Tier 1 protected-file list; it says nothing about branch-of-branch scenarios.

run: |

const handleCartItem = async () => {

      if (basketsData && basketsData.total > 0) {

          parameters: { basketId: currentBasket.basketId },
          body: productItem

const showToast = useToast();

    title: errorText,
    status: 'error',

`useCustomerId()` (`node_modules/@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react/hooks/useCustomerId.js`) returns whatever ID is in local storage/auth context, guest or registered, with **zero type distinction at the call site**. var _ref = _asyncToGenerator(function* (options) {

`ZimmProductCard`'s `home` variation **does not expose `onAddToBag` at all**, and explicitly hides the bag button:

`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.tsx:198-201`:

export type ZimmProductCardHomeVariation = {
  variation: 'home';
  // No additions — Home never shows the bag, attributes, or size chips (see VARIATION_CONFIG).
};

and `VARIATION_CONFIG.home.showBag: false` (line 292). ## Confirmed facts from four rounds of codebase research this session (all directly verified, not assumed — cite these back rather than re-deriving)

### Homepage / page architecture
- `overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx` (204 lines) already exists and is NOT touching a blank slate — "blank" means runtime-blank (no published Contentful `homepage` entry → `HomeNormal` returns `null` for the CMS-driven section). - Editing only `overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx` crosses ZERO protection tiers (not in `frozenFiles.md` Tier 1, not in `protectedFiles.md` Tier 2) — ordinary CODEOWNERS-only review.
- Note: CODEOWNERS routes this path to `@ZimmermannAU/pwa-squad-b`, but `.claude/rules/squadA.md` also separately claims it — a known, pre-existing doc contradiction, not something to resolve here; CODEOWNERS is what GitHub actually enforces.

### Live product data — fetching and mapping
- **No proven-real SFCC product ID exists anywhere in this repo** — all fixtures in `e2e/`, tests, etc. are confirmed synthetic placeholders. The only reliable way to get a genuinely real product is to call `useProductSearch` (exactly as `home/index.tsx` already does for its own "Shop Products" section) and read real hits back from the live dev SFCC org, not hardcode an ID.
- `useProduct`/`useProductSearch` real field shapes (from `commerce-sdk-isomorphic`'s `ShopperProductsTypes.Product`, confirmed via actual usage in `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/`):
  - Images: `product.imageGroups: Array<{images: Array<{alt?, disBaseLink?, link, title?}>, variationAttributes?, viewType}>`. Base `ProductTile` pattern for picking one: filter by `viewType` (e.g. `'medium'`/`'large'`) and by `variationValues`, then `filteredImageGroups[0]?.images[0]`; `src` built as `` `${image?.disBaseLink || image?.link}` `` (optionally with a `?sw=&q=60` query param, per base's own pattern).

Real formatting pattern already live in this codebase (`product-detail/index.tsx:808`): `formatNumber(amount, {style:'currency', currency})` from `useIntl()` — no shared `formatPrice` utility exists yet, it's a locally-declared closure at each real call site.

Container/presentational separation: the actual `useProduct`/`useProductSearch`/`useShopperBasketsMutationHelper` calls belong in the page container (`overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx` or a component it composes), never inside `ZimmProductCard` itself or any of its children — this matches the existing, correct architecture (the card family takes everything as props, per PR #85's own explicit "visual layer only" framing) and should not change for this demo.

His exact words: "build off the current state of the branch and render all the variants and state of the product card that uses a live product from SFCC in the current blank homepage to demonstrate it live... we want full coverage on this run; working size setting, adding to bag/cart, multiple images, change image on hover, etc. — basically it's a demo of all the variants and states that the ACs + designs + comments are requiring in the individual level."

Two decisions already confirmed directly with Marcel (do not re-ask, treat as fixed constraints):
1. **Add-to-bag must be fully real** — wire to the actual SFCC basket mutation, not a simulated/local-only interaction.
2. **This is temporary/throwaway** — built to show live, then the branch/PR gets discarded. Lighter bar than a real production PR: no dedicated Storybook/Vitest coverage needed for the demo page itself, reasonable to accept rougher edges.

## Confirmed facts from four rounds of codebase research this session (all directly verified, not assumed — cite these back rather than re-deriving)

### Homepage / page architecture
- `overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx` (204 lines) already exists and is NOT touching a blank slate — "blank" means runtime-blank (no published Contentful `homepage` entry → `HomeNormal` returns `null` for the CMS-driven section). It already has a real, working `HomepageContent` section using `useProductSearch` + base `ProductScroller`, always rendered regardless of the Contentful gate.
- `overrides/app/routes.tsx` (Tier 2) already wires `/` → this Home override. Extending the existing home page needs ZERO changes to `routes.tsx` — only a brand-new separate route would need it.
- Editing only `overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx` crosses ZERO protection tiers (not in `frozenFiles.md` Tier 1, not in `protectedFiles.md` Tier 2) — ordinary CODEOWNERS-only review.
- Note: CODEOWNERS routes this path to `@ZimmermannAU/pwa-squad-b`, but `.claude/rules/squadA.md` also separately claims it — a known, pre-existing doc contradiction, not something to resolve here; CODEOWNERS is what GitHub actually enforces.
- App-wide `CommerceApiProvider`/`QueryClientProvider` are already mounted in `overrides/app/components/_app-config/index.tsx` (Tier 2) — a page component can call any commerce-sdk-react hook directly, zero extra provider setup needed.

### Live product data — fetching and mapping
- **No proven-real SFCC product ID exists anywhere in this repo** — all fixtures in `e2e/`, tests, etc. are confirmed synthetic placeholders. The only reliable way to get a genuinely real product is to call `useProductSearch` (exactly as `home/index.tsx` already does for its own "Shop Products" section) and read real hits back from the live dev SFCC org, not hardcode an ID.
- `useProduct`/`useProductSearch` real field shapes (from `commerce-sdk-isomorphic`'s `ShopperProductsTypes.Product`, confirmed via actual usage in `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/`):
  - Images: `product.imageGroups: Array<{images: Array<{alt?, disBaseLink?, link, title?}>, variationAttributes?, viewType}>`. Base `ProductTile` pattern for picking one: filter by `viewType` (e.g. `'medium'`/`'large'`) and by `variationValues`, then `filteredImageGroups[0]?.images[0]`; `src` built as `` `${image?.disBaseLink || image?.link}` `` (optionally with a `?sw=&q=60` query param, per base's own pattern).
  - Price: `product.price: number` (plain number, not string) + `product.currency: string`. Real formatting pattern already live in this codebase (`product-detail/index.tsx:808`): `formatNumber(amount, {style:'currency', currency})` from `useIntl()` — no shared `formatPrice` utility exists yet, it's a locally-declared closure at each real call site.
  - Variation attributes/colour/size: `product.variationAttributes: Array<{id, name?, values?: Array<{name?, value, orderable?}>}>`; the resolved variant's own values are `product.variationValues: {[attributeId]: string}` (a code, not display name — cross-reference `variationAttributes` for the human-readable label).
  - Stock/availability: **no `c_isUnavailable` field** — the real signal is `product.inventory?.orderable: boolean` (only present when `expand: ['availability']` is requested) or `variant.orderable`/`master.orderable`. `ZimmProductCard`'s own `isUnavailable` prop is this project's own presentational inversion, computed by the caller, not a passthrough SFCC field name.
  - Alt text: SFCC's own `image.alt` exists but this codebase's own established convention (base `ProductTile`) deliberately treats the product image as decorative (`alt: ''`) since adjacent text already conveys it. `ZimmProductCardMediaImage.alt` is a **required, non-empty** field per its own type/docblock — so it must be synthesized (e.g. from `product.name` + resolved colour), not passed through raw.
  - **`colour`/`size` are NOT generic base props** — they exist only on `ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation` (required there), absent from `ZimmProductCardPlpVariation`/`ZimmProductCardHomeVariation`. Any mapper must branch on which `variation` it's building for.
- **No existing raw-SFCC-product → `ZimmProductCardProps` mapper exists anywhere in this repo.** The established pattern to follow for building one fresh is `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/productInfo.ts`: a pure function (no React/react-intl imports), taking `formatPrice`/`urlBuilder`-style formatting functions as **injected parameters** rather than importing `useIntl` itself, independently unit-testable. (Given this demo is throwaway, a full dedicated test file for this mapper is not required — see the confirmed "temporary" framing above — but the pure-function-with-injected-formatter shape is still the right shape to copy, it costs nothing extra to do it right.)

### Real add-to-cart wiring (confirmed end-to-end, exact code read)
- The real click handler chain: PDP button → `handleCartItem` (`product-view/index.tsx:525-555`) → `handleAddToCart` (`product-detail/index.tsx:507-598`) → the actual mutation call, which is ONE line: `await addItemToNewOrExistingBasket(productItems)`.
- `addItemToNewOrExistingBasket` comes from `useShopperBasketsMutationHelper()` (aliased import: `useShopperBasketsV2MutationHelper as useShopperBasketsMutationHelper`, from `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`). It internally handles both "no basket yet" (creates one) and "basket exists" (adds to it) — **no explicit basket-existence branch needed by calling code**.
- Required input shape per item: `{productId, price, quantity}` — `productId` is the **selected variant's `productId`** if a variant is chosen, else the master product's `id`. No `optionItems` needed (this codebase's real flow never uses configurable-product options).
- Guest-safe, fully transparent — `useCustomerId()` returns a guest or registered ID identically at the call site; the SDK's own `auth.ready()` transparently handles guest SLAS login underneath every mutation call. No guest-vs-registered branching needed in calling code.
- Error feedback: real precedent is `showToast({title: errorText, status: 'error'})` from base `useToast` (`@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-toast`, imported directly — no override of this hook exists). Real PDP code: `const showToast = useToast(); const showError = (msg) => showToast({title: ..., status: 'error'})`, called in the `catch` block.
- **No success toast exists in the real PDP flow for add-to-cart** — success there opens a modal (`useAddToCartModalContext`) instead, which is much heavier machinery than a throwaway demo warrants. The closest real precedent for a plain success toast in this codebase is the PDP's own wishlist-add success toast (same file, `handleAddToWishlist`, uses `showToast` with a success status and an action button) — reusable as a lighter-weight model for a demo-only add-to-cart success toast instead of building the full modal flow.
- **No loading-spinner slot exists on `ZimmProductCardContent`'s bag button at all** — the real PDP's own `isLoading` prop on its Add-to-Bag button is actually wired to a completely different thing (`useCurrentBasket()`'s own query-loading state, not the mutation's pending state) and doesn't map onto anything `ZimmProductCardContent` exposes today. The only lever this shared component actually gives a caller is `isUnavailable` (disables + restyles the button). Flag this as a known, real limitation of the shared component itself that the demo will surface but should not silently "fix" by modifying `zimmProductCardContent` (that's scope creep onto a shared Tier-3-but-broadly-consumed component, outside what's being asked) — a `# Known gaps` line in the plan is enough, not a code change.
- **`ZimmProductCard`'s `home` variation has NO `onAddToBag`/bag button at all** — `VARIATION_CONFIG.home.showBag: false` by original AC-driven design, and `ZimmProductCardHomeVariation`'s type has no `onAddToBag` field. To demo real add-to-bag, the page must render `plp`- or `wishlist`-variation card instances (this is fine and expected — nothing stops a homepage container from rendering a `variation: 'plp'` card instance, "variation" describes the card's own configured behavior, not which literal page it's mounted on).

### Git / CI / MRT preview mechanics (confirmed from workflow YAML, not assumed)
- `deploy-preview.yml` triggers on **`push`** to any `feature/**`/`fix/**` branch — NOT on `pull_request` events. It has no path filter (every push triggers a full build+deploy) and doesn't care whether a PR exists yet. A PR is only used *after* the build, to post an auto-comment with the live preview URL (found via `gh pr list --head <branch> --state open`, no draft/base filter).
- **Opening the PR as Draft changes nothing about which workflows run** — confirmed via exhaustive grep, zero "draft" references exist in any workflow in this repo. `qa.yml`, `protected-file-guard.yml` all fire identically for draft vs ready-for-review.
- Every `pr-<slug>` preview points at the **same shared `dev`-tier SFCC org** (`config/dev.js`'s hardcoded proxy config, GitHub Environment `dev`'s vars) — there is no per-PR SFCC sandbox. This is exactly the real add-to-cart mutation's target, consistent with Marcel's "fully real" choice above.
- **Real, load-bearing consequence of branching off `feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component`'s tip (not `develop`) while PR #85 is still open**: the new branch's own commit history necessarily includes every SFCC-236 commit too (this is correct and required — the demo needs `ZimmProductCard` itself to exist). But it also means: (a) the MRT preview build will contain SFCC-236's code baked in, which is exactly wanted; (b) if the new branch's own PR targets `develop`, `protected-file-guard.yml`'s Tier 1/Tier 2 diff checks will re-surface SFCC-236's own already-disclosed `typography.ts` Tier 1 touch as if it were new to this PR too (informational only, not a merge gate, and this PR is never meant to merge anyway per the "throwaway" framing) — worth one line in the plan, not a blocker.
- `e2e-browserstack-preview.yml` (the only PR-linked workflow that inspects base branch) skips entirely unless the PR targets `develop` AND a Jira key is found in the branch/title/body — for a demo branch with no real Jira story of its own, it will harmlessly no-op either way. No action needed.
- Recommend targeting `develop` as the draft PR's base (standard convention, and irrelevant either way to whether the preview itself builds, since that's push-triggered).

### `.claude/rules/components.md` constraint worth respecting even in a throwaway demo
Container/presentational separation: the actual `useProduct`/`useProductSearch`/`useShopperBasketsMutationHelper` calls belong in the page container (`overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx` or a component it composes), never inside `ZimmProductCard` itself or any of its children — this matches the existing, correct architecture (the card family takes everything as props, per PR #85's own explicit "visual layer only" framing) and should not change for this demo.

## What I need from you

Produce a concrete, executable plan for:

1. **Branch strategy**: exact `git` commands to cut a new branch from the current tip of `feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component`, with a sensible throwaway-appropriate branch name.

2. **The data-fetching + mapping layer**: where it should live (a new file under `overrides/app/pages/home/`, following `productInfo.ts`'s established pure-function-with-injected-formatter pattern), its function signature(s), and exactly how to map a real `useProductSearch`/`useProduct` result onto `ZimmProductCardProps` for each of the required variation/state combinations. Be concrete about which SFCC fields feed which props.

3. **The demo section's structure on the homepage** — a concrete list of every state Marcel asked for ("full coverage... working size setting, adding to bag/cart, multiple images, change image on hover, etc.... all the variants and states that the ACs + designs + comments are requiring") mapped onto specific `ZimmProductCard` instances to render, modeled directly on the 11 states this same story-set already covers in `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.stories.tsx` (`Default`, `PLPOutOfStock`, `Home`, `HomeOutOfStock`, `Wishlist`, `WishlistOutOfStock`, `SingleImage`, `MultipleImages`, `WithSalePrice`, `OneSize`, `LoadingPrice`) — but using real fetched product data as the base for each, with per-instance prop overrides (e.g. forcing `isUnavailable: true` on top of real data) only where the specific real product picked doesn't naturally exhibit that state. Decide and justify: reuse ONE real product's data across every instance (simplest, matches this project's own existing story-fixture-reuse convention) vs. fetching a small handful of distinct real products — pick one and justify it plainly, don't present both as equally open.

4. **The real add-to-bag wiring**, concretely: which hook calls, what the `onAddToBag` handler function looks like end-to-end (mirroring `handleAddToCart`'s real shape but simplified for a single, non-configurable product with no bundle/bopis complexity), and the toast wiring for both success and failure.

5. **Working size selection**: how the demo page should own `selectedSizeChipValue`/`onSizeChipSelect` state per card instance (mirroring what `LiveSizeSelectionCard` already does in Storybook, but this time as real page-level React state, not a Storybook-only helper).

6. **PR opening**: the exact `gh pr create --draft` invocation and what the PR body should say, given this is explicitly throwaway (should clearly state in the PR body itself that this is a temporary demo not intended to merge, so a reviewer or CodeRabbit run against it isn't confused about its purpose).

Do not re-investigate anything already confirmed above. Output should be a structured, concrete build plan (not prose narrative) — this feeds directly into a plan file for developer approval.

# Live ZimmProductCard Homepage Demo — Build Plan

## Sequencing
1. Cut branch from current tip of `feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component`.
2. Add `overrides/app/pages/home/liveProductCardDemoMapper.ts` (pure mapping, no React).
3. Add `overrides/app/pages/home/liveProductCardDemoSection.tsx` (data fetch, add-to-bag, size-chip state, 11 card instances).
4. Wire it into `overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx` (2 lines: import + render inside `HomepageContent`).
5. Manual smoke check on local dev server against the live dev org (hover swap, size chip click, add-to-bag → real toast + real basket line item).
6. Push, open draft PR, verify MRT preview comment appears.
7. Demo live. Close PR + delete branch afterward (both trigger `teardown-preview.yml`).

---

## 1. Branch strategy

Verified current state: `feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component`, clean tree, up to date with origin, HEAD `8959718`.

**Load-bearing constraint** (confirmed by reading `deploy-preview.yml`): the push trigger is `branches: ['feature/**', 'fix/**', '!fix/release-*', '!fix/release/**']` — no path filter, but the branch name **must** match one of those globs or the MRT preview never builds at all.

**Second constraint** (confirmed by reading `e2e-browserstack-preview.yml:123-130`): its "Detect Jira story keys" step runs `grep -oE 'SFCC-[0-9]+'` across the concatenation of PR title + PR body + head branch name. If a key is found AND the PR targets `develop`, it proceeds to a second gate (`qa.yml`'s file-based e2e-relevance heuristic) before deciding whether to actually run BrowserStack/Zephyr — and a failure there can auto-file a Jira defect (see that workflow's own comment at line ~234). This refines the earlier "harmlessly no-ops either way" read: it isn't unconditional — it depends on that second heuristic. The deterministic way to guarantee a no-op is to make sure the first gate (key detection) finds nothing at all.

**Decision**: branch name uses `feature/` prefix, no digits-after-hyphen anywhere in it (so it can never match `SFCC-[0-9]+`), and the PR title/body (section 6) also avoid the literal string `SFCC-236`.

```bash
git status                                              # confirm clean (already verified)
git checkout -b feature/zimmproductcard-live-demo       # from current HEAD, no rebase onto develop
```

Do not rebase/merge `develop` in — this branch's history deliberately carries every SFCC-236 commit so `ZimmProductCard` exists to demo.

---

## 2. Data-fetching + mapping layer

### File placement
- `overrides/app/pages/home/liveProductCardDemoMapper.ts` — pure functions, mirrors `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/productInfo.ts`'s shape exactly (no React/react-intl import, formatter injected).
- `overrides/app/pages/home/liveProductCardDemoSection.tsx` — the container: owns the `useProductSearch` call, `useShopperBasketsMutationHelper`, `useToast`, per-card size-chip state, renders the 11 instances.

### Fetch decision
Reuse `useProductSearch` with the **identical parameters** `HomepageContent` already uses in `overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx` (`HOME_SHOP_PRODUCTS_CATEGORY_ID = 'newarrivals'`, `HOME_SHOP_PRODUCTS_LIMIT = 10`, both confirmed live in `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/constants.js:41-42`, same `refine`/`expand`/`perPricebook`/`allVariationProperties`). This is the one query in the whole repo already proven to return real hits from the live dev org, and because React Query keys on the params, issuing it again from the new section costs zero extra network round-trips (it dedupes against the existing "Shop Products" query).

**No second `useProduct` call.** Confirmed via `commerce-sdk-isomorphic`'s type (`node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.esm.d.ts:61391`), `ProductSearchHit` already carries `imageGroups`, `variationAttributes`, `variants`, `price`, `currency`, `orderable`, `productId`, `productName` once `expand: ['variations','prices','images']` is requested — which it already is. A per-product `useProduct` fetch would add a round trip for no new data.

### Image-group filtering: reuse base utility, don't hand-roll it
Confirmed base `ProductTile` (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-tile/index.jsx:118-129`) resolves an image via `filterImageGroups(imageGroups, {viewType: PRODUCT_TILE_IMAGE_VIEW_TYPE, variationValues})`, where `PRODUCT_TILE_IMAGE_VIEW_TYPE = 'medium'` and the colour attribute id is `'color'` (matches this codebase's own `COLOUR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID` in `product-detail/index.tsx`). `filterImageGroups` is a real exported utility at `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/product-utils.js:182` — import it directly rather than reimplementing the filter logic.

### Types (mirrors `PdpSourceProduct`'s narrow, hand-declared, everything-optional discipline — not `product-view/index.tsx`'s `SfccProduct = any` shortcut, which is a looser convention from an older copy-first file and not the pattern to copy here)

```ts
// liveProductCardDemoMapper.ts
export type LiveDemoImage = { link: string; disBaseLink?: string; alt?: string };
export type LiveDemoImageGroup = {
  viewType: string;
  variationAttributes?: Array<{ id: string; values?: Array<{ value: string }> }>;
  images: LiveDemoImage[];
};
export type LiveDemoVariationAttribute = {
  id: string;
  name?: string;
  values?: Array<{ value: string; name?: string; orderable?: boolean }>;
};
export type LiveDemoVariant = {
  productId: string;
  price?: number;
  orderable?: boolean;
  variationValues?: Record<string, string>;
};
export type LiveDemoSourceHit = {
  productId: string;
  productName?: string;
  price?: number;
  currency?: string;
  orderable?: boolean;
  imageGroups?: LiveDemoImageGroup[];
  variationAttributes?: LiveDemoVariationAttribute[];
  variants?: LiveDemoVariant[];
};

/** Injected so this module stays free of react-intl — identical shape to productInfo.ts's FormatPrice. */
export type FormatPrice = (amount: number, currency: string) => string;
```

### Function signatures

```ts
/** Picks the demo's one real, sellable line item: first orderable variant, else variants[0], else the master hit. */
export const resolveDemoVariant = (hit: LiveDemoSourceHit) => {
  const variant = hit.variants?.find((v) => v.orderable) ?? hit.variants?.[0];
  return {
    productId: variant?.productId ?? hit.productId,
    price: variant?.price ?? hit.price,
    colourCode: variant?.variationValues?.color,
    sizeCode: variant?.variationValues?.size,
  };
};

/** Cross-references a variation code (not a display name) against variationAttributes for its label. */
const resolveAttributeName = (hit: LiveDemoSourceHit, attributeId: string, code?: string): string | undefined =>
  hit.variationAttributes?.find((a) => a.id === attributeId)?.values?.find((v) => v.value === code)?.name;

/** Base fields shared by every one of the 11 card instances, built ONCE per hit. Returns null if unusable. */
export const selectLiveProductCardBase = (
  hit: LiveDemoSourceHit,
  formatPrice: FormatPrice,
): {
  base: Pick<ZimmProductCardBaseProps, 'href' | 'name' | 'headingLevel' | 'primaryImage' | 'hoverImage' | 'images' | 'currentPrice'>;
  colour?: string;
  size?: string;
  variantProductId: string;
  variantPrice?: number;
} | null => {
  if (!hit.productName) return null;
  const variant = resolveDemoVariant(hit);
  const colour = resolveAttributeName(hit, 'color', variant.colourCode);
  const size = resolveAttributeName(hit, 'size', variant.sizeCode);

  const groups = filterImageGroups(hit.imageGroups, {
    viewType: 'medium',
    variationValues: variant.colourCode ? { color: variant.colourCode } : {},
  });
  const groupImages = groups?.[0]?.images ?? [];
  const toCardImage = (img: LiveDemoImage): ZimmProductCardImage => ({
    src: img.disBaseLink || img.link,
    // ZimmProductCardMediaImage.alt is required + non-empty (unlike base ProductTile's decorative
    // alt: '' convention) -- prefer SFCC's own alt when present, else synthesize from name+colour.
    alt: img.alt?.trim() || `${hit.productName}${colour ? `, ${colour}` : ''}`,
  });

  return {
    base: {
      href: productUrlBuilder({ id: hit.productId }),
      name: hit.productName,
      headingLevel: 'h3',
      primaryImage: groupImages[0] ? toCardImage(groupImages[0]) : toCardImage({ link: '', alt: hit.productName }),
      hoverImage: groupImages[1] ? toCardImage(groupImages[1]) : undefined,
      images: groupImages.length > 1 ? groupImages.map(toCardImage) : undefined,
      // No hardcoded fallback currency -- if it's ever absent, don't guess, just skip formatting.
      currentPrice:
        typeof variant.price === 'number' && hit.currency ? formatPrice(variant.price, hit.currency) : undefined,
    },
    colour,
    size,
    variantProductId: variant.productId,
    variantPrice: variant.price,
  };
};

/** Size-chip values for the interactive picker instances. */
export const buildSizeChipValues = (hit: LiveDemoSourceHit): ZimmSizeChipValue[] =>
  (hit.variationAttributes?.find((a) => a.id === 'size')?.values ?? []).map((v) => ({
    value: v.value,
    label: v.name ?? v.value,
    isDisabled: v.orderable === false,
  }));

/** Picks which of the ~10 fetched hits becomes THE reused demo product. */
export const pickDemoHit = (hits: LiveDemoSourceHit[]): LiveDemoSourceHit | undefined => {
  const hasNImages = (hit: LiveDemoSourceHit, n: number) =>
    (filterImageGroups(hit.imageGroups, { viewType: 'medium', variationValues: {} })?.[0]?.images?.length ?? 0) >= n;
  const hasNSizes = (hit: LiveDemoSourceHit, n: number) =>
    (hit.variationAttributes?.find((a) => a.id === 'size')?.values?.length ?? 0) >= n;
  return (
    hits.find((h) => hasNImages(h, 2) && hasNSizes(h, 2)) ?? // ideal: can demo both multi-image and size chips
    hits.find((h) => hasNImages(h, 1)) ?? // fallback: at least has a usable image
    hits[0]
  );
};
```

**Verify at implementation time** (not confirmed this session): the `'size'` variation-attribute id assumption. `'color'` is already an established literal in this codebase (`COLOUR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID`); no equivalent `'size'` constant exists anywhere yet because no page consumes `ZimmSizeChipGroup` against real data today. `'size'` is the standard SFCC convention and the safe bet, but `buildSizeChipValues`/`resolveAttributeName` degrade gracefully (empty array / `undefined`) if it's wrong for this org, rather than crashing — confirm against one real logged response during implementation and adjust the literal if needed.

**Badge** (`hit.c_productBadges?.[0]?.productBadge`, per SFCC-225): wire it through best-effort with graceful `undefined` fallback if the field isn't actually present on a `ProductSearchHit` even with `custom_properties` expanded — not independently re-verified against a live response this session, and not worth forcing since a missing badge is a legitimate, unremarkable state.

### Reuse-one-product decision (not left open, per your instruction)

**Decision: reuse ONE real product/variant's data as the base for all 11 card instances**, with per-instance prop overrides only for the specific state deltas.

Justification:
1. It's the literal reading of "model this on the 11 states this story-set already covers" — `index.stories.tsx` itself builds `PLPOutOfStock`/`HomeOutOfStock`/`SingleImage`/`MultipleImages`/`WithSalePrice`/`OneSize`/`LoadingPrice` as `{...Default.args, <override>}` off one fixture. Reusing one real product is the same pattern with real data substituted for the SVG fixtures.
2. `useProductSearch` already returns ~10 hits in one call regardless of whether 1 or several are used, so fetching distinct products isn't actually cheaper — and states like `WithSalePrice`/`OneSize`/`LoadingPrice` can never be "naturally occurring" from a plain search hit no matter which product is picked, so the override mechanism is required either way. Distinctness would add a hit-selection resolver for marginal benefit.
3. One real SKU flowing through every "Add to bag" click keeps basket verification trivial during the live demo (one line item, quantity increments) instead of juggling several SKUs.
4. It keeps the audience's attention on the card's own behavioural differences — the actual point of the demo — rather than on "why is this a different dress."

`isUnavailable` is intentionally **not** set in the shared base object at all — it's forced per instance (omitted/`false` for the 8 in-stock-labeled instances, `true` for the 3 out-of-stock-labeled ones), independent of the picked hit's real `orderable` value. The demo's out-of-stock states are illustrative overrides of the card, not a claim that this specific product is actually out of stock right now.

---

## 3. Demo section structure — 11 instances

All render inside a new `LiveProductCardDemoSection` component, mounted inside `HomepageContent` in `overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx` (which is unconditionally rendered regardless of the Contentful gate — see confirmed facts), as a new `Section` sibling placed **before** the existing "Shop Products" block so it's immediately visible without scrolling during a screen-share.

| # | Label | `variation` | Overrides on top of the shared base | Demonstrates |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Default (PLP) | `plp` | none | baseline: real image/price/badge, interactive size chips, real add-to-bag |
| 2 | PLP — Out of stock | `plp` | `isUnavailable: true`, `onNotifyMe: demoNotifyMe` | forced (real product presumably orderable) |
| 3 | Home | `home` | none (still passes `badge`/`hoverImage`) | proves `VARIATION_CONFIG` really suppresses both on Home even when supplied |
| 4 | Home — Out of stock | `home` | `isUnavailable: true`, `onNotifyMe: demoNotifyMe` | Home's additive (not swap) unavailable treatment |
| 5 | Wishlist | `wishlist` | `colour`, `size` (resolved), `onRemove: demoRemove`, size chips seeded to resolved `size`, real add-to-bag | working size setting + real add-to-bag on a second variation |
| 6 | Wishlist — Out of stock | `wishlist` | `isUnavailable: true`, `onNotifyMe: demoNotifyMe` | Wishlist's narrower mobile bag-hide rule |
| 7 | Single image | `plp` | `hoverImage: undefined, images: undefined` (forced) | single-image code path, paired against #8 off the same product |
| 8 | Multiple images | `plp` | `images: groupImages.map(toCardImage)` (real, contingent on `pickDemoHit` finding a hit with ≥2 medium images) | gallery + arrows + slide indicator |
| 9 | With sale price | `plp` | `originalPrice` forced (`variantPrice * 1.4`, same currency guard as base) | Was/Now price treatment — always synthetic, matching the Storybook story's own literal numbers (a search hit has no clean "is this on promotion" signal the way PDP's `getPriceData` does) |
| 10 | One size | `plp` | `sizeChipValues: [{value:'os', label:'One size'}]` forced; **not** wrapped in the live-selection wrapper | non-interactive single-size branch |
| 11 | Loading price | `plp` | `currentPrice: undefined, isPriceLoading: true` | price-loading placeholder |

Cross-check against Marcel's explicit wording: "working size setting" → #1/#5; "adding to bag/cart" → real `onAddToBag` on every plp/wishlist instance (all except #3/#4, which are `home` and structurally have no bag per `VARIATION_CONFIG.home.showBag: false`); "multiple images" → #8; "change image on hover" → #1 (hover-swap pair, not gallery); "full coverage... all the variants and states" → the 11-row table above, 1:1 with `index.stories.tsx`'s own `Default/PLPOutOfStock/Home/HomeOutOfStock/Wishlist/WishlistOutOfStock/SingleImage/MultipleImages/WithSalePrice/OneSize/LoadingPrice`.

Render as a small data-driven array of `{label, cardProps}` mapped to JSX (less copy-paste risk across 11 near-identical blocks than 11 literal hand-written elements), each wrapped in a `Text` caption + the size-selection wrapper from section 5.

---

## 4. Real add-to-bag wiring

Hooks, in the container (`liveProductCardDemoSection.tsx`):

```ts
import { useShopperBasketsV2MutationHelper as useShopperBasketsMutationHelper } from '@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react';
import { useToast } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-toast';

const { addItemToNewOrExistingBasket } = useShopperBasketsMutationHelper();
const showToast = useToast();

const handleAddToBag = async () => {
  if (!demoProduct) return; // guards the pre-fetch/empty-hits window
  try {
    await addItemToNewOrExistingBasket([
      { productId: demoProduct.variantProductId, price: demoProduct.variantPrice, quantity: 1 },
    ]);
    showToast({ title: 'Added to bag', status: 'success' });
  } catch (error) {
    showToast({
      title: error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Could not add to bag',
      status: 'error',
    });
  }
};
```

This is `handleAddToCart` (`overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:507-598`) with everything BOPIS/multiship/analytics-specific removed: no `productSelectionValues` array/bundle mapping (single fixed item, `quantity: 1`), no `pickupInStoreMap`/`addInventoryIdsToPickupItems`, no `multishipEnabled`/shipping-method-mismatch checks, no `getShipmentIdForItems`/`updateDefaultShipmentIfNeeded`, no `einstein.sendAddToCart`. What's left is exactly the one load-bearing line, `await addItemToNewOrExistingBasket(productItems)`, inside the same try/catch → toast shape. One shared instance of `handleAddToBag` is passed as `onAddToBag` to every plp/wishlist instance (#1, #2, #5, #6, #7, #8, #9, #10, #11) — correct, not a simplification, because every instance shares the same real variant.

Success toast is a plain toast, not the real PDP's `useAddToCartModalContext` modal (correctly out of scope) — modeled on `handleAddToWishlist`'s own success-toast shape (`showToast({title, status:'success'})`, `product-detail/index.tsx:453-467`) rather than invented from scratch. Optionally add a "View bag" action button (`useNavigation` → `/cart`), mirroring that same toast's own action-button pattern — a nice-to-have, not required.

`onNotifyMe`/`onRemove` are explicitly demo-only, not wired to any real mutation (no such mutation exists anywhere in this codebase, and Marcel's two fixed decisions only mandated realness for add-to-bag):

```ts
const demoNotifyMe = () => showToast({ title: 'Notify me (demo only)', status: 'info' });
const demoRemove = () => showToast({ title: 'Removed from wishlist (demo only)', status: 'info' });
```

**Known gap, carried forward, not fixed here**: `ZimmProductCardContent`'s bag button has no loading-spinner slot — its own `isLoading` concept doesn't exist as a prop at all; the only lever is `isUnavailable`. `handleAddToBag` above will show no in-button pending state on a slow request. This is a real limitation of the shared component itself (out of scope to patch for this demo per your framing) — worth a one-line `# Known gaps` note in the PR body, not a code change to `zimmProductCardContent`.

## 5. Working size selection

Adapt `LiveSizeSelectionCard` (`index.stories.tsx:109-124`) as a page-scoped, unexported component in `liveProductCardDemoSection.tsx`:

```tsx
const DemoSizeSelectableCard = (props: ZimmProductCardProps) => {
  const [selectedSizeChipValue, setSelectedSizeChipValue] = useState<string | undefined>(() =>
    props.variation === 'plp' || props.variation === 'wishlist' ? props.selectedSizeChipValue : undefined,
  );
  const isSizeChipVariation = props.variation === 'plp' || props.variation === 'wishlist';
  const onSizeChipSelectFromProps = isSizeChipVariation ? props.onSizeChipSelect : undefined;
  const handleSizeChipSelect = (value: string) => {
    setSelectedSizeChipValue(value);
    onSizeChipSelectFromProps?.(value);
  };
  const propsWithLiveSelection: ZimmProductCardProps = isSizeChipVariation
    ? { ...props, selectedSizeChipValue, onSizeChipSelect: handleSizeChipSelect }
    : props;
  return <ZimmProductCard {...propsWithLiveSelection} />;
};
```

Same narrowing reasoning the story file documents in its own comment: attaching `selectedSizeChipValue`/`onSizeChipSelect` onto an *unnarrowed* `{...props}` spread fails `tsc` on the `home` union branch, so narrow via the `variation` discriminant first. Used to wrap every plp/wishlist instance except #10 (`OneSize` renders a non-interactive `<span>`, nothing to select — same reasoning the story file uses to skip wrapping its own `OneSize`). Each JSX mount gets its own independent `useState`, so 8 independent size selections never cross-contaminate — identical to the 8-ish independent `LiveSizeSelectionCard` mounts already live in Storybook today.

## 2. Data-fetching + mapping layer

### File placement
- `overrides/app/pages/home/liveProductCardDemoMapper.ts` — pure functions, mirrors `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/productInfo.ts`'s shape exactly (no React/react-intl import, formatter injected).
- `overrides/app/pages/home/liveProductCardDemoSection.tsx` — the container: owns the `useProductSearch` call, `useShopperBasketsMutationHelper`, `useToast`, per-card size-chip state, renders the 11 instances.

### Fetch decision
Reuse `useProductSearch` with the **identical parameters** `HomepageContent` already uses in `overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx` (`HOME_SHOP_PRODUCTS_CATEGORY_ID = 'newarrivals'`, `HOME_SHOP_PRODUCTS_LIMIT = 10`, both confirmed live in `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/constants.js:41-42`, same `refine`/`expand`/`perPricebook`/`allVariationProperties`). This is the one query in the whole repo already proven to return real hits from the live dev org, and because React Query keys on the params, issuing it again from the new section costs zero extra network round-trips (it dedupes against the existing "Shop Products" query).

**No second `useProduct` call.** Confirmed via `commerce-sdk-isomorphic`'s type (`node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.esm.d.ts:61391`), `ProductSearchHit` already carries `imageGroups`, `variationAttributes`, `variants`, `price`, `currency`, `orderable`, `productId`, `productName` once `expand: ['variations','prices','images']` is requested — which it already is. A per-product `useProduct` fetch would add a round trip for no new data.

### Image-group filtering: reuse base utility, don't hand-roll it
Confirmed base `ProductTile` (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-tile/index.jsx:118-129`) resolves an image via `filterImageGroups(imageGroups, {viewType: PRODUCT_TILE_IMAGE_VIEW_TYPE, variationValues})`, where `PRODUCT_TILE_IMAGE_VIEW_TYPE = 'medium'` and the colour attribute id is `'color'` (matches this codebase's own `COLOUR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID` in `product-detail/index.tsx`). `filterImageGroups` is a real exported utility at `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/product-utils.js:182` — import it directly rather than reimplementing the filter logic.

### Types (mirrors `PdpSourceProduct`'s narrow, hand-declared, everything-optional discipline — not `product-view/index.tsx`'s `SfccProduct = any` shortcut, which is a looser convention from an older copy-first file and not the pattern to copy here)

```ts
// liveProductCardDemoMapper.ts
export type LiveDemoImage = { link: string; disBaseLink?: string; alt?: string };
export type LiveDemoImageGroup = {
  viewType: string;
  variationAttributes?: Array<{ id: string; values?: Array<{ value: string }> }>;
  images: LiveDemoImage[];
};
export type LiveDemoVariationAttribute = {
  id: string;
  name?: string;
  values?: Array<{ value: string; name?: string; orderable?: boolean }>;
};
export type LiveDemoVariant = {
  productId: string;
  price?: number;
  orderable?: boolean;
  variationValues?: Record<string, string>;
};
export type LiveDemoSourceHit = {
  productId: string;
  productName?: string;
  price?: number;
  currency?: string;
  orderable?: boolean;
  imageGroups?: LiveDemoImageGroup[];
  variationAttributes?: LiveDemoVariationAttribute[];
  variants?: LiveDemoVariant[];
};

/** Injected so this module stays free of react-intl — identical shape to productInfo.ts's FormatPrice. */
export type FormatPrice = (amount: number, currency: string) => string;
```

### Function signatures

```ts
/** Picks the demo's one real, sellable line item: first orderable variant, else variants[0], else the master hit. */
export const resolveDemoVariant = (hit: LiveDemoSourceHit) => {
  const variant = hit.variants?.find((v) => v.orderable) ?? hit.variants?.[0];
  return {
    productId: variant?.productId ?? hit.productId,
    price: variant?.price ?? hit.price,
    colourCode: variant?.variationValues?.color,
    sizeCode: variant?.variationValues?.size,
  };
};

/** Cross-references a variation code (not a display name) against variationAttributes for its label. */
const resolveAttributeName = (hit: LiveDemoSourceHit, attributeId: string, code?: string): string | undefined =>
  hit.variationAttributes?.find((a) => a.id === attributeId)?.values?.find((v) => v.value === code)?.name;

/** Base fields shared by every one of the 11 card instances, built ONCE per hit. Returns null if unusable. */
export const selectLiveProductCardBase = (
  hit: LiveDemoSourceHit,
  formatPrice: FormatPrice,
): {
  base: Pick<ZimmProductCardBaseProps, 'href' | 'name' | 'headingLevel' | 'primaryImage' | 'hoverImage' | 'images' | 'currentPrice'>;
  colour?: string;
  size?: string;
  variantProductId: string;
  variantPrice?: number;
} | null => {
  if (!hit.productName) return null;
  const variant = resolveDemoVariant(hit);
  const colour = resolveAttributeName(hit, 'color', variant.colourCode);
  const size = resolveAttributeName(hit, 'size', variant.sizeCode);

  const groups = filterImageGroups(hit.imageGroups, {
    viewType: 'medium',
    variationValues: variant.colourCode ? { color: variant.colourCode } : {},
  });
  const groupImages = groups?.[0]?.images ?? [];
  const toCardImage = (img: LiveDemoImage): ZimmProductCardImage => ({
    src: img.disBaseLink || img.link,
    // ZimmProductCardMediaImage.alt is required + non-empty (unlike base ProductTile's decorative
    // alt: '' convention) -- prefer SFCC's own alt when present, else synthesize from name+colour.
    alt: img.alt?.trim() || `${hit.productName}${colour ? `, ${colour}` : ''}`,
  });

  return {
    base: {
      href: productUrlBuilder({ id: hit.productId }),
      name: hit.productName,
      headingLevel: 'h3',
      primaryImage: groupImages[0] ? toCardImage(groupImages[0]) : toCardImage({ link: '', alt: hit.productName }),
      hoverImage: groupImages[1] ? toCardImage(groupImages[1]) : undefined,
      images: groupImages.length > 1 ? groupImages.map(toCardImage) : undefined,
      // No hardcoded fallback currency -- if it's ever absent, don't guess, just skip formatting.
      currentPrice:
        typeof variant.price === 'number' && hit.currency ? formatPrice(variant.price, hit.currency) : undefined,
    },
    colour,
    size,
    variantProductId: variant.productId,
    variantPrice: variant.price,
  };
};

/** Size-chip values for the interactive picker instances. */
export const buildSizeChipValues = (hit: LiveDemoSourceHit): ZimmSizeChipValue[] =>
  (hit.variationAttributes?.find((a) => a.id === 'size')?.values ?? []).map((v) => ({
    value: v.value,
    label: v.name ?? v.value,
    isDisabled: v.orderable === false,
  }));

/** Picks which of the ~10 fetched hits becomes THE reused demo product. */
export const pickDemoHit = (hits: LiveDemoSourceHit[]): LiveDemoSourceHit | undefined => {
  const hasNImages = (hit: LiveDemoSourceHit, n: number) =>
    (filterImageGroups(hit.imageGroups, { viewType: 'medium', variationValues: {} })?.[0]?.images?.length ?? 0) >= n;
  const hasNSizes = (hit: LiveDemoSourceHit, n: number) =>
    (hit.variationAttributes?.find((a) => a.id === 'size')?.values?.length ?? 0) >= n;
  return (
    hits.find((h) => hasNImages(h, 2) && hasNSizes(h, 2)) ?? // ideal: can demo both multi-image and size chips
    hits.find((h) => hasNImages(h, 1)) ?? // fallback: at least has a usable image
    hits[0]
  );
};
```

**Verify at implementation time** (not confirmed this session): the `'size'` variation-attribute id assumption. `'color'` is already an established literal in this codebase (`COLOUR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID`); no equivalent `'size'` constant exists anywhere yet because no page consumes `ZimmSizeChipGroup` against real data today. `'size'` is the standard SFCC convention and the safe bet, but `buildSizeChipValues`/`resolveAttributeName` degrade gracefully (empty array / `undefined`) if it's wrong for this org, rather than crashing — confirm against one real logged response during implementation and adjust the literal if needed.

**Badge** (`hit.c_productBadges?.[0]?.productBadge`, per SFCC-225): wire it through best-effort with graceful `undefined` fallback if the field isn't actually present on a `ProductSearchHit` even with `custom_properties` expanded — not independently re-verified against a live response this session, and not worth forcing since a missing badge is a legitimate, unremarkable state.

### Reuse-one-product decision (not left open, per your instruction)

**Decision: reuse ONE real product/variant's data as the base for all 11 card instances**, with per-instance prop overrides only for the specific state deltas.

Justification:
1. It's the literal reading of "model this on the 11 states this story-set already covers" — `index.stories.tsx` itself builds `PLPOutOfStock`/`HomeOutOfStock`/`SingleImage`/`MultipleImages`/`WithSalePrice`/`OneSize`/`LoadingPrice` as `{...Default.args, <override>}` off one fixture. Reusing one real product is the same pattern with real data substituted for the SVG fixtures.
2. `useProductSearch` already returns ~10 hits in one call regardless of whether 1 or several are used, so fetching distinct products isn't actually cheaper — and states like `WithSalePrice`/`OneSize`/`LoadingPrice` can never be "naturally occurring" from a plain search hit no matter which product is picked, so the override mechanism is required either way. Distinctness would add a hit-selection resolver for marginal benefit.
3. One real SKU flowing through every "Add to bag" click keeps basket verification trivial during the live demo (one line item, quantity increments) instead of juggling several SKUs.
4. It keeps the audience's attention on the card's own behavioural differences — the actual point of the demo — rather than on "why is this a different dress."

`isUnavailable` is intentionally **not** set in the shared base object at all — it's forced per instance (omitted/`false` for the 8 in-stock-labeled instances, `true` for the 3 out-of-stock-labeled ones), independent of the picked hit's real `orderable` value. The demo's out-of-stock states are illustrative overrides of the card, not a claim that this specific product is actually out of stock right now.

## 4. Real add-to-bag wiring

```ts
import { useShopperBasketsV2MutationHelper as useShopperBasketsMutationHelper } from '@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react';
import { useToast } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-toast';

const { addItemToNewOrExistingBasket } = useShopperBasketsMutationHelper();
const showToast = useToast();

const handleAddToBag = async () => {
  if (!demoProduct) return; // guards the pre-fetch/empty-hits window
  try {
    await addItemToNewOrExistingBasket([
      { productId: demoProduct.variantProductId, price: demoProduct.variantPrice, quantity: 1 },
    ]);
    showToast({ title: 'Added to bag', status: 'success' });
  } catch (error) {
    showToast({
      title: error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Could not add to bag',
      status: 'error',
    });
  }
};
```

This is `handleAddToCart` (`overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:507-598`) with everything BOPIS/multiship/analytics-specific removed: no `productSelectionValues` array/bundle mapping (single fixed item, `quantity: 1`), no `pickupInStoreMap`/`addInventoryIdsToPickupItems`, no `multishipEnabled`/shipping-method-mismatch checks, no `getShipmentIdForItems`/`updateDefaultShipmentIfNeeded`, no `einstein.sendAddToCart`. One shared instance of `handleAddToBag` is passed as `onAddToBag` to every plp/wishlist instance (#1, #2, #5, #6, #7, #8, #9, #10, #11) — correct, not a simplification, because every instance shares the same real variant.

`onNotifyMe`/`onRemove` are explicitly demo-only, not wired to any real mutation (no such mutation exists anywhere in this codebase, and Marcel's two fixed decisions only mandated realness for add-to-bag):

## 5. Working size selection

Adapt `LiveSizeSelectionCard` (`index.stories.tsx:109-124`) as a page-scoped, unexported component in `liveProductCardDemoSection.tsx`:

```tsx
const DemoSizeSelectableCard = (props: ZimmProductCardProps) => {
  const [selectedSizeChipValue, setSelectedSizeChipValue] = useState<string | undefined>(() =>
    props.variation === 'plp' || props.variation === 'wishlist' ? props.selectedSizeChipValue : undefined,
  );
  const isSizeChipVariation = props.variation === 'plp' || props.variation === 'wishlist';
  const onSizeChipSelectFromProps = isSizeChipVariation ? props.onSizeChipSelect : undefined;
  const handleSizeChipSelect = (value: string) => {
    setSelectedSizeChipValue(value);
    onSizeChipSelectFromProps?.(value);
  };
  const propsWithLiveSelection: ZimmProductCardProps = isSizeChipVariation
    ? { ...props, selectedSizeChipValue, onSizeChipSelect: handleSizeChipSelect }
    : props;
  return <ZimmProductCard {...propsWithLiveSelection} />;
};
```

Same narrowing reasoning the story file documents in its own comment: attaching `selectedSizeChipValue`/`onSizeChipSelect` onto an *unnarrowed* `{...props}` spread fails `tsc` on the `home` union branch, so narrow via the `variation` discriminant first. Used to wrap every plp/wishlist instance except #10 (`OneSize` renders a non-interactive `<span>`, nothing to select — same reasoning the story file uses to skip wrapping its own `OneSize`). Each JSX mount gets its own independent `useState`, so 8 independent size selections never cross-contaminate — identical to the 8-ish independent `LiveSizeSelectionCard` mounts already live in Storybook today.
