content.text:
Checked — this isn't a bug in your grid, it's two different Figma sources disagreeing with each other.

`ZimmProductCardContent`'s own recipe (`zimmProductCardContent.css.ts`) has its own, independently-confirmed citations from the *real, reusable* Figma component (not the "Recently Viewed" mockup):
- Image: 432px tall at 288px wide (2:3 ratio) — not 440px. The "Recently Viewed" frame's image area is a rough placeholder rectangle, not an instance of the actual "Image Group" component, so its 440px is a slightly different (and less authoritative) number.
- Content block: `paddingTop: 32px` (desktop) — and **no `paddingBottom` at all**. The recipe only documents a top padding citation; there's no bottom-padding value anywhere in it. So the card's total height is however tall its content naturally is (padding-top + name row + price, plus more rows for variations that have them) — not a fixed box padded out to some total.

Put together: 542px (33.875rem) is specifically the "Recently Viewed" *mockup's* number — a static placeholder frame, not a measurement of the real card component. The actual `ZimmProductCard` was built and documented against its own separate Figma citations, which don't add up to a fixed 542px for any variation, including the minimal `home` one (image+name+price only, closest match to the Recently Viewed card).

On top of that real discrepancy, two things in my demo specifically add height beyond even that:
1. Every grid cell has my own instance-label caption ("Default (PLP)", "Wishlist", etc.) stacked above the card — that's demo scaffolding, not part of the real component.
2. The `plp`/`wishlist` instances render more than the Recently-Viewed card ever shows (add-to-bag button, size chips, colour/size line) — those are correctly taller, not broken.

I haven't touched `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts` — it's a Tier-3 shared component with its own established recipe/tests, and the "no bottom padding" gap looks like it predates this session, not something introduced here. ## ✅ UPDATE 2026-09-02 (later) — Figma nodes received; gate re-scored

Marcel supplied ~83 node URLs. All resolved (80 live, **3 dead**). Net effect: **7 🔴 → 4 🔴**,
and **SFCC-236 is now unblocked**.

### Blocker #1 — CLEARED for SFCC-236 and SFCC-83

`40000223:2822` **`Product card / Product-card`** is a single component set, **20 variants**:

| Axis | Values |
|---|---|
| `Size` | Desktop (288w) · Mobile (179w) · Hero (288w) |
| `State` | Default · Hover |
| `Type` | Home · **PLP/PDP** · Wishlist · `Defualt` *(sic, Hero only)* |
| `Unavailable/coming soon` | False · True |

Maps onto the ACs cleanly. Figma merges PLP and PDP into one `Type`; SFCC-236's
"Recently Viewed Full History" variation states *"same behavior as PLP card"*, so it is
`Type=PLP/PDP` — **there is no fifth variant to design.**

The rail is `40000587:38471` **`Recently Viewed / Recently Viewed`**, 3 sizes:
Desktop **1440** (5 cards @288, exact fit) · Tablet **768** (3 @256 visible, 2 hidden) ·
Mobile **402** (2 @201 visible, 3 hidden).

### Blocker #3 — RESOLVED BY THE DESIGN. It is a bag icon.

`Card-content Size=Desktop` (`40002109:26906`) contains, at
`Content > Frame > Product name and attributes > Product name and icons > Icons > touchContainer`:

```
<instance id="40002109:26891" name="Icon_bag" x="4" y="4" width="16" height="16" />
```

**`Icon_bag`, not a wishlist heart.** The `atom/add-to-wishlist` set (`40000214:6159`) exists on the
documentation board but is **not placed inside any card variant**. Figma therefore agrees with
**SPR-14/SPR-15** (amended wishlist→cart) and **contradicts CRM-113–119**.

Downgraded 🔴 → 🟡: the build direction is unambiguous (build the bag icon); what remains is
housekeeping — someone should strike the CRM rows so the next reader isn't misled.

Also confirmed in the same subtree: `Size Selector` is `hidden="true"` in the default state and
reveals on hover — matching the AC exactly. `Attributes` (Colour + Size text) and `Price` and a
`Link` atom are all present in the shared Card-content, with per-`Type` visibility set on the instance.

### Blocker #2 — CORRECTED, and narrower than first reported

Verified 04.72 (408944644) directly. Its ownership rule: *"Each component is owned by the earliest
epic in the sequence where it appears… if a product card component appears on PDP, PLP and Homepage,
all three variations must be designed and locked as part of the PDP."* **PDP's design scope lists
"product card"; PDP components-finalised = Aug 13 (Sprint 3), passed.** Search & Recommendations
(lists "recently viewed carousels") = **Aug 24, passed**. The Sep 7 dates are PLP-template /
homepage-template scope, not the card.

The one survivor: the Wishlist row separately lists **"wishlist product card"** at **Sep 21**, which
contradicts the same page's ownership rule. 🔴 → 🟡, wishlist variant only.

### Also verified directly (both drop out)

- **SPR-05** (model/item view toggle) is **struck through**: *"as per new designs - this FR is no
  longer relevant. CC: @Dani Rivett"*. Finding about the undefined toggle interaction is void.
- **SPR-16** reads *"~~clickable~~ product badges"* — display-only confirmed; no conflict with the card.

### New findings from the actual designs

| Finding | Severity |
|---|---|
| **No Tablet variant of the Product-card exists** — only Desktop/Mobile/Hero. But the rail's Tablet (768) variant uses **256-wide** cards, which is neither 288 nor 179. Card internals at 256 are a stretched instance, undesigned. | 🟡 |
| **The 768–1022 band is confirmed empty.** Artboards exist at 402, 768, 1440. Tablet sits *exactly* on 768 — the boundary, not inside the band — and the next is 1440, so **769–1439 is unspecified**. Chakra's `md` is 768, so the one tablet artboard lands on a breakpoint edge. | 🟡 |
| **`Hero` size / `Type=Defualt`** — a fourth type covered by no AC, with a **misspelled variant value** and **two byte-identical variants** (`40004599:89265`, `40004638:120484`), which Figma treats as a variant conflict. | 🟡 |
| **`.base-size-selector` (`40003038:125876`) has a leading dot** — Figma's convention for a private/unpublished component. Won't appear in instance-swap for consuming files. | 🟡 |
| **Mobile has no Hover variant** (12 Desktop / 6 Mobile / 2 Hero). Correct for touch, and consistent with the AC — recorded so it isn't later read as a gap. | 🔵 |
| **No loading state and no empty state** anywhere in the set. `Card heading Type=Message` is the nearest thing. | 🟡 |
| **Hover is an expand, not a restyle** — heights grow (Home 489→522, PLP/PDP 522→541, Wishlist 546→565; with unavailable=True, Home 489→**570**). Budget for reflow, not a colour swap. | 🔵 |
| **The AC says "arrows appear to click through product images"; Figma ships `Slide indicator`** (`40002536:7957`, 13 variants, Qty images 5\|8) — a **dot/bar indicator**, not arrows. | 🟡 |
| **The rail's hidden cards are stale**, not a deliberate overflow depiction — 200×472.04 vs visible 201×299.82 / 256×381.85; never resized when the visible ones were. Scroll intent is an inference. | 🟡 |
| **Touch target is exactly 24×24** (`touchContainer`). Meets WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 minimum with zero margin. AGENTS.md targets 2.2 AA. | 🔵 |
| **3 dead node links** supplied: `40004756:477`, `40004756:479` (File A), `8641:2` (File B). | 🔵 |
| **Naming hazards for any automation**: `Image Group ` (trailing space), `Products  Module Desktop` (double space), File B's only page named `-----`, its divider frame named `-`. | 🔵 |

### SFCC-84 — still 🔴, and the design is weaker than the others

The only page frame anywhere is **File B `3332:35655` "Recently Viewed", 1440×3335** — confirmed as
the See-Full-History page by its `PLP Bar desktop` containing text layers literally named
`Recently Viewed Text` and `Full History Text`. But:
- It is in the **legacy** `Zimmermann_Designs` file, which Marcel flagged **PENDING CONFIRMATION FROM DESIGNER**.
- It is **desktop-only** — no mobile, no tablet page frame exists.
- Its grid is a static **4×4 of `Products  Module Desktop` @288** — not the rail, and not a paginated grid.
- Its `Sidebar` frame is **misnamed** (holds the product grid + footer, no sidebar), and it contains

content.content:
PLP, Search, Home, Cart, PDP and empty-search-results, and `product-list/index.jsx:51-53` imports
`{Skeleton as ProductTileSkeleton}`, so an override without that named export breaks PLP at import time.

`zimmProductCardShared.ts` holds DOM-contract constants (`data-card-slot` names). No design values, so it
was originally co-located with the organism (precedent: `zimmColourSwatchGroupShared.ts`).

**Corrected 2026-09-04 (postbuild Round 3, commit `0f35e0c`):** that co-location was wrong for this file's
actual consumers. Unlike `zimmColourSwatchGroupShared.ts` — imported only by its one owning molecule —
this file is imported by two *sibling* molecules (`zimmProductCardMedia`, `zimmProductCardContent`), which
had to reach up into the organism's own folder to get it. Relocated to `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/`
directly — a genuine common ancestor, not owned by any one of the three components — and every import path
updated accordingly. `CARD_BP` was never actually added to this file in the first place; both consuming
`.css.ts` recipes import `breakpoints` from `theme/foundation` directly instead, which carries no drift
risk (single real source) but never matched this paragraph's original claim — corrected here too.

**A second file, added later in the same pattern, was found, fixed, then un-extracted entirely
(2026-09-04, Round 6) — its full history, for the record:** `organisms/zimmProductCard/productCardFixtures.ts`
(added Round 3, commit `5b49864`) held Storybook-only fixture data plus a demo wrapper component, imported
by the same two sibling molecules from the same backward direction `zimmProductCardShared.ts` was fixed
for. Its docblock cited `overrideStyling.md`'s "SFCC bridge pattern" section as justification — that
section says nothing about Storybook fixtures; the citation was fabricated (Round 4 finding). Rather than
just fix the citation and relocate it the same way (done first, commit `d0b0889`), Marcel questioned the
premise directly: unlike `zimmProductCardShared.ts` (a genuine cross-component DOM contract — a mismatch
silently breaks hover CSS), this file's contents were pure test/story sample data with no production
coupling, so duplicating it across files carries no real risk. Un-extracted entirely (commit `3814db6`) —
each piece restored locally to whichever file(s) actually use it, including a second, independently
duplicated copy of the demo wrapper in `nodeCoverage/index.stories.tsx`, an accepted tradeoff.
**`zimmProductCardShared.ts` is the one file this reasoning still supports** — it stays at `ui-kits/` root.

**Manifest count correction:** four files exist with no citation in this section, all added mid-build and
disclosed only in their own commit messages: `zimmSizeChip.css.test.ts`, `zimmSizeChipGroup.css.test.ts`,
`zimmSlideIndicator.css.test.ts` (dedicated recipe unit tests, beyond the four-file template above), and
`organisms/zimmProductCard/nodeCoverage/index.stories.tsx` (a per-Figma-node coverage folder). None cross a
tier or CODEOWNERS owner — all resolve to the same `pwa-squad-a` + `pwa-squad-b` line as everything else in
`ui-kits/`.

**Superseded 2026-09-05 (commit `02a3203`):** `nodeCoverage/index.stories.tsx`, cited above, no longer
exists. Marcel asked for the two separate Storybook surfaces (this file's own curated stories plus that
folder's 12 per-Figma-node stories) to become one consolidated collection organized by real product
variant/state rather than Figma node ID — every one of the 12 node-coverage stories was confirmed to be a
finer-grained decomposition of a state the main file already demonstrated via manual hover/resize, not
distinct coverage. `nodeCoverage/` was deleted wholesale (confirmed fully isolated first — only two
self-referential JSDoc mentions anywhere in the repo, no test file, no Storybook/CI config reference) and
`zimmProductCard/index.stories.tsx` rebuilt as the single collection: the original 8 stories kept verbatim
plus 3 new ones (`WithSalePrice`, `OneSize`, `LoadingPrice`) closing confirmed gaps with zero prior
organism-level coverage. Net `ui-kits/`-scoped created-file count is now 28, not 29 — the manifest
correction above stands for the historical record of how the count reached 29, but 29 is no longer the
live total.

---

## 4. Architecture decisions

**Variation axis = discriminated union (data contract) + declarative config table (layout).**
`typescript.md` mandates the union, and the ACs require it: Wishlist alone needs `colour` + `size` + mandatory
`onRemove`; PLP alone needs `sizes` + `onNotifyMe`. A flat optional-everything bag lets you build a Wishlist
card with no remove CTA (AC violation) and a PLP card with one (design violation).

```
ZimmProductCardProps = Base & (PlpVariation | HomeVariation | WishlistVariation)
  base:       id, href, name, headingLevel, primaryImage, hoverImage?, images?,
              currentPrice?, originalPrice?, isUnavailable?, badge?
  'plp':      sizes?, selectedSize?, onSizeSelect?, onAddToBag?, onNotifyMe?
  'home':     —
  'wishlist': colour, size, onRemove (required), onAddToBag?
```

`'recently-viewed'` is **not** a fourth member — the AC says it behaves identically to PLP, so consumers pass
`variation: 'plp'`. Recorded as an assumption, not a silent choice.

The render body must **not** `switch` on `props.variation`. Layout comes from a module-level `VARIATION_CONFIG`

I checked the ACTUAL current `zimmProductCard/index.stories.tsx` file directly (not memory) — that's the real, audited canonical set: `plan.md`'s own build history confirms it's "8 original stories plus 3 new ones (`WithSalePrice`, `OneSize`, `LoadingPrice`) closing confirmed gaps with zero prior organism-level coverage." My demo's 11 instances already map 1:1 onto those 11 real stories (`Default`, `PLPOutOfStock`, `Home`, `HomeOutOfStock`, `Wishlist`, `WishlistOutOfStock`, `SingleImage`, `MultipleImages`, `WithSalePrice`, `OneSize`, `LoadingPrice`) — same names, same variation/price/size-chip prop shapes. The component's real prop surface (`plp`/`home`/`wishlist` + `isUnavailable`, nothing more granular like a separate "region-unavailable") caps at exactly these 11 — there isn't a broader AC-prescribed set beyond what's already shipped.

But diffing prop-by-prop against the real file did turn up two genuine discrepancies worth fixing:

1. **Real `Default`/`Home`/`Wishlist` never pass `images`** — only `primaryImage`+`hoverImage` (the 2-image hover-swap). My `plpBase`/`homeBase`/`wishlistBase` all spread `base`, which includes the mapper's full `images` array whenever the real product has ≥2 images — meaning my "Default (PLP)" could already be rendering as a full gallery, making it visually indistinguishable from "Multiple images" instead of demonstrating the hover-swap specifically.
2. **Real `Wishlist` pre-selects a size chip** matching the item's own size (`selectedSizeChipValue: 'm'`, matching its `size: 'M'`) — mine starts with nothing selected.

Fixing both now.

content.text:
Both clean. Here's what changed and why.

**Demo now has 17 cards across 5 labeled sections**, replacing the flat 11:

| Section | Cards |
|---|---|
| **Core component** | Single image · Hover-swap pair (2 images, no gallery — new, wasn't explicit before) · Multiple images (gallery) · With sale price · Loading price |
| **PLP** | Default · Out of stock · One size |
| **Home** | Default (badge/hover-swap suppressed) · Out of stock (additive reveal) |
| **Wishlist** | Default · Out of stock · **One size — new, the one genuinely missing card** |
| **Recently Viewed (Full History)** | 4× reused PLP cards |

Each section has an on-page note explaining anything that isn't a separate buildable card — the three mobile-viewport-gated behaviors (tell you which existing card to resize the browser against instead of duplicating it), the real `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)` reveal (provable on any interactive card here, which Storybook can't do), and the Recently Viewed / Wishlist framing.

**What I did *not* add, and why** (all confirmed via the research pass, documented in the file's own updated docblock):
- **Hero variant** — orphaned Figma node, no owning ticket, no 4th `variation` value exists in the component.
- **Tablet-specific design** — no such Figma variant exists.
- **Recently Viewed *carousel*** (SFCC-83) — a different surface from the Full History grid shown here; genuinely has no code path today.
- **Three Wishlist CRM-backed states** (a distinct "What's Now" price type, a region-unavailable state, a destructive add-to-bag treatment) — PRD-confirmed but never actually built into the shipped component, so there's nothing real to demo.
- **VIC/customer-group price precedence** — explicitly deferred to SFCC-778.

One thing worth your attention, not mine to resolve here: the Wishlist section's note flags that the shipped hover-revealed size-chip picker matches PLP/Figma, but the literal Jira AC text for Wishlist only calls out image-swap + arrows on hover. That's an already-accepted design-over-AC-text call from earlier in this build, not something introduced by this demo — surfacing it since you wanted the ACs directly checkable.

The developer reports: "the multiple images state on mobile doesn't work on swipe — the slide indicator is there, but the swipe/gesture isn't focusing on swiping through the images." I need you to find the exact mechanism so we can plan a fix.

Background already known (don't re-derive from scratch, verify and go deeper):
- The component is `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/index.tsx`, composed inside `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.tsx`.
- The gallery is native CSS scroll-snap: a `scrollContainer` div (`overflowX: 'auto'`, `scrollSnapType: 'x mandatory'`, `WebkitOverflowScrolling: 'touch'`, scrollbar hidden) containing `slide` children (`flex: '0 0 100%'`, `scrollSnapAlign: 'start'`).
- The touch-only slide indicator (`ZimmSlideIndicator`, rendered when `totalSlides > 1`) is meant to track the ACTIVE slide as the user swipes — it listens for a native `scrollend` event on the scroll container and computes the nearest slide from `scrollLeft`/`clientWidth` (see the `useEffect` with `handleScrollEnd` in `index.tsx`).
- Desktop hover-only prev/next arrow buttons exist in the same component; a separate always-on keyboard handler (`onKeyDown` on the scroll container, ArrowLeft/ArrowRight) also calls `goToRelativeSlide`, which calls `scrollTo({left, behavior:'smooth'})` on the container.
- The developer's report is specific: the indicator dot UI is visibly present (so `totalSlides > 1` is true and images did load), but the actual touch swipe gesture doesn't scroll/page through the images at all on a real mobile device.

What to actually investigate and report:
1. Read `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/index.tsx` in FULL and its `.css.ts` in FULL if you haven't already.
2. Read `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.tsx` and its `.css.ts` in FULL — specifically looking for anything on an ANCESTOR of the media component's scroll container that could block/override touch scrolling: `overflow: hidden`, `touchAction` set to anything other than the default (e.g. `pan-y`/`none`), `pointer-events: none` inherited oddly, a `position: absolute`/`fixed` overlay sitting on top of the scroll container intercepting touch-start (check the `badge`/`close`/`carousel`/`indicatorWrapper` overlay parts' z-index/positioning relative to the scroll container — do any of them, even though visually small, have a stacking/sizing bug that puts an invisible hit-area over the whole image where swipes would start?), or any `onClick`/`onTouchStart`/`onPointerDown` handler anywhere in the ancestor chain that calls `preventDefault()` and could suppress the native touch-scroll gesture.
3. Specifically check: does the `slide`'s own hover-swap or any other CSS use `transform`/`will-change` in a way that could create a new stacking/scroll context that breaks the parent's scroll-snap? Does `scrollContainer` have an explicit `height`/`width`, or could it be collapsing to 0 real scrollable width on a real device despite working in Storybook/desktop dev (Storybook's own iframe or a specific dev-server viewport-emulation quirk could mask a real-device-only bug)?

5. Check git log/blame on `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts` and `index.tsx` for when the scroll container's styles were last touched, and whether any commit message suggests this was tested only via Storybook/desktop browser resize rather than a real touch device or Playwright mobile project.

Check `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/index.test.tsx` (if it exists) and any Playwright specs under `e2e/tests/zimm/` referencing this component for touch/swipe coverage — was a real touch gesture ever actually simulated/tested (Playwright's mobile-chrome project + `page.touchscreen` or similar), or only keyboard/click paths?

Check for any recent commit changing this file.

Report back: the exact current CSS/DOM mechanism (file + line numbers) governing touch scroll on this component, whether `touch-action` is set anywhere relevant and to what, any ancestor `overflow`/positioning/pointer-events finding that could block the gesture, and your best-supported theory (or theories, ranked) for why a real touch swipe doesn't page the gallery despite the indicator rendering. Do not propose a fix yet — this is investigation only, feeding into a plan. Be thorough and cite exact file:line locations for everything you assert.

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:

   This summary window covers three phases of a continuous session building on PR #85 (SFCC-236, `feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component`):

   **A. Live ZimmProductCard homepage demo** (built on a new throwaway branch `feature/zimmproductcard-live-demo`, branched from SFCC-236's tip): Marcel's original ask — "with PR #85 now open, i want to do something more with the work that we did for SFCC-236... to build off the current state of the branch and render all the variants and state of the product card that uses a live product from SFCC in the current blank homepage to demonstrate it live and to open a draft PR so that a feature-level MRT ENV is spun up." Escalated scope: "we want full coverage on this run; working size setting, adding to bag/cart, multiple images, change image on hover, etc." Confirmed via AskUserQuestion: add-to-bag must be fully real; the demo is temporary/throwaway (not intended to merge). He offered his own local dev server (port 3000) for live SFCC testing.

   **B. Iterative debugging and refinement of that demo**, driven entirely by Marcel's live browser testing feedback: fixing "nothing appears," then "images are not loading," then layout requests ("implement the provisional recently viewed full history approach" per 4 Figma links), then a card-oversizing bug ("are they up to spec height and width wise?"), then a full-bleed-grid gap bug (shown via before/after screenshots), then a total rebuild of which variants/states are shown ("i want ALL variants/states... under the Core component, PLP, Home, Wishlist, and Recently Viewed criterias — this is so that the outputs and ACs are straightforward to check/test"), then an aesthetics pass ("title case labels for each variant/state, etc."), then: "commit the changes and let's take a pause at the work."

   **C. Return to the real SFCC-236 branch to fix two real bugs** (current active work): "we need to go back to the actual SFCC-236 Product Card branch and we have some fixes to do." Then, specifically: "flagging 2 things i've encountered while testing: a) the fix we did to get the hover states working to spec affected how it works via keyboard nav and screenreader/voiceover and b) the multiple images state on mobile doesn't work on swipe, the slide indicator is there, but the swipe/gesture isn't focusing on swiping through the images - let's investigate." This immediately triggered Plan Mode re-entry (system-imposed), requiring Phase 1 (Initial Understanding) investigation via Explore agents only, before any plan is written.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Zimmermann PWA Kit override architecture (`overrides/app/...`), Tier 1/Tier 2 file protection, branch rules (`feature/*` from `develop`, never operate on `develop`/`main`).
   - `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` hooks: `useProductSearch`, `useShopperBasketsV2MutationHelper` (aliased `useShopperBasketsMutationHelper`).
   - Real `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` `productSearch` parameter shape (confirmed via direct grep of `node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.esm.d.ts`): `q?: string`, `refine?: string` (singular, not array — no top-level `htype` field exists; `htype` is only a documented `refine` VALUE), `allImages?: boolean` ("If no flag is passed, the `imageGroups` property is omitted from the response").
   - `ZimmProductCard`'s discriminated union (`ZimmProductCardBaseProps` + `PlpVariation | HomeVariation | WishlistVariation`); `home` variation has no `onAddToBag`/bag button (`VARIATION_CONFIG.home.showBag: false`); `colour`/`size` only on `WishlistVariation`.
   - `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s deliberately fluid image sizing contract: `aspectRatio: '2 / 3'`, `width: 100%` — explicitly documented as "fluid, not a fixed px width" (matching Figma's Large 288×432 and Small 179×268 variants at the same ratio, not fixed pixels).
   - `HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY = '@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)'` and `DESKTOP_QUERY` (from `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/zimmProductCardShared.ts`).
   - `CARD_SLOT` constants (`media`, `badge`, `close`, `carousel`, `indicator`, `content`, `bag`, `price`, `sizeChips`, `notifyMe`) wiring `data-card-slot` attributes between molecules and the organism's own hover/reveal CSS.
   - `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s native scroll-snap gallery: `scrollContainer` (`overflowX:auto`, `scrollSnapType:'x mandatory'`, `WebkitOverflowScrolling:'touch'`), `slide` (`flex:'0 0 100%'`, `scrollSnapAlign:'start'`); keyboard paging via `onKeyDown` (ArrowLeft/ArrowRight) independent of pointer capability (WCAG 2.1.1); touch-only `ZimmSlideIndicator` driven by a native `scrollend` listener computing nearest slide from `scrollLeft`/`clientWidth`; hover-only desktop arrows.
   - The organism recipe (`zimmProductCard.css.ts`)'s `root` part reportedly implements the REAL arrows-reveal via `:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)` on the whole card (per that file's own docblock "point 6", not yet independently read in full this session).

# SFCC-236: fix two live-testing regressions in ZimmProductCard

## Context

While testing PR #85 (`feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component`) live, Marcel found two
real bugs in the shared `ZimmProductCard` family:

**(a) A recent hover-reveal fix broke keyboard nav and VoiceOver.** The most recent fix on this
branch (`983bddf`) replaced `:focus-within` with `:has(:focus-visible)` across five hover-reveal
sites, specifically to stop the carousel arrows (and everything else gated the same way) from
staying visible after a mouse click even once the mouse moved away — a real, correctly-diagnosed
bug, and that part of the fix is not being reverted. The regression is elsewhere: every one of
those five reveals uses `display: 'none'` as its "hidden" state, gated behind an *interaction*
heuristic (`:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)`). `display: none` unconditionally strips an element
from the accessibility tree — it answers "is this painted," not "does this exist for assistive
tech," and this recipe has been using it to answer both questions at once. `:focus-visible` is
itself a browser heuristic for "does this focus event look keyboard-like," and VoiceOver-driven
focus (VO+Arrow, rotor, swipe) is not guaranteed to satisfy it in every engine — a real, documented
mismatch, and *not* a touch-only concern: `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` is true on any Mac
trackpad, so a VoiceOver user on ordinary MacBook hardware is exactly the population this gate
applies to. If that heuristic never matches for a given user, all five reveals (carousel arrows,
Home's price reveal, PLP/Wishlist's price↔size-selector swap, notify-me) stay invisible to them
for the entire session, no matter how they navigate. A secondary, lower-severity effect confirmed
alongside it: because these controls only exist as Tab stops *while* the interaction condition is
currently true, Shift+Tab entry into the card from something after it lands on the last
unconditionally-visible stop (the bag button) — the user has already tabbed past controls that,
at that instant, didn't exist yet, and must reverse direction to reach them. (Forward-Tab is fine:
landing on the always-present scroll container triggers the reveal before reaching the arrows.)

**(b) Multi-image cards don't respond to touch swipe on mobile.** The slide indicator renders
correctly (so the image data and gallery logic are fine), but swiping the image doesn't page
through it at all. Root cause: the organism's whole-card stretched-link overlay
(`[data-card-slot="content"] a::after`, `position: absolute; inset: 0`) resolves its containing
block to the organism root — because `ZimmProductCardContent` never sets `position` anywhere —
so it's sized to the *entire* card, image included, not just the name-link row. That overlay
carries no `z-index`, and the recipe already lifts exactly three things above it (`close`,
`carousel`, buttons inside `content`) — the media/gallery scroll region was never added to that
list. A touch swipe on the image actually starts on the invisible overlay `<a>`, so the browser's
native swipe-scroll gesture never engages the real scroll container at all.

Both root causes were confirmed via direct investigation of this exact code (file/line citations
below) before any fix was designed, and both fixes reuse patterns already shipped elsewhere in
this same codebase rather than inventing anything new — `ZimmColourSwatchGroup`'s already-tested
off-page-swatch technique for (a), and this recipe's own existing z-index-lift pattern for (b).

## Fix (b) — swipe blocked by the stretched-link overlay

**File:** `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/zimmProductCard.css.ts`

- Add a fourth lift entry alongside the existing three (currently lines 240-253):
  ```
  [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.media}"]`]: { zIndex: 1 },
  ```
  `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own root is already `position: 'relative'` (its own recipe), so only
  `zIndex` is needed here — identical in shape to the existing `close`/`carousel` entries.
- Extend docblock point 2 (the "lifting every interactive control" explanation, ~lines 62-101)
  with a new dated fix note, continuing this file's own Fix 1/Fix 3/Fix H lettered convention,
  explaining the media/gallery region needed the same lift the click targets already got, and
  that this was missed because clicking `close`/`carousel`/content-buttons was checked live but
  swiping the image itself never was.
- Extend `index.test.tsx`'s existing z-index-lift describe block (or add a sibling one) to assert
  the new entry's object shape, matching that file's own established idiom for these proofs.

**Verification:** jsdom cannot prove this (no stacking-context resolution — this file's own
"KNOWN LIMITATION" docblock already says so). Needs a real touch check: Playwright's
`mobile-chrome` project with a real drag/swipe gesture on the image, or Marcel's own device,
confirming the gallery pages and the indicator updates.

## Fix (a) — hover-reveal content invisible to VoiceOver / skipped on Shift+Tab

**Files:** `zimmProductCard.css.ts` (all 5 reveal sites) and
`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`
(carousel's own base state)

**Recommended fix** — keep every one of the five reveal targets permanently present in the DOM,
focusable, and in the accessibility tree at all times. Stop using `display` to express "hidden";
use the exact technique `ZimmColourSwatchGroup` already ships for its own off-page swatches
(confirmed real, `molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx:215`:
`{ position: 'absolute', clipPath: 'inset(50%)' }`):

- **Hidden (default) state:** `position: 'absolute'`, `clipPath: 'inset(50%)'` instead of
  `display: 'none'` — out of flow (no layout gap, same as today), paints nothing, but stays in
  the DOM/tab order/accessibility tree.
- **Revealed state** (same `&:hover [...]` / `&:has(:focus-visible) [...]` selectors, byte-for-byte
  unchanged): `position: 'static'`, `clipPath: 'none'` instead of `display: 'block'/'flex'`.
- Applies at all 5 sites in `zimmProductCard.css.ts`: Home price reveal (~293-297, 323-325),
  PLP/Wishlist price hide (~330-332, 338-340), PLP/Wishlist size-selector reveal (~344-346,
  348-350), notify-me reveal (~359-362, 364-366), carousel arrow reveal (~379-384).
- `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s `carousel` part: its own unconditional base `display: 'none'`
  becomes the same clip-path equivalent (already `position: 'absolute'` unconditionally, so only
  the hidden-state property changes).
- **Carousel-specific addition:** the wrapper deliberately sets `pointerEvents: 'none'` with each
  `arrowButton` individually re-enabling `pointerEvents: 'auto'` (so clicks in the empty centre
  pass through to the image). Once the wrapper is no longer `display:none`, add an explicit
  belt-and-braces rule in the organism recipe — `[data-card-slot="carousel"] button` gets
  `pointerEvents: 'none'` by default and `'auto'` only in the two revealed selectors — rather than
  relying on clip-path's hit-testing suppression alone. (Price/size-selector/notify-me need no
  equivalent — none of them sets `pointerEvents` at all today.)

**Why this is the recommended path, not one of several open options** (a JS-tracked hover/focus
state was considered and rejected): there is no signal exposed to page-level JavaScript, any more
than to CSS, that says "this focus event was AT-originated." A hand-rolled heuristic (e.g.
flagging `focusin` as non-keyboard when preceded by `pointerdown`) has exactly the same blind spot
as the native `:focus-visible` heuristic it would be reimplementing. It would also break this
organism's own stated design principle ("CSS alone decides what is visible... no JS-tracked reveal
state," `index.tsx` ~349-350) and introduce real SSR/hydration-mismatch risk pure CSS structurally
can't have, for no correctness gain.

**Why this doesn't reintroduce the `983bddf` stuck-open bug:** that bug was entirely about *when*
`:has(:focus-visible)` matches (a click-focused button not un-matching on mouseout until focus
moved elsewhere) — a selector-matching-timing question, completely orthogonal to which property
the matched rule sets. The trigger selectors aren't touched at all; only the property values
inside the already-existing blocks change.

**Docblock updates:** extend/rewrite docblock points 3 and 6 and the "Fix H" note with a new dated
fix note (continuing the lettered sequence), stating explicitly that Fix H's `:focus-within` →
`:has(:focus-visible)` swap was and remains correct for the paint-timing question it solved, and
that the actual defect was using `display` (an AT-tree-removal property) to answer a different
question than the one it should answer. Explicitly out of scope, left as `display:none`: the
permanent, non-hover-capable-pointer hides (`sizeSelectorUnavailable`'s unconditional size-chip
hide, the PLP-mobile bag-icon hide) — separate, correct, Figma-confirmed, non-regressed decisions,
since nothing about them is gated behind an interaction heuristic.

**Test updates:** the existing `.matches()`-based selector-proof describe block in
`index.test.tsx` needs no change (it doesn't depend on which property the matched rule sets). Any
structural/object-shape assertions elsewhere in the same file checking the recipe's declared
`display` values for these 5 sites need updating to the new property values — identify the exact
assertions at implementation time against the real current file, don't guess line numbers here.

**New real-browser verification** (jsdom can't prove any of this): this repo already has
scaffolded-but-empty Playwright a11y projects (`playwright.config.js`'s `a11y-desktop` →
`e2e/tests/a11y/desktop`, `a11y-mobile` → `e2e/tests/a11y/mobile`; both Chromium-only, no WebKit
project configured — not touching `playwright.config.js` itself, only adding specs inside the
already-existing target directories). Add specs for:

1. **Accessibility-tree presence** — load a card in its default (non-hovered, non-focused) state
   and assert, via a real Chromium accessibility-tree snapshot, that the size-chip radiogroup,
   notify-me button, and carousel arrow buttons are present with correct role/name — proving
   AT-tree presence no longer depends on any hover/focus-visible condition having matched.
2. **Tab-order parity** — forward-Tab from before the card and Shift+Tab from after it, asserting
   the stop set/sequence is now identical in both directions (today Shift+Tab skips the
   reveal-gated controls entirely).
3. **No regression on the original stuck-open bug** — real mouse click on an arrow button, move
   the mouse off the card, assert the control is no longer visually painted by reading
   `getComputedStyle(el).clipPath` directly (Playwright's default `toBeVisible()` is primarily a
   bounding-box/`visibility` check and may not reliably catch clip-path-based hiding).

**Honest limitation, not skippable:** the actual disputed claim — does real VoiceOver announce and
activate these controls — can't be fully closed out by any automated check above. Chromium's
accessibility tree isn't the engine VoiceOver actually talks to (WebKit), no WebKit Playwright
project exists in this repo, and Playwright can't drive real VoiceOver at all. The automated specs
give strong, real regression-prevention signal (AT-tree presence + tab-order parity are both real,
previously-uncaught bugs), but final confirmation needs one manual pass from Marcel: navigate a
card via VO+Right-Arrow/rotor only (no mouse, no literal Tab keypress) on real macOS Safari +
VoiceOver, confirming price, the size-chip radiogroup, notify-me, and the carousel arrows are all
announced and activatable via VO+Space.

## Verification (both fixes)

1. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
2. Full local Storybook build + `test-storybook --ci` — same pattern used earlier on this branch
   for the axe-contrast fix; confirms no regression across the whole story set.
3. Updated/new Vitest assertions in both `index.test.tsx` files pass.
4. New Playwright a11y specs (AT-tree presence, tab-order parity, stuck-open non-regression) pass.
5. Real-device/manual checks, both required before calling this done:
   - Real touch swipe (device or Playwright mobile-chrome touch simulation) confirms gallery
     paging works.
   - Real VoiceOver + Safari pass (Marcel, one-time) confirms AT reachability/activation for all
     five previously-broken controls.

## Files touched

All within one protection tier — squad-owned `ui-kits` component recipes/tests, no Tier 1/2 file:

- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/zimmProductCard.css.ts`

  carousel base-state change needs an assertion update there too — confirm at implementation time)

skills.name: zimmerMANNPostBuild
skills.content:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/skills/zimmerMANNPostBuild

Marcel's own senior dev. Nothing built here — this skill judges what was built, writes what goes
public, and holds the conversation with CodeRabbit and the reviewer.

**Intended model: Sonnet 5 at maximum effort.**

**Input:** `Final wrap-up pass for SFCC-236 (Product Card Shared Component) before opening the PR. HEAD is now at 4740dd5, 5 commits past Round 9's last audit (72ee2a9 arrows hover-gating fix, 983bddf :has(:focus-visible) stuck-open-hover fix, 0748af3 was/now sale price story for ProductCardContent, 02a3203 ZimmProductCard stories consolidation — nodeCoverage/ deleted, 11 stories in one file, 4740dd5 slide-indicator docblock clarification). Explicit checks requested by the developer for this round:
- Check against the build plan (~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-236/plan.md) — confirm the shipped state still matches, flag any drift.
- Check the JIRA ticket (SFCC-236) details, ACs, and comment thread directly — not just prior session summaries of them.
- Check the designs: design spec accuracy, tokens, etc., via the live Figma design nodes (not cached descriptions).
- Run visual checks (Storybook, real rendering).
- Run accessibility checks (keyboard nav, screen reader/ARIA correctness, WCAG 2.2 AA per AGENTS.md).
This is intended to be the final round before the PR is opened — treat it as a genuinely fresh, thorough audit, not a diff-only check of the 5 recent commits.` — a Jira key. Reads three files under
`~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/`:

- **`handoff.md`** — Build's record: steps, commits, Scorer verdicts, rework rounds, gate numbers,
  UNIFORM findings, what went unverified
- **`plan.md`** — what was meant to be built
- **`findings.md`** — the gate table, with its 🟡 CLARIFY assumptions

If `handoff.md` is missing, Build either did not finish or ran before this was written. Say so and
reconstruct what you can from the branch's commits — but flag the audit as partial, because the
Scorer verdicts and UNIFORM findings are not recoverable from git.

**Scale to the work.** A two-point story does not get a five-agent sweep. Honour the scale the
plan chose. Nothing too crazy, no overthinking.

---

## Phase 1 — audit against both artefacts

Two documents, two different questions. Neither is covered by the loop that just ran.

### `findings.md` — did the gate hold?

Walk every row. For each:

- **🔴 BLOCKED** — was it resolved before Build started, and by what?
- **🟡 CLARIFY** — this is the one that matters. Each of these carried a **stated assumption** into
  the plan. **Did that assumption actually hold once the code existed?** Nothing else in the chain
  revisits them. An assumption that turned out wrong mid-build, that nobody went back to, is the
  most likely thing to reach the PR unnoticed.
- **🔵 NOTE** — still true? A note that has become a defect is a finding.

### `plan.md` — did the build deliver?

- Every step shipped what it promised, with its Scorer verdict.
- The diff matches the file manifest. Anything in the diff that isn't in the manifest is a scope
  finding — even if it looks correct.
- Every file's tier is what the plan said it was.
- **Registry churn under `.claude/registry/*.md` is automatic and expected.** Never a finding.

Use `zm-orchestrator` for the manifest-versus-diff conformance pass. It already does exactly this
judgement at step scope.

---

## Phase 2 — the whole-feature sweep

Per-step scoring is **structurally blind** to a pattern applied consistently but wrongly: it
passes every individual review. On this project a systematic spacing error survived five commits
and every score, and was only found afterwards. This phase exists for that.

Run it in two directions, internal first.

### Internal — does the feature agree with itself?

No external rubric. One question: is this internally consistent?

- Every recipe the same shape — same `parts` convention, same registration, same naming
- Every component the same structure — export, props type, story, test
- Every token used the same way for the same purpose
- The same value not typed twice in two places

A divergence here is a finding even when both variants are individually defensible.

### External — does that shared shape conform?

Only once you know what the feature's own pattern *is*:

- **The exemplar PR** — does the feature match what it established? Where the exemplar is itself
  inconsistent, say which variant this work followed and whether that was the better choice. Do
  not report a divergence from an unstable pattern as a defect.
- **`.claude/rules/*`** — do the rules hold across the whole feature, not just per file?
- **Figma, end to end** — the rendered feature against the named nodes, every variant and state.
  Remember the node-type discriminator and never cross-compare the two Figma files.

Use `zm-tester` for this, fanning out across the feature rather than one step. Every finding
carries **UNIFORM** or **ONE-OFF** — at this scope, UNIFORM is what you are hunting.

---

## Phase 3 — if the audit fails

**Hand back to `zimmerMANNBuild`. Do not fix it here.**

The auditor becoming the author is exactly the independence that makes this phase worth running,
and Build has a Scorer and a rework cap that this skill does not.

Report the defect with its evidence, return the work, and **re-audit when it comes back.** A
re-audit is a fresh pass, not a check that the named item changed.

---

## Phase 4 — the PR

Write the body yourself. Do not call `/pr-checklist` — its output is the team's format, and this
one is yours.

**The body describes the diff that actually shipped, not the plan.** If the two differ, the diff
wins and the difference is worth a line.

Include: what changed and why · the tier of every touched file, with any Tier 2 approver named ·
what was tested and the real numbers · anything deliberately deferred, with the owning ticket ·
anything left unverified.

**Never in a PR title, body, commit message or code comment:**
- Claude attribution of any kind — no `Co-Authored-By`, no mention
- CodeRabbit mentions
- A citation of any local-only doc. `~/Dev/fed-handbook.md` and its predecessors are Marcel's
  personal files. Where the same rule exists in `AGENTS.md` or `.claude/rules/*`, cite that.
- Draft or pending disclaimers

Match the house standard by reading Marcel's own previously authored PRs on this repo, not by
inferring a format.

---

## Phase 5 — write it down, then present

**First write `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/postbuild.md`:**

```
# PostBuild — <TICKET>
Branch: <branch>   Head: <sha>   Audited: <date>

## Audit — findings.md
| # | Gate item | Severity | Held? | Evidence |
<one row per row of findings.md. For every 🟡 CLARIFY: did the assumption hold?>

## Audit — plan.md
| Step | Delivered? | Commit | Notes |
<plus: files in the diff that were not in the manifest>

## Sweep — internal consistency
<does the feature agree with itself — recipes, structure, token use>

## Sweep — external conformance
<exemplar PR · .claude/rules/* · Figma end to end>

## UNIFORM findings
<the ones a per-step review structurally cannot catch>

## PR body as written
<the exact text>

## Could not verify
<named, with why>
```

**Then append a block per review round**, as the loop runs:

```
## Round <n> — <date>
Findings received: <n> (CodeRabbit <n>, reviewer <n>)
| # | Finding | Verdict | Fixed in | Reply posted? |
<VALID / INVALID / OUT OF SCOPE / DEFER, with the evidence for each decline>
```

This file is read by **`zimmerMANNBuild rework`** — so it knows what was already declined and why,
rather than re-litigating it — and by **`zimmerMANNDevImprover`**. Write it even when the audit is
clean; a clean audit that left no record is indistinguishable from one that never ran.

## Then present

Give him, in **"ELI5 but I'm the FED Lead"** register:

1. The diff summary — files, tiers, commits
2. The audit result — every gate item and plan step, with anything that failed
3. The sweep result — **UNIFORM findings first**, they are the point of this skill
4. The proposed PR title and body
5. What could not be verified

Then **stop.**

**On his go: push and open the PR.** Not before. Push is the first irreversible, outward-facing
step in the chain, and it is his to authorise.

---

## Phase 6 — the review loop

When CodeRabbit or a reviewer requests changes:

1. **Hand the findings to `zimmerMANNBuild rework`.** It verifies each finding is real before
   anything is touched — CodeRabbit has run as low as 1-in-6 correct on this repo — then fixes and
   commits the valid ones.

2. **Draft a reply for every finding when it comes back.** Every thread gets a written answer:
   - **Fixed** — what changed, and the commit
   - **Declined** — the specific quotable repo rule, doc, or empirical result that makes it wrong.
     Not an opinion.
   - **Deferred** — the owning ticket or the person who decides

   **A fix commit with no in-thread reply does not count.** A prior PR here carried 18 threads with
   zero human replies; the process was being followed on the PR before it and was dropped entirely.

3. **Show him the full batch, then post on his go.** One approval covers the set.

4. Repeat until approved. If CodeRabbit raises the same objection a third time, stop re-running it
   and answer the threads instead — it has nothing to learn from unanswered comments.

**Before final hand-off, re-run the manifest check — not just once, at the end.** Phase 2's
manifest-versus-diff audit is a snapshot, not a standing guarantee. Any fix round in this phase
(a CodeRabbit rework, a reviewer's requested change, or a gap Marcel spots and Build fixes
directly) can add a file outside the original manifest — including a legitimate, individually-
authorized Tier 1/2 exception. If it does, that file belongs in the plan's manifest and in
postbuild.md's own audit paragraph, not left for the audit to silently go stale. Before presenting
the final state for merge, confirm the manifest audit's claim still matches `git diff
<base>..HEAD --numstat` exactly — if it doesn't, append a dated correction (same pattern as
plan.md's own "Open questions" section) rather than leaving the original claim uncorrected.

---

## The owner rule — everywhere outward-facing

The audit report, the PR body, and every reply.

Every finding names **who resolves it**: Marcel, Tim, a designer, a BA, QA. A blocker owned by the
designer and one owned by Marcel need different actions.

**Where the owner is senior or lateral, phrase it as a question to them — never a directive.**
"Should this route via X, or have I misread it?" not "change this to X." Ask confirmatorily.

Before anything posts, count the asks. A review that mentions one person eight times reads as
hiding behind their authority.

---

## Hard rules

- **Never write code.** Every fix goes back to Build. This skill audits, writes, and posts.
- **Never push or post without an explicit go.** Both are outward-facing and irreversible in
  practice.
- **Never write to the repo's config** — `.claude/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CODEOWNERS`,
  `.docs/memory/**`, `.docs/prd/**`. Tier 1 Governance.
- **Never re-litigate a settled decision.** If the plan decided it and the build honoured it, it
  is not a finding — report a *mechanical consequence* of a decision, never the decision.
- **Say what you could not verify.** An audit that finds nothing has not been shown to be capable
  of finding anything.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/skills/zimmerMANNPreBuild

The gate before code. Nothing gets built until every source has been checked and every gap has
been named.

**Intended model: Opus 5 at maximum effort.** A skill cannot pin the session model — set it
yourself before invoking. The plan synthesis step delegates to the `zm-planner` agent, which is
pinned to Opus regardless of the session model, so the expensive judgement runs on Opus either
way.

**Input:** `SFCC-83 and SFCC-84 packaged together. Key question to answer explicitly: are both blocked by / reliant on SFCC-743? https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-83 https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-84 https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-743` — a Jira key (e.g. `SFCC-194`), optionally followed by a depth.
If no key is given, ask for one before doing anything else.

## Depth

Depth is a parameter, not an adverb. Pick one and say which you are using:

| Depth | Jira + Confluence | Codebase | Figma |
|---|---|---|---|
| `quick` | the ticket and its direct links | branch state, file tiers | the named node only |
| `standard` *(default)* | ticket, links, comments; targeted Confluence search | tiers, blast radius, nearest existing pattern | node, variants, states |
| `exhaustive` | full link graph, all comments, related epics, all matching Confluence | above, plus every consumer of every touched file and the exemplar PR diffs | node, all variants, all states, all viewports, token mapping |

Never substitute a stronger adverb for a depth. "In-depth full-on exhaustive" is not a level;
`exhaustive` is.

---

## Phase 0 — position

Call `/session-start`. It confirms the branch, reads the tracking docs, runs health checks and
states current position.

Then confirm one thing it does not: **you cannot be on `develop` or `main`.** A `PreToolUse` hook
blocks every Write and Edit on those branches, so a plan handed to the builder from `develop` is
dead on arrival. If the branch is wrong, say so and stop — do not create a branch unasked.

---

## Phase 1 — gather

Run these **in parallel**. Each one ends in its own findings block. Never let a clean source hide
a broken one — report all five, even when four are fine.

### Jira — `mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_get_issue`

Pull the story and read all of it: description, requirements, acceptance criteria, linked design,
attachments, linked work items, and the full comment thread. Comments routinely carry the
decision that contradicts the description.

Flag: missing or untestable ACs · requirements that contradict each other or the comments ·
no linked design · attachments referenced in prose but not attached · linked work items that are
still open and block this one · a decision made in comments that never made it into the description.

### Confluence — `confluence_search`, `confluence_get_page`

Search for anything bearing on this story: TSDs, integration docs, data dictionaries, decisions.

Flag: no TSD where the work clearly needs one · a TSD that contradicts the ticket · documentation
describing an approach the codebase does not implement · a page last updated before a decision
that supersedes it.

### FED handbook — `~/Dev/fed-handbook.md`

The build approach: tokens, components, CSS structure, overriding, accessibility, tests, stories.
Part I is the machine, Part II the procedure, Part III the role.

Flag: handbook guidance that contradicts what the codebase now does · a claim whose cited
`file:line` no longer resolves · anything the story needs that the handbook does not cover.

The handbook is a derived account, not the source. **Where it disagrees with
`.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`, that file wins** — and say so, because it means the handbook
is stale.

### Codebase

Branch state, and the shape of what is about to be touched.

- Confirm `develop` is current with `origin/develop`.
- For every likely-touched file: tier and owner, from `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` and
  `protectedFiles.md`. **Never from `.claude/registry/*.md`** — its Tier column is a derived
  heuristic and is wrong in places.
- Call `/audit-tier <path>` for anything you are unsure about. It also returns import blast radius.
- Find the nearest existing pattern. This codebase has strong precedent; matching it is cheaper
  and more reviewable than inventing.
- Read the exemplar PRs when the story touches their surface: **PR #64** (ui-kit atom/molecule,
  four-file pattern, co-located recipe, render-slot wiring), **PR #59** (global-chrome component,
  co-located recipe with shared cross-file values), **PR #56** (pure token layer, no component
  change), **PR #85** (organism composing multiple molecules under a table-driven
  `VARIATION_CONFIG` — the reference for any future story that adds a variation to an existing
  organism, or builds a new one).

Flag: any Tier 1 file in the likely set · high blast radius (a shared file with many consumers) ·
work that crosses squad territory · an existing pattern the story would contradict.

### Figma

- Design System 2026 — `https://www.figma.com/design/wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm/Zimmermann_Design_System_2026`
- Zimmermann_Designs — `https://www.figma.com/design/QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs/Zimmermann_Designs`

**Ask for one node URL per variant and per state**, not one per component. If the file-level
links are not enough to resolve the specific component, stop and ask Marcel. Do not guess at
which node the story means, and do not build from a neighbouring node that looks close.

Check:

- **Completeness** — every variant and every state: hover, focus, active, disabled, loading,
  error, empty, success.
- **Currency** — is this design archived or superseded? Triage archived against current before
  anyone builds to it. An archived node that still renders is a trap.
- **Tokenisation** — does every value map to an existing `--zimm-*` token, or is a new token
  being introduced? A new token is Tier 1 and needs the designer.
- **Responsiveness** — frames exist at 402 / 1023 / 1440; breakpoint tokens are 768 / 860 / 1024.
  **The 768–1022 band is unframed**, so anything in it is an inference, not a design.

Two measurement traps that have produced false defects here. Flag a comparison that hits either:

- **Node type decides comparability.** Figma TEXT nodes report a cap-height box, which is not
  comparable to a CSS line box — never file a mismatch from one. FRAMES and INSTANCES report a
  real box and are directly comparable.
- **The two Figma files must never be cross-compared.** The Design System file and the Designs
  file are different sources; a delta between them is not a defect.

**No design is a blocker, not licence to invent.** If the ACs name something Figma does not have,
that is a finding for Marcel — or an explicit **provisional**, labelled as such and carried into
the plan as an assumption. Never fill the gap silently.

Flag: missing variants or states · a design that is archived or superseded · values with no token
· the unframed tablet band left to inference · a design that contradicts an established component
· no design at all where the story implies one.

---

## Phase 2 — reuse

These already exist. Call them; do not reimplement them.

1. `/feature-spec` — turns the gathered picture into a scoped implementation plan and emits a
   ready-to-paste scoped prompt.
2. `/scope-check` — run it **on that prompt**. It verdicts SAFE / RISKY / BLOCKED and rewrites
   risky prompts. This is the highest-leverage gate available; do not skip it.
3. `/audit-tier <path>` — per file, wherever scope-check flags something specific.

Two known traps when calling these:

- `/code-quality` defaults to diffing against **`main`**; `/pr-checklist` diffs against
  **`develop`**. On a feature branch these give different file sets. Always pass explicit scope.
- `/pr-checklist` already calls `/code-quality` internally. Calling both doubles the audit.

None of these skills emits machine-readable output — they all return prose for a human. If you
need to branch on a result, restate the verdict yourself rather than parsing theirs.

---

## Phase 3 — the gate

This is the part that earns the skill. Produce one table, every source, every gap:

| # | Source | Finding | Severity | What unblocks it |
|---|---|---|---|---|

Severity is one of:

- 🔴 **BLOCKED** — cannot plan around it. A missing AC, an absent design, a Tier 1 file with no
  owner approval, a `scope-check` BLOCKED verdict. **Stop here.** Report and wait for Marcel.
- 🟡 **CLARIFY** — plannable, but the plan carries a stated assumption. Name the assumption
  explicitly in the plan so it is visible if it turns out wrong.
- 🔵 **NOTE** — worth knowing, does not affect the plan.

**Do not fill a gap with an assumption and carry on silently.** A missing acceptance criterion is
a finding, not something to infer. The whole point of the gate is that it stops.

---

## Phase 4 — plan

Delegate to the `zm-planner` agent (Opus). Give it everything gathered — all five findings blocks,
the `/feature-spec` output, and the `/scope-check` verdict.

It returns: goal statement · scale call (multi-commit or multi-branch, with reasoning) · file
manifest with tiers and owners · steps with concrete pass criteria · per-step loop configuration ·
open questions.

Write the result to `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/plan.md`, and write the Phase 3 gate
table to `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/findings.md`.

Create the run directory if it does not exist. **Never write run state into the repo.**

---

## Phase 5 — handoff

Present to Marcel, in **"ELI5 but I'm the FED Lead"** register — not dumbed down, but without
jargon that gets in the way. Lead with the consequence, then the mechanism, then the fix.

1. The gate table — blockers first.
2. The plan summary — scale call, step count, file count with tier breakdown.
3. Every stated assumption, gathered in one place.
4. The paths to `plan.md` and `findings.md`.

Then say plainly whether this is ready for `zimmerMANNBuild`, or what is blocking it.

**Put decisions to him one at a time, using AskUserQuestion.** Do not present a wall of choices
and do not bundle unrelated calls into one question.

**This skill stops here. It never invokes `zimmerMANNBuild`** — Marcel does, once he has read the
gate. Discover → report → wait for approval → and execution is a separate, deliberate act.

**Do not hand off with an unresolved 🔴.** Handing a blocked plan to the builder is how a
build burns an afternoon on the wrong thing.

---

## Hard rules

- **Never modify anything.** This skill reads, checks and plans. The only files it writes are
  under `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/`. No repo file is touched — not one.
- **Never write to the repo's config** — `zimmermann-pwa/.claude/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`,
  `CODEOWNERS`, `.docs/memory/**`, `.docs/prd/**`. All Tier 1 Governance.
- **Never infer squad ownership** from `squadA.md` / `squadB.md`. They contradict each other on
  PDP/PLP and are both drafts. Read `CODEOWNERS`.
- **Never present a gap as resolved because it seems minor.** Report it and let Marcel decide.
- **Say what you did not check.** A source you skipped is itself a finding.
- **Provenance, not proximity.** A document living in the codebase is a downstream artifact, not
  a source. If you cannot locate the original source for a claim, flag it **provenance unknown**
  and ask. Never fabricate a source, and never fall back to citing a codebase path as one.
- **Local-only docs are never citable.** `~/Dev/fed-handbook.md` and its predecessors are
  Marcel's personal files. **They must never appear in a PR, a commit message, or a code
  comment.** Where the same rule exists in `AGENTS.md` or `.claude/rules/*`, cite the repo file
  instead — that is the citable source.
- **Scale to the work.** A two-point story does not get the full treatment. At `quick` depth,
  drop the exemplar-PR read and the blast-radius sweep, and keep the gate. Nothing too crazy,
  no overthinking.

**Run date:** 2026-09-04

**Branch:** `feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component` (clean, 10 commits ahead of `origin/develop`, unpushed)

---

## Gate table

| # | Source | Finding | Severity | What unblocks it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Jira SFCC-84 | The story has **no acceptance criteria at all**. Its entire description is: *"This is a follow-up user story for the page behind the 'See Full History' link."* Plus two reference images. Nothing on fields, layout, pagination, item cap, empty state, or auth behaviour. | 🔴 BLOCKED | Jasmijn writes ACs. Cannot be inferred — see #2/#3, which disagree about the page's basic content. |
| 2 | `.docs/prd/search.md` §7.4 (SPR-61, Confirmed) vs Jira SFCC-83 | In-repo PRD: *"Open: additional surfaces from Work & Co redesigns (**PLP**, Find in Boutique, Z.Immerse) are TBC — **do not implement on those surfaces until confirmed**."* Jira SFCC-83 says: *"Confirmed surfaces are **PLP**, PDP, and Cart."* Direct contradiction on whether PLP is in scope. | 🔴 BLOCKED | Adjudicate PRD vs story AC. AGENTS.md doc-integrity makes the confirmed PRD the source of truth for requirements, so the story AC is the thing that needs changing — or the PRD needs updating. |
| 3 | `.docs/prd/search.md` §7.4 + Confluence 04.2 | PRD: *"Current display shows **thumbnail image only (no product name or price)** — dependent on new designs."* Confluence 04.2 (Recommendation Carousels row) open item: *"In recently viewed — what does the full history page look like? Conscious choice for **minimal info, no price no product name**?"* Both contradict the working assumption that SFCC-84 reuses `ZimmProductCard`'s `plp` variation, which renders name + price + bag + size chips. | 🔴 BLOCKED | Confirm the card treatment against the actual Figma. If it is thumbnail-only, that is a **fourth variation** of `ZimmProductCard` that does not exist and is not in SFCC-236's confirmed matrix (`home`/`plp`/`wishlist`). |
| 4 | Jira SFCC-83 AC vs Confluence PRD-027 (Confirmed) | SFCC-83: authenticated history *"persisted cross-session… survives browser close and is **available on login from any device**."* PRD-027 (Confirmed, exhaustively checked — it is the only Recently-Viewed row on the page): *"based on the customer's browsing **session** history."* PRD-027 **does not specify** where history is stored, does not mention cross-session or cross-device, and does not mention authenticated-vs-guest. Cross-device rules out `localStorage` and requires server-side storage; the repo has **zero** storage code and **zero** customer-attribute write patterns under `overrides/`. | 🔴 BLOCKED | Name the mechanism: SFCC customer custom attribute, Omneo, or Einstein. Per the handbook's own rule, *"an invented data source is a story problem, not a code problem — fix the story."* Note Omneo is "Not started" per `projectState.md`. |
| 5 | Jira SFCC-118 (Ready For Review) vs SFCC-83 | The nearest sibling carousel story states: *"The component renders using the **Product Card Group** component (SFCC-743), which controls layout, header display, and product card rendering."* That is the established pattern for a recommendation rail on this project. **SFCC-743 is Blocked** (by SFCC-236), and **SFCC-83 has no Jira link to SFCC-743 at all**. So SFCC-83 either follows the pattern and inherits a Blocked dependency, or contradicts it with a bespoke rail. | 🔴 BLOCKED | Decide: does Recently Viewed render via SFCC-743, or is it deliberately its own component? If via 743, that dependency needs to be linked in Jira and 743 unblocked first. |
| 6 | Jira SFCC-106 (Blocked) | SFCC-106 carries real behavioural ACs for this feature: *"Given a guest shopper has **not** given consent… then there is **no** Recently Viewed rail."* SFCC-106 is Blocked pending a Tell No Lies / Vicky Routley consent review that will confirm the Didomi category and per-storefront default. Confluence 04.6 records the same open question. There is **zero Didomi implementation** under `overrides/`. | 🔴 BLOCKED | Either the consent review lands, or SFCC-83 explicitly descopes consent gating with that carve-out written into its AC (and the gap owned by SFCC-106). |
| 7 | Confluence 04.2 Design Tracker | Two requirements recorded in Confluence that appear in **neither** ticket: *"See full history CTA should be visible if there's more than one product"* and *"include quick links like save to my wishlist."* | 🟡 CLARIFY | Confirm whether these are in scope. If yes they belong in the ACs. Planning would otherwise carry them as unstated assumptions. |
| 8 | Confluence 04.72 vs 04.2 | 04.72 (Component Design & User Story Tracker) says Search & Recommendations design components were **finalised Aug 24** and stories are *"ready for development **Sep 7**"* — three days from now. 04.2 still records Recently Viewed as Design **PENDING** / Sign-off **PENDING**, last dated note *"07-07: Full history still pending."* The two trackers disagree, and both stories are already `In Progress`. | 🟡 CLARIFY | Marcel has stated the designs now exist (answered in-session), which supersedes 04.2. Confirm 04.2 is simply stale and should be updated, so the next person reading it isn't misled. |
| 9 | Confluence 04.72 governance | Hard rule on that page: *"Once a component is finalised and added to the UI kit, **it is locked — no further UX or design changes are permitted**. User stories are written against locked designs only."* This bears on SFCC-236's two unreconciled judgement calls (Home badge visibility, Home hover image-swap), which were resolved in code against Dani's comment rather than against Figma. | 🟡 CLARIFY | Get Dani/Jasmijn to confirm those two calls formally, since design-freeze means the Figma file and the comment should not disagree. |
| 10 | Codebase — `overrides/app/pages/` | Only five page dirs exist: `contentfulPreview`, `experience`, `home`, `my-new-route`, `product-detail`. **`product-list`, `cart`, `wishlist`, `search`, `account` are all base-only.** Putting the rail on PLP or Cart therefore requires copy-first porting those large base pages as a **prerequisite** (AGENTS.md copy-first rule) — separate, substantial work not in either ticket. | 🟡 CLARIFY | Scope decision: which surface does the rail actually land on first? ## Storage-mechanism investigation (2026-09-04) — downgrades #4 from 🔴 to 🟡

Marcel's recollection was right: it is Einstein, and it is already live.

### Established from code

- **Live today on the PDP:** `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:1120` renders base
  `RecommendedProducts` with `recommender={EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED}` =
  `'viewed-recently-einstein'`, inside `<Island hydrateOn='visible'>`.
- **Write path:** `einstein.sendViewProduct(product)` → `POST /activities/{siteId}/viewProduct`.
- **Read path:** `getRecommendations(name)` → `POST /personalization/recs/{siteId}/{name}`.
- **Both paths append the same identifier pair** (`use-einstein.js:522-527`, applied on every activity
  and on `getRecommendations` at `:581-589`):

  ```js
  const getEventUserParameters = async () => ({
      cookieId: await getUsidWhenReady(),                                 // SLAS usid — session/device
      userId: isRegistered ? await getEncUserIdWhenReady() : undefined    // encrypted customer id
  })
  ```

  resolved from `useUsid()`, `useEncUserId()` and `useCustomerType()` (`:447-449`).

**Consequence:** the base SDK already implements exactly the guest-vs-authenticated split the ACs
describe. Guests send only a device/session `cookieId` → history is device-scoped and dies with the
session (**AC 6**). Authenticated shoppers additionally send a stable encrypted `userId` → history is
keyed to the customer, not the device (**AC 7**'s "on any device"). **No custom storage layer needs
designing, and nothing needs persisting to a `c_*` customer attribute.**

**This also dissolves the PRD-vs-AC tension** inside #4: PRD-027's "browsing *session* history" and
AC 7's cross-device restore are not contradictory — Einstein does both, selected by auth state.

### What Marcel saw in development was demo-org data

- `.env.sample:96` → `EINSTEIN_API_SITE_ID=aaij-MobileFirst` — Salesforce's **reference/demo** site ID.
- `config/default.js:143` → `einsteinId: '1ea06c6e-c936-4324-bcf0-fada93f83bb1'` — the SDK's demo ID,
  hardcoded (Tier 1 file, read-only here).

So the working Recently Viewed rail was returning **Salesforce demo catalogue** recommendations, not
Zimmermann's. It proves the *plumbing* works; it proves nothing about Zimmermann's own data.

### Honest residuals — why this is 🟡 and not cleared

1. **Vendor behaviour unverified.** The `userId` is present on both calls, but whether the
   `viewed-recently` **recommender** actually returns cross-device history for an authenticated user is
   Einstein-side behaviour that cannot be established from this codebase. Needs Salesforce doc
   confirmation or a live test against a provisioned org.
2. **Zimmermann's Einstein is not provisioned.** But the dependency is **narrower than first recorded**:
   SFCC-112's scope is creating named **zones**, and its zone list covers Recommended-for-You and
   More-from-Category — *not* Recently Viewed. `viewed-recently-einstein` is a **recommender**, not a
   zone, so this likely needs only Einstein *enabled*, not SFCC-112's zone work. Confirm with Bianca.
3. **Einstein is policy-barred on SIT** (project policy, not code-enforced), which constrains where this
   can be demoed and tested.

### Knock-on: #6 (consent) is strengthened, not weakened

If the data source is Einstein, Recently Viewed **is** a third-party personalisation call — and SFCC-106
lists *"Einstein Recommendations — Analytics"* in its own consent-gating scope. So consent gating is
structural to this feature, not incidental, and SFCC-106 being Blocked matters more, not less.

 *             attribute on "Size Selector" at all) — this is NOT what the SFCC-236 Jira AC text

 *             matching the design anyway — a judgment call made during implementation, not a
 *             conflict that was raised on the ticket or separately ratified.
 *
 * "Recently Viewed Full History" is not a fourth variation — the AC states it behaves exactly
 * like PLP, so callers pass `variation: 'plp'` for it.
 *
 * Unavailable=True (Fix C, SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit) is confirmed designed for **every**
 * variation, not just `plp` — an earlier revision of this paragraph claimed the opposite, before
 * the Default+Hover Unavailable instances for `home` (40002163:39981 / :39990) and `wishlist`
 * (40002187:58452 / :58464) were actually checked. The confirmed rule, identical across all three:
 *   - The PLP/Wishlist size-selector hover-swap is suppressed entirely when unavailable — nothing
 *     to pick for an out-of-stock item, so price stays visible on hover instead of being replaced
 *     (`hoverHidesPrice`/`hoverRevealsSizeSelector` are both AND-ed with `!isUnavailable` below).
 *     Home's own hover-reveals-price behaviour is unaffected — its Unavailable Hover reference
 *     still reveals price exactly as the in-stock case does.
 *   - "Notify me" is hover-gated on hover-capable devices (hidden by default, revealed on
 *     hover/focus-visible, confirmed via every Desktop Unavailable+Hover reference) but
 *     unconditionally visible on touch (confirmed via the Mobile Unavailable references —
 *     Mobile has no Hover variant at all, so whatever they show is the only state a touch
 *     pointer ever sees, and all of them show notify-me plainly).
 * `isUnavailable` and `onNotifyMe` are threaded through uniformly to `ZimmProductCardContent`
 * (the only one of the two composed children with an `isUnavailable` concept at all —
 * `ZimmProductCardMedia` has no such prop); this organism does not itself restrict `showNotifyMe`
 * to any one variation — a caller that never passes `onNotifyMe` simply gets no notify-me button.

 * Fix F (full-sweep follow-up audit, after the above was already built and approved): the
 * Desktop-only "price stays, notify-me is simply added on hover" behaviour above is NOT what

117- * followed the AC, passing `swapOnHover` to `ZimmProductCardMedia` unconditionally with no

119: * `VARIATION_CONFIG.showHoverImageSwap` now suppresses the swap for `home` specifically. This

127- * the Recently Viewed product carousel" — the Badge note above and this Hover image-swap note
128- * each only implement and discuss the Homepage half. The Recently Viewed carousel half has no
129- * code path in this file today: that surface is SFCC-83's rail component, which does not exist
130- * yet and has no entry in the `ZimmProductCardVariation` union above. A rail caller reaching
131- * for the closest existing option, `variation: 'plp'`, would get `showBadge: true` and
132: * `showHoverImageSwap: true` from `VARIATION_CONFIG` — the opposite of what Dani asked for on
133: * that surface. Whoever builds SFCC-83 needs to either add a dedicated `VARIATION_CONFIG` entry
134- * for the rail (both flags `false`) or get explicit written confirmation on the ticket that the
135- * suppression doesn't apply there — not assume `'plp'` already covers it.
136- *
137- * Fix I (SFCC-236, found via live mobile-device testing on this branch, same round that found
138- * Fix H): multi-image cards did not respond to a real touch swipe at all — the slide indicator
139- * rendered correctly (so the image data/gallery logic was fine), but swiping the image never
140- * paged it. Root cause and CSS fix are `zimmProductCard.css.ts`'s own Fix I (docblock point 2):
141- * `ZimmProductCardMedia` was the one interactive region never lifted above the stretched-link
142- * overlay, so a swipe gesture starting on the image landed on the invisible overlay `<a>` first
143- * and never reached the real scroll container underneath. Lifting Media above the overlay fixes
144- * the swipe, but has a side effect: a plain tap/click on the image used to "work" by landing on
145- * that same overlay and navigating to the PDP — once Media sits on top, the tap no longer reaches
146- * it, and Media itself had no click behaviour of its own. `handleMediaClick` below restores that
147- * navigation deliberately, via `useHistory().push(href)` rather than depending on the overlay by
148- * accident: this repo is pinned to react-router-dom v5.3.4 (`package.json`), which has no
149- * `useNavigate` — `useHistory()` + `history.push()` is the correct v5 primitive, already
150- * established in this codebase (`footer/index.tsx`, `zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx`,
151- * `pages/product-detail/index.tsx`) and the same one the base SFCC `product-list` page itself
152- * uses. `href` needed no new prop plumbing — this organism already destructures it from its own
153- * base props (above) and previously only forwarded it to `ZimmProductCardContent`. The handler
154- * guards against the two arrow buttons and the remove/close button — all real `<button>`
155- * descendants of `ZimmProductCardMedia` — via `(event.target as HTMLElement).closest('button')`,
