content.text:
Right — walking every gate item properly. What it is, why it stops you, who owns it.

---

# 🔴 The two hard blockers

## #2 — The ticket tells you to build on PLP. The PRD tells you not to.

**What's in conflict.** SFCC-83's AC 9 reads: *"Given the Recently Viewed component is embedded on **PLP**, PDP and anywhere else, then the same browsing history and tile design is shown consistently across all surfaces."*

The repo's confirmed PRD, `.docs/prd/search.md` §7.4 (marked *SPR-61, Confirmed*), says the opposite in two places:

> Carousel shown on **PDP and Cart**.
> *Open: additional surfaces from Work & Co redesigns (**PLP**, Find in Boutique, Z.Immerse) are TBC — **do not implement on those surfaces until confirmed**.*

That second line isn't vague. It's an explicit instruction not to build the thing AC 9 asks for.

**And it's not one-against-one.** SPR-61 on Confluence (which marks itself *source of truth*) says *"on the PDP and Cart page."* The 04.7 Component Inventory lists Recently Viewed against **PDP only**. So it's four sources saying PDP(+Cart) against one AC saying PLP.

**Why this stops the gate rather than being a judgement call.** AGENTS.md's doc-integrity rule makes a Confirmed PRD the source of truth for *requirements*, and says that when an instruction contradicts one you pause, cite the doc, and ask — you don't pick a side quietly. So:

- Build to AC 9 → you've knowingly broken the repo's own governance rule.
- Build to the PRD → you've shipped a story that fails its own acceptance criteria. QA rejects it.

Either way someone has to change a document. That's not a developer decision.

**Owner: Jasmijn.** She wrote both the story and the PRD row. It's a one-line answer — either AC 9 drops PLP, or §7.4 gets updated.

---

## #6 — Consent. You'd be firing a tracking call the shopper may have declined.

**The mechanism.** Recently Viewed is powered by Einstein (established from code — see #4). Einstein is third-party personalisation. AGENTS.md is unambiguous:

> Do not load any third-party script until Didomi consent is granted. Gate all analytics, marketing, and tracking scripts behind Didomi callbacks.

and, under Graceful Degradation:

> **fail closed on consent** — if consent state is unknown, load no third-party scripts.

Wire the rail to Einstein with no gate and it calls out on every page load regardless of what the shopper chose in the banner. On the EU storefronts that's a compliance problem, not a tidiness one.

**Why you can't just build the gate yourself.** The consent work is SFCC-106, which is **Blocked**. 106 is itself blocked by SFCC-107 (*Didomi SDK — Load & Expose Consent Signal in PWA*), which is still **To Do** — not started. There is zero consent code in the repo; `DIDOMI_API_KEY` sits in `.env.sample` and nothing reads it. **You cannot gate on a signal that doesn't exist yet.**

**One detail worth seeing.** SFCC-83's AC 6 literally reads:

> `Given a guest shopper{color:#ff5630} {color}browses products…`

That red-highlighted empty span is where the consent condition used to be, before Jasmijn moved consent out to SFCC-106 (her comment 13403). The AC isn't just silent on consent — it carries the visible scar of the clause being cut out.

**Owner: Tell No Lies / Vicky Routley.** SFCC-106 needs their review to confirm the Didomi category and the per-storefront default. Not yours to unblock.

**The escape hatch:** this only bites when the rail *actually fetches from Einstein on a live page*. A component receiving products as props touches none of it.

---

# 🟡 The four ambers

## #25 — PR #85 needs a reviewer (was red this morning)

Both stories consume `ZimmProductCard`. Until today that component existed only on your laptop — unpushed, no PR — which made 83/84 unbuildable in practice no matter how anything else resolved.

That's changed. **PR #85 is open, not draft, mergeable into `develop`, and every check that runs is green**: Deploy Preview ✅, Branch Target ✅, File Tier & Squad ✅, Vitest ✅, Storybook interaction + a11y ✅. Playwright and BrowserStack show *skipped* — that's the change-scoped E2E rule doing its job, not a failure.

What's left is `reviewDecision: REVIEW_REQUIRED` — a human hasn't looked at it.

**Why it's still amber:** starting SFCC-83 now means branching off an unreviewed PR. If review changes `ZimmProductCard`'s API, that ripples straight into your rail. It's stacked-PR risk, not a wall — but it's real, and it's why this didn't go green.

## #26 — The rail needs a fourth card variation, and your own code says so

`ZimmProductCard` ships three variations: `home`, `plp`, `wishlist`. Dani's scope note (SFCC-236 comment 13880) says no product badge and no hover model-photo swap on *"the Homepage **or on the Recently Viewed product carousel** at the bottom of pages."*

The Homepage half got built — `'home'` carries `showBadge: false` + `showHoverImageSwap: false`. **The Recently Viewed half has no code path at all**, because the rail doesn't exist yet.

So a rail reaching for the nearest option, `'plp'`, gets `showBadge: true` and `showHoverImageSwap: true` — precisely what Dani said not to do. And `'home'` isn't a drop-in substitute: right two flags, but it also sets `hoverRevealsPrice: true`, authored for the homepage.

`zimmProductCard/index.tsx:124-135` already records this as a **KNOWN GAP** and states the requirement: add a dedicated `VARIATION_CONFIG` entry for the rail with both flags false, *or* get written confirmation on the ticket that the suppression doesn't apply — don't assume `'plp'` covers it.

Same question in a different costume: SFCC-83's AC 3 says the rail tile *"displays the product's index image"* — that's the whole AC. But the Figma rail composes full `Product-card` instances, which carry name and price. "What does the rail tile actually show" needs one answer.

**Amber not red because this is yours to decide**, and SFCC-236's own *Variation extensibility* AC explicitly sanctions adding one.

**Important: this bites SFCC-83 only.** SFCC-84's full-history page gets badge ✅ and hover-swap ✅ — `'plp'` is correct there, confirmed by both SFCC-84 AC 2 and SFCC-236's own *Recently Viewed Full History variation* AC section.

## #4 — Einstein: the good news is you don't have to build storage

This was the scariest-looking item and it mostly dissolved. Established from code, not assumed:

- **Recently Viewed already ships live on the PDP today** — base `RecommendedProducts` with recommender `viewed-recently-einstein`, at `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:1120`.
- Write path: `einstein.sendViewProduct(product)`. Read path: `getRecommendations(name)`.
- Both attach a `cookieId` (SLAS usid — device/session) and, for logged-in shoppers, an encrypted `userId`.

That's the guest-vs-authenticated split the ACs describe, already implemented by the base SDK. Guests get device-scoped history that dies with the session (AC 6); authenticated shoppers get customer-keyed history that follows them across devices (AC 7). **No custom storage layer to design, nothing to persist to a `c_*` customer attribute.**

Four residuals keep it amber:

1. Whether Einstein's `viewed-recently` recommender genuinely returns cross-device history for a logged-in user is **vendor behaviour** — can't be proven from this repo.
2. **Zimmermann's Einstein isn't provisioned.** What you saw working in dev was Salesforce's *demo catalogue* — `.env.sample` has `EINSTEIN_API_SITE_ID=aaij-MobileFirst`, and `config/default.js` hardcodes the SDK's demo `einsteinId`. The plumbing works; that says nothing about Zimmermann's data.
3. SFCC-112 is Blocked — but the dependency is **narrower than it looks**. 112 creates named *zones*; `viewed-recently-einstein` is a *recommender*. This likely needs Einstein simply enabled, not 112's zone work. Worth one question to Bianca.
4. Einstein is policy-barred on SIT, which constrains where this can be demoed.

## #10 — The surfaces you'd put this on don't exist in `overrides/`

`overrides/app/pages/` contains exactly five directories: `contentfulPreview`, `experience`, `home`, `my-new-route`, `product-detail`.

No `product-list`. No `cart`. Those pages run entirely off the base Salesforce template.

The copy-first rule means overriding a base page starts with porting it verbatim, converting to TypeScript, and getting it verified as rendering *before* any functional change. So "put the rail on PLP or Cart" silently contains "first port two large base pages" — prerequisite work in neither ticket.

**PDP is the only confirmed surface whose page already exists in overrides.** That's a strong argument for PDP-first regardless of how #2 lands.

Two things sitting underneath this:

Confirmed — and it's gated on `isOnScreen`, so it's **impression** tracking tied to the response's `recoUUID` (I saw that field come back in my own API test). Any re-home has to carry both calls plus the on-screen gate, or we silently lose recommendation analytics on PDP and Cart.

**Where things stand while the planner runs:**

Gate is **cleared** — your six answers resolved both reds. Three assumptions are now on the record in the artefact: no consent gating (dev-phase carve-out, must not ship to prod that way), AC 9's PLP requirement knowingly unmet, and the base being an unmerged PR.

Two new findings came out of actually exercising your Einstein creds:

**The mechanism works — properly verified, not inferred.** View a product → it appears in the rail within ~4 seconds, correctly isolated per visitor, ordered most-recent-first. That closes the cross-session question AC 6/AC 7 depend on. No custom storage layer needed.

**But a brand-new visitor with zero history gets two products back anyway.** That's what you saw. It's not your browsing history — it's a baseline the recommender returns regardless. The consequence is concrete: AC 8 says *don't render the component at all* when there's no history, and `ProductScroller` already implements exactly that check (`products.length < 1 → return null`) — but it will **never fire**, because the response is never empty. So the rail would always show, populated with products the shopper never looked at. Whether that's a demo-org artefact or inherent to the recommender is one question for Bianca; either way the build can't use response length as the empty signal.

Also: the API **ignores `limit`** — I asked for 2 and got 4 — so the rail has to cap client-side.

One older amber I want to put back in front of you, because it's now build-affecting rather than academic:

**AC 5's "See Full History" trigger is specified two different ways.** Both tickets say the link appears when items *"exceed the visible rail width"* — which is viewport-dependent and awkward to implement honestly. Confluence 04.2 says it should be visible when there's *"more than one product"*. Those are different rules and they produce different UI on the same data.

I'll fold that into the handoff rather than block on it — but it needs an answer before the rail's header is built, and it's Jasmijn's to give.

## 1. Goal statement

Build the Recently Viewed rail and its full-history page as prescribed by **SFCC-83** and **SFCC-84** (ACs in Jira `customfield_10231`), as designed in **`Zimmermann_Design_System_2026` component set `40000587:38471`** (Desktop `40000307:12444`, Tablet `40000730:13363`, Mobile `40000538:25030` — all three authoritative and corroborated by the PDP-template instances `7998:13508` / `8272:28947`) with SFCC-84's page from the **provisional** `Zimmermann_Designs` `3332:35655`, as approached by `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` (token hierarchy) and `.claude/rules/components.md` (container/presentational split), as established by **PR #85 / SFCC-236's** `ZimmProductCard` family — using a **new `VARIATION_CONFIG` entry** on the existing organism (not a new card), a **copy-first override of `recommended-products/`** to re-home rendering on both live surfaces, and **co-located `<name>.css.ts` recipes** registered in `theme/components/index.ts`.

Scope follows `.docs/prd/search.md` §7.4 (PDP + Cart). **PLP is out** and SFCC-83 AC 9 is knowingly not met. **No consent gating** is implemented (development-phase carve-out, Marcel 2026-09-05) — this must be stated in both PR bodies and must not reach production.

---

## 2. Scale call

### The architecture fork — resolved in favour of overriding `recommended-products/`, and it removes the Cart port entirely

I verified the PWA Kit overrides resolver directly at `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev/configs/webpack/overrides-plugin.js`. Its `isFromExtends` returns true when the request names `@salesforce/retail-react-app` **and the issuing file is not itself inside `overrides/`** — the plugin's own comment says so: *"This will return true if the issuer is a file in a base template."*

Base Cart imports at line 36 of `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/cart/index.jsx`:

```js
import RecommendedProducts from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/recommended-products'
```

That is a package-path import issued from a base file, so it **is** redirected to `overrides/app/components/recommended-products/` once that exists. Base Cart is loaded by base `routes.jsx` via a relative `import('./pages/cart')`, which is not redirected — so the base Cart page keeps rendering, and picks up our override for free.

**Consequence: the ~2,460-line Cart copy-first (`index.jsx` 1515 lines + 8 real partials ≈ 948) is not required.** This is a departure from the scope Marcel set at adjudication item #10 ("we only have to copy-first for cart"), in the direction of less work, and it is the fork the brief asked me to resolve. Flagged in Open Questions for a nod, but I am planning on it.

The cost of this choice is that one override module serves five rails (PDP Complete-the-Set / Might-Also-Like / Recently Viewed, Cart Recently Viewed / May-Also-Like). It is therefore a **faithful port plus exactly one branch**, keyed off `EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED` (`'viewed-recently-einstein'`, the same string as `CART_RECENTLY_VIEWED` — `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/constants.js:156,160`). The other four rails must render identically before and after; that is a hard pass criterion.

Rejected alternative (i), re-homing the fetch into a new Zimmermann container: it would still need a per-surface caller, and Cart is a base page we cannot pass props to without the 2,460-line port. It buys nothing and costs the port.

### Branches: two, stacked

- **Branch A — `feature/SFCC-83_recently-viewed-rail`**, cut from `feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component` (PR #85).
- **Branch B — `feature/SFCC-84_recently-viewed-full-history`**, cut from Branch A.

Justification for splitting rather than one branch:

1. **Reviewer cost.** `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/routes.tsx` is Tier 2 Global Shell with a four-team fan-out (`CODEOWNERS:94`: `pwa-squad-a`, `pwa-squad-b`, `tier-2-approvers`, `tier-1-approvers`). It is only needed by SFCC-84. Isolating it keeps Branch A on a three-team review.
2. **Design confidence differs by an order of magnitude.** SFCC-83's rail has authoritative Figma at all three viewports, corroborated twice. SFCC-84's page is entirely provisional. A provisional-design page must not gate a confirmed-design rail that re-skins two live surfaces.

**Consequence to state on the ticket:** SFCC-83 AC 5 ("See Full History link becomes available…") and SFCC-84 AC 1 are the *same* requirement. Branch A ships the rail with `seeAllHref` as an **optional, unsupplied** prop; Branch B adds the route and supplies it. **SFCC-83 cannot be marked Done until Branch B merges.** The alternative — shipping a link to a 404 — is worse.

### How much loop this warrants

Two stories, ~22 files, one copy-first file of 236 lines. This is a mid-size build, not a two-pointer and not a platform change. Scaling accordingly:

**Full implementer → tester → scorer loop on four steps only** (A2 variation config, A3 mapper, A4 gate hook, A5 rail organism, plus B1 grid organism). These are where a silent wrong answer ships: a variation flag misread from Figma, an ordering/cap bug that a naive test would encode (FED handbook finding 18), or an AC-8 gate that never fires.

**Implementer + scorer only, no separate tester pass, on the mechanical steps** (A1 copy-first, A6 container wiring, B2 route/page, and both pre-PR gate steps). Their gate is entirely mechanical — `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run test`, a diff read — and a tester pass would add a round-trip without adding a check.

**Deliberately dropped, with reasons:**
- **No Playwright / E2E.** Adding an allow-list group to `.github/workflows/qa.yml` is Tier 1 CI config (`CODEOWNERS:65`) — out of scope. Without it, `detect-changes` resolves these paths to `e2e_scope: skip` and there is no PR-time E2E run either way (`.claude/rules/testing.md` > Change-scoped E2E). Note this in both PR bodies rather than pretending coverage exists.
- **No page-level Storybook story.** No page in this repo has one; the presentational organisms carry the stories instead, matching the real `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/*.stories.tsx` precedent.
- **No new `theme/components/*Shared.ts` module.** Both new recipes derive their media queries from `breakpoints` imported from `app/theme/foundation` — one source, two importers, no copied literal. Creating a shared module here would be Tier 2 churn for nothing.
- **No visual-regression tooling.** None exists in this repo; Figma parity is checked by eye against named nodes.

**A4 — AC-8 gate hook, plus the PDP write.**

Create `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/hooks/useRecentlyViewedGate.ts`.

This is the answer to **finding 28** — the recommender returns a two-product baseline for a visitor with zero history, so `recs.length === 0` never fires and AC 8 is not implementable from the response. The gate is a **local boolean**, not a copy of Einstein's list:

```
hasRecentlyViewed = sessionFlagIsSet || isRegistered
```

- `markProductViewed()` writes a session-scoped flag to `sessionStorage`, called from the existing Einstein `useEffect` in `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` (lines 772–801), alongside the `einstein.sendViewProduct` calls already there. - `isRegistered` from `useCustomerType()` (`@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`) — the same hook `use-einstein.js:449` already uses.

**Why this shape maps the ACs exactly:** `sessionStorage` is literally session-scoped and cleared at session end — **AC 6**. `isRegistered` short-circuits the local flag, so an authenticated shopper on a device they have never browsed on still gets their server-side history — **AC 7**. It is a strict improvement on trusting Einstein alone: the SLAS `usid` can outlive a browser session, so this gate makes AC 6 *true* rather than assumed.

**Stated assumption (must appear in the PR body):** a *registered* shopper who has genuinely never viewed anything still sees the two-product baseline. That residual is owned by the open Bianca question. Do not paper over it with a heuristic.

- JSDoc with `@returns`, per `components.md` > Hooks.
- Vitest covers: no flag + guest → `false`; flag + guest → `true`; no flag + registered → `true`; `sessionStorage` throwing → `false`; first render before effect → `false`.

### A4 — AC-8 gate hook, plus the PDP write

Create `overrides/app/hooks/useRecentlyViewedGate.ts`.

This answers **finding 28** — the recommender returns a two-product baseline for a visitor with zero
history, so `recs.length === 0` never fires and AC 8 is not implementable from the response. The gate
is a **local boolean**, not a copy of Einstein's list:

```
hasRecentlyViewed = sessionFlagIsSet || isRegistered
```

- `markProductViewed()` writes a session-scoped flag to `sessionStorage`, called from the existing
  Einstein `useEffect` in `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` (lines 772–801), alongside

**Why this maps the ACs exactly:** `sessionStorage` is literally session-scoped and cleared at session
end — **AC 6**. `isRegistered` short-circuits the local flag, so an authenticated shopper on a device
they have never browsed on still gets server-side history — **AC 7**. It is a strict improvement on
trusting Einstein alone: the SLAS `usid` can outlive a browser session, so this gate makes AC 6 *true*
rather than assumed.

**Stated assumption (must appear in the PR body):** a *registered* shopper who has genuinely never
viewed anything still sees the two-product baseline. That residual is owned by Open Question 6. Do not
paper over it with a heuristic.

content.text:
Plan's written. Here it is.

## The headline: your Cart copy-first isn't needed

You scoped Cart as copy-first at #10. It turns out it isn't, and I verified this myself rather than take the planner's word for it.

`node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev/configs/webpack/overrides-plugin.js` redirects any import that *names* `@salesforce/retail-react-app` **when the importing file isn't itself in `overrides/`**. Its own comment: *"This will return true if the issuer is a file in a base template... This allow the base template to import from overrides."*

Base Cart imports `RecommendedProducts` by package path from `node_modules`. So once `overrides/app/components/recommended-products/` exists, **base Cart picks it up for free** — no port. That's ~2,460 lines you don't write (1515 + 8 partials).

One catch worth knowing: that resolver is webpack-only. Storybook and Vitest don't load it. So **nothing automated can prove Cart works** — it has to be eyeballed in the running app. That's why step A1 stops and asks you to confirm the marker log fires on Cart, and why the plan says no PASS without it.

## Shape

**Two stacked branches**, A → B off PR #85.

**Branch A (SFCC-83, the rail)** — 7 steps. Copy-first the container, add the `recentlyViewed` variation to `ZimmProductCard`, a pure mapper, the AC-8 gate hook, the rail organism, wire one branch in the container, gates.

**Branch B (SFCC-84, the page)** — 4 steps. Grid organism, page container + route, turn the link on, gates.

Split because `routes.tsx` costs a **four-team review** and only B needs it — and because A's design is authoritative at all three viewports while B's is entirely provisional. A provisional page shouldn't gate a confirmed rail that re-skins two live surfaces.

**One consequence you need to know:** AC 5 (the See-Full-History link) and SFCC-84 AC 1 are the *same* requirement. A ships the link prop unsupplied; B supplies it. So **SFCC-83 can't be marked Done until B merges.** The alternative is shipping a link to a 404.

## The AC-8 answer

Finding 28 said Einstein's baseline breaks the empty state. The fix is a local boolean, not a copy of Einstein's list:

```
hasRecentlyViewed = sessionFlagIsSet || isRegistered
```

`sessionStorage` is literally session-scoped and clears at session end — that's **AC 6**, and it's actually *stronger* than trusting Einstein, because the SLAS `usid` can outlive a browser session. `isRegistered` short-circuits it so an authenticated shopper on a new device still gets server-side history — **AC 7**.

Residual, stated not hidden: a registered shopper who's genuinely never viewed anything still sees the two-product baseline. That's Bianca's question.

## Tiers — no Tier 1, nothing blocked

Two tiers per PR (2 + 3), which trips **AGENTS.md Hard Rule #10** — needs one scope confirmation from you covering both branches. Tier 2 touches: `recommended-products/` (squad-b + both approver teams), `theme/components/index.ts`, and `routes.tsx` (four teams).

## One thing I added to the plan myself

`RecommendedProducts` fires `sendViewReco` **and** `dataCloud.sendViewRecommendations` on an `isOnScreen` gate, keyed to the response's `recoUUID`. Neither ticket mentions them. I made "these survive on the Recently Viewed branch too" a hard pass criterion on A6 — dropping analytics on one of five rails would be a real regression that no test would catch.

## Seven open questions — two want answers before work starts

The rest can ride along, but these two shape the code:

content.text:
Order's right now. Here are your four items.

---

## 1. `hideBagOnMobile` — ELI5

The card has an **add-to-bag icon**. Whether it shows isn't one rule — it depends on the variation *and* the screen size, and Figma is inconsistent about it on purpose.

What's already built:
- **PLP cards:** bag icon is hidden on mobile, *always* — in stock or not. Figma's mobile PLP nodes have it `hidden="true"` either way, while desktop shows it.
- **Wishlist cards:** bag shows on mobile when in stock, hides only when out of stock. Narrower rule, so it needed its own separate flag.

So there are two flags (`hideBagOnMobile`, `hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable`) that the component ORs together into one boolean before the CSS ever sees it.

**The question for our new rail variation is just: does the mobile rail card show a bag icon or not?** I can't reason it out — Dani's note only covered badges and hover swaps, and PLP and Wishlist genuinely disagree. The answer is sitting in Figma node `40000538:25030` (the Mobile rail): open its card's `Icons` frame and read whether `hidden` is set. One attribute, 30 seconds during step A2. I flagged it rather than guessing because guessing here silently ships the wrong affordance on every mobile rail card.

Since you're supplying link-state nodes anyway, you could grab this one at the same time — otherwise the builder reads it in A2.

---

## 2. Empty state — the codebase already has a house pattern

You were right to ask rather than let me invent it. Three precedents, all consistent:

| Page | Empty component | Shape |
|---|---|---|
| Cart | `EmptyCart` | heading + copy + CTA button(s) |
| PLP | `EmptySearchResults` | heading + copy + CTA + **recommendation rails** |
| Wishlist | inline `empty-wishlist` | heading + copy |

**Nowhere renders nothing.** And `EmptyCart` is the near-exact analogue — a personal page that can legitimately be empty:

> "Your cart is empty."
> *signed in:* "Continue shopping to add items to your cart."
> *guest:* "Sign in to retrieve your saved items or continue shopping."
> \[Continue Shopping] \[Sign In — guests only]

That maps onto `/recently-viewed` almost word for word — and it branches on `isRegistered`, **which our gate hook already computes**. No new concept, no invention, just the existing pattern applied.

So my proposal for SFCC-84's missing AC: heading, `isRegistered`-branched copy, Continue Shopping CTA, plus Sign In for guests. It's derived from shipped code rather than made up, which is the difference between filling a gap and guessing at one. Still worth Jasmijn confirming the copy, but the build isn't blocked on her.

---

## 3. Indexing — ELI5, then your call

**What "indexing" means here.** Google sends a crawler around your site. Anything it's allowed to read can end up in search results. `noindex` tells it "read this if you like, but never put it in results." `nofollow` tells it "don't treat the links on this page as recommendations."

**Why `/recently-viewed` is a weird page.** Every other page on the site shows the *same* thing to everyone — a dress PDP is the same dress for you, me, and Google. `/recently-viewed` shows **whatever that particular visitor happened to browse**. Google's crawler has browsed nothing. So what Google indexes is either an empty page or, given Einstein's baseline, two arbitrary products.

**The three real risks of indexing it:**
1. **Google indexes a page that's meaningless to everyone else.** Someone searches, lands on `/recently-viewed`, sees their own empty state. Bad first impression.
2. **Thin-content penalty.** Google actively downranks sites with many low-value pages. A personalised page with near-zero stable content is a textbook example.
3. **Crawl budget.** Google allocates finite crawl effort per site. Spending it on a page that can't rank takes it from PDPs and PLPs that can.

**The argument for indexing it:** essentially none. It has no search demand — nobody googles "zimmermann recently viewed."

**Where it does matter:** it should still be *crawlable* enough that the "See Full History" link isn't broken, and it must not accidentally leak one shopper's history into another's view — but that's a caching concern, not an indexing one, and it's already handled by the page being client-fetched per session.

My recommendation is `noindex, nofollow`. The only reason I flagged it instead of just doing it is that AGENTS.md says the storefront must be SEO-friendly, and deliberately hiding a page from Google is the sort of thing that should be a decision on the record, not a quiet default.

---

## 4. Einstein backfill — I ran it, and it's worse than I first reported

Fresh visitor, then viewing products one at a time:

| views | returned |
|---|---|
| 0 | `[11736753M, 12416789M]` |
| 1 | `[11736753M, 12416789M, A]` |
| 2 | `[11736753M, 12416789M, B, A]` |
| 3 | `[11736753M, 12416789M, C, B, A]` |
| 4 | `[11736753M, 12416789M, D, C, B, A]` |
| 7 | `[11736753M, 12416789M, G, D, C, B, A]` |

**Those two never leave, and they never move.** They sit at positions 0 and 1 permanently. Real history accumulates *behind* them, correctly most-recent-first among itself.

Recorded. One note on your scope confirmation: it's on the record, but **no Tier 1 file is in the manifest** — so your Tier 1 status isn't actually load-bearing here. Rule #10 just wanted the developer to confirm the two-tier scope, and you have.

---

# Item 4 explained

## What the thing actually is

`ZimmProductCard` has a lookup table. Each variation is a named row of booleans:

```
home:     { showBadge: false, showHoverImageSwap: false, hoverRevealsPrice: true,  showBag: false }
plp:      { showBadge: true,  showHoverImageSwap: true,  showBag: true,  showSizeChips: true }
wishlist: { showBadge: true,  showHoverImageSwap: true,  showRemove: true }
```

A caller writes `variation="plp"` and gets that row.

We're adding a fourth row for the rail: **badge off, hover-swap off**, otherwise PLP-like.

**The entire question is what to call that row.** No behaviour changes either way.

## Why I raised it

Dani's comment says the *same* suppression applies to editorial and landing pages. So there'll eventually be a second surface wanting this exact row.

If it's called `recentlyViewed`, whoever builds an editorial page later sees `home` / `plp` / `wishlist` / `recentlyViewed`, finds nothing matching, and does one of three things:

1. Passes `recentlyViewed` on an editorial page — works, but the name now lies
2. Adds a fifth row that's a byte-for-byte copy — duplication that can drift apart
3. Passes `plp` and ships badges Dani doesn't want — an actual bug

A behaviour-based name like `minimal` would cover all of them.

## But having thought it through, I'd keep `recentlyViewed`

Two things push back harder than the argument above:

**The existing three are all named by surface.** `home`, `plp`, `wishlist`. Adding `minimal` breaks that pattern — you'd have three surface names and one behaviour name in the same table, and the next person has to work out why. Internal consistency beats anticipating an unscoped surface.

**SFCC-236's own extensibility AC already solves the problem I was worried about:**

> *"Given a new style is introduced in future (e.g. Search), when added to the component, then it can be configured without restructuring the base component."*

That's a written promise that adding a fifth row is cheap. So "avoid a future variation" isn't much of a benefit — the architecture was built to make that easy, and option 2 above costs one table row, not a refactor.

And naming it `recentlyViewed` is honest about what's actually confirmed. Dani's editorial remark has no ticket, no design, no AC. Naming a public API around a surface nobody has scoped is speculative.

**Why I flagged it at all rather than just picking:** the variation name is public API — it's in the exported TypeScript union, every call site, the story name, the tests. Free to change now because nothing consumes it; annoying once it ships. That asymmetry made it worth thirty seconds of your time, and I'd rather have raised it and been talked down than renamed it in a follow-up PR.

No 743 code exists anywhere — no branch, no PR, nothing ever committed. (The one line that grep printed is a false positive; that SHA happens to contain the digits `743`.)

## Short answer: no, and the overlap is smaller than the names suggest

**There's nothing to depend on.** 743 has produced zero code. No module to import, no base to extend, no interface to conform to. Every file in the plan is buildable today.

But you're asking the better question — *would we be building the same thing twice?* Here's the honest breakdown.

## What genuinely overlaps

| | Product Card Group (743) | Recently Viewed rail (83) |
|---|---|---|
| Header: heading + optional right-aligned link | ✅ | ✅ |
| "Render nothing sensible when empty" | ✅ | ✅ |
| Semantic heading, native anchor, keyboard-reachable link, labelled group | ✅ | ✅ |

That's real — roughly a header row and some a11y plumbing.

## What doesn't, and it's the load-bearing part

**Scroll.** Our rail *must* scroll horizontally with snap — 5 cards × 288px fills 1440 on desktop, but mobile is 402px wide and shows about one and a half cards. 743 has **no scroll concept in any of its ten ACs**; AC 1 is *"the correct number of ProductCard instances are rendered matching the display value."* That's a static row. Scroll container, snap alignment, and the indicator logic are all ours alone.

**The card itself.** 743 composes a **360×630** card. That component **does not exist in code**. Ours composes 288×432 — the geometry `ZimmProductCard` already implements from PR #85. So building 743 first would mean building a *second* card, not reusing the first.

**The count.** 743's `display` enum is `3, 4, 6`. We need **5**. Not expressible.

**Tablet.** Our rail has a real designed Tablet frame at 768 — unusual in this design system. 743's AC 6 covers only `size=Desktop or size=Mobile`.

**Link semantics.** 743's is "Shop All / View More", shown whenever `showLink=true`. Ours is "See Full History", shown conditionally on count > 5. Different trigger, different meaning.

## Should we extract the shared header anyway?

I considered proposing that — build the title row as its own molecule so 743 reuses it. **Two things say no.**

`conventions.md` says extract *"once the same pattern appears in two places."* It appears in one. 743 doesn't exist, so extracting for it is exactly the speculative abstraction the same rule tells us to resist.

More decisively: **Figma models them as different components.** The rail's `title-and-link` is `40000538:20306` at height **96**; 743's is `40000587:34900` at height **88**. Different IDs, different geometry. Merging them in code would be inventing a shared thing the design deliberately keeps separate — and that's precisely the error the earlier gate made on this exact pair and had to formally retract.

## The sequencing angle, since you're now Developer on 743

Worth naming: 743's only blocker is SFCC-236, which is in Code Review right now. So it could land on you soon. But building it first wouldn't help 83/84 — it needs a card component that doesn't exist, its contract can't express our rail, and its real drivers are Dani's three stories (118, 314, 80), not ours.

**One caveat on my confidence:** the 88-vs-96 heights and component IDs come from the earlier exhaustive Figma pass, not from me re-opening the nodes today. That pass did compare node IDs directly — and produced a formal retraction when it got this pair wrong the first time — so I'd treat it as solid. But when you're in Figma pulling the link-state nodes, glancing at those two header components would close the last bit of doubt cheaply.

## The rail tile is **image only** — on every viewport

Every `Product-card` in the rail has its entire `Card-content` block hidden, plus `Tag`, `Close` and `Carousel`:


I screenshotted the desktop rail to be sure rather than trust the attribute: a title row and five bare product images. Nothing else.

| Viewport | Card | Count |
|---|---|---|
| Desktop 1440×528 | 288×432 | 5 |
| Tablet 768×437.85 | 256×381.85 | 3 |
| Mobile 402×355.82 | 201×299.82 | 2 (exactly full-bleed) |

All 2:3.

## What it resolves

**AC 3 was the whole spec, not part of it.** *"Then it displays the product's index image"* — that's literally all the tile shows. The "tension" the gate recorded between AC 3 and "Figma composes full Product-cards" is resolved: the instances are there with everything switched off.

**It also explains the 17 Aug AC edit.** Jasmijn removed *"and product name"* from the Core "always displayed regardless of variation" AC. That only makes sense if a variation exists showing no name. This is that variation. Two independent findings corroborating each other.

**And Dani's no-badge instruction is in the file**, not just the comment — `Tag` is `hidden` on all three.

## What it breaks

The A2 variation table was specced as "`plp` with two flags flipped." Wrong:

| Flag | Planned | Actual |
|---|---|---|
| `showBadge` / `showHoverImageSwap` | `false` | `false` ✓ |

## Three things now need you

**1. A real conflict with the PRD.** `.docs/prd/search.md` §7.5 (SPR-62, *Confirmed*) says *"Add to Bag via size variant selection directly from recommendation carousels on PDP and Cart pages."* That's what justified `showBag: true`. The design shows no bag. Mitigating: §7.5's own note says the add-to-bag-vs-wishlist choice is *"pending design refinement"*, and Recently Viewed is §7.4 — a different row. Per AGENTS.md doc-integrity I won't pick a side silently.

**2. Does the rail even use `ZimmProductCard`?** With everything off, the tile is an image in a link. Figma models it as `Product-card` instances with layers hidden — which argues for the organism plus an all-off variation. But there's no flag today to suppress `ZimmProductCardContent` wholesale, so that'd be new.

**3. The link states still aren't there — and the planned fallback is now definitively wrong.** I did get the default: `linkLg` textStyle, uppercase, colour `#191919`, and **underlined at rest**. A5 was going to borrow `zimmNavItem`'s "underline appears on hover" — which can't work on a link that's already underlined. Plan's consistent again.

## Nothing is blocking the build anymore

**Eight of eleven questions closed.** The two you just answered closed the last blockers, and reading the nodes closed two more on its own.

| | |
|---|---|
| ✅ Closed | link trigger · **link states** · empty state · indexing · Cart approach · **`hideBagOnMobile`** · variation name · PRD-vs-design bag conflict |
| ⏸ Parked by you | Einstein backfill · AC 9 PLP · stale PRD line · PR #85 merge · #85 docblock fix |
| 🔵 Noted only | `9086:9335` doesn't resolve — nothing depends on it |

## What reading the nodes actually bought

**It caught a wrong build.** A2 was going to ship the rail with a bag icon, size chips and a hover size-selector, justified by PRD §7.5. The design has none of that — the tile is a bare image on all three viewports. That's not a detail; it's most of the component. Had we built from the plan as written, it'd have failed visual review and the fix would have touched the variation table, the recipe and the tests.

**It closed the link states without the variants existing.** I never found a hover/focus node — but I didn't need to. `linkLg` already encodes uppercase + underline (matching the default node exactly), and `--zimm-color-link-default` / `--zimm-color-link-hover` / `--zimm-focus-ring` are all registered in the designer-owned foundation. So all four states come from tokens, not invention. I've flagged in the plan that hover is *derived* from `colors.link.hover` rather than read off a node — defensible, since it's the system's only link-hover colour, but it's a derivation and the code should say so.

**It killed the fallback I'd have used.** `zimmNavItem`'s treatment is "underline on hover." This link is underlined at rest. Applying it would have produced a link that does nothing on hover.

**And two findings corroborated each other independently.** The rail hides the card's name — and Jasmijn's 17 Aug AC edit removed *"and product name"* from the Core "always displayed regardless of variation" AC. Neither was derived from the other; they only make sense together.

## Real geometry now in the plan

| Viewport | Card | Across |
|---|---|---|
| Mobile 402 | 201×299.82 | 2 — exactly full-bleed |
| Tablet 768 | 256×381.85 | 3 |
| Desktop | 288×432 | 5 |

All 2:3, matching `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s existing aspect ratio — so only card *width* varies per breakpoint.

## One thing A2 gained

`ZimmProductCard` has no way today to suppress `ZimmProductCardContent` wholesale — name and price render unconditionally. The all-off variation needs a new flag for that, kept table-driven (no `variation === 'recentlyViewed'` branch, which A2's pass criteria already forbid).

## Artefacts

- `plan.md` — 645 lines
- `findings.md` — 1031 lines, seven passes

**Ready for `zimmerMANNBuild`.** Branch `feature/SFCC-83-84_recently-viewed` off PR #85, ten steps, A1 pauses for you to confirm the copy-first marker fires on Cart.

Two things I'd want you to carry into the PR body, since both are live conflicts rather than settled: the §7.5 bag divergence needs Jasmijn or Dani to ratify, and the link's hover colour is derived rather than read from a design node.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/skills/zimmerMANNBuild

The executor. Takes an approved plan and builds it, one step at a time, with every step tested,
scope-checked, scored and seen by Marcel before it becomes a commit.

**Intended model: Sonnet 5 at maximum effort.** A skill cannot pin the session model — the loop
agents are pinned to Sonnet in their own frontmatter regardless.

**Scale to the work.** A two-point story does not get the full loop. The plan states the scale it
chose and why; honour it. Over-scaled machinery is a defect, not thoroughness. Nothing too crazy,
no overthinking.

---

## Two modes

**`build`** — `` is a Jira key. Reads `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/plan.md`
and executes it. This is the default.

**`rework`** — invoked as `rework <TICKET>` after a PR is open and CodeRabbit or a reviewer has
requested changes. Skips planning entirely; see the last section.

If no plan exists for the ticket, stop and say so. **Do not plan here** — that is
`zimmerMANNPreBuild`'s job, and building from an unplanned story is how an afternoon gets burned
on the wrong thing.

---

## Before the first step

1. Confirm the branch. **Not `develop`, not `main`** — a `PreToolUse` hook blocks every Write and
   Edit there. If the branch is wrong, stop.
2. Confirm the working tree is clean, or that everything dirty is expected and belongs to this
   story. Registry churn under `.claude/registry/*.md` is automatic and expected.
3. Read the plan's file manifest, tiers and per-step pass criteria. **Any file marked BLOCKED
   stops the run** until Marcel confirms owner approval.
4. Record the baseline: run the four per-step gates now and note the numbers. A gate that is
   non-zero at baseline is not a failure you introduced.

---

## The loop — once per step

```
Implementer  →  Tester  →  Orchestrator  →  Scorer  →  [Marcel]  →  commit
                   ↑                          │
                   └────── REWORK, max 3 ─────┘
```

**1. `zm-implementer`** builds the step. Only the files the step names. It never stages and never
commits.

**2. `zm-tester`** fans out its own angle sub-agents, re-pointed for this step, and reports
findings with CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE and UNIFORM/ONE-OFF labels, plus what it tried to falsify and
what it could not verify.

**3. `zm-orchestrator`** returns a scope verdict — IN SCOPE / UNDER / OVER / BLOCKED. Under and
over carry equal weight.

**4. `zm-scorer`** takes both and scores six axes. PASS or REWORK.

**REWORK returns to the Implementer with a specific instruction. Maximum three rounds.** On the
third, stop and surface to Marcel — three failures means the plan or the criteria are wrong, not
the implementation.

### Per-step gates — the cheap four

Run every step. Seconds each.

```
npx tsc --noEmit
npm run test                        # includes recipeGuards, the hard styling gate
npm run lint                        # compare counts, not the exit code
node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs    # new unacknowledged findings only
```

Two traps: `npm run lint` exits non-zero at a healthy baseline, so **compare the count against
your baseline and ignore the exit code**. And never append arguments to it — `pwa-kit-dev lint`
forwards `--`-args into `execSync`, which can silently turn the gate into a writer.

The plan's per-step pass criteria layer **on top of** these, they do not replace them.

### The visual checkpoint

**After any step that changes rendered output, the loop stops.** The plan marks which steps those
are; if it doesn't, assume any step touching a component, a recipe or a page does.

Tell Marcel exactly:
- the URL and the viewport to open
- the Figma node to compare against — the one for **that variant and state**
- what should be on screen
- what would indicate a defect, including anything that will look wrong but is correct

Then **wait.** Do not proceed on assumption. This is the only gate on this stack that catches a
layout defect — `width: 'xl'` passed every automated check and destroyed the global footer.

Until it has happened, the Scorer's Design fidelity axis is UNVERIFIED, not passed.

### The commit

**The skill commits, not an agent.** Only after: Scorer PASS, and the visual checkpoint passed if
one was owed.

One step, one commit. Conventional Commits — the `commit-msg` hook enforces it. **No Claude
attribution, no CodeRabbit mentions, no `Co-Authored-By` line.** Use Marcel's previously authored
commits on this repo as the reference for tone and body.

Then move to the next step.

---

## Before handing off

Once every step has passed, run the expensive gates **once**:

```
npm run build-storybook             # then run the interaction + a11y suite against it
npm run test:story                  # real BrowserStack, scoped to the Jira key
npm run test:max-file-size          # runs a full build
cr review --base develop            # CodeRabbit locally, full review before anything is public
```

Storybook needs a verified-free port and a build you can prove is yours — a stale server on 6006
produced a silently meaningless pass once. Check the served build matches your own before trusting
any result.

Then **write the handoff** to `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/handoff.md`:

```
# Handoff — <TICKET>
Branch: <branch>   Base: <sha>   Head: <sha>

## Steps
| # | What | Commit | Scorer verdict | Rework rounds |

## Gates (real numbers, not claims)
| Gate | Result | Baseline |

## UNIFORM findings
<each one, with file:line — these are what a per-step review structurally cannot catch>

## Could not verify
<named, with why>

## Outstanding
<anything left, or "none">
```

**Write it even when everything passed.** PostBuild reads this file, and it may run in a different
session — a handoff that exists only in conversation does not survive the session ending.

Then present the same content to Marcel and **hand off to `zimmerMANNPostBuild`. This skill does
not push and does not open a PR.**

---

## Rework mode

Entered after a PR is open and CodeRabbit or a reviewer has requested changes.

**Read `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/postbuild.md` first.** It records what earlier rounds
already declined and why. A finding that was declined with evidence in round one does not get
re-litigated in round three — check before you verify anything, and if you disagree with a previous
decline, say so rather than silently reversing it.

**1. Verify every finding before touching anything.** CodeRabbit has been wrong on this repo
often — one batch ran 1-in-6 correct. Treat each finding as a hypothesis, not a fact. Per finding:

- **VALID** — reproduce it, cite `file:line`, fix it
- **INVALID** — say what is actually true, with the evidence, and draft the reply
- **OUT OF SCOPE** — real but not this story's problem; name the owning ticket or the person
- **DEFER** — real, in scope, but blocked on a decision; name who decides

**2. Fix only the VALID ones.** Same rules as build mode — the Implementer touches only what the
finding names, never stages, never commits.

**3. Re-run the cheap four**, plus the visual checkpoint if the fix changes rendered output.

**4. Commit the fixes here**, same rule as build mode — the skill commits, never an agent. Reference
the review thread each commit answers.

**5. Hand back to `zimmerMANNPostBuild`** with: what was fixed and in which commit, what was
declined and why, and the evidence behind each decline. **PostBuild owns the push and the
in-thread replies** — every finding gets a written answer, including the declined ones.

---

## Hard rules

- **Never push. Never open or update a PR.** That boundary belongs to PostBuild, which presents
  first and pushes only once Marcel has given the go.
- **Never write to the repo's config** — `.claude/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CODEOWNERS`,
  `.docs/memory/**`, `.docs/prd/**`. Tier 1 Governance.
- **Never touch a Tier 1 file** without Marcel naming it and confirming owner approval.
- **Never expand scope.** Something worth doing that the plan didn't ask for gets reported, not
  done. Report it and let Marcel decide.
- **Local-only docs are never citable** in a commit message or a code comment. Cite `AGENTS.md`
  or `.claude/rules/*` instead.
- **Say what you could not verify.** Silence reads as "nothing wrong" when it may mean
  "didn't look there".

# Tier 2 — Protected Files

These can be modified on a feature branch but require a PR review from a developer who is not
the author before merging to develop.

> Paths reference `overrides/app/...` per this project's slim overrides layout. Override files
> keep the original Salesforce filename (kebab-case) but are TypeScript (`.ts`/`.tsx`).

## Global Shell (Owner: Both Squads — coordinate before touching)

```text
overrides/app/components/header/
overrides/app/components/footer/
overrides/app/components/drawer-menu/
overrides/app/components/list-menu/
overrides/app/components/seo/
overrides/app/components/_app/
overrides/app/components/_app-config/
overrides/app/components/uiCopyProvider/
overrides/app/routes.tsx
```

`uiCopyProvider/` is mounted once inside `_app-config` and provides `useUiCopy()`'s context
value to every page on every site — the same blast radius as `_app-config` itself, so it
belongs in this tier alongside it rather than defaulting to Tier 4 by omission.

## Shared Product Components (Owner: Squad B — notify Squad A)

```text
overrides/app/components/product-tile/
overrides/app/components/product-item/
overrides/app/components/display-price/
```

# Tagging & Environment Promotion

How releases are versioned, tagged, and promoted through the environments. This is the
day-to-day companion to the branch rules in [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) (Branch Rules) and the
supervised-release flow in [.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md](../../.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md) —
this file covers **tags and promotion**, those cover **branches**.

---

## Tag taxonomy

Every deployable version is an **immutable, annotated git tag**. The **tag-promoted** tiers
(`test` / `uat` / `staging` / `prod`) deploy a specific tag — never "whatever's on a branch right
now." (The continuous tiers are the exception: `dev` and `sit` deploy commit refs, and Test also
takes a branch ref for on-demand quick looks — see the Environment model below.)

| Pattern | Meaning | Example | Cut from | Who |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `vX.Y.Z-rc.N` | Release candidate — a stabilising snapshot, cheap to iterate | `v0.1.0-rc.2` | a commit on `release/vX.Y.Z` | **any developer** |
| `vX.Y.Z` | Final release — the exact candidate that passed every gate | `v0.1.0` | the `release/vX.Y.Z` commit merged to `main` | **tier-1-approver only** |
| `vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N` | Emergency fix candidate, outside the normal train | `v0.1.1-hotfix.1` | a commit on `hotfix/vX.Y.Z` | **tier-1-approver only** |

**Versioning:**
- **MAJOR** locked at `0` pre-launch (SemVer reserves `0.y.z` for initial development). `v1.0.0`
  is reserved for **go-live**; MAJOR reverts to its normal rare-breaking-change meaning after.
- **MINOR** bumps once per sprint, when a new `release/vX.Y.Z` branch is cut — sprint 1 = `v0.1.0`,
  sprint 2 = `v0.2.0`.
- **PATCH** = bug-fix-only release against an already-shipped `MAJOR.MINOR` (e.g. a hotfix after
  `v0.1.0` → `v0.1.1`).
- The `-rc.N` counter is a plain incrementing number, **not** an environment reference — it counts
  candidate builds, not deployments. The same `v0.1.0-rc.1` can be deployed (and re-deployed) to
  Test on demand; which environment ran which candidate is tracked via each `deploy-*.yml`'s Actions
  run history, not the tag name.
- The dot in `-rc.N` matters: SemVer compares `rc.10 > rc.2` numerically only as dot-separated
  fields; `rc10`/`rc2` would sort alphabetically (wrong). This is exactly what the version-guard
  relies on.

Non-`v*` tags are a separate namespace and unaffected by any of this: `sprint/{N}/{date}` (sprint
rollover, auto-cut by `deploy-dev.yml`) and any `sit/deploy/*` refs.

---

## Cutting a tag

Tags are cut with a **tag-only push** — a raw annotated `git tag`, then pushing the tag alone. We
deliberately avoid `npm version`: it creates a local `package.json`-bump *commit* alongside the tag,
and pushing that commit to the release branch is blocked by `release/**` branch protection
(`isAdminEnforced`, no bypass). Pushing only the tag sidesteps this — a tag push is not a branch
push. **Consequence:** `package.json`'s `version` field does not auto-track each candidate — it is
bumped once, deliberately, at the final-release PR.

**Release candidate (any developer):**

```bash
git checkout release/v0.1.0 && git pull --ff-only   # fail rather than tag a local merge commit
git tag -a v0.1.0-rc.0 -m "Release candidate v0.1.0-rc.0"
git push origin v0.1.0-rc.0           # tag only — NOT a branch push
gh workflow run deploy-test.yml -f ref=v0.1.0-rc.0
```

- Always **annotated** (`-a -m`) — the tagger identity, timestamp, and message live in the tag
  object (`git show v0.1.0-rc.0`). Never lightweight.
- A tag push is not a branch push, so branch protection doesn't block it.

**Final release (tier-1-approver only):** cut `vX.Y.Z` on the release-branch commit being merged to
`main`, then promote it up through `uat` → `staging` → `prod`. Run [`/generate-changelog`](../skills/generate-changelog/SKILL.md)
at this point to produce the GitHub Release.

**Rollback.** The downgrade guard (see below) deliberately blocks deploying an older tag, so a
rollback takes one of two authorised paths:

- **Emergency (fastest) — re-activate the previous bundle in Managed Runtime**, outside the deploy
  pipeline (the rollback procedure in the Environment Topology doc). This does not run the guard, so
  afterwards re-record the baseline so it doesn't treat a superseded tag as live:
  `node scripts/versionGuard.mjs record prod v0.1.0`.
- **Controlled — pipeline rollback with the guard override.** Redeploy the known-good tag with
  `rollback=true`; the guard's downgrade check is skipped (the run logs the skip for audit) and
  `record` still runs, so the rolled-back tag becomes the new live baseline:
  `gh workflow run deploy-prod.yml -f ref=v0.1.0 -f rollback=true`. Because this bypasses the guard,
  its only human gate is the environment's **required reviewers** — so `prod` (and `staging`/`uat`)
  must have required reviewers with "prevent self-review" configured. **Prerequisite: until that is
  set, `rollback=true` is not gated.**

---

## Enforcement — what actually holds the line

On this org's GitHub **`team`** plan, ruleset *metadata* rules (`tag_name_pattern`) are
Enterprise-only and silently **inert** — a malformed `v*` tag is not blocked at push time by a
ruleset. Naming is enforced by the hook and workflow below, not the rulesets. Three layers, in
order of reliability:

1. **Pre-push hook** ([.husky/pre-push](../../.husky/pre-push) → [scripts/hooks/pre-push](../../scripts/hooks/pre-push))
   — *best-effort prevention*. Rejects a malformed `v*` tag before it leaves the developer's machine
   — the earliest catch, but bypassable (`git push --no-verify`, or a checkout without the hook
   installed), so not a hard guarantee. Allowed: `vX.Y.Z-rc.N`, `vX.Y.Z`, `vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N`.
   Non-`v*` tags and branch pushes pass through untouched.
2. **`tag-validate.yml`** ([.github/workflows/tag-validate.yml](../../.github/workflows/tag-validate.yml))
   — *detection*. Fails if a malformed `v*` tag lands on the remote (post-hoc alert, not a block).
3. **GitHub Rulesets** `tag-rc` (id 20487306) + `tag-release` (id 20487243) — enforce what core rules
   *can* on the `team` plan: **immutability** (`update` + `deletion` restricted) and **tier-1-only
   final tags** (`creation` restricted on `tag-release`, bypass = `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`).
   Their `tag_name_pattern` rules (`^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+-rc\.\d+$` and `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-hotfix\.\d+)?$`)
   are **kept but inert on `team`** — they self-activate if the org ever upgrades to Enterprise.

GitHub ruleset objects have no free-text description field, so the "inert on team" caveat can't
live on the ruleset itself — this section is its canonical record. The rulesets may optionally be
renamed in Settings → Rules to append " — naming inert on team plan" for an at-a-glance signal.

---

## Environment model — two categories

| Category | Environments | How it deploys |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Continuous / auto** | `dev`, `sit` | No human-picked tag. `dev` auto-deploys every `develop` merge; `sit` deploys the gate's commit via `workflow_run` off the SIT Gate on `release/**`. |
| **Tag-promoted / deliberate** | `test`, `uat`, `staging`, `prod` | `workflow_dispatch` with a specific tag `ref`. Each can sit on a different tag simultaneously, decoupling their cadences. |

**SIT stays branch/gate-driven** — its `workflow_run` trigger off the SIT Gate on `release/**` is
unchanged. This is an intentional exception to "every environment sits on a named tag": SIT is a
continuous auto-integration tier, the same category as `dev`, not a deliberate pinned-promotion
tier. Using tags is not the same as being triggered by a tag — tags and Releases still exist and are
visible; SIT simply auto-refreshes.

**Environment names are the real GitHub Environment names** — `dev / test / sit / uat / staging /
prod`. Tooling must key off these, not the workflow-file suffix: `deploy-stg.yml` binds
`environment: staging` (the `stg`≠`staging` mismatch already caused a bug once).

---

## Downgrade protection (version-guard)

[scripts/versionGuard.mjs](../../scripts/versionGuard.mjs), wired into the four tag-promoted
`deploy-*.yml` workflows:

- **`check <env> <ref>`** runs *before* the push: reads the environment's last recorded deployed tag
  and **blocks** if `ref` is semver-older (`semver.lt`). Skips non-`v*` refs, allows the first-ever
  deploy, and **fails closed** on any lookup/parse error.
- **`record <env> <ref>`** runs *after* a successful push: stamps the deployed tag as an explicit
  GitHub Deployment (the auto-created Deployment records the *trigger* ref, not the deployed tag, so
  we record it ourselves and read it back).
- **`dev` and `sit` are excluded** — they have no human-picked `ref` to compare (consistent with the
  two-category model above).
- Guard/record key off the **GitHub Environment name** (`stg`→`staging`).

---

## The Test gate

`deploy-test.yml` runs **deploy-then-gate**: it deploys first (Test is the fast, disposable
quick-look tier), then a post-deploy gate verifies the same build. The run's overall pass/fail is the
**"safe to promote to SIT"** signal.

- **`bundle-size`** — `npm run test:max-file-size`, enforcing the `package.json` budgets
  (`main.js` ≤ 180 kB, `vendor.js` ≤ 550 kB). Bundle-size is cheap, deterministic, and mobile
  page-speed is a top project priority, so bloat is caught at the earliest deployed tier.
- **P0 Playwright** — attaches to the same gate once a `*.p0.spec` exists (Lead QA, gherkin-first);
  it targets the Test storefront via the `test` env's `RETAIL_APP_HOME` variable.

This intentionally differs from SIT's **gate-then-deploy** (`digital-sit.yml`), which can hang a
pre-check on a `release/**` push event that Test doesn't have.

---
