# SFCC-236: fix two live-testing regressions in ZimmProductCard

## Context

While testing PR #85 (`feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component`) live, Marcel found two
real bugs in the shared `ZimmProductCard` family:

**(a) A recent hover-reveal fix broke keyboard nav and VoiceOver.** The most recent fix on this
branch (`983bddf`) replaced `:focus-within` with `:has(:focus-visible)` across five hover-reveal
sites, specifically to stop the carousel arrows (and everything else gated the same way) from
staying visible after a mouse click even once the mouse moved away — a real, correctly-diagnosed
bug, and that part of the fix is not being reverted. The regression is elsewhere: every one of
those five reveals uses `display: 'none'` as its "hidden" state, gated behind an *interaction*
heuristic (`:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)`). `display: none` unconditionally strips an element
from the accessibility tree — it answers "is this painted," not "does this exist for assistive
tech," and this recipe has been using it to answer both questions at once. `:focus-visible` is
itself a browser heuristic for "does this focus event look keyboard-like," and VoiceOver-driven
focus (VO+Arrow, rotor, swipe) is not guaranteed to satisfy it in every engine — a real, documented
mismatch, and *not* a touch-only concern: `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` is true on any Mac
trackpad, so a VoiceOver user on ordinary MacBook hardware is exactly the population this gate
applies to. If that heuristic never matches for a given user, all five reveals (carousel arrows,
Home's price reveal, PLP/Wishlist's price↔size-selector swap, notify-me) stay invisible to them
for the entire session, no matter how they navigate. A secondary, lower-severity effect confirmed
alongside it: because these controls only exist as Tab stops *while* the interaction condition is
currently true, Shift+Tab entry into the card from something after it lands on the last
unconditionally-visible stop (the bag button) — the user has already tabbed past controls that,
at that instant, didn't exist yet, and must reverse direction to reach them. (Forward-Tab is fine:
landing on the always-present scroll container triggers the reveal before reaching the arrows.)

**(b) Multi-image cards don't respond to touch swipe on mobile.** The slide indicator renders
correctly (so the image data and gallery logic are fine), but swiping the image doesn't page
through it at all. Root cause: the organism's whole-card stretched-link overlay
(`[data-card-slot="content"] a::after`, `position: absolute; inset: 0`) resolves its containing
block to the organism root — because `ZimmProductCardContent` never sets `position` anywhere —
so it's sized to the *entire* card, image included, not just the name-link row. That overlay
carries no `z-index`, and the recipe already lifts exactly three things above it (`close`,
`carousel`, buttons inside `content`) — the media/gallery scroll region was never added to that
list. A touch swipe on the image actually starts on the invisible overlay `<a>`, so the browser's
native swipe-scroll gesture never engages the real scroll container at all.

Both root causes were confirmed via direct investigation of this exact code (file/line citations
below) before any fix was designed, and both fixes reuse patterns already shipped elsewhere in
this same codebase rather than inventing anything new — `ZimmColourSwatchGroup`'s already-tested
off-page-swatch technique for (a), and this recipe's own existing z-index-lift pattern for (b).

## Fix (b) — swipe blocked by the stretched-link overlay

**File:** `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/zimmProductCard.css.ts`

- Add a fourth lift entry alongside the existing three (currently lines 240-253):
  ```
  [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.media}"]`]: { zIndex: 1 },
  ```
  `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own root is already `position: 'relative'` (its own recipe), so only
  `zIndex` is needed here — identical in shape to the existing `close`/`carousel` entries.
- Extend docblock point 2 (the "lifting every interactive control" explanation, ~lines 62-101)
  with a new dated fix note, continuing this file's own Fix 1/Fix 3/Fix H lettered convention,
  explaining the media/gallery region needed the same lift the click targets already got, and
  that this was missed because clicking `close`/`carousel`/content-buttons was checked live but
  swiping the image itself never was.
- Extend `index.test.tsx`'s existing z-index-lift describe block (or add a sibling one) to assert
  the new entry's object shape, matching that file's own established idiom for these proofs.

**Verification:** jsdom cannot prove this (no stacking-context resolution — this file's own
"KNOWN LIMITATION" docblock already says so). Needs a real touch check: Playwright's
`mobile-chrome` project with a real drag/swipe gesture on the image, or Marcel's own device,
confirming the gallery pages and the indicator updates.

## Fix (a) — hover-reveal content invisible to VoiceOver / skipped on Shift+Tab

**Files:** `zimmProductCard.css.ts` (all 5 reveal sites) and
`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`
(carousel's own base state)

**Recommended fix** — keep every one of the five reveal targets permanently present in the DOM,
focusable, and in the accessibility tree at all times. Stop using `display` to express "hidden";
use the exact technique `ZimmColourSwatchGroup` already ships for its own off-page swatches
(confirmed real, `molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx:215`:
`{ position: 'absolute', clipPath: 'inset(50%)' }`):

- **Hidden (default) state:** `position: 'absolute'`, `clipPath: 'inset(50%)'` instead of
  `display: 'none'` — out of flow (no layout gap, same as today), paints nothing, but stays in
  the DOM/tab order/accessibility tree.
- **Revealed state** (same `&:hover [...]` / `&:has(:focus-visible) [...]` selectors, byte-for-byte
  unchanged): `position: 'static'`, `clipPath: 'none'` instead of `display: 'block'/'flex'`.
- Applies at all 5 sites in `zimmProductCard.css.ts`: Home price reveal (~293-297, 323-325),
  PLP/Wishlist price hide (~330-332, 338-340), PLP/Wishlist size-selector reveal (~344-346,
  348-350), notify-me reveal (~359-362, 364-366), carousel arrow reveal (~379-384).
- `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s `carousel` part: its own unconditional base `display: 'none'`
  becomes the same clip-path equivalent (already `position: 'absolute'` unconditionally, so only
  the hidden-state property changes).
- **Carousel-specific addition:** the wrapper deliberately sets `pointerEvents: 'none'` with each
  `arrowButton` individually re-enabling `pointerEvents: 'auto'` (so clicks in the empty centre
  pass through to the image). Once the wrapper is no longer `display:none`, add an explicit
  belt-and-braces rule in the organism recipe — `[data-card-slot="carousel"] button` gets
  `pointerEvents: 'none'` by default and `'auto'` only in the two revealed selectors — rather than
  relying on clip-path's hit-testing suppression alone. (Price/size-selector/notify-me need no
  equivalent — none of them sets `pointerEvents` at all today.)

**Why this is the recommended path, not one of several open options** (a JS-tracked hover/focus
state was considered and rejected): there is no signal exposed to page-level JavaScript, any more
than to CSS, that says "this focus event was AT-originated." A hand-rolled heuristic (e.g.
flagging `focusin` as non-keyboard when preceded by `pointerdown`) has exactly the same blind spot
as the native `:focus-visible` heuristic it would be reimplementing. It would also break this
organism's own stated design principle ("CSS alone decides what is visible... no JS-tracked reveal
state," `index.tsx` ~349-350) and introduce real SSR/hydration-mismatch risk pure CSS structurally
can't have, for no correctness gain.

**Why this doesn't reintroduce the `983bddf` stuck-open bug:** that bug was entirely about *when*
`:has(:focus-visible)` matches (a click-focused button not un-matching on mouseout until focus
moved elsewhere) — a selector-matching-timing question, completely orthogonal to which property
the matched rule sets. The trigger selectors aren't touched at all; only the property values
inside the already-existing blocks change.

**Docblock updates:** extend/rewrite docblock points 3 and 6 and the "Fix H" note with a new dated
fix note (continuing the lettered sequence), stating explicitly that Fix H's `:focus-within` →
`:has(:focus-visible)` swap was and remains correct for the paint-timing question it solved, and
that the actual defect was using `display` (an AT-tree-removal property) to answer a different
question than the one it should answer. Explicitly out of scope, left as `display:none`: the
permanent, non-hover-capable-pointer hides (`sizeSelectorUnavailable`'s unconditional size-chip
hide, the PLP-mobile bag-icon hide) — separate, correct, Figma-confirmed, non-regressed decisions,
since nothing about them is gated behind an interaction heuristic.

**Test updates:** the existing `.matches()`-based selector-proof describe block in
`index.test.tsx` needs no change (it doesn't depend on which property the matched rule sets). Any
structural/object-shape assertions elsewhere in the same file checking the recipe's declared
`display` values for these 5 sites need updating to the new property values — identify the exact
assertions at implementation time against the real current file, don't guess line numbers here.

**New real-browser verification** (jsdom can't prove any of this): this repo already has
scaffolded-but-empty Playwright a11y projects (`playwright.config.js`'s `a11y-desktop` →
`e2e/tests/a11y/desktop`, `a11y-mobile` → `e2e/tests/a11y/mobile`; both Chromium-only, no WebKit
project configured — not touching `playwright.config.js` itself, only adding specs inside the
already-existing target directories). Add specs for:

1. **Accessibility-tree presence** — load a card in its default (non-hovered, non-focused) state
   and assert, via a real Chromium accessibility-tree snapshot, that the size-chip radiogroup,
   notify-me button, and carousel arrow buttons are present with correct role/name — proving
   AT-tree presence no longer depends on any hover/focus-visible condition having matched.
2. **Tab-order parity** — forward-Tab from before the card and Shift+Tab from after it, asserting
   the stop set/sequence is now identical in both directions (today Shift+Tab skips the
   reveal-gated controls entirely).
3. **No regression on the original stuck-open bug** — real mouse click on an arrow button, move
   the mouse off the card, assert the control is no longer visually painted by reading
   `getComputedStyle(el).clipPath` directly (Playwright's default `toBeVisible()` is primarily a
   bounding-box/`visibility` check and may not reliably catch clip-path-based hiding).

**Honest limitation, not skippable:** the actual disputed claim — does real VoiceOver announce and
activate these controls — can't be fully closed out by any automated check above. Chromium's
accessibility tree isn't the engine VoiceOver actually talks to (WebKit), no WebKit Playwright
project exists in this repo, and Playwright can't drive real VoiceOver at all. The automated specs
give strong, real regression-prevention signal (AT-tree presence + tab-order parity are both real,
previously-uncaught bugs), but final confirmation needs one manual pass from Marcel: navigate a
card via VO+Right-Arrow/rotor only (no mouse, no literal Tab keypress) on real macOS Safari +
VoiceOver, confirming price, the size-chip radiogroup, notify-me, and the carousel arrows are all
announced and activatable via VO+Space.

## Verification (both fixes)

1. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
2. Full local Storybook build + `test-storybook --ci` — same pattern used earlier on this branch
   for the axe-contrast fix; confirms no regression across the whole story set.
3. Updated/new Vitest assertions in both `index.test.tsx` files pass.
4. New Playwright a11y specs (AT-tree presence, tab-order parity, stuck-open non-regression) pass.
5. Real-device/manual checks, both required before calling this done:
   - Real touch swipe (device or Playwright mobile-chrome touch simulation) confirms gallery
     paging works.
   - Real VoiceOver + Safari pass (Marcel, one-time) confirms AT reachability/activation for all
     five previously-broken controls.

## Files touched

All within one protection tier — squad-owned `ui-kits` component recipes/tests, no Tier 1/2 file:

- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/zimmProductCard.css.ts`
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.test.tsx`
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/index.test.tsx` (only if the
  carousel base-state change needs an assertion update there too — confirm at implementation time)
- New: `e2e/tests/a11y/desktop/*.spec.ts`, `e2e/tests/a11y/mobile/*.spec.ts` (exact filenames
  follow this repo's existing spec-naming convention, decided at implementation time)

skills.name: zimmerMANNBuild
skills.content:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/skills/zimmerMANNBuild

The executor. Takes an approved plan and builds it, one step at a time, with every step tested,
scope-checked, scored and seen by Marcel before it becomes a commit.

**Intended model: Sonnet 5 at maximum effort.** A skill cannot pin the session model — the loop
agents are pinned to Sonnet in their own frontmatter regardless.

**Scale to the work.** A two-point story does not get the full loop. The plan states the scale it
chose and why; honour it. Over-scaled machinery is a defect, not thoroughness. Nothing too crazy,
no overthinking.

---

## Two modes

**`build`** — `` is a Jira key. Reads `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/plan.md`
and executes it. This is the default.

**`rework`** — invoked as `rework <TICKET>` after a PR is open and CodeRabbit or a reviewer has
requested changes. Skips planning entirely; see the last section.

If no plan exists for the ticket, stop and say so. **Do not plan here** — that is
`zimmerMANNPreBuild`'s job, and building from an unplanned story is how an afternoon gets burned
on the wrong thing.

---

## Before the first step

1. Confirm the branch. **Not `develop`, not `main`** — a `PreToolUse` hook blocks every Write and
   Edit there. If the branch is wrong, stop.
2. Confirm the working tree is clean, or that everything dirty is expected and belongs to this
   story. Registry churn under `.claude/registry/*.md` is automatic and expected.
3. Read the plan's file manifest, tiers and per-step pass criteria. **Any file marked BLOCKED
   stops the run** until Marcel confirms owner approval.
4. Record the baseline: run the four per-step gates now and note the numbers. A gate that is
   non-zero at baseline is not a failure you introduced.

---

## The loop — once per step

```
Implementer  →  Tester  →  Orchestrator  →  Scorer  →  [Marcel]  →  commit
                   ↑                          │
                   └────── REWORK, max 3 ─────┘
```

**1. `zm-implementer`** builds the step. Only the files the step names. It never stages and never
commits.

**2. `zm-tester`** fans out its own angle sub-agents, re-pointed for this step, and reports
findings with CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE and UNIFORM/ONE-OFF labels, plus what it tried to falsify and
what it could not verify.

**3. `zm-orchestrator`** returns a scope verdict — IN SCOPE / UNDER / OVER / BLOCKED. Under and
over carry equal weight.

**4. `zm-scorer`** takes both and scores six axes. PASS or REWORK.

**REWORK returns to the Implementer with a specific instruction. Maximum three rounds.** On the
third, stop and surface to Marcel — three failures means the plan or the criteria are wrong, not
the implementation.

### Per-step gates — the cheap four

Run every step. Seconds each.

```
npx tsc --noEmit
npm run test                        # includes recipeGuards, the hard styling gate
npm run lint                        # compare counts, not the exit code
node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs    # new unacknowledged findings only
```

Two traps: `npm run lint` exits non-zero at a healthy baseline, so **compare the count against
your baseline and ignore the exit code**. And never append arguments to it — `pwa-kit-dev lint`
forwards `--`-args into `execSync`, which can silently turn the gate into a writer.

The plan's per-step pass criteria layer **on top of** these, they do not replace them.

### The visual checkpoint

**After any step that changes rendered output, the loop stops.** The plan marks which steps those
are; if it doesn't, assume any step touching a component, a recipe or a page does.

Tell Marcel exactly:
- the URL and the viewport to open
- the Figma node to compare against — the one for **that variant and state**
- what should be on screen
- what would indicate a defect, including anything that will look wrong but is correct

Then **wait.** Do not proceed on assumption. This is the only gate on this stack that catches a
layout defect — `width: 'xl'` passed every automated check and destroyed the global footer.

Until it has happened, the Scorer's Design fidelity axis is UNVERIFIED, not passed.

### The commit

**The skill commits, not an agent.** Only after: Scorer PASS, and the visual checkpoint passed if
one was owed.

One step, one commit. Conventional Commits — the `commit-msg` hook enforces it. **No Claude
attribution, no CodeRabbit mentions, no `Co-Authored-By` line.** Use Marcel's previously authored
commits on this repo as the reference for tone and body.

Then move to the next step.

---

## Before handing off

Once every step has passed, run the expensive gates **once**:

```
npm run build-storybook             # then run the interaction + a11y suite against it
npm run test:story                  # real BrowserStack, scoped to the Jira key
npm run test:max-file-size          # runs a full build
cr review --base develop            # CodeRabbit locally, full review before anything is public
```

Storybook needs a verified-free port and a build you can prove is yours — a stale server on 6006
produced a silently meaningless pass once. Check the served build matches your own before trusting
any result.

Then **write the handoff** to `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/handoff.md`:

```
# Handoff — <TICKET>
Branch: <branch>   Base: <sha>   Head: <sha>

## Steps
| # | What | Commit | Scorer verdict | Rework rounds |

## Gates (real numbers, not claims)
| Gate | Result | Baseline |

## UNIFORM findings
<each one, with file:line — these are what a per-step review structurally cannot catch>

## Could not verify
<named, with why>

## Outstanding
<anything left, or "none">
```

**Write it even when everything passed.** PostBuild reads this file, and it may run in a different
session — a handoff that exists only in conversation does not survive the session ending.

Then present the same content to Marcel and **hand off to `zimmerMANNPostBuild`. This skill does
not push and does not open a PR.**

---

## Rework mode

Entered after a PR is open and CodeRabbit or a reviewer has requested changes.

**Read `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/postbuild.md` first.** It records what earlier rounds
already declined and why. A finding that was declined with evidence in round one does not get
re-litigated in round three — check before you verify anything, and if you disagree with a previous
decline, say so rather than silently reversing it.

**1. Verify every finding before touching anything.** CodeRabbit has been wrong on this repo
often — one batch ran 1-in-6 correct. Treat each finding as a hypothesis, not a fact. Per finding:

- **VALID** — reproduce it, cite `file:line`, fix it
- **INVALID** — say what is actually true, with the evidence, and draft the reply
- **OUT OF SCOPE** — real but not this story's problem; name the owning ticket or the person
- **DEFER** — real, in scope, but blocked on a decision; name who decides

**2. Fix only the VALID ones.** Same rules as build mode — the Implementer touches only what the
finding names, never stages, never commits.

**3. Re-run the cheap four**, plus the visual checkpoint if the fix changes rendered output.

**4. Commit the fixes here**, same rule as build mode — the skill commits, never an agent. Reference
the review thread each commit answers.

**5. Hand back to `zimmerMANNPostBuild`** with: what was fixed and in which commit, what was
declined and why, and the evidence behind each decline. **PostBuild owns the push and the
in-thread replies** — every finding gets a written answer, including the declined ones.

---

## Hard rules

- **Never push. Never open or update a PR.** That boundary belongs to PostBuild, which presents
  first and pushes only once Marcel has given the go.
- **Never write to the repo's config** — `.claude/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CODEOWNERS`,
  `.docs/memory/**`, `.docs/prd/**`. Tier 1 Governance.
- **Never touch a Tier 1 file** without Marcel naming it and confirming owner approval.
- **Never expand scope.** Something worth doing that the plan didn't ask for gets reported, not
  done. Report it and let Marcel decide.
- **Local-only docs are never citable** in a commit message or a code comment. Cite `AGENTS.md`
  or `.claude/rules/*` instead.
- **Say what you could not verify.** Silence reads as "nothing wrong" when it may mean
  "didn't look there".

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/skills/zimmerMANNBuild

The executor. Takes an approved plan and builds it, one step at a time, with every step tested,
scope-checked, scored and seen by Marcel before it becomes a commit.

**Intended model: Sonnet 5 at maximum effort.** A skill cannot pin the session model — the loop
agents are pinned to Sonnet in their own frontmatter regardless.

**Scale to the work.** A two-point story does not get the full loop. The plan states the scale it
chose and why; honour it. Over-scaled machinery is a defect, not thoroughness. Nothing too crazy,
no overthinking.

---

## Two modes

**`build`** — `SFCC-83+84 branch=feature/SFCC-83-84_recently-viewed plan=~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-83+84/plan.md` is a Jira key. Reads `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/plan.md`
and executes it. This is the default.

**`rework`** — invoked as `rework <TICKET>` after a PR is open and CodeRabbit or a reviewer has
requested changes. Skips planning entirely; see the last section.

If no plan exists for the ticket, stop and say so. **Do not plan here** — that is
`zimmerMANNPreBuild`'s job, and building from an unplanned story is how an afternoon gets burned
on the wrong thing.

---

## Before the first step

1. Confirm the branch. **Not `develop`, not `main`** — a `PreToolUse` hook blocks every Write and
   Edit there. If the branch is wrong, stop.
2. Confirm the working tree is clean, or that everything dirty is expected and belongs to this
   story. Registry churn under `.claude/registry/*.md` is automatic and expected.
3. Read the plan's file manifest, tiers and per-step pass criteria. **Any file marked BLOCKED
   stops the run** until Marcel confirms owner approval.
4. Record the baseline: run the four per-step gates now and note the numbers. A gate that is
   non-zero at baseline is not a failure you introduced.

---

## The loop — once per step

```
Implementer  →  Tester  →  Orchestrator  →  Scorer  →  [Marcel]  →  commit
                   ↑                          │
                   └────── REWORK, max 3 ─────┘
```

**1. `zm-implementer`** builds the step. Only the files the step names. It never stages and never
commits.

**2. `zm-tester`** fans out its own angle sub-agents, re-pointed for this step, and reports
findings with CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE and UNIFORM/ONE-OFF labels, plus what it tried to falsify and
what it could not verify.

**3. `zm-orchestrator`** returns a scope verdict — IN SCOPE / UNDER / OVER / BLOCKED. Under and
over carry equal weight.

**4. `zm-scorer`** takes both and scores six axes. PASS or REWORK.

**REWORK returns to the Implementer with a specific instruction. Maximum three rounds.** On the
third, stop and surface to Marcel — three failures means the plan or the criteria are wrong, not
the implementation.

### Per-step gates — the cheap four

Run every step. Seconds each.

```
npx tsc --noEmit
npm run test                        # includes recipeGuards, the hard styling gate
npm run lint                        # compare counts, not the exit code
node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs    # new unacknowledged findings only
```

Two traps: `npm run lint` exits non-zero at a healthy baseline, so **compare the count against
your baseline and ignore the exit code**. And never append arguments to it — `pwa-kit-dev lint`
forwards `--`-args into `execSync`, which can silently turn the gate into a writer.

The plan's per-step pass criteria layer **on top of** these, they do not replace them.

### The visual checkpoint

**After any step that changes rendered output, the loop stops.** The plan marks which steps those
are; if it doesn't, assume any step touching a component, a recipe or a page does.

Tell Marcel exactly:
- the URL and the viewport to open
- the Figma node to compare against — the one for **that variant and state**
- what should be on screen
- what would indicate a defect, including anything that will look wrong but is correct

Then **wait.** Do not proceed on assumption. This is the only gate on this stack that catches a
layout defect — `width: 'xl'` passed every automated check and destroyed the global footer.

Until it has happened, the Scorer's Design fidelity axis is UNVERIFIED, not passed.

### The commit

**The skill commits, not an agent.** Only after: Scorer PASS, and the visual checkpoint passed if
one was owed.

One step, one commit. Conventional Commits — the `commit-msg` hook enforces it. **No Claude
attribution, no CodeRabbit mentions, no `Co-Authored-By` line.** Use Marcel's previously authored
commits on this repo as the reference for tone and body.

Then move to the next step.

---

## Before handing off

Once every step has passed, run the expensive gates **once**:

```
npm run build-storybook             # then run the interaction + a11y suite against it
npm run test:story                  # real BrowserStack, scoped to the Jira key
npm run test:max-file-size          # runs a full build
cr review --base develop            # CodeRabbit locally, full review before anything is public
```

Storybook needs a verified-free port and a build you can prove is yours — a stale server on 6006
produced a silently meaningless pass once. Check the served build matches your own before trusting
any result.

Then **write the handoff** to `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/handoff.md`:

```
# Handoff — <TICKET>
Branch: <branch>   Base: <sha>   Head: <sha>

## Steps
| # | What | Commit | Scorer verdict | Rework rounds |

## Gates (real numbers, not claims)
| Gate | Result | Baseline |

## UNIFORM findings
<each one, with file:line — these are what a per-step review structurally cannot catch>

## Could not verify
<named, with why>

## Outstanding
<anything left, or "none">
```

**Write it even when everything passed.** PostBuild reads this file, and it may run in a different
session — a handoff that exists only in conversation does not survive the session ending.

Then present the same content to Marcel and **hand off to `zimmerMANNPostBuild`. This skill does
not push and does not open a PR.**

---

## Rework mode

Entered after a PR is open and CodeRabbit or a reviewer has requested changes.

**Read `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/postbuild.md` first.** It records what earlier rounds
already declined and why. A finding that was declined with evidence in round one does not get
re-litigated in round three — check before you verify anything, and if you disagree with a previous
decline, say so rather than silently reversing it.

**1. Verify every finding before touching anything.** CodeRabbit has been wrong on this repo
often — one batch ran 1-in-6 correct. Treat each finding as a hypothesis, not a fact. Per finding:

- **VALID** — reproduce it, cite `file:line`, fix it
- **INVALID** — say what is actually true, with the evidence, and draft the reply
- **OUT OF SCOPE** — real but not this story's problem; name the owning ticket or the person
- **DEFER** — real, in scope, but blocked on a decision; name who decides

**2. Fix only the VALID ones.** Same rules as build mode — the Implementer touches only what the
finding names, never stages, never commits.

**3. Re-run the cheap four**, plus the visual checkpoint if the fix changes rendered output.

**4. Commit the fixes here**, same rule as build mode — the skill commits, never an agent. Reference
the review thread each commit answers.

**5. Hand back to `zimmerMANNPostBuild`** with: what was fixed and in which commit, what was
declined and why, and the evidence behind each decline. **PostBuild owns the push and the
in-thread replies** — every finding gets a written answer, including the declined ones.

---

## Hard rules

- **Never push. Never open or update a PR.** That boundary belongs to PostBuild, which presents
  first and pushes only once Marcel has given the go.
- **Never write to the repo's config** — `.claude/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CODEOWNERS`,
  `.docs/memory/**`, `.docs/prd/**`. Tier 1 Governance.
- **Never touch a Tier 1 file** without Marcel naming it and confirming owner approval.
- **Never expand scope.** Something worth doing that the plan didn't ask for gets reported, not
  done. Report it and let Marcel decide.
- **Local-only docs are never citable** in a commit message or a code comment. Cite `AGENTS.md`
  or `.claude/rules/*` instead.
- **Say what you could not verify.** Silence reads as "nothing wrong" when it may mean
  "didn't look there".

3	**Produced:** 2026-09-06 · **Gate:** `findings.md` (four passes, cleared at the 2026-09-06 adjudication)

6	## 1. Goal statement
7	
8	Build the Recently Viewed rail and its full-history page per **SFCC-83** and **SFCC-84** (ACs in Jira
9	`customfield_10231`), designed in **`Zimmermann_Design_System_2026` component set `40000587:38471`**
10	(Desktop `40000307:12444`, Tablet `40000730:13363`, Mobile `40000538:25030` — all authoritative,
11	corroborated by PDP-template instances `7998:13508` / `8272:28947`), with SFCC-84's page from the
12	**provisional** `Zimmermann_Designs` `3332:35655` — following `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`
13	(token hierarchy) and `.claude/rules/components.md` (container/presentational split), and extending
14	**PR #85 / SFCC-236's** `ZimmProductCard` family via a **new `VARIATION_CONFIG` entry** (not a new
15	card), a **copy-first override of `recommended-products/`**, and **co-located `<name>.css.ts`**
16	recipes registered in `theme/components/index.ts`.
17	
18	Scope follows `.docs/prd/search.md` §7.4 (PDP + Cart). **PLP is out**; SFCC-83 AC 9 knowingly not met.
19	**No consent gating** (development-phase carve-out, Marcel 2026-09-06) — must be stated in both PR
20	bodies; must not reach production.
21	
22	## 2. Scale call
23	
24	### Architecture fork — resolved: override `recommended-products/`, which removes the Cart port
25	
26	Verified directly at `node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev/configs/webpack/overrides-plugin.js`.
27	`isFromExtends` returns true when the request names `@salesforce/retail-react-app` **and the issuing
28	file is not itself inside `overrides/`**. The plugin's own comment (lines 116–127): *"This will return
29	true if the issuer is a file in a base template... This allow the base template to import from
30	overrides."* Implementation: `this.extends.includes(pkgName) && !filepath.includes(issuerPath)`.
31	
32	Base Cart imports at `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/cart/index.jsx:36`:
33	`import RecommendedProducts from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/recommended-products'`
34	— a package-path import issued from a base file, so it **is** redirected once our override exists.
35	Base Cart is itself loaded by base `routes.jsx` via a relative `import('./pages/cart')`, which is not
36	redirected — so base Cart keeps rendering and picks up our override for free.
37	
38	**Consequence: the ~2,460-line Cart copy-first (`index.jsx` 1515 + 8 real partials ≈ 948) is not
39	required.** This departed from adjudication item #10 ("we only have to copy-first for cart"), in the
40	direction of *less* work. **APPROVED by Marcel, 2026-09-06**, on the evidence that this is already the
41	dominant pattern in this repo: nine component overrides shadow base paths and are reached purely by
42	the resolver (`icons` at 64 base import sites — and mandated by AGENTS.md — `responsive` 12,
43	`product-view` 6, `drawer-menu`/`list-menu` 2 each, `header`/`footer` 1 each). The single page port
44	(`product-detail`) exists only because base `routes.jsx` loads pages by *relative* import, which the
45	resolver never redirects — a constraint that does not apply to components. Open Question 5 is closed.
46	
47	**Caveat:** this is a *build-time webpack* resolver. It runs in the dev server and production build
48	only — **not** Storybook (`.storybook/main.js` aliases straight to `node_modules`) and **not** Vitest.
49	So the Cart behaviour cannot be proven by any automated test in this repo; it must be checked in the
50	running app. That is why A1's pause is a hard gate.
51	
52	Cost of this choice: the override module loads at **four base import sites serving eight rails**, not
53	five as an earlier draft of this plan stated:
54	
55	| Base import site | Rails | Takes the new branch? |
56	|---|---|---|
57	| `app/pages/cart/index.jsx:36` | Cart Recently Viewed, Cart May-Also-Like | **Yes** (1 of 2) |
58	| `app/pages/product-detail/index.jsx:40` | *(shadowed by our own PDP override — 3 rails)* | **Yes** (1 of 3) |
59	| `app/hooks/use-add-to-cart-modal.js:30` | add-to-cart modal (`pdp-similar-items`) | No |
60	| `app/pages/product-list/partials/empty-results.jsx:20` | PLP empty-search top-sellers, most-viewed | No |
61	
62	It is therefore a **faithful port plus exactly one branch**, keyed off
63	`EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED` (`'viewed-recently-einstein'` — the same string as
64	`CART_RECENTLY_VIEWED`, `constants.js:156,160`). **Two rails take the new branch; the other six must
65	render identically before and after** — a hard pass criterion.
66	
67	Two of those six are on **PLP**, explicitly descoped at adjudication #2. The override *loads* there
68	but its branch never fires (those rails use `EMPTY_SEARCH_RESULTS_*` recommenders), so **no Recently
69	Viewed rail appears on PLP**. State this in the PR body so a reviewer does not read the override's
70	presence on PLP as scope creep.
71	
72	Rejected alternative — re-homing the fetch into a new Zimmermann container: still needs a per-surface
73	caller, and Cart is a base page we cannot pass props to without the 2,460-line port. Buys nothing,
74	costs the port.
75	
76	### Branch: ONE, single PR (Marcel, 2026-09-06)
77	
78	**`feature/SFCC-83-84_recently-viewed`**, cut from `feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component`.
79	
80	An earlier draft proposed two stacked branches. **Marcel chose a single branch / single PR to
81	maintain**, which is now the plan. Step IDs keep their `A*`/`B*` prefixes (they read as "rail work"
82	and "page work") but execute as one sequence on one branch:
83	
84	> A1 → A2 → A3 → A4 → A5 → A6 → B1 → B2 → B3 → GATES
85	
86	**What this buys:**
87	- **The AC 5 / AC 84-1 split disappears.** Those two ACs are the *same* requirement. On two branches
88	  the rail would have shipped with an unsupplied `seeAllHref` and SFCC-83 could not be marked Done
89	  until the second PR merged. On one branch the link and its destination land together — no
90	  interim state where the link points at a 404, and both stories close on one merge.
91	- One review conversation, one CI run, one changelog entry.
92	
93	**What it costs, stated plainly:**
94	- **The four-team CODEOWNERS fan-out on `overrides/app/routes.tsx` (`CODEOWNERS:94`) now applies to
95	  the whole PR**, not just the page half. Every reviewer group sees the full diff.
96	- **The provisional-design page now gates the confirmed-design rail.** SFCC-83's rail is authoritative
97	  at all three viewports and corroborated twice; SFCC-84's page comes entirely from a provisional
98	  source. If the page's design is challenged in review, the rail — which re-skins two live surfaces
99	  and has no such doubt — waits with it. Accepted deliberately; flag it in the PR body so a reviewer
100	  knows the rail can be split back out if the page stalls.
101	
102	### Loop depth
103	
104	Two stories, ~22 files, one 236-line copy-first file. Mid-size build.
105	
106	- **Full implementer → tester → scorer** on A2, A3, A4, A5, B1, B3 — where a silent wrong answer
107	  ships (a variation flag misread from Figma; an ordering/cap bug of exactly the shape the FED
108	  handbook's finding 18 warns encodes itself into a passing test; an AC-8 gate that never fires).
109	- **Implementer + scorer only** on A1, A6, B2, A7, B4 — their gate is mechanical (`tsc`, `npm run
110	  test`, a diff read); a tester pass adds a round-trip without adding a check.
111	
112	**Deliberately dropped, with reasons:**
113	- **No Playwright/E2E.** Adding an allow-list group to `.github/workflows/qa.yml` is Tier 1 CI config
114	  (`CODEOWNERS:65`) — out of scope. Without it these paths resolve to `e2e_scope: skip` and there is
115	  no PR-time E2E run either way (`.claude/rules/testing.md` > Change-scoped E2E). State this in both
116	  PR bodies rather than implying coverage exists.
117	- **No page-level Storybook story.** No page in this repo has one; the presentational organisms carry
118	  the stories, matching `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/*.stories.tsx`.
119	- **No new `theme/components/*Shared.ts`.** Both recipes derive media queries from `breakpoints`
120	  imported from `app/theme/foundation` — one source, two importers, no copied literal.
121	- **No visual-regression tooling.** None exists; Figma parity is checked by eye against named nodes.
122

170	## 4. Steps
171	
172	One commit per step. `conventions.md`'s no-magic-strings rule throughout: `'viewed-recently-einstein'`
173	is only ever referenced as `EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED`.
174	
175	### A1 — Copy-first: `recommended-products` override *(AGENTS.md step 3 — mandatory pause)*
176	
177	Copy `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/recommended-products/index.jsx`
178	verbatim to `overrides/app/components/recommended-products/index.tsx`; convert to TypeScript (replace
179	`PropTypes` with a `type`, type all params/returns, no `any`/`@ts-ignore`); add
180	`console.log('[overrides] recommended-products/index.tsx')`. **No functional change whatsoever.**
181	Then **STOP and present to Marcel** to verify the override renders on both PDP and Cart.
182	
183	**Pass criteria**
184	- `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0.
185	- Diff vs base is TypeScript-only: no changed JSX, hook calls, prop names, or reordered `useEffect`s.
186	- `propTypes` removed, replaced by a `RecommendedProductsProps` type; the `...props` passthrough to
187	  `ProductScroller` preserved.
188	- `ProductScroller` and `use-einstein` imports stay on `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` base paths —
189	  no local override exists for either, so `overrideStyling.md`'s relative-import rule does not apply.
190	- Marcel confirms the marker log appears **five** times across a PDP visit and a Cart visit (3 PDP
191	  rails + 2 Cart rails). **Seeing it on Cart is the direct proof the resolver reaches base pages and
192	  no Cart port is needed** — and the only possible proof, since Storybook/Vitest do not load the
193	  resolver.
194	- Commit does **not** remove the `console.log` — that happens in A6.
195	
196	### A2 — Add the `recentlyViewed` variation to `ZimmProductCard`
197	
198	Add `ZimmProductCardRecentlyViewedVariation` to the exported union and one `VARIATION_CONFIG` row.
199	Update the docblock's KNOWN GAP paragraph (lines 124–135) from "whoever builds SFCC-83 needs to…" to a
200	record of what was done, citing Jira comment 13880.
201	
202	**Also record in that same docblock update (finding 34; naming decided 2026-09-06):** comment 13880
203	asks for the same badge/hover-swap suppression on **editorial and landing pages** — a surface with no
204	ticket, design or AC today. The variation is named `recentlyViewed` for the one confirmed surface, per
205	this repo's existing surface-naming convention (`home` / `plp` / `wishlist`). When editorial/landing
206	is scoped it needs **its own `VARIATION_CONFIG` row** with both flags `false`: it must not reuse
207	`recentlyViewed` (the name would lie) and must not use `plp` (which ships the badge Dani ruled out).
208	SFCC-236's *Variation extensibility* AC makes that a one-row change.
209	
210	**REWRITTEN 2026-09-06 after reading the real Figma nodes (findings 36-38).** An earlier draft
211	specced this as "`plp` with two flags flipped", justified partly by PRD §7.5. **That was wrong.** Every
212	`Product-card` instance in the rail hides its entire `Card-content` block plus `Tag`, `Close` and
213	`Carousel`, on all three viewports — verified by node metadata *and* a rendered screenshot of
214	`40000307:12444` (a title row and five bare images, nothing else).
215	
216	**The rail tile is IMAGE ONLY.** Every flag is off:
217	
218	| Flag | Value | Source |
219	|---|---|---|
220	| `showBadge` | `false` | `Tag` `hidden="true"` on all 3 viewport cards; corroborates Dani, comment 13880 |
221	| `showHoverImageSwap` | `false` | Dani, comment 13880 |
222	| `showBag` | **`false`** | `Card-content` `hidden="true"` — no bag anywhere. **Overrides the earlier §7.5/SPR-62 reading — see below.** |
223	| `showSizeChips` | **`false`** | same |
224	| `hoverRevealsSizeSelector` | **`false`** | same |
225	| `hoverHidesPrice` | **n/a** | no price is rendered at all |
226	| `showAttributes` / `hoverRevealsPrice` / `hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable` | `false` | nothing in `Card-content` renders |
227	| `showRemove` | `false` | `Close` `hidden="true"` |
228	| `hideBagOnMobile` | **moot** | there is no bag on any viewport, so the flag never applies. **Open question 7 is closed** — the node was read; the answer is that the whole content block is hidden, not just the icon. |
229	
230	**New flag required.** `ZimmProductCard` has no way today to suppress `ZimmProductCardContent`
231	wholesale — name and price render unconditionally. Add one (`showContent: false` or equivalent) and
232	gate the `ZimmProductCardContent` render on it. Keep it table-driven like every other flag; **do not**
233	add a `variation === 'recentlyViewed'` branch (A2's own pass criterion below forbids it).
234	
235	**Carousel arrows:** driven by image count in `ZimmProductCardMedia`, not by this table. Pass a
236	**single** image — AC 3's *"the product's index image"* — and they never appear, matching `Carousel`
237	`hidden="true"`.
238	
239	**PRD conflict, adjudicated (Marcel, 2026-09-06): design wins.** `.docs/prd/search.md` §7.5 (SPR-62,
240	Confirmed) says *"Add to Bag via size variant selection directly from recommendation carousels on PDP
241	and Cart pages."* The rail shows neither. Rationale for following the design: §7.5's own Open note
242	says the Add-to-Bag-vs-Wishlist choice is *"pending design refinement"*, and Recently Viewed is §7.4 —
243	a separate row — so §7.5 arguably never covered this rail. **State the divergence in the PR body for
244	Jasmijn**; do not treat it as settled doctrine.
245	
246	**Pass criteria**
247	- `grep -n 'variation ===\|switch (variation)' index.tsx` still returns zero hits — the extensibility
248	  AC's mechanism is table-driven and must stay so.
249	- `index.test.tsx` gains `@ts-expect-error` cases proving the new variation's narrow props type
250	  rejects `colour`/`size`/`onRemove`, assigning to the **narrow shape, not the union alias** — or the
251	  excess-property check is vacuous.
252	- A test asserts no badge renders even when `badge` is passed, and no hover swap even when
253	  `hoverImage` is passed. **Both must be made to fail on purpose first** (flip the flag, watch it
254	  fail) before the pass counts.
255	- `index.stories.tsx` gains a `RecentlyViewed` named export.
256	- `hideBagOnMobile` carries an inline comment naming its Figma node.
257	- `npm run test` passes, including `ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts`.
258	
259	### A3 — Card mapper utility
260	
261	Create `overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedCard.ts` — a pure module mapping one Einstein rec to
262	`ZimmProductCard` props. Modelled on the proven prior art at
263	`overrides/app/pages/home/liveProductCardDemoMapper.ts` (on `feature/zimmproductcard-live-demo`,
264	**not** on PR #85's branch — read it, port the approach, do not import it).
265	
266	Input is what `use-einstein.js`'s `fetchRecProductDetails` produces: `{...rec, ...product, productId,
267	image: {disBaseLink, alt}}`. Reuse base `filterImageGroups` (`app/utils/product-utils`) and
268	`productUrlBuilder` (`app/utils/url`). Inject `formatPrice` as a parameter so the module stays free of
269	`react-intl`, matching `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/productInfo.ts`.
270	
271	**Pass criteria**
272	- No React, no `react-intl`, no hook import anywhere (`conventions.md` > Utilities).
273	- Returns `null` for a rec with no `productName` or no usable image — never throws, never emits a card
274	  with an empty `alt` (`ZimmProductCardMediaImage.alt` is required and non-empty).
275	- Tests: happy path; missing `productName`; missing `imageGroups`; single image (no `hoverImage`, no
276	  `images`); price without currency (**skip formatting, do not guess a currency**).
277	- This is a production path, unlike the throwaway demo mapper: SDK shapes come from
278	  `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` / `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` where they exist (AGENTS.md > Type
279	  Definitions). Hand-rolled narrow types only for genuinely unexported shapes, each with a why-comment.
280	
281	### A4 — AC-8 gate hook, plus the PDP write
282	
283	Create `overrides/app/hooks/useRecentlyViewedGate.ts`.
284	
285	This answers **finding 28** — the recommender returns a two-product baseline for a visitor with zero
286	history, so `recs.length === 0` never fires and AC 8 is not implementable from the response. The gate
287	is a **local boolean**, not a copy of Einstein's list:
288	
289	```
290	hasRecentlyViewed = sessionFlagIsSet || isRegistered
291	```
292	
293	- `markProductViewed()` writes a session-scoped flag to `sessionStorage`, called from the existing
294	  Einstein `useEffect` in `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` (lines 772–801), alongside
295	  the `einstein.sendViewProduct` calls already there. One import, one call, guarded by the same
296	  `if (product)`.
297	- `isRegistered` from `useCustomerType()` — the same hook `use-einstein.js:449` already uses.
298	
299	**Why this maps the ACs exactly:** `sessionStorage` is literally session-scoped and cleared at session
300	end — **AC 6**. `isRegistered` short-circuits the local flag, so an authenticated shopper on a device
301	they have never browsed on still gets server-side history — **AC 7**. It is a strict improvement on
302	trusting Einstein alone: the SLAS `usid` can outlive a browser session, so this gate makes AC 6 *true*
303	rather than assumed.
304	
305	**Stated assumption (must appear in the PR body):** a *registered* shopper who has genuinely never
306	viewed anything still sees the two-product baseline. That residual is owned by Open Question 6. Do not
307	paper over it with a heuristic.
308	
309	**Pass criteria**
310	- SSR-safe: initial state `false`, resolved in `useEffect`. No `sessionStorage` access during render.
311	  No hydration mismatch — the rail does not exist on first paint and appears after hydration. (Also
312	  good for LCP; the PDP rail is inside `<Island hydrateOn='visible'>` anyway.)
313	- Wrapped in `try/catch` — Safari private mode throws on `sessionStorage`. Failure degrades to `false`
314	  (no rail), never an exception.
315	- JSDoc with `@returns` (`components.md` > Hooks).
316	- Vitest: no flag + guest → `false`; flag + guest → `true`; no flag + registered → `true`;
317	  `sessionStorage` throwing → `false`; first render before effect → `false`.
318	- **Make each fail on purpose first.** The FED handbook's finding 18 trap is a test that passes
319	  because it was written against the only arrangement already correct.
320	- The PDP change is exactly two lines. Nothing else in `product-detail/index.tsx` moves (AGENTS.md
321	  Hard Rule #5 — no refactoring upward).
322	
323	### A5 — `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` organism + recipe
324	
325	Create `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmRecentlyViewedRail/` (`index.tsx`,
326	`zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts`, `index.stories.tsx`, `index.test.tsx`); register
327	`ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` in `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts`.
328	
329	**Purely presentational — data as props.** Props: `title: ReactNode`, `cards: readonly
330	ZimmProductCardProps[]`, `seeAllHref?: string`, `seeAllLabel?: string`. No `useEinstein`, no
331	`useIntl` — the container owns the copy. (An `IntlProvider` wrapper is still needed in the test
332	because `ZimmProductCard` itself calls `useIntl`; follow `zimmProductCard/index.test.tsx`'s wrapper.)
333	
334	Structure mirrors Figma: a `title-and-link` row (title left, See-Full-History link right) above a
335	horizontally scrollable `group` of `ZimmProductCard`s at `variation: 'recentlyViewed'`.
336	
337	**No rail-level arrow buttons.** Desktop `40000307:12444` decomposes into exactly two children —

# SFCC-83 + SFCC-84 — Build Plan

**Produced:** 2026-09-06 · **Gate:** `findings.md` (four passes, cleared at the 2026-09-06 adjudication)
**Base branch:** `feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component` (PR #85, open, unmerged)

## 1. Goal statement

Build the Recently Viewed rail and its full-history page per **SFCC-83** and **SFCC-84** (ACs in Jira
`customfield_10231`), designed in **`Zimmermann_Design_System_2026` component set `40000587:38471`**
(Desktop `40000307:12444`, Tablet `40000730:13363`, Mobile `40000538:25030` — all authoritative,
corroborated by PDP-template instances `7998:13508` / `8272:28947`), with SFCC-84's page from the
**provisional** `Zimmermann_Designs` `3332:35655` — following `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`
(token hierarchy) and `.claude/rules/components.md` (container/presentational split), and extending
**PR #85 / SFCC-236's** `ZimmProductCard` family via a **new `VARIATION_CONFIG` entry** (not a new
card), a **copy-first override of `recommended-products/`**, and **co-located `<name>.css.ts`**
recipes registered in `theme/components/index.ts`.

Scope follows `.docs/prd/search.md` §7.4 (PDP + Cart). **PLP is out**; SFCC-83 AC 9 knowingly not met.
**No consent gating** (development-phase carve-out, Marcel 2026-09-06) — must be stated in both PR
bodies; must not reach production.

## 2. Scale call

### Architecture fork — resolved: override `recommended-products/`, which removes the Cart port

Verified directly at `node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev/configs/webpack/overrides-plugin.js`.
`isFromExtends` returns true when the request names `@salesforce/retail-react-app` **and the issuing
file is not itself inside `overrides/`**. The plugin's own comment (lines 116–127): *"This will return
true if the issuer is a file in a base template... This allow the base template to import from
overrides."* Implementation: `this.extends.includes(pkgName) && !filepath.includes(issuerPath)`.

Base Cart imports at `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/cart/index.jsx:36`:
`import RecommendedProducts from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/recommended-products'`
— a package-path import issued from a base file, so it **is** redirected once our override exists.
Base Cart is itself loaded by base `routes.jsx` via a relative `import('./pages/cart')`, which is not
redirected — so base Cart keeps rendering and picks up our override for free.

**Consequence: the ~2,460-line Cart copy-first (`index.jsx` 1515 + 8 real partials ≈ 948) is not
required.** This departed from adjudication item #10 ("we only have to copy-first for cart"), in the
direction of *less* work. **APPROVED by Marcel, 2026-09-06**, on the evidence that this is already the
dominant pattern in this repo: nine component overrides shadow base paths and are reached purely by
the resolver (`icons` at 64 base import sites — and mandated by AGENTS.md — `responsive` 12,
`product-view` 6, `drawer-menu`/`list-menu` 2 each, `header`/`footer` 1 each). The single page port
(`product-detail`) exists only because base `routes.jsx` loads pages by *relative* import, which the
resolver never redirects — a constraint that does not apply to components. Open Question 5 is closed.

**Caveat:** this is a *build-time webpack* resolver. It runs in the dev server and production build
only — **not** Storybook (`.storybook/main.js` aliases straight to `node_modules`) and **not** Vitest.
So the Cart behaviour cannot be proven by any automated test in this repo; it must be checked in the
running app. That is why A1's pause is a hard gate.

Cost of this choice: the override module loads at **four base import sites serving eight rails**, not
five as an earlier draft of this plan stated:

| Base import site | Rails | Takes the new branch? |
|---|---|---|
| `app/pages/cart/index.jsx:36` | Cart Recently Viewed, Cart May-Also-Like | **Yes** (1 of 2) |
| `app/pages/product-detail/index.jsx:40` | *(shadowed by our own PDP override — 3 rails)* | **Yes** (1 of 3) |
| `app/hooks/use-add-to-cart-modal.js:30` | add-to-cart modal (`pdp-similar-items`) | No |
| `app/pages/product-list/partials/empty-results.jsx:20` | PLP empty-search top-sellers, most-viewed | No |

It is therefore a **faithful port plus exactly one branch**, keyed off
`EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED` (`'viewed-recently-einstein'` — the same string as
`CART_RECENTLY_VIEWED`, `constants.js:156,160`). **Two rails take the new branch; the other six must
render identically before and after** — a hard pass criterion.

Two of those six are on **PLP**, explicitly descoped at adjudication #2. The override *loads* there
but its branch never fires (those rails use `EMPTY_SEARCH_RESULTS_*` recommenders), so **no Recently
Viewed rail appears on PLP**. State this in the PR body so a reviewer does not read the override's
presence on PLP as scope creep.

Rejected alternative — re-homing the fetch into a new Zimmermann container: still needs a per-surface
caller, and Cart is a base page we cannot pass props to without the 2,460-line port. Buys nothing,
costs the port.

### Branch: ONE, single PR (Marcel, 2026-09-06)

**`feature/SFCC-83-84_recently-viewed`**, cut from `feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component`.

An earlier draft proposed two stacked branches. **Marcel chose a single branch / single PR to
maintain**, which is now the plan. Step IDs keep their `A*`/`B*` prefixes (they read as "rail work"
and "page work") but execute as one sequence on one branch:

> A1 → A2 → A3 → A4 → A5 → A6 → B1 → B2 → B3 → GATES

**What this buys:**
- **The AC 5 / AC 84-1 split disappears.** Those two ACs are the *same* requirement. On two branches
  the rail would have shipped with an unsupplied `seeAllHref` and SFCC-83 could not be marked Done
  until the second PR merged. On one branch the link and its destination land together — no
  interim state where the link points at a 404, and both stories close on one merge.
- One review conversation, one CI run, one changelog entry.

**What it costs, stated plainly:**
- **The four-team CODEOWNERS fan-out on `overrides/app/routes.tsx` (`CODEOWNERS:94`) now applies to
  the whole PR**, not just the page half. Every reviewer group sees the full diff.
- **The provisional-design page now gates the confirmed-design rail.** SFCC-83's rail is authoritative
  at all three viewports and corroborated twice; SFCC-84's page comes entirely from a provisional
  source. If the page's design is challenged in review, the rail — which re-skins two live surfaces
  and has no such doubt — waits with it. Accepted deliberately; flag it in the PR body so a reviewer
  knows the rail can be split back out if the page stalls.

### Loop depth

Two stories, ~22 files, one 236-line copy-first file. Mid-size build.

- **Full implementer → tester → scorer** on A2, A3, A4, A5, B1, B3 — where a silent wrong answer
  ships (a variation flag misread from Figma; an ordering/cap bug of exactly the shape the FED
  handbook's finding 18 warns encodes itself into a passing test; an AC-8 gate that never fires).
- **Implementer + scorer only** on A1, A6, B2, A7, B4 — their gate is mechanical (`tsc`, `npm run
  test`, a diff read); a tester pass adds a round-trip without adding a check.

**Deliberately dropped, with reasons:**
- **No Playwright/E2E.** Adding an allow-list group to `.github/workflows/qa.yml` is Tier 1 CI config
  (`CODEOWNERS:65`) — out of scope. Without it these paths resolve to `e2e_scope: skip` and there is
  no PR-time E2E run either way (`.claude/rules/testing.md` > Change-scoped E2E). State this in both
  PR bodies rather than implying coverage exists.
- **No page-level Storybook story.** No page in this repo has one; the presentational organisms carry
  the stories, matching `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/*.stories.tsx`.
- **No new `theme/components/*Shared.ts`.** Both recipes derive media queries from `breakpoints`
  imported from `app/theme/foundation` — one source, two importers, no copied literal.
- **No visual-regression tooling.** None exists; Figma parity is checked by eye against named nodes.

## 3. File manifest

Tiers from `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md`, `.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md`, `CODEOWNERS` — **never**
`.claude/registry/*.md`. **No Tier 1 file is touched. Nothing is BLOCKED.**

### Rail work (SFCC-83)

|---|---|---|---|
| `overrides/app/components/recommended-products/index.tsx` | CREATE (copy-first, 236 lines) | **Tier 2** | `pwa-squad-b` + `tier-2-approvers` + `tier-1-approvers` (`CODEOWNERS:104`) |

### Page work (SFCC-84)

| File | Action | Tier | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmRecentlyViewedGrid/index.tsx` | CREATE | Tier 3 | `pwa-squad-a` + `pwa-squad-b` |
| `.../zimmRecentlyViewedGrid/zimmRecentlyViewedGrid.css.ts` | CREATE | Tier 3 | as above (`CODEOWNERS:186`) |

| `.../zimmRecentlyViewedGrid/index.test.tsx` | CREATE | Tier 3 | as above |

| `overrides/app/routes.tsx` | MODIFY (one route entry) | **Tier 2 Global Shell** | 4 teams (`CODEOWNERS:94`) — highest fan-out in this work |

| `overrides/app/constants/index.ts` | MODIFY (`RECENTLY_VIEWED_ROUTE`) | Untiered | — |

**Two protection tiers are touched** (Tier 2 + Tier 3). AGENTS.md Hard Rule #10 requires confirming
scope with the developer — one confirmation at plan approval covers the single PR.

## 4. Steps

One commit per step. `conventions.md`'s no-magic-strings rule throughout: `'viewed-recently-einstein'`
is only ever referenced as `EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED`.

### A1 — Copy-first: `recommended-products` override *(AGENTS.md step 3 — mandatory pause)*

Copy `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/recommended-products/index.jsx`
verbatim to `overrides/app/components/recommended-products/index.tsx`; convert to TypeScript (replace
`PropTypes` with a `type`, type all params/returns, no `any`/`@ts-ignore`); add
`console.log('[overrides] recommended-products/index.tsx')`. **No functional change whatsoever.**
Then **STOP and present to Marcel** to verify the override renders on both PDP and Cart.

**Pass criteria**
- `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0.
- Diff vs base is TypeScript-only: no changed JSX, hook calls, prop names, or reordered `useEffect`s.
- `propTypes` removed, replaced by a `RecommendedProductsProps` type; the `...props` passthrough to
  `ProductScroller` preserved.
- `ProductScroller` and `use-einstein` imports stay on `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` base paths —
  no local override exists for either, so `overrideStyling.md`'s relative-import rule does not apply.
- Marcel confirms the marker log appears **five** times across a PDP visit and a Cart visit (3 PDP
  rails + 2 Cart rails). **Seeing it on Cart is the direct proof the resolver reaches base pages and
  no Cart port is needed** — and the only possible proof, since Storybook/Vitest do not load the
  resolver.
- Commit does **not** remove the `console.log` — that happens in A6.

### A2 — Add the `recentlyViewed` variation to `ZimmProductCard`

Add `ZimmProductCardRecentlyViewedVariation` to the exported union and one `VARIATION_CONFIG` row.
Update the docblock's KNOWN GAP paragraph (lines 124–135) from "whoever builds SFCC-83 needs to…" to a
record of what was done, citing Jira comment 13880.

**Also record in that same docblock update (finding 34; naming decided 2026-09-06):** comment 13880
asks for the same badge/hover-swap suppression on **editorial and landing pages** — a surface with no
ticket, design or AC today. The variation is named `recentlyViewed` for the one confirmed surface, per
this repo's existing surface-naming convention (`home` / `plp` / `wishlist`). When editorial/landing
is scoped it needs **its own `VARIATION_CONFIG` row** with both flags `false`: it must not reuse
`recentlyViewed` (the name would lie) and must not use `plp` (which ships the badge Dani ruled out).
SFCC-236's *Variation extensibility* AC makes that a one-row change.

**REWRITTEN 2026-09-06 after reading the real Figma nodes (findings 36-38).** An earlier draft
specced this as "`plp` with two flags flipped", justified partly by PRD §7.5. **That was wrong.** Every
`Product-card` instance in the rail hides its entire `Card-content` block plus `Tag`, `Close` and
`Carousel`, on all three viewports — verified by node metadata *and* a rendered screenshot of
`40000307:12444` (a title row and five bare images, nothing else).

**The rail tile is IMAGE ONLY.** Every flag is off:

| Flag | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `showBadge` | `false` | `Tag` `hidden="true"` on all 3 viewport cards; corroborates Dani, comment 13880 |
| `showHoverImageSwap` | `false` | Dani, comment 13880 |
| `showBag` | **`false`** | `Card-content` `hidden="true"` — no bag anywhere. **Overrides the earlier §7.5/SPR-62 reading — see below.** |
| `showSizeChips` | **`false`** | same |
| `hoverRevealsSizeSelector` | **`false`** | same |
| `hoverHidesPrice` | **n/a** | no price is rendered at all |
| `showAttributes` / `hoverRevealsPrice` / `hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable` | `false` | nothing in `Card-content` renders |
| `showRemove` | `false` | `Close` `hidden="true"` |
| `hideBagOnMobile` | **moot** | there is no bag on any viewport, so the flag never applies. **Open question 7 is closed** — the node was read; the answer is that the whole content block is hidden, not just the icon. |

**New flag required.** `ZimmProductCard` has no way today to suppress `ZimmProductCardContent`
wholesale — name and price render unconditionally. Add one (`showContent: false` or equivalent) and
gate the `ZimmProductCardContent` render on it. Keep it table-driven like every other flag; **do not**
add a `variation === 'recentlyViewed'` branch (A2's own pass criterion below forbids it).

**Carousel arrows:** driven by image count in `ZimmProductCardMedia`, not by this table. Pass a
**single** image — AC 3's *"the product's index image"* — and they never appear, matching `Carousel`
`hidden="true"`.

**PRD conflict, adjudicated (Marcel, 2026-09-06): design wins.** `.docs/prd/search.md` §7.5 (SPR-62,
Confirmed) says *"Add to Bag via size variant selection directly from recommendation carousels on PDP
and Cart pages."* The rail shows neither. Rationale for following the design: §7.5's own Open note
says the Add-to-Bag-vs-Wishlist choice is *"pending design refinement"*, and Recently Viewed is §7.4 —
a separate row — so §7.5 arguably never covered this rail. **State the divergence in the PR body for
Jasmijn**; do not treat it as settled doctrine.

**Pass criteria**
- `grep -n 'variation ===\|switch (variation)' index.tsx` still returns zero hits — the extensibility
  AC's mechanism is table-driven and must stay so.
- `index.test.tsx` gains `@ts-expect-error` cases proving the new variation's narrow props type
  rejects `colour`/`size`/`onRemove`, assigning to the **narrow shape, not the union alias** — or the
  excess-property check is vacuous.
- A test asserts no badge renders even when `badge` is passed, and no hover swap even when
  `hoverImage` is passed. **Both must be made to fail on purpose first** (flip the flag, watch it
  fail) before the pass counts.
- `index.stories.tsx` gains a `RecentlyViewed` named export.
- `hideBagOnMobile` carries an inline comment naming its Figma node.
- `npm run test` passes, including `ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts`.

### A3 — Card mapper utility

Create `overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedCard.ts` — a pure module mapping one Einstein rec to
`ZimmProductCard` props. Modelled on the proven prior art at
`overrides/app/pages/home/liveProductCardDemoMapper.ts` (on `feature/zimmproductcard-live-demo`,
**not** on PR #85's branch — read it, port the approach, do not import it).

Input is what `use-einstein.js`'s `fetchRecProductDetails` produces: `{...rec, ...product, productId,
image: {disBaseLink, alt}}`. Reuse base `filterImageGroups` (`app/utils/product-utils`) and
`productUrlBuilder` (`app/utils/url`). Inject `formatPrice` as a parameter so the module stays free of
`react-intl`, matching `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/productInfo.ts`.

**Pass criteria**
- No React, no `react-intl`, no hook import anywhere (`conventions.md` > Utilities).
- Returns `null` for a rec with no `productName` or no usable image — never throws, never emits a card
  with an empty `alt` (`ZimmProductCardMediaImage.alt` is required and non-empty).
- Tests: happy path; missing `productName`; missing `imageGroups`; single image (no `hoverImage`, no
  `images`); price without currency (**skip formatting, do not guess a currency**).
- This is a production path, unlike the throwaway demo mapper: SDK shapes come from
  `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` / `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` where they exist (AGENTS.md > Type
  Definitions). Hand-rolled narrow types only for genuinely unexported shapes, each with a why-comment.

### A4 — AC-8 gate hook, plus the PDP write

Create `overrides/app/hooks/useRecentlyViewedGate.ts`.

This answers **finding 28** — the recommender returns a two-product baseline for a visitor with zero
history, so `recs.length === 0` never fires and AC 8 is not implementable from the response. The gate
is a **local boolean**, not a copy of Einstein's list:

```
hasRecentlyViewed = sessionFlagIsSet || isRegistered
```

- `markProductViewed()` writes a session-scoped flag to `sessionStorage`, called from the existing
  Einstein `useEffect` in `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` (lines 772–801), alongside
  the `einstein.sendViewProduct` calls already there. One import, one call, guarded by the same
  `if (product)`.
- `isRegistered` from `useCustomerType()` — the same hook `use-einstein.js:449` already uses.

**Why this maps the ACs exactly:** `sessionStorage` is literally session-scoped and cleared at session
end — **AC 6**. `isRegistered` short-circuits the local flag, so an authenticated shopper on a device
they have never browsed on still gets server-side history — **AC 7**. It is a strict improvement on
trusting Einstein alone: the SLAS `usid` can outlive a browser session, so this gate makes AC 6 *true*
rather than assumed.

**Stated assumption (must appear in the PR body):** a *registered* shopper who has genuinely never
viewed anything still sees the two-product baseline. That residual is owned by Open Question 6. Do not
paper over it with a heuristic.

**Pass criteria**
- SSR-safe: initial state `false`, resolved in `useEffect`. No `sessionStorage` access during render.
  No hydration mismatch — the rail does not exist on first paint and appears after hydration. (Also
  good for LCP; the PDP rail is inside `<Island hydrateOn='visible'>` anyway.)
- Wrapped in `try/catch` — Safari private mode throws on `sessionStorage`. Failure degrades to `false`
  (no rail), never an exception.
- JSDoc with `@returns` (`components.md` > Hooks).
- Vitest: no flag + guest → `false`; flag + guest → `true`; no flag + registered → `true`;
  `sessionStorage` throwing → `false`; first render before effect → `false`.
- **Make each fail on purpose first.** The FED handbook's finding 18 trap is a test that passes
  because it was written against the only arrangement already correct.
- The PDP change is exactly two lines. Nothing else in `product-detail/index.tsx` moves (AGENTS.md
  Hard Rule #5 — no refactoring upward).

### A5 — `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` organism + recipe

Create `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmRecentlyViewedRail/` (`index.tsx`,
`zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts`, `index.stories.tsx`, `index.test.tsx`); register
`ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` in `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts`.

**Purely presentational — data as props.** Props: `title: ReactNode`, `cards: readonly
ZimmProductCardProps[]`, `seeAllHref?: string`, `seeAllLabel?: string`. No `useEinstein`, no
`useIntl` — the container owns the copy. (An `IntlProvider` wrapper is still needed in the test
because `ZimmProductCard` itself calls `useIntl`; follow `zimmProductCard/index.test.tsx`'s wrapper.)

Structure mirrors Figma: a `title-and-link` row (title left, See-Full-History link right) above a
horizontally scrollable `group` of `ZimmProductCard`s at `variation: 'recentlyViewed'`.

**No rail-level arrow buttons.** Desktop `40000307:12444` decomposes into exactly two children —
`title-and-link` (1440×96) and `group` (1440×432) — with no arrow layer. `ZimmProductCard` already
carries its own intra-card arrows; rail arrows would collide. Native scroll with scroll-snap only.

**Three explicit media queries** off `breakpoints` imported from `app/theme/foundation`, never Chakra's
array shorthand (it fails `recipeGuards.test.ts`). Real geometry, read from the nodes 2026-09-06:

| Viewport | Rail node | Card | Cards across |
|---|---|---|---|

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/skills/zimmerMANNBuild

The executor. Takes an approved plan and builds it, one step at a time, with every step tested,
scope-checked, scored and seen by Marcel before it becomes a commit.

**Intended model: Sonnet 5 at maximum effort.** A skill cannot pin the session model — the loop
agents are pinned to Sonnet in their own frontmatter regardless.

**Scale to the work.** A two-point story does not get the full loop. The plan states the scale it
chose and why; honour it. Over-scaled machinery is a defect, not thoroughness. Nothing too crazy,
no overthinking.

---

## Two modes

**`build`** — `` is a Jira key. Reads `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/plan.md`
and executes it. This is the default.

**`rework`** — invoked as `rework <TICKET>` after a PR is open and CodeRabbit or a reviewer has
requested changes. Skips planning entirely; see the last section.

If no plan exists for the ticket, stop and say so. **Do not plan here** — that is
`zimmerMANNPreBuild`'s job, and building from an unplanned story is how an afternoon gets burned
on the wrong thing.

---

## Before the first step

1. Confirm the branch. **Not `develop`, not `main`** — a `PreToolUse` hook blocks every Write and
   Edit there. If the branch is wrong, stop.
2. Confirm the working tree is clean, or that everything dirty is expected and belongs to this
   story. Registry churn under `.claude/registry/*.md` is automatic and expected.
3. Read the plan's file manifest, tiers and per-step pass criteria. **Any file marked BLOCKED
   stops the run** until Marcel confirms owner approval.
4. Record the baseline: run the four per-step gates now and note the numbers. A gate that is
   non-zero at baseline is not a failure you introduced.

---

## The loop — once per step

```
Implementer  →  Tester  →  Orchestrator  →  Scorer  →  [Marcel]  →  commit
                   ↑                          │
                   └────── REWORK, max 3 ─────┘
```

**1. `zm-implementer`** builds the step. Only the files the step names. It never stages and never
commits.

**2. `zm-tester`** fans out its own angle sub-agents, re-pointed for this step, and reports
findings with CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE and UNIFORM/ONE-OFF labels, plus what it tried to falsify and
what it could not verify.

**3. `zm-orchestrator`** returns a scope verdict — IN SCOPE / UNDER / OVER / BLOCKED. Under and
over carry equal weight.

**4. `zm-scorer`** takes both and scores six axes. PASS or REWORK.

**REWORK returns to the Implementer with a specific instruction. Maximum three rounds.** On the
third, stop and surface to Marcel — three failures means the plan or the criteria are wrong, not
the implementation.

### Per-step gates — the cheap four

Run every step. Seconds each.

```
npx tsc --noEmit
npm run test                        # includes recipeGuards, the hard styling gate
npm run lint                        # compare counts, not the exit code
node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs    # new unacknowledged findings only
```

Two traps: `npm run lint` exits non-zero at a healthy baseline, so **compare the count against
your baseline and ignore the exit code**. And never append arguments to it — `pwa-kit-dev lint`
forwards `--`-args into `execSync`, which can silently turn the gate into a writer.

The plan's per-step pass criteria layer **on top of** these, they do not replace them.

### The visual checkpoint

**After any step that changes rendered output, the loop stops.** The plan marks which steps those
are; if it doesn't, assume any step touching a component, a recipe or a page does.

Tell Marcel exactly:
- the URL and the viewport to open
- the Figma node to compare against — the one for **that variant and state**
- what should be on screen
- what would indicate a defect, including anything that will look wrong but is correct

Then **wait.** Do not proceed on assumption. This is the only gate on this stack that catches a
layout defect — `width: 'xl'` passed every automated check and destroyed the global footer.

Until it has happened, the Scorer's Design fidelity axis is UNVERIFIED, not passed.

### The commit

**The skill commits, not an agent.** Only after: Scorer PASS, and the visual checkpoint passed if
one was owed.

One step, one commit. Conventional Commits — the `commit-msg` hook enforces it. **No Claude
attribution, no CodeRabbit mentions, no `Co-Authored-By` line.** Use Marcel's previously authored
commits on this repo as the reference for tone and body.

Then move to the next step.

---

## Before handing off

Once every step has passed, run the expensive gates **once**:

```
npm run build-storybook             # then run the interaction + a11y suite against it
npm run test:story                  # real BrowserStack, scoped to the Jira key
npm run test:max-file-size          # runs a full build
cr review --base develop            # CodeRabbit locally, full review before anything is public
```

Storybook needs a verified-free port and a build you can prove is yours — a stale server on 6006
produced a silently meaningless pass once. Check the served build matches your own before trusting
any result.

Then **write the handoff** to `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/handoff.md`:

```
# Handoff — <TICKET>
Branch: <branch>   Base: <sha>   Head: <sha>

## Steps
| # | What | Commit | Scorer verdict | Rework rounds |

## Gates (real numbers, not claims)
| Gate | Result | Baseline |

## UNIFORM findings
<each one, with file:line — these are what a per-step review structurally cannot catch>

## Could not verify
<named, with why>

## Outstanding
<anything left, or "none">
```

**Write it even when everything passed.** PostBuild reads this file, and it may run in a different
session — a handoff that exists only in conversation does not survive the session ending.

Then present the same content to Marcel and **hand off to `zimmerMANNPostBuild`. This skill does
not push and does not open a PR.**

---

## Rework mode

Entered after a PR is open and CodeRabbit or a reviewer has requested changes.

**Read `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/postbuild.md` first.** It records what earlier rounds
already declined and why. A finding that was declined with evidence in round one does not get
re-litigated in round three — check before you verify anything, and if you disagree with a previous
decline, say so rather than silently reversing it.

**1. Verify every finding before touching anything.** CodeRabbit has been wrong on this repo
often — one batch ran 1-in-6 correct. Treat each finding as a hypothesis, not a fact. Per finding:

- **VALID** — reproduce it, cite `file:line`, fix it
- **INVALID** — say what is actually true, with the evidence, and draft the reply
- **OUT OF SCOPE** — real but not this story's problem; name the owning ticket or the person
- **DEFER** — real, in scope, but blocked on a decision; name who decides

**2. Fix only the VALID ones.** Same rules as build mode — the Implementer touches only what the
finding names, never stages, never commits.

**3. Re-run the cheap four**, plus the visual checkpoint if the fix changes rendered output.

**4. Commit the fixes here**, same rule as build mode — the skill commits, never an agent. Reference
the review thread each commit answers.

**5. Hand back to `zimmerMANNPostBuild`** with: what was fixed and in which commit, what was
declined and why, and the evidence behind each decline. **PostBuild owns the push and the
in-thread replies** — every finding gets a written answer, including the declined ones.

---

## Hard rules

- **Never push. Never open or update a PR.** That boundary belongs to PostBuild, which presents
  first and pushes only once Marcel has given the go.
- **Never write to the repo's config** — `.claude/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CODEOWNERS`,
  `.docs/memory/**`, `.docs/prd/**`. Tier 1 Governance.
- **Never touch a Tier 1 file** without Marcel naming it and confirming owner approval.
- **Never expand scope.** Something worth doing that the plan didn't ask for gets reported, not
  done. Report it and let Marcel decide.
- **Local-only docs are never citable** in a commit message or a code comment. Cite `AGENTS.md`
  or `.claude/rules/*` instead.
- **Say what you could not verify.** Silence reads as "nothing wrong" when it may mean
  "didn't look there".
