<Helmet>
        <title>{product?.pageTitle}</title>
        {product?.pageMetaTags?.length > 0 &&
          product.pageMetaTags.map(({ id, value }: { id: string; value: string }) => (
            <meta name={id} content={value} key={id} />
          ))}
        {/* Fallback for description if not included in pageMetaTags */}
        {!product?.pageMetaTags?.some((tag: { id: string }) => tag.id === 'description') &&
          product?.pageDescription && <meta name="description" content={product.pageDescription} />}
      </Helmet>

      <Stack spacing={16}>
        {isProductASet || isProductABundle ? (
          <Fragment>
            <Island hydrateOn={'visible'}>
              <ProductView
                product={product}
                category={primaryCategory?.parentCategoryTree || []}
                addToCart={isProductASet ? handleProductSetAddToCart : handleProductBundleAddToCart}
                addToWishlist={handleAddToWishlist}
                isProductLoading={isProductLoading}
                isBasketLoading={isBasketLoading}
                isWishlistLoading={isWishlistLoading}
                validateOrderability={handleChildProductValidation}
                childProductOrderability={childProductOrderability}
                setSelectedBundleQuantity={setSelectedBundleQuantity}
                selectedBundleParentQuantity={selectedBundleQuantity}
                pickupInStore={!!pickupInStoreMap[product?.id]}
                setPickupInStore={(checked: boolean) => product && handlePickupInStoreChange(product.id, checked)}
                onOpenStoreLocator={onOpenStoreLocator}
                showDeliveryOptions={storeLocatorEnabled}
              />
            </Island>

            <hr />

            {
              // Render the child products
              product?.childProducts?.map(
                ({ product: childProduct, quantity: childQuantity }: { product: SfccProduct; quantity: number }) => (
                  <Box key={childProduct.id} data-testid="child-product">
                    <ProductView
                      // Do not use an arrow function as we are manipulating the functions scope.
                      ref={function (this: ProductViewRefScope, ref: ChildProductRef['ref']) {
                        // Assign the "set" scope of the ref, this is how we access the internal
                        // validation.
                        childProductRefs.current[childProduct.id] = {
                          ref,
                          validateOrderability: this.validateOrderability,
                        };
                      }}
                      product={childProduct}
                      isProductPartOfSet={isProductASet}
                      isProductPartOfBundle={isProductABundle}
                      childOfBundleQuantity={childQuantity}
                      selectedBundleParentQuantity={selectedBundleQuantity}
                      addToCart={
                        isProductASet
                          ? (productSelectionValues: ProductSelectionValue[]) => handleAddToCart(productSelectionValues)
                          : null
                      }
                      addToWishlist={isProductASet ? handleAddToWishlist : null}
                      onVariantSelected={(product: SfccProduct, variant: SfccVariant, quantity: number) => {
                        if (quantity) {
                          setChildProductSelection((previousState) => ({
                            ...previousState,
                            [product.id]: {
                              product,
                              variant,
                              quantity: isProductABundle ? childQuantity : quantity,

| Base import site | Rails | Takes the new branch? |

| `app/pages/product-list/partials/empty-results.jsx:20` | PLP empty-search top-sellers, most-viewed | No |

It is therefore a **faithful port plus exactly one branch**, keyed off
`EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED` (`'viewed-recently-einstein'` — the same string as
`CART_RECENTLY_VIEWED`, `constants.js:156,160`). **Two rails take the new branch; the other six must
render identically before and after** — a hard pass criterion.

**🔴 Correction, 2026-09-06 — the PDP row above is misleading, verified directly against
`overrides-plugin.js`'s actual source, not just this plan's earlier paraphrase of it.** The
table's "Yes (1 of 3)" for `product-detail/index.jsx:40` describes the **base** file's import —
but that file is shadowed by our own PDP override page and never loads. What actually matters is
*our own* `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx`'s import of `RecommendedProducts`, and
`isFromExtends` (`overrides-plugin.js:128-146`) returns **false** whenever the issuing file is
itself inside `overrides/` — its own doc comment says so plainly: *"This will return false if the
issuer is a file in the overrides dir."* Our PDP page's current package-path import
(`product-detail/index.tsx:59`) is therefore **not** redirected to our override, at all, regardless
of `Island`, scroll position, or Einstein data — none of which were ever the actual blocker.
Discovered live during A1's mandatory Cart/PDP verification (Marcel: zero marker fires on PDP even
after a full scroll to the bottom, while Cart fired correctly and repeatedly).

**Consequence, and why this isn't just a testing nuisance:** as originally planned, PDP's Recently
Viewed rail would never render even after A6 lands the branch — Cart would work, PDP would
silently not, and SFCC-83's PDP requirement would ship broken with no test catching it (no PR-time
E2E on this path either, per the Loop depth section below). **Fix, folded into A6 (Marcel,
2026-09-06):** change `product-detail/index.tsx:59`'s `RecommendedProducts` import from the base
package path to a relative path pointing at our own override, per
[overrideStyling.md](../../../../zimmermann-pwa/.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md)'s existing
"Importing an already-overridden component from a new component" rule — the exact same doctrine
A6 already applies to `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` below, just missed for `RecommendedProducts` itself
in the original draft of this plan. See A6's updated step and pass criteria.

  controls' hidden state was unconditional (applying to touch too), and touch
  never enters HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY at all -- so on that pointer type they

fix(ui-kits): restore ZimmProductCard swipe paging and hover-reveal a11y
---BODY---
Three regressions found live-testing PR #85's shared product-card family:

- Touch swipe never paged multi-image galleries. The organism's whole-card
  stretched-link overlay was never lifted above the media/gallery region (only
  close/carousel/content buttons were), so a swipe landed on the invisible
  overlay <a> instead of the real scroll container. Fixed by adding the media
  slot to the existing z-index lift, plus a click passthrough (useHistory().push)
  so a plain tap still navigates to the PDP now that the overlay no longer
  receives that click.

- The most recent hover-reveal fix (replacing :focus-within with
  :has(:focus-visible) to stop arrows sticking open after a mouse click) used
  display:none as the hidden state for five reveal sites. display:none
  unconditionally strips an element from the accessibility tree, and
  :has(:focus-visible) is a browser heuristic that VoiceOver-driven focus isn't
  guaranteed to satisfy -- a real regression, not touch-only (true on any Mac
  trackpad). Fixed by keeping every reveal target permanently in the DOM/tab
  order, using position+clip-path (the same technique ZimmColourSwatchGroup
  already ships) instead of display to express hidden vs revealed, so the
  :hover/:has(:focus-visible) trigger logic itself is untouched.

- The touch slide-indicator only updated once a swipe gesture fully settled
  (scrollend), never during the drag itself. Fixed with a
  requestAnimationFrame-throttled scroll listener alongside the existing
  scrollend one.

===END===

453	    sizeSelectorUnavailable,
454	    // Same Fix C audit: notify-me is hover-gated on hover-capable devices (hidden by default,
455	    // revealed on hover/focus-visible — every Desktop Unavailable+Hover reference shows it
456	    // appearing only there) but unconditionally visible on touch (every Mobile Unavailable
457	    // reference — the only state a touch pointer ever sees, per the "Mobile has no Hover variant"
458	    // finding — shows it plainly, with no hover to reveal it). This flag is deliberately keyed off
459	    // `showNotifyMe` itself, not `variation`: the confirmed behaviour is identical across all
460	    // three variations, and the recipe's selector simply matches nothing when notify-me isn't
461	    // mounted at all.
462	    hoverRevealsNotifyMe: showNotifyMe,
463	    hideBagOnMobile: bagHiddenOnMobile,
464	  });
465	
466	  // Fix I — see the module docblock's own "Fix I" paragraph for the full narrative. Guards the
467	  // two arrow buttons and the remove/close button (all real <button> descendants of
468	  // ZimmProductCardMedia) so paging/onRemove keep firing on their own and never also navigate.
469	  // Fix L (CodeRabbit finding on PR #85, verified correct before fixing): a real <a> lets the
470	  // browser handle Cmd/Ctrl-click (new tab), Shift-click (new window), and non-primary-button
471	  // clicks natively — this handler only ever replaces the in-page navigation an UNMODIFIED,
472	  // primary-button click used to reach via the stretched-link overlay (see Fix I). Bailing out on
473	  // any of those instead of forcing an in-tab `history.push` regardless of what the shopper
474	  // actually asked for; a no-op here is a real gap (it doesn't open a new tab the way a real link
475	  // would) but is strictly better than silently overriding an explicit "open elsewhere" signal.
476	  const handleMediaClick = (event: React.MouseEvent<HTMLDivElement>): void => {
477	    const target = event.target as HTMLElement;
478	    if (target.closest('button')) return;
479	    if (event.metaKey || event.ctrlKey || event.shiftKey || event.altKey || event.button !== 0) return;
480	    history.push(href);
481	  };
482	
483	  return (
484	    <chakra.div __css={styles.root} data-testid="product-card" data-product-id={id}>
485	      <ZimmProductCardMedia
486	        primaryImage={primaryImage}
487	        hoverImage={hoverImage}
488	        images={images}
489	        swapOnHover={config.showHoverImageSwap && Boolean(hoverImage)}
490	        showControls
491	        badge={resolvedBadge}
492	        onRemove={onRemove}
493	        removeLabel={removeLabel}
494	        onClick={handleMediaClick}
495	      />
496	      <ZimmProductCardContent
497	        name={name}
498	        headingLevel={headingLevel}
499	        href={href}
500	        currentPrice={currentPrice}
501	        originalPrice={originalPrice}
502	        isPriceLoading={isPriceLoading}
503	        showAttributes={config.showAttributes}
504	        colour={colour}
505	        size={size}
506	        showBag={config.showBag}
507	        isUnavailable={isUnavailable}
508	        onAddToBag={onAddToBag}
509	        showSizeChips={config.showSizeChips}
510	        sizeChipValues={sizeChipValues}
511	        selectedSizeChipValue={selectedSizeChipValue}
512	        onSizeChipSelect={onSizeChipSelect}
513	        showNotifyMe={showNotifyMe}
514	        onNotifyMe={onNotifyMe}
515	      />
516	    </chakra.div>
517	  );
518	};
519	
520	export default ZimmProductCard;
521

import React from 'react';
import { chakra, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
import { useHistory } from 'react-router-dom';
import { defineMessages, useIntl } from 'react-intl';
import { ZimmProductCardMedia } from '../../molecules/zimmProductCardMedia';
import type { ZimmProductCardMediaImage } from '../../molecules/zimmProductCardMedia';
import { ZimmProductCardContent } from '../../molecules/zimmProductCardContent';
import type { ZimmSizeChipValue } from '../../molecules/zimmSizeChipGroup';

/**
 * SFCC-236 Step 6 — the organism that assembles Step 4's `ZimmProductCardMedia` and Step 5's
 * `ZimmProductCardContent` into the full product card, across the three confirmed variations.
 * Figma component set `Product-card`, node `40000223:2822` (20 variants: Size x State x Type x
 * Unavailable), file `wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm`. The variation matrix below reflects the resolved
 * `hidden`-attribute reading confirmed against the real assembled Card-content instances:
 *
 *   Home      (40000214:6141 default / 40002163:36593 hover)   — image + name only by default;
 *             bag/attributes/size-selector hidden always; a hover-CAPABLE pointer reveals price
 *             on hover. Mobile (`40000223:2821`) shows price unconditionally instead — it has no
 *             Hover variant at all, so a price hidden "by default, revealed on hover" like the
 *             original build shipped would never be revealed there at all (Fix E, found in the
 *             full-sweep follow-up audit; confirmed live as a real bug, not just a Figma reading).
 *             Arrows appear on hover-capable pointers regardless of variation (Media's own
 *             concern, driven purely by image count).
 *   PLP/PDP   (40002163:41441 default / 40002163:41459 hover)  — image + name + bag (always) +
 *             price by default, no attributes, size-selector hidden; hover hides price and
 *             reveals the size-selector in its place; arrows appear.
 *   Wishlist  (40002187:58446 default / 40002187:58458 hover)  — image + name + bag (always) +
 *             attributes (colour+size) + price by default, size-selector hidden; hover hides
 *             price and reveals the size-selector, confirmed identical to PLP's own hover reveal
 *             via node `40002187:58460` (the Wishlist hover instance carries no `hidden`
 *             attribute on "Size Selector" at all) — this is NOT what the SFCC-236 Jira AC text
 *             says (it only mentions the image switch + arrows for Wishlist hover). It shipped
 *             matching the design anyway — a judgment call made during implementation, not a
 *             conflict that was raised on the ticket or separately ratified.
 *
 * "Recently Viewed Full History" is not a fourth variation — the AC states it behaves exactly
 * like PLP, so callers pass `variation: 'plp'` for it.
 *
 * Unavailable=True (Fix C, SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit) is confirmed designed for **every**
 * variation, not just `plp` — an earlier revision of this paragraph claimed the opposite, before
 * the Default+Hover Unavailable instances for `home` (40002163:39981 / :39990) and `wishlist`
 * (40002187:58452 / :58464) were actually checked. The confirmed rule, identical across all three:
 *   - The PLP/Wishlist size-selector hover-swap is suppressed entirely when unavailable — nothing
 *     to pick for an out-of-stock item, so price stays visible on hover instead of being replaced
 *     (`hoverHidesPrice`/`hoverRevealsSizeSelector` are both AND-ed with `!isUnavailable` below).
 *     Home's own hover-reveals-price behaviour is unaffected — its Unavailable Hover reference
 *     still reveals price exactly as the in-stock case does.
 *   - "Notify me" is hover-gated on hover-capable devices (hidden by default, revealed on
 *     hover/focus-visible, confirmed via every Desktop Unavailable+Hover reference) but
 *     unconditionally visible on touch (confirmed via the Mobile Unavailable references —
 *     Mobile has no Hover variant at all, so whatever they show is the only state a touch
 *     pointer ever sees, and all of them show notify-me plainly).
 * `isUnavailable` and `onNotifyMe` are threaded through uniformly to `ZimmProductCardContent`
 * (the only one of the two composed children with an `isUnavailable` concept at all —
 * `ZimmProductCardMedia` has no such prop); this organism does not itself restrict `showNotifyMe`
 * to any one variation — a caller that never passes `onNotifyMe` simply gets no notify-me button.
 *
 * Fix F (full-sweep follow-up audit, after the above was already built and approved): the
 * Desktop-only "price stays, notify-me is simply added on hover" behaviour above is NOT what
 * Mobile does. Mobile PLP/Wishlist Unavailable (`40002163:41488`, `40002187:58475`) both have
 * `Price` `hidden="true"` and only "Notify me" visible — a genuine SWAP, unlike Desktop's additive
 * treatment — where Mobile Home Unavailable (`40002163:41204`) keeps price visible alongside
 * notify-me, unchanged from Desktop. `sizeSelectorUnavailable` (already computed below for the
 * size-chip permanent-hide) drives this too, in zimmProductCard.css.ts, since it is already
 * exactly "PLP/Wishlist and unavailable" — the same condition, no new variable needed.
 *
 * The bag icon also has two Mobile-breakpoint hides, both viewport-width concerns unrelated to
 * hover capability (see zimmProductCard.css.ts's own responsive rules, keyed off the same
 * `breakpoints` token `zimmProductCardContent.css.ts` already uses for its padding steps):
 *   - `hideBagOnMobile` — PLP only, unconditional. Figma's Mobile PLP/PDP Card-content instances
 *     (`40002163:41479` available / `40002163:41488` unavailable) both have the bag icon's
 *     `Icons` frame `hidden="true"` regardless of stock status, where Desktop's own PLP instance
 *     leaves it visible.
 *   - `hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable` (Fix G, same follow-up audit) — Wishlist only, and only
 *     when unavailable. Wishlist's Mobile instance shows the bag when available
 *     (`40002187:58470`) and hides it only when unavailable (`40002187:58473`) — narrower than
 *     PLP's own unconditional rule, so it needs its own flag rather than reusing
 *     `hideBagOnMobile`. `index.tsx` combines both into one `bagHiddenOnMobile` boolean before
 *     the recipe ever sees it — the recipe only needs "hide this on mobile for this render", not
 *     which of the two reasons applies.
 *
 * KNOWN GAP: `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s `priority` prop (its LCP eager-load escape hatch) has no
 * passthrough here — every card composed via this organism lazy-loads its primary image. Not in
 * the given component contract for this step; flagged rather than added silently, since a PLP
 * page placing this organism above the fold would want it.
 *
 * Badge (feature addition, not a "Fix" like the ones above — the underlying design gap was
 * genuinely closed, not misread): `ZimmProductCardContent`'s docblock used to claim no Figma
 * design existed for SFCC-236's badge AC. It does — the "Tag" overlay, confirmed present and
 * pixel-identical on every Size/Type variant checked (nodes 40002163:41442, 40002096:12223,
 * 40002187:58447, 40002163:41478, 40004599:89266, 40004638:120485) — it was just nested one
 * level deeper (inside "Image Group", i.e. `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s domain) than the first pass
 * looked. Per Dani Rivett's scope note on the ticket, the badge shows on PLP and Wishlist (and
 * therefore Recently Viewed Full History, which already reuses the `plp` variation) and is
 * suppressed on Home — driven by `VARIATION_CONFIG.showBadge` below, the same table-driven
 * mechanism as every other variation decision in this file. Figma's own Home node still shows
 * the Tag layer un-hidden, contradicting that scope note — treating the confirmed written
 * requirement as authoritative over the file's possibly-stale layer visibility here, flagged
 * rather than silently picked.
 *
 * Badge count (confirmed after the above shipped, via a Dev Mode Connect Note on the separate
 * "Product Cards" Figma file — QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs, node 3448:35976 — distinct from the
 * design-system component-set file cited throughout this docblock): "only 1 product badge will
 * show up on these product cards - depending on the configured hierarchy, the highest priority
 * badge will be shown," with that priority logic owned by SFCC-225. This confirms `badge?:
 * string` (a single value, not a list) is the correct, final shape for this prop — not a
 * placeholder pending a possible future move to an array. SFCC-225's own already-merged SCAPI
 * hook writes `c_productBadges` as an array sorted by `badgePriorityOrder`, so whatever mapper
 * eventually feeds this prop (none exists yet — no page consumes this organism) just needs
 * `c_productBadges[0]?.productBadge`, not any re-sorting of its own.
 *
 * Hover image-swap on Home (same Dani-vs-AC contradiction as the Badge note above, resolved the
 * same direction): Dani's comment also says "we don't want the hover action (model photo) on
 * the homepage," but the AC update three days later frames the tile-image hover-swap as an
 * unconditional Core Component behaviour with no Home exclusion — and the code as first shipped
 * followed the AC, passing `swapOnHover` to `ZimmProductCardMedia` unconditionally with no
 * variation gate at all. Treated the comment as more authoritative than the AC text here too:
 * `VARIATION_CONFIG.showHoverImageSwap` now suppresses the swap for `home` specifically. This
 * is unrelated to, and does not affect, Home's own
 * `hoverRevealsPrice` — that is a separate mechanism (a style flag consumed by this organism's
 * own recipe), not `swapOnHover`.
 *
 * KNOWN GAP (postbuild doc/traceability audit, comment-only — no behaviour change): both
 * quotes above, from Dani's scope note (Jira comment 13880 on SFCC-236), truncate at the same
 * point. In full, her instruction is no badge and no hover-image-swap on "the Homepage or on
 * the Recently Viewed product carousel" — the Badge note above and this Hover image-swap note
 * each only implement and discuss the Homepage half. The Recently Viewed carousel half has no
 * code path in this file today: that surface is SFCC-83's rail component, which does not exist
 * yet and has no entry in the `ZimmProductCardVariation` union above. A rail caller reaching
 * for the closest existing option, `variation: 'plp'`, would get `showBadge: true` and
 * `showHoverImageSwap: true` from `VARIATION_CONFIG` — the opposite of what Dani asked for on
 * that surface. Whoever builds SFCC-83 needs to either add a dedicated `VARIATION_CONFIG` entry
 * for the rail (both flags `false`) or get explicit written confirmation on the ticket that the
 * suppression doesn't apply there — not assume `'plp'` already covers it.
 *
 * Fix I (SFCC-236, found via live mobile-device testing on this branch, same round that found
 * Fix H): multi-image cards did not respond to a real touch swipe at all — the slide indicator
 * rendered correctly (so the image data/gallery logic was fine), but swiping the image never
 * paged it. Root cause and CSS fix are `zimmProductCard.css.ts`'s own Fix I (docblock point 2):
 * `ZimmProductCardMedia` was the one interactive region never lifted above the stretched-link
 * overlay, so a swipe gesture starting on the image landed on the invisible overlay `<a>` first
 * and never reached the real scroll container underneath. Lifting Media above the overlay fixes
 * the swipe, but has a side effect: a plain tap/click on the image used to "work" by landing on
 * that same overlay and navigating to the PDP — once Media sits on top, the tap no longer reaches
 * it, and Media itself had no click behaviour of its own. `handleMediaClick` below restores that
 * navigation deliberately, via `useHistory().push(href)` rather than depending on the overlay by
 * accident: this repo is pinned to react-router-dom v5.3.4 (`package.json`), which has no
 * `useNavigate` — `useHistory()` + `history.push()` is the correct v5 primitive, already
 * established in this codebase (`footer/index.tsx`, `zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx`,
 * `pages/product-detail/index.tsx`) and the same one the base SFCC `product-list` page itself
 * uses. `href` needed no new prop plumbing — this organism already destructures it from its own
 * base props (above) and previously only forwarded it to `ZimmProductCardContent`. The handler
 * guards against the two arrow buttons and the remove/close button — all real `<button>`
 * descendants of `ZimmProductCardMedia` — via `(event.target as HTMLElement).closest('button')`,
 * so paging and `onRemove` keep firing on their own and never also navigate. No custom drag-vs-tap
 * detection is needed for the swipe/tap split itself: browsers natively suppress the synthetic
 * `click` event after a real drag/scroll on the same element, so a swipe pages the gallery without
 * ever reaching this handler, while a plain tap (no movement) still fires it exactly as the old
 * overlay click did.
 */

/** Re-exported under this organism's own name so a page-level caller never has to reach into a
 *  molecule's type — the shape itself is Media's own `ZimmProductCardMediaImage`, not a
 *  redeclaration (a hand-copied duplicate would silently drift from its source). */
export type ZimmProductCardImage = ZimmProductCardMediaImage;

/** `ZimmProductCardContent`'s own already-derived heading-level type (`'h1' | 'h2' | 'h3'`,
 *  itself derived from `ZimmProductName`'s `as` prop) — read via `ComponentProps` off the
 *  component this organism actually forwards it to, rather than a hand-typed duplicate union. */
type ZimmProductCardHeadingLevel = React.ComponentProps<typeof ZimmProductCardContent>['headingLevel'];

/**
 * Exported alongside `ZimmProductCardProps` (not just kept module-private) so a test/fixture can
 * build a properly *narrowed* per-variation props object — e.g.
 * `ZimmProductCardBaseProps & ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation` — instead of a value typed as the
 * full union. This matters for real, not just for convenience: TypeScript's excess-property
 * check on a *union* target is weak (a property valid on any one member is not flagged as excess
 * on a fresh literal discriminated toward a different member), so proving "the wishlist-only
 * fields don't exist on Home" needs an assignment to Home's own narrow shape specifically, not to
 * the union alias — see index.test.tsx's `@ts-expect-error` cases and its overloaded
 * `buildCardProps` helper.
 */
export type ZimmProductCardBaseProps = {
  /** Stable per-card identifier. Not used for any layout/behavioural decision — exposed as a
   *  `data-product-id` attribute on the root element as a DOM hook for QA automation/analytics,
   *  the same kind of caller-facing marker `data-testid` already serves in this build's other
   *  components, without overloading that attribute's own testing-only convention. */
  id: string;
  /** PDP destination, pre-site-prefixed by the caller — forwarded straight to
   *  `ZimmProductCardContent`'s own `href` (see that component's own JSDoc on trust level). */
  href: string;
  name: string;
  headingLevel: ZimmProductCardHeadingLevel;
  primaryImage: ZimmProductCardImage;
  hoverImage?: ZimmProductCardImage;
  images?: ZimmProductCardImage[];
  currentPrice?: string;
  originalPrice?: string;
  isPriceLoading?: boolean;
  isUnavailable?: boolean;
  /** Only meaningful when `isUnavailable` is true. See the module docblock for why this is not
   *  restricted to the `plp` variation at the type level. */
  onNotifyMe?: () => void;
  /**
   * Merchandiser-configured badge label (e.g. "Runway", "Exclusive"). Always a single value —
   * confirmed via a Figma Dev Mode Connect Note that only the single highest-priority badge is
   * ever shown, never a list (see the module docblock's "Badge count" note). Not restricted to
   * any variation at the type level, same reasoning as `onNotifyMe` above — whether it actually
   * renders is `VARIATION_CONFIG.showBadge`'s job (PLP/Wishlist show it, Home suppresses it; see
   * the module docblock's "Badge" note).
   */
  badge?: string;
};

export type ZimmProductCardPlpVariation = {
  variation: 'plp';
  onAddToBag?: () => void;
  sizeChipValues?: ZimmSizeChipValue[];
  selectedSizeChipValue?: string;
  onSizeChipSelect?: (value: string) => void;
};

export type ZimmProductCardHomeVariation = {
  variation: 'home';
  // No additions — Home never shows the bag, attributes, or size chips (see VARIATION_CONFIG).
};

export type ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation = {
  variation: 'wishlist';
  /** Required, not optional — the Wishlist AC always shows the attributes line. */
  colour: string;
  size: string;
  /** Required — a wishlist card with no way to remove itself is a spec violation. */
  onRemove: () => void;
  /** Bag is always visible for Wishlist per the confirmed matrix above. */
  onAddToBag?: () => void;
  /** Same trio `ZimmProductCardPlpVariation` declares, and for the same reason: confirmed via the
   *  real Figma Wishlist Hover instance (node 40002187:58458) during the SFCC-236 Step 6 visual
   *  audit that Wishlist's hover reveal is a genuine, populated size-selector swap identical to
   *  PLP's — not a PLP-only affordance. `index.tsx`'s render body already forwarded these
   *  unconditionally to `ZimmProductCardContent` for every variation (via the
   *  `ZimmProductCardVariationFields` cast below); this type previously just didn't expose them
   *  to a Wishlist caller, which is what let the Wishlist story ship without ever populating them. */
  sizeChipValues?: ZimmSizeChipValue[];
  selectedSizeChipValue?: string;
  onSizeChipSelect?: (value: string) => void;
};

export type ZimmProductCardProps = ZimmProductCardBaseProps &
  (ZimmProductCardPlpVariation | ZimmProductCardHomeVariation | ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation);

type ZimmProductCardVariation =
  | ZimmProductCardPlpVariation['variation']
  | ZimmProductCardHomeVariation['variation']
  | ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation['variation'];

/**
 * Widened, not narrowed: every variation-specific field is optional here regardless of which
 * branch is actually active, purely so the component body below can destructure once with no
 * `if`/`switch` on `props.variation` — the extensibility AC requires every layout/visibility
 * decision to come from `VARIATION_CONFIG`, keyed by the discriminant, never a branching
 * statement. The exported `ZimmProductCardProps` discriminated union above is what actually
 * enforces correct usage at every call site (proven by the `@ts-expect-error` cases in
 * index.test.tsx) — this cast only relaxes internal access inside this file; it changes nothing
 * about what a caller may legally pass in.
 */
type ZimmProductCardVariationFields = Partial<
  Omit<ZimmProductCardPlpVariation, 'variation'> &
    Omit<ZimmProductCardWishlistVariation, 'variation'> &
    Omit<ZimmProductCardHomeVariation, 'variation'>
>;

type ZimmProductCardVariationConfig = {
  showBag: boolean;
  showAttributes: boolean;
  showSizeChips: boolean;
  /** PLP/Wishlist: price is visible by default and hides on hover. */
  hoverHidesPrice: boolean;
  /** Home only: price is hidden by default and reveals on hover. */
  hoverRevealsPrice: boolean;
  /** PLP/Wishlist: the size-chip picker is hidden by default and reveals on hover. */
  hoverRevealsSizeSelector: boolean;
  showRemove: boolean;
  /** PLP only (found during the SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit): Figma's Mobile Card-content
   *  instance has the bag icon's `Icons` frame `hidden="true"`, unlike Desktop and unlike
   *  Wishlist's own Mobile instance (bag stays visible there on every breakpoint). A viewport-
   *  width concern, not a hover one — see zimmProductCard.css.ts's own responsive rule. */
  hideBagOnMobile: boolean;
  /** Wishlist only (found during the follow-up full-sweep visual audit against every variant x
   *  state node): unlike PLP's unconditional `hideBagOnMobile`, Wishlist's Mobile Card-content
   *  instance shows the bag icon when available (`40002187:58470`) and hides it
   *  (`Icons` frame `hidden="true"`) only when unavailable (`40002187:58473`) — narrower than
   *  `hideBagOnMobile`, and combined with it (not replacing it) in the `bagHiddenOnMobile`
   *  derivation below, since the two are mutually exclusive per variation today but there is no
   *  reason to assume that stays true forever. */
  hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable: boolean;
  /** Shown on PLP/Wishlist, suppressed on Home — see the module docblock's "Badge" note. */
  showBadge: boolean;
  /**
   * Allows `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s primary/hover image crossfade for this variation. Suppressed
   * on Home per Dani Rivett's scope note, overriding the AC's unconditional framing — see the
   * module docblock's "Hover image-swap on Home" note. `false` here means a supplied
   * `hoverImage` is simply never swapped to, regardless of pointer capability.
   */
  showHoverImageSwap: boolean;
};

/**
 * The extensibility AC's actual mechanism: every layout/visibility decision this organism makes
 * reads from this table, keyed by `variation` — adding a future variation means adding a union
 * member above and one row here, touching no JSX. `index.tsx`'s render body contains no
 * `switch`/`if` on `props.variation` anywhere (verify with
 * `grep -n 'variation ===\|switch (variation)' index.tsx` — zero hits).
 */
const VARIATION_CONFIG: Record<ZimmProductCardVariation, ZimmProductCardVariationConfig> = {
  home: {
    showBag: false,
    showAttributes: false,
    showSizeChips: false,
    hoverHidesPrice: false,
    hoverRevealsPrice: true,
    hoverRevealsSizeSelector: false,
    showRemove: false,
    hideBagOnMobile: false,
    hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable: false,
    showBadge: false,
    showHoverImageSwap: false,
  },
  plp: {
    showBag: true,
    showAttributes: false,
    showSizeChips: true,
    hoverHidesPrice: true,
    hoverRevealsPrice: false,
    hoverRevealsSizeSelector: true,
    showRemove: false,
    hideBagOnMobile: true,
    hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable: false,
    showBadge: true,
    showHoverImageSwap: true,
  },
  wishlist: {
    showBag: true,
    showAttributes: true,
    showSizeChips: true,
    hoverHidesPrice: true,
    hoverRevealsPrice: false,
    hoverRevealsSizeSelector: true,
    showRemove: true,
    hideBagOnMobile: false,
    hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable: true,
    showBadge: true,
    showHoverImageSwap: true,
  },
};

const messages = defineMessages({
  // Interpolated with the product name, matching ZimmProductPrice's WAS/NOW pattern — Media's
  // own `removeLabel` prop is a plain string, so the interpolation happens here, at the one call
  // site that actually knows the product name.
  removeFromWishlist: {
    id: 'product_card.remove.from_wishlist',
    defaultMessage: 'Remove {name} from wishlist',
  },
});

const ZIMM_PRODUCT_CARD_RECIPE = 'ZimmProductCard';

/**
 * Organism — the full product card, composing `ZimmProductCardMedia` and `ZimmProductCardContent`
 * across the `home` / `plp` / `wishlist` variations. See the module docblock above for the
 * confirmed Figma variation matrix and this component's own recipe (`zimmProductCard.css.ts`) for
 * the stretched-link and hover-reveal mechanics that live entirely in CSS, not in this render
 * body — both children are always rendered in full, with every one of their own sub-parts; CSS
 * alone decides what is visible for a given variation and pointer capability.
 *
 * @param props see `ZimmProductCardProps` — a discriminated union on `variation`.
 */
export const ZimmProductCard = (props: ZimmProductCardProps) => {
  const {
    id,
    href,
    name,
    headingLevel,
    primaryImage,
    hoverImage,
    images,
    currentPrice,
    originalPrice,
    isPriceLoading,
    isUnavailable,
    onNotifyMe,
    badge,
    variation,
  } = props;

  const { onAddToBag, sizeChipValues, selectedSizeChipValue, onSizeChipSelect, colour, size, onRemove } =
    props as ZimmProductCardVariationFields;

  const intl = useIntl();
  const history = useHistory();
  const config = VARIATION_CONFIG[variation];

  // Both conditions required — an organism that sets isUnavailable without a real callback
  // should not show a dead notify-me button. Mirrors ZimmProductCardContent's own
  // showNotifyMeButton co-requirement.
  const showNotifyMe = Boolean(isUnavailable) && Boolean(onNotifyMe);

  // Fix C (SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit): confirmed against the real Figma Default+Hover
  // instances for every variation × Unavailable=True (including the Mobile/no-hover variants,
  // which show the only state a touch pointer ever sees) that `isUnavailable` suppresses the
  // size-selector hover-swap entirely — there is nothing to pick for an out-of-stock item, so
  // price stays visible on hover instead of being replaced. Home's own hover-reveals-price
  // behaviour is untouched by this — Home's Unavailable Hover reference (node 40002163:39990)
  // still reveals price on hover exactly as the in-stock case does; only the PLP/Wishlist
  // hide-and-swap needs suppressing.
  //
  // Suppressing `hoverRevealsSizeSelector` alone is not enough to reproduce that reference: it
  // only stops the organism adding its OWN hide/reveal pair, which leaves the size-chip wrapper
  // at Content's own natural (visible) default — briefly shipped that way mid-fix and caught by
  // re-checking the real Storybook render against Figma, which confirms size chips stay hidden
  // in BOTH states when unavailable, not just "not swapped in on hover". `sizeSelectorUnavailable`
  // carries that permanent hide separately, unconditional (not gated by hover-capability at all —
  // this isn't a pointer-type concern, unlike everything else in this recipe).
  //
  // Follow-up (full-sweep visual audit against every variant x state node, not just the sampled
  // set the first pass checked): `sizeSelectorUnavailable` ALSO drives a mobile-only price hide
  // in the recipe now (Fix F) — confirmed via `get_metadata` that Mobile PLP/Wishlist Unavailable
  // hide price and show notify-me in its place (`40002163:41488`, `40002187:58475`), the OPPOSITE
  // of Desktop's additive treatment (price stays, notify-me is simply added on hover). Nothing
  // extra is computed here for it — the recipe reads the same `sizeSelectorUnavailable` boolean
  // for both the size-chip permanent-hide and this new price rule, since both only ever apply to
  // the same PLP/Wishlist-and-unavailable case.
  const hoverHidesPrice = config.hoverHidesPrice && !isUnavailable;
  const hoverRevealsSizeSelector = config.hoverRevealsSizeSelector && !isUnavailable;
  const sizeSelectorUnavailable = config.hoverRevealsSizeSelector && Boolean(isUnavailable);

  // Fix G (same follow-up audit): Wishlist-only. `hideBagOnMobile` alone only covers PLP's own
  // unconditional mobile hide; Wishlist's bag stays visible on mobile UNLESS unavailable
  // (`40002187:58470` vs `40002187:58473`). Combined into one boolean here rather than exposing
  // both conditions to the recipe — it only needs to know "hide this on mobile for this render",
  // not why.
  const bagHiddenOnMobile = config.hideBagOnMobile || (config.hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable && Boolean(isUnavailable));

  const removeLabel = config.showRemove ? intl.formatMessage(messages.removeFromWishlist, { name }) : undefined;
  const resolvedBadge = config.showBadge ? badge : undefined;

  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_PRODUCT_CARD_RECIPE, {
    hoverHidesPrice,
    hoverRevealsPrice: config.hoverRevealsPrice,
    hoverRevealsSizeSelector,
    sizeSelectorUnavailable,
    // Same Fix C audit: notify-me is hover-gated on hover-capable devices (hidden by default,
    // revealed on hover/focus-visible — every Desktop Unavailable+Hover reference shows it
    // appearing only there) but unconditionally visible on touch (every Mobile Unavailable
    // reference — the only state a touch pointer ever sees, per the "Mobile has no Hover variant"
    // finding — shows it plainly, with no hover to reveal it). This flag is deliberately keyed off
    // `showNotifyMe` itself, not `variation`: the confirmed behaviour is identical across all
    // three variations, and the recipe's selector simply matches nothing when notify-me isn't
    // mounted at all.
    hoverRevealsNotifyMe: showNotifyMe,
    hideBagOnMobile: bagHiddenOnMobile,
  });

  // Fix I — see the module docblock's own "Fix I" paragraph for the full narrative. Guards the
  // two arrow buttons and the remove/close button (all real <button> descendants of
  // ZimmProductCardMedia) so paging/onRemove keep firing on their own and never also navigate.
  // Fix L (CodeRabbit finding on PR #85, verified correct before fixing): a real <a> lets the
  // browser handle Cmd/Ctrl-click (new tab), Shift-click (new window), and non-primary-button
  // clicks natively — this handler only ever replaces the in-page navigation an UNMODIFIED,
  // primary-button click used to reach via the stretched-link overlay (see Fix I). Bailing out on
  // any of those instead of forcing an in-tab `history.push` regardless of what the shopper
  // actually asked for; a no-op here is a real gap (it doesn't open a new tab the way a real link
  // would) but is strictly better than silently overriding an explicit "open elsewhere" signal.
  const handleMediaClick = (event: React.MouseEvent<HTMLDivElement>): void => {
    const target = event.target as HTMLElement;
    if (target.closest('button')) return;
    if (event.metaKey || event.ctrlKey || event.shiftKey || event.altKey || event.button !== 0) return;
    history.push(href);
  };

  return (
    <chakra.div __css={styles.root} data-testid="product-card" data-product-id={id}>
      <ZimmProductCardMedia
        primaryImage={primaryImage}
        hoverImage={hoverImage}
        images={images}
        swapOnHover={config.showHoverImageSwap && Boolean(hoverImage)}
        showControls
        badge={resolvedBadge}
        onRemove={onRemove}
        removeLabel={removeLabel}
        onClick={handleMediaClick}
      />
      <ZimmProductCardContent
        name={name}
        headingLevel={headingLevel}
        href={href}
        currentPrice={currentPrice}
        originalPrice={originalPrice}
        isPriceLoading={isPriceLoading}
        showAttributes={config.showAttributes}
        colour={colour}
        size={size}
        showBag={config.showBag}
        isUnavailable={isUnavailable}
        onAddToBag={onAddToBag}
        showSizeChips={config.showSizeChips}
        sizeChipValues={sizeChipValues}
        selectedSizeChipValue={selectedSizeChipValue}
        onSizeChipSelect={onSizeChipSelect}
        showNotifyMe={showNotifyMe}
        onNotifyMe={onNotifyMe}
      />
    </chakra.div>
  );
};

export default ZimmProductCard;

content.text:
Before I brief A2's implementer, I found a real gap the plan's Figma investigation didn't catch — worth stopping for.

**The problem:** Figma's "image only" reading for the rail (findings 36-38) means A2's plan is to add a `showContent: false` flag that suppresses `ZimmProductCardContent` entirely. But `ZimmProductCardContent` is where the card's real `<a href>` (the "name link") lives — the element that makes the whole card keyboard-reachable and screen-reader-navigable. `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own `onClick={handleMediaClick}` (built in an earlier fix for click-passthrough) is a plain `<div>` handler, mouse-only, with no `tabIndex`/`onKeyDown`/role.

So as currently planned, a `recentlyViewed` card with content fully suppressed would have **zero focusable elements** — a real WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) violation, not a nitpick, and this project explicitly targets 2.2 AA. Figma's `hidden="true"` on Card-content tells us what's *visually* shown, not whether keyboard/AT access still needs to exist underneath — six prior findings passes never surfaced this because nothing before now needed to fully suppress content.

**My recommendation:** when `showContent` is false, render a minimal real `<a href={href} aria-label={name}>` wrapping the image region — no visible content of its own (matching the design exactly), but restoring real link semantics and keyboard operability. Simpler than reviving any part of `ZimmProductCardContent`, and it's the same "just use a native interactive element" default `components.md` already prefers over reimplementing keyboard behavior.

Want me to build it that way, or did you have something else in mind?

content.text:
Good push — my first answer wasn't the cheapest. Digging in further:

The existing stretched-link overlay pattern (used by the other three variations) earns its complexity because those cards have *other* clickable things inside Media — arrows, a remove button — competing for the same click. A `recentlyViewed` card has none of that: single image only, no remove, no arrows (config already forces all of that off). So there's nothing to route around.

That means the cheapest fix is simpler than my first idea: skip the overlay/z-index machinery entirely and just wrap the image **directly** in a real `<a href={href} aria-label={name}>` for this one variation. A native anchor click already handles Cmd/Ctrl/Shift/middle-click and keyboard Enter for free — no JS needed. `handleMediaClick` (the existing click-passthrough handler) becomes unnecessary for this branch specifically, since there's no invisible overlay for a native click to miss.

Net cost: no new recipe CSS for stretching/z-index, no aria-label reinvention, one JSX branch, existing config flags already guarantee the "no competing interactive elements" precondition holds. That's cheaper than my first proposal, not just equally good.

content.text:
Good questions — walking through them in order:

**Do we have a variant that already fits?** No. Closest is `home` (image + name only, bag/attributes/size-chips already hidden) — but Home still shows the product **name** and reveals **price** on hover. Figma's reading for the rail is stricter than that: literally nothing but the image, ever. No existing variant matches, so something new is needed either way.

**If one matched exactly, would the link problem disappear?** No — and this is worth being clear about: Figma has no concept of "real `<a>` vs. styled `<div>`." It only encodes pixels. Even a pixel-perfect variant match can't tell us anything about accessibility-tree structure — that's inherently a frontend decision Figma is never going to resolve for us, regardless of how exact the visual match is.

**Is "build a variant for exactly this" not an option?** It is (that's what I'd been describing) — but your question made me check something I hadn't: I just read `ZimmProductCardMedia` directly, and it's a genuinely clean, standalone molecule — plain props, no Context, no coupling to the `ZimmProductCard` organism except one documented gotcha (hover-reveal arrows only work when composed inside that organism's recipe) that doesn't apply to us since a recently-viewed card only ever gets one image.

That opens a real third option I'd been missing: **skip `ZimmProductCard` entirely for this surface.** Compose `ZimmProductCardMedia` directly inside the rail component (A5), wrapped in a plain real link. No new variation, no new `showContent` flag, no touching a shared, already-complex organism with an eleven-fix bug history behind it, no new `@ts-expect-error` cases, zero risk to Home/PLP/Wishlist. **This makes A2 (as currently scoped) unnecessary** — nothing in `zimmProductCard/index.tsx` needs to change at all.

The tradeoff: this surface stops being a "variation of ZimmProductCard" and becomes its own small composition — but SFCC-236's extensibility AC is about that organism itself being easy to extend, not a mandate that every card-shaped surface in the app must route through it. Given AGENTS.md's own "smallest change that achieves the task" rule, and that A5 is greenfield anyway, I think this is the better answer, not just a cheaper one.

This does ripple into A3 (its mapper would target `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s smaller prop shape instead) and A5 (composes the molecule, not the organism). Want me to drop A2 and update the plan this way?

Browsing history storage:

Empty state: Given a shopper has not viewed any products in their current session (and is not authenticated with any history), then the Recently Viewed component is not rendered on the page — no empty rail or placeholder is shown.

Cross-page consistency: Given the Recently Viewed component is embedded on PLP, PDP and anywhere else, then the same browsing history and tile design is shown consistently across all surfaces.

Good call checking the tickets — this changes the picture, though not as cleanly as I'd like to claim, so let me be precise about what's actually established vs. inferred.

**SFCC-236's own scope list is the key new fact:** *"Variations in scope: Homepage, PLP, Wish List, Recently Viewed."* Four variations, named explicitly — and "Recently Viewed" here is genuinely ambiguous. The AC body never defines a standalone "Recently Viewed" variation; it only ever defines "**Recently Viewed Full History** variation (same behavior as PLP card)" — and every comment thread I can find (Emma's, Jasmijn's) is specifically about the *"see full recently viewed page,"* i.e. SFCC-84, never the rail. So the description's 4th list item could mean "a dedicated rail variation was intended, just never written up," or it could just be shorthand for Full History. I can't fully resolve which from the text alone — worth flagging as a real ticket gap either way, not something to paper over.

**One thing I want to flag and set aside, not build on:** Jasmijn's Aug 17 comment proposes adding *"and product name"* to the Core AC (name always shown, every variation, no exceptions) — which would directly contradict the Figma image-only reading. But comparing against the **current live AC text** you pasted, that addition isn't there — the live Core AC still only says the primary image is universal, nothing about name. Whatever happened with that proposal, it didn't survive into the live ticket, so I'm treating the live text as authoritative and not chasing the discrepancy further.

**SFCC-743 is the stronger signal.** It's explicitly a generic wrapper — title+link header around "**a responsive row of ProductCard components (SFCC-236)**" — and its own example usages ("More from this category," "Recommended for you") are the exact same shape of UI Recently Viewed is. Even without a direct link between the two tickets, this tells us the established pattern in this system for "labelled rail of product cards" is *compose `ZimmProductCard` instances*, not assemble smaller molecules bespoke. If SFCC-743 ever unblocks, it's going to want to wrap `ZimmProductCard`s — building the rail some other way now just creates a mismatch to reconcile later.

**Net effect on my recommendation:** I'm walking back what I said last turn. Given this, going through `ZimmProductCard` (Option A) is the better-aligned choice, not because a ticket mandates it outright, but because it matches the one concrete architectural pattern this system already commits to for this exact shape of UI, and diverging from it now is a cost with no real offsetting benefit once you weigh it against the ticket evidence. The accessibility fix (real link wrapping the image when content is suppressed) is needed either way — that part doesn't change.

One more thing worth noting: `recentlyViewed` as the variation name is now directly corroborated — it's the literal term SFCC-236 uses.

Want me to proceed with A2 on that basis — extend `ZimmProductCard`, add the link-wrapping fix for the `showContent:false` case?

content.text:
Reading `ZimmProductCardContent`'s actual source settles this. Two things I didn't know before:

- **Price is unconditionally rendered today, by design** — its own docblock states it explicitly: *"Always rendered regardless of variation; the organism's own CSS is what shows/hides it on hover... not this component."* There's no `showPrice` flag anywhere — it's a hard invariant.
- **There's no existing mechanism to hide the name's visible text at all.** Name and the wrapping link are always rendered together, unconditionally, same as price.

That changes the comparison:

**Option 1 — extend `ZimmProductCardContent` to support a "link-only" mode.** To make this work I'd need to: (a) add a way to suppress the name's visible text while keeping the link, and (b) break the stated "price always renders" invariant to also suppress it. That's two new capabilities in a *second* shared, already-tested component, one of which contradicts something this file currently guarantees on purpose. More invasive than it looked two turns ago.

**Option 2 — don't render `ZimmProductCardContent` at all for this variation** (the original A2 idea), and instead add a small `<Link to={href}>` directly in `ZimmProductCard`'s own render body, wrapping `ZimmProductCardMedia`, only when `!config.showContent`. The accessible name comes from Chakra's own `VisuallyHidden` wrapping the product name as real (but visually-hidden) text inside the link — costs nothing new, it's a stock Chakra export, not a new utility to build. No stretched-overlay/z-index trick needed either: since the link directly *contains* the image rather than being an invisible sibling overlay, it's just... a link around an image. Confined entirely to the one file A2 already scopes.

Option 2 is cheaper on every axis now: one file, no new props on a second component, no invariant broken, no new CSS. Recommending that.

**New flag required.** `ZimmProductCard` has no way today to suppress `ZimmProductCardContent`
wholesale — name and price render unconditionally. Add one (`showContent: false`) and gate the
`ZimmProductCardContent` render on it. Keep it table-driven like every other flag; **do not** add a
`variation === 'recentlyViewed'` branch (A2's own pass criterion below forbids it).

**Accessibility gap found and closed, 2026-09-07 — not rendering `ZimmProductCardContent` at all
would remove the only real `<a>` this card has.** `ZimmProductCardContent` owns the card's one real
link (the name-link, via `react-router-dom`'s `Link`) — `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own `onClick` is a
plain, mouse-only `<div>` handler with no `tabIndex`/`onKeyDown`. With Content fully unmounted, a
single-image `recentlyViewed` card (no gallery, no remove button, no badge, per the table above)
would have **zero focusable elements at all** — unreachable by keyboard, a real WCAG 2.1.1 violation,
not a style nitpick, and directly contradicts SFCC-83 AC 4 (*"Given a shopper clicks a recently viewed
product tile, then they are navigated to that product's PDP"*).

Two fixes were considered and rejected before landing on the one below:
- Extending `ZimmProductCardContent` itself with a "link-only" render mode — rejected after reading
  its actual source: price is rendered **unconditionally today, by design** (its own docblock: *"Always
  rendered regardless of variation... not this component"*) and there is no existing mechanism to
  suppress the name's visible text either. Doing this properly would mean breaking a stated invariant
  in a second shared, already-heavily-tested component, not a small addition.
- Composing `ZimmProductCardMedia` directly in the rail organism (A5), bypassing `ZimmProductCard`
  entirely — seriously considered mid-build, reversed after the SFCC-236/SFCC-743 ticket evidence
  above confirmed this codebase's established pattern for "labelled row of product cards" is
  composing `ZimmProductCard` instances, not smaller molecules directly.

**Decided fix (Marcel, 2026-09-07):** when `!config.showContent`, don't render
`ZimmProductCardContent` at all (as originally planned) — instead render a small `react-router-dom`
`Link` (matching the exact import `ZimmProductCardContent` itself already uses, `chakra(RouteLink)`)
wrapping *only* `ZimmProductCardMedia`, with the product name as real (not `aria-label`) but
visually-hidden text via Chakra's own `VisuallyHidden` export inside the link — zero new dependency,
zero new CSS utility to build. `ZimmProductCardMedia` gets no `onClick={handleMediaClick}` in this
branch — a real `<Link>` directly containing the image needs no click-passthrough workaround at all
(that mechanism exists purely to route around the *other* variations' invisible stretched-overlay
`<a>`, which doesn't exist here since the link directly wraps the image instead of sitting behind
it). Confined entirely to `zimmProductCard/index.tsx` — no touch to `ZimmProductCardContent` or
`ZimmProductCardMedia`, matching this step's existing file manifest exactly.

### A2 — Add the `recentlyViewed` variation to `ZimmProductCard`

Add `ZimmProductCardRecentlyViewedVariation` to the exported union and one `VARIATION_CONFIG` row.
Update the docblock's KNOWN GAP paragraph (lines 124–135) from "whoever builds SFCC-83 needs to…" to a
record of what was done, citing Jira comment 13880.

**Also record in that same docblock update (finding 34; naming decided 2026-09-06):** comment 13880
asks for the same badge/hover-swap suppression on **editorial and landing pages** — a surface with no
ticket, design or AC today. The variation is named `recentlyViewed` for the one confirmed surface, per
this repo's existing surface-naming convention (`home` / `plp` / `wishlist`). When editorial/landing
is scoped it needs **its own `VARIATION_CONFIG` row** with both flags `false`: it must not reuse
`recentlyViewed` (the name would lie) and must not use `plp` (which ships the badge Dani ruled out).
SFCC-236's *Variation extensibility* AC makes that a one-row change.

**Corroborated 2026-09-07, straight from the ticket text.** SFCC-236's own description lists
*"Variations in scope: Homepage, PLP, Wish List, **Recently Viewed**"* — the exact term `recentlyViewed`
already uses. The AC body itself never separately defines this variation (it only ever defines
"Recently Viewed **Full History**," always "same as PLP" — every comment thread on the ticket
confirms that's specifically about the *"see full recently viewed page,"* never the rail), so this
doesn't pin down the rail's own behaviour — but it does settle the architecture question raised while
building this step: **should the SFCC-83 rail be a `ZimmProductCard` variation at all, or a separate,
bespoke composition of smaller molecules?** SFCC-743 (Product Card Group, currently Blocked) answers
this more concretely: it's an explicit wrapper around *"a responsive row of ProductCard components
(SFCC-236),"* citing "More from this category"/"Recommended for you" as its own example usage — the
same shape of UI as this rail. That's the established pattern this codebase already commits to for
"labelled row of product cards," so extending `ZimmProductCard` here (rather than composing
`ZimmProductCardMedia` directly, which was seriously considered mid-build) matches it, and avoids a
mismatch to reconcile later if/when SFCC-743 unblocks.

**REWRITTEN 2026-09-06 after reading the real Figma nodes (findings 36-38).** An earlier draft
specced this as "`plp` with two flags flipped", justified partly by PRD §7.5. **That was wrong.** Every
`Product-card` instance in the rail hides its entire `Card-content` block plus `Tag`, `Close` and
`Carousel`, on all three viewports — verified by node metadata *and* a rendered screenshot of
`40000307:12444` (a title row and five bare images, nothing else).

**The rail tile is IMAGE ONLY.** Every flag is off:

| Flag | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `showBadge` | `false` | `Tag` `hidden="true"` on all 3 viewport cards; corroborates Dani, comment 13880 |
| `showHoverImageSwap` | `false` | Dani, comment 13880 |
| `showBag` | **`false`** | `Card-content` `hidden="true"` — no bag anywhere. **Overrides the earlier §7.5/SPR-62 reading — see below.** |
| `showSizeChips` | **`false`** | same |
| `hoverRevealsSizeSelector` | **`false`** | same |
| `hoverHidesPrice` | **n/a** | no price is rendered at all |
| `showAttributes` / `hoverRevealsPrice` / `hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable` | `false` | nothing in `Card-content` renders |
| `showRemove` | `false` | `Close` `hidden="true"` |
| `hideBagOnMobile` | **moot** | there is no bag on any viewport, so the flag never applies. **Open question 7 is closed** — the node was read; the answer is that the whole content block is hidden, not just the icon. |

**New flag required.** `ZimmProductCard` has no way today to suppress `ZimmProductCardContent`
wholesale — name and price render unconditionally. Add one (`showContent: false`) and gate the
`ZimmProductCardContent` render on it. Keep it table-driven like every other flag; **do not** add a
`variation === 'recentlyViewed'` branch (A2's own pass criterion below forbids it).

**Accessibility gap found and closed, 2026-09-07 — not rendering `ZimmProductCardContent` at all
would remove the only real `<a>` this card has.** `ZimmProductCardContent` owns the card's one real
link (the name-link, via `react-router-dom`'s `Link`) — `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own `onClick` is a
plain, mouse-only `<div>` handler with no `tabIndex`/`onKeyDown`. With Content fully unmounted, a
single-image `recentlyViewed` card (no gallery, no remove button, no badge, per the table above)
would have **zero focusable elements at all** — unreachable by keyboard, a real WCAG 2.1.1 violation,
not a style nitpick, and directly contradicts SFCC-83 AC 4 (*"Given a shopper clicks a recently viewed
product tile, then they are navigated to that product's PDP"*).

Two fixes were considered and rejected before landing on the one below:
- Extending `ZimmProductCardContent` itself with a "link-only" render mode — rejected after reading
  its actual source: price is rendered **unconditionally today, by design** (its own docblock: *"Always
  rendered regardless of variation... not this component"*) and there is no existing mechanism to
  suppress the name's visible text either. Doing this properly would mean breaking a stated invariant
  in a second shared, already-heavily-tested component, not a small addition.
- Composing `ZimmProductCardMedia` directly in the rail organism (A5), bypassing `ZimmProductCard`
  entirely — seriously considered mid-build, reversed after the SFCC-236/SFCC-743 ticket evidence
  above confirmed this codebase's established pattern for "labelled row of product cards" is
  composing `ZimmProductCard` instances, not smaller molecules directly.

**Decided fix (Marcel, 2026-09-07):** when `!config.showContent`, don't render
`ZimmProductCardContent` at all (as originally planned) — instead render a small `react-router-dom`
`Link` (matching the exact import `ZimmProductCardContent` itself already uses, `chakra(RouteLink)`)
wrapping *only* `ZimmProductCardMedia`, with the product name as real (not `aria-label`) but
visually-hidden text via Chakra's own `VisuallyHidden` export inside the link — zero new dependency,
zero new CSS utility to build. `ZimmProductCardMedia` gets no `onClick={handleMediaClick}` in this
branch — a real `<Link>` directly containing the image needs no click-passthrough workaround at all
(that mechanism exists purely to route around the *other* variations' invisible stretched-overlay
`<a>`, which doesn't exist here since the link directly wraps the image instead of sitting behind
it). Confined entirely to `zimmProductCard/index.tsx` — no touch to `ZimmProductCardContent` or
`ZimmProductCardMedia`, matching this step's existing file manifest exactly.

**Carousel arrows:** driven by image count in `ZimmProductCardMedia`, not by this table. Pass a
**single** image — AC 3's *"the product's index image"* — and they never appear, matching `Carousel`
`hidden="true"`.

**PRD conflict, adjudicated (Marcel, 2026-09-06): design wins.** `.docs/prd/search.md` §7.5 (SPR-62,
Confirmed) says *"Add to Bag via size variant selection directly from recommendation carousels on PDP
and Cart pages."* The rail shows neither. Rationale for following the design: §7.5's own Open note
says the Add-to-Bag-vs-Wishlist choice is *"pending design refinement"*, and Recently Viewed is §7.4 —
a separate row — so §7.5 arguably never covered this rail. **State the divergence in the PR body for
Jasmijn**; do not treat it as settled doctrine.

**Pass criteria**
- `grep -n 'variation ===\|switch (variation)' index.tsx` still returns zero hits — the extensibility
  AC's mechanism is table-driven and must stay so.
- `index.test.tsx` gains `@ts-expect-error` cases proving the new variation's narrow props type
  rejects `colour`/`size`/`onRemove`, assigning to the **narrow shape, not the union alias** — or the
  excess-property check is vacuous.
- A test asserts no badge renders even when `badge` is passed, and no hover swap even when
  `hoverImage` is passed. **Both must be made to fail on purpose first** (flip the flag, watch it
  fail) before the pass counts.
- **`ZimmProductCardContent` does not render at all for `recentlyViewed`** — assert
  `document.querySelector('[data-card-slot="content"]')` is absent (no name, no price, no bag —
  nothing from that component reaches the DOM).
- **A real, keyboard-reachable link wraps the image, with the product name as its accessible name**
  — `screen.getByRole('link', {name: <product name>})` finds it. Confirm it renders exactly one
  link for this variation (same shape as the existing "exactly one real anchor" test for the other
  three variations), and that it's a real `to={href}` `Link`, not `onClick`-only.
- `ZimmProductCardMedia` receives no `onClick` for this variation — the click-passthrough handler
  exists only to route around the *other* variations' invisible overlay, which this branch has no
  need for. A lingering `onClick` here would be dead, confusing code, not a functional bug — flag it
  as a should-fix if the implementer leaves it in.
- `index.stories.tsx` gains a `RecentlyViewed` named export.
- `hideBagOnMobile` carries an inline comment naming its Figma node.
- `npm run test` passes, including `ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts`.

Test step A2 of the build plan at `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-83+84/plan.md` (search for `### A2 — Add the` for the full spec — read it in full, this prompt summarises but isn't a substitute).

## What was built

`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.tsx` (+ its `index.test.tsx` + `index.stories.tsx`) gained a fourth variation, `recentlyViewed` (SFCC-83's rail tile): every existing `VARIATION_CONFIG` flag is `false`, plus a brand-new `showContent` flag (also `false` only for this variation) that suppresses the composed `ZimmProductCardContent` child entirely. Since that child owns the card's only real link (keyboard-reachable, accessible name = product name), a small replacement `Link` (react-router-dom, wrapping `ZimmProductCardMedia` directly) was added in the `!config.showContent` render branch, with the product name as `VisuallyHidden` text supplying the link's accessible name, and `alt: ''` overridden on the copies of `primaryImage`/`hoverImage` passed to `ZimmProductCardMedia` in that branch only (so the image's own alt text doesn't get redundantly concatenated onto the link's accessible name).

Read the current `index.tsx`, `index.test.tsx`, and `index.stories.tsx` in full before testing anything — don't rely solely on this summary.

## Specific things to independently verify, not just re-read

1. **Redo the fail-first proof yourself, don't trust the implementer's self-report.** Temporarily flip `showBadge: true` on the `recentlyViewed` row in `VARIATION_CONFIG`, run only the badge-suppression test, confirm it actually fails, then revert and confirm the suite is green again. Do the same for `showHoverImageSwap: true`. Report the actual failure output you saw, not just "it failed."
2. **The accessible-name fix.** Confirm the rendered link's accessible name is *exactly* the product name (e.g. `screen.getByRole('link', {name: 'Natura Dress'})` with no partial/regex match needed) — not just that a test asserting this currently passes, but that it would genuinely *fail* if the `alt: ''` override were removed (try removing it locally, confirm the test breaks, put it back).
3. **`grep -n 'variation ===\|switch (variation)' index.tsx`** — confirm zero real hits (the one match should only be the docblock's own self-referential mention of this exact grep command in a comment, not real branching logic).
4. **`ZimmProductCardContent` genuinely does not mount for `recentlyViewed`** — confirm `document.querySelector('[data-card-slot="content"]')` is null even when `currentPrice`/`badge`/other Content-relevant props are supplied (proving they're suppressed, not just never passed).
5. **Keyboard reachability, for real** — render a `recentlyViewed` card and Tab to it; confirm it's reachable and that Enter/Space would activate a real `<a href>` (not a div with a JS handler). Check the rendered DOM's actual `href` attribute value, not just that `to={href}` was passed as a prop.
6. **Click behaviour parity with the other three variations** — for `home`/`plp`/`wishlist`, `handleMediaClick` handles Cmd/Ctrl/Shift/middle-click by bailing out (letting the browser handle it natively via the stretched overlay). For `recentlyViewed`, there's no `handleMediaClick` at all — confirm this doesn't need to exist here: a real anchor already handles all of those modifier/button cases natively with zero JS, so there's nothing to test-and-possibly-regress. Note this in your report rather than treating its absence as a gap.
7. **Type-level enforcement** — confirm assigning `colour`/`size`/`onRemove`/`onAddToBag`/`sizeChipValues` (any PLP/Wishlist-only field) to `ZimmProductCardBaseProps & ZimmProductCardRecentlyViewedVariation` genuinely fails to compile (not just that a `@ts-expect-error` comment exists — confirm it's *needed*, i.e. remove it locally and confirm `tsc` now complains about an unused directive would NOT occur — rather confirm removing the directive causes a real compile error to surface).
8. **`hideBagOnMobile`'s inline comment** cites a real Figma node ID (not a placeholder).
9. **Storybook**: the `RecentlyViewed` story should visually show nothing but a single bare image — no visible name, price, badge, or bag. If you can build/check Storybook, confirm this; if not, confirm the story's own args don't pass anything (`hoverImage`, `badge`, `onAddToBag`, etc.) that would misleadingly imply those apply.
10. **Regression check on the other three variations** — confirm `home`/`plp`/`wishlist` are byte-identical in rendered behaviour to before this change (the `showContent: true` addition to their config rows should be a pure no-op for them). Spot-check by running the existing (pre-A2) test suites for those three and confirming nothing broke — the full `npm run test` run should already show this, but call out specifically if anything in the `home`/`plp`/`wishlist` describe blocks needed any change at all to keep passing (it shouldn't have).

## Gates to run and report real output for

`npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run test`, `npm run lint` (compare against baseline: 26 problems / 5 errors / 21 warnings — report the delta, not just whether it exits 0), `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` (baseline: 2 unacknowledged, both pre-existing in unrelated files — confirm no new ones).

## What NOT to do

Do not fix anything you find — report it. Do not modify any file (you may make temporary local edits to prove a fail-first case as instructed above, but revert every one of them before finishing, and confirm via `git diff`/`git status` that the working tree matches exactly what it was before you started, modulo nothing).

Report findings labelled CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE and UNIFORM/ONE-OFF where relevant, what you tried to falsify and couldn't, and anything you could not verify (say so explicitly rather than staying silent).

input.message:
Independent Tester pass on your A2 work found one real bug and two smaller gaps. All three are closing confirmed gaps against already-established design intent, not new decisions — proceed directly.

**1. Must-fix — confirmed, reproduced bug: the `images` gallery prop isn't sanitized in the `recentlyViewed` branch.** `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own gallery mode activates purely off `images.length > 1`, completely independent of any of this variation's config flags. The Tester proved, with a real render: if `recentlyViewed` ever receives `images` with >1 entries, you get (a) carousel arrow `<button>`s nested inside the wrapping `<Link>` — invalid nested-interactive HTML, (b) a real double-navigation bug — clicking "Next image" bubbles to the ancestor `<Link>` and also fires PDP navigation (confirmed via a mounted `<Route>` marker), and (c) every gallery image's own un-blanked `alt` text concatenating onto the link's accessible name — the exact bug you already fixed for `primaryImage`/`hoverImage`, just multiplied across every slide.

This is currently dormant (nothing shipped calls it this way — A3's mapper is designed to always supply exactly one image), but it's a live gap in this component's exported, extensibility-oriented contract (`images` lives on `ZimmProductCardBaseProps`, unrestricted by variation).

Fix: in the `!config.showContent` branch only, don't forward `images` to `ZimmProductCardMedia` at all — this variation's entire design intent is single-image, so just omit the prop there (Media already defaults to single-image mode with no `images` supplied). Leave the `true` branch (home/plp/wishlist) completely untouched. Add a short comment at the omission citing why (gallery mode must never activate for this variation — nested-interactive HTML + a real double-navigation bug otherwise, found during A2's own Tester pass).

**2. Should-fix — no explicit focus ring on `MediaOnlyCardLink`.** Every other interactive control in this component family (`zimmColourSwatch`, `zimmNavItem`, `zimmSizeChip`, `zimmButton`, Media's own `close`/`arrowButton`, Content's `nameLink`/`bagButton`/`notifyMeButton`) carries an explicit `var(--zimm-focus-ring)`-family rule. This new link relies on the browser's native default outline instead — WCAG 2.4.7 is technically satisfied (nothing strips it), but it's a real, visible inconsistency with the established convention, and your own doc-comment says it copies `ProductNameLink`'s pattern when it only copied the wrap, not the focus styling.

Fix confined to `index.tsx` only — do NOT touch `zimmProductCard.css.ts` (still off-limits per your original brief). Add an inline `sx`/`__css` prop directly on `MediaOnlyCardLink` with a `_focusVisible` rule using the same tokens every other control uses: `outline: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring)'`, `outlineOffset: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)'`. This is a plain Chakra `sx` escape hatch referencing already-registered tokens, not a new recipe part — consistent with `overrideStyling.md`'s styling hierarchy.

feat(ui-kits): add recentlyViewed variation to ZimmProductCard (SFCC-83)

Adds a fourth ZimmProductCard variation for SFCC-83's Recently Viewed rail
tile, table-driven like every other variation (new VARIATION_CONFIG row,
zero variation === branches). Every flag is false: Figma's Card-content,
Tag and Close are all hidden="true" across Desktop/Tablet/Mobile
(40000307:12444 / 40000730:13363 / 40000538:25030) -- the rail tile is
image only, no name, price, badge or bag. An earlier draft of this variation
assumed it could reuse `plp` with two flags flipped, justified by a PRD
line about Add to Bag on recommendation carousels; reading the actual nodes
showed that was wrong, and the PRD line doesn't cover this rail to begin
with (a separate, deliberately-parked conflict for Jasmijn/Dani to ratify).

Went with extending this shared organism rather than composing
ZimmProductCardMedia directly in the rail (seriously considered mid-build):
SFCC-236 lists Recently Viewed as one of its four in-scope variations, and
SFCC-743 (Product Card Group, currently blocked) is explicitly designed to
wrap rows of ProductCard instances -- matching that established pattern now
avoids a mismatch to reconcile later.

Suppressing ZimmProductCardContent wholesale (new showContent flag) removes
this card's only real link -- its name-link is otherwise the sole keyboard-
reachable element, and Media's own onClick is a mouse-only div handler with
no tabIndex/onKeyDown. Fixed with a small react-router Link wrapping Media
directly in this one branch only, product name as VisuallyHidden text
supplying the accessible name, alt overridden to '' on the image copies
passed through so the image's own alt doesn't concatenate onto that name,
and an explicit focus ring matching every other interactive control in this
component family. Confined entirely to this file -- no change to
ZimmProductCardContent or ZimmProductCardMedia.

Live testing during this step's own review found the images gallery prop
wasn't sanitized the same way as primaryImage/hoverImage: ZimmProductCardMedia
activates gallery mode purely off images.length > 1, independent of any
config flag, so a multi-image card here would have nested carousel buttons
inside the wrapping Link and a real double-navigation bug (a click on
"Next image" bubbling up and also firing the Link's own PDP navigation).
Currently dormant -- nothing shipped calls it this way -- but closed anyway
by never forwarding images in this branch at all, matching the variation's
own single-image design intent.

Visually confirmed against Storybook's new RecentlyViewed story: image
only at all three breakpoints, focus ring appears correctly on keyboard Tab.
EOF
