Execute step A3 of the build plan at `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-83+84/plan.md` — read that file's A3 section (search for `### A3 — Card mapper utility`) in full; this prompt gives you precise, pre-researched decisions the plan itself leaves more open, so follow this prompt's specifics where it's more concrete than the plan text.

## Files to create (only these two)

- `overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedCard.ts`
- `overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedCard.test.ts`

## Required reading before writing anything

1. `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/productInfo.ts` — the established house pattern for this exact kind of mapper (injected `FormatPrice`, no React/react-intl, real SDK types where they exist, hand-rolled narrow types only for genuinely-unexported shapes with a why-comment). Mirror its conventions closely.
2. Read (via `git show feature/zimmproductcard-live-demo:overrides/app/pages/home/liveProductCardDemoMapper.ts` — do NOT check out that branch, do NOT import from it, it's on a different branch and doesn't exist here) the prior-art demo mapper for the general shape of this kind of transform (alt-never-empty fallback, image-group filtering, no-currency-no-guess price handling). That file deliberately hand-rolled types because it's throwaway-demo scope — yours is production scope, so you must use real SDK types instead where `productInfo.ts` shows they exist (see below).
3. `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-einstein.js` — read `fetchRecProductDetails` (search for that name) to see the *exact* real input shape this mapper receives, already merged: `{...rec, ...product, productId: rec.id, image: {disBaseLink: rec.imageUrl, alt: rec.productName}}`. `product` here is a real Commerce API product resource fetched via `getProducts` with `expand: ['availability','links','promotions','options','images','prices','variations']`.

## The real SDK type to import (already verified present)

`commerce-sdk-isomorphic` exports `ShopperProductsTypes.Product` (and `.ImageGroup`, `.Image`) — confirmed directly in `node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.esm.d.ts`. Relevant fields on `Product`: `id: string` (required), `name?: string`, `price?: number`, `currency?: string`, `imageGroups?: Array<ImageGroup>`. `ImageGroup = {images: Array<Image>, variationAttributes?, viewType: string}`. `Image = {alt?: string, disBaseLink?: string, link: string (required), title?: string}`.

Import this type directly (`import type {ShopperProductsTypes} from 'commerce-sdk-isomorphic'`) — do not hand-roll a duplicate `Product`/`ImageGroup`/`Image` shape. The *only* genuinely-unexported extra fields are the two `fetchRecProductDetails` bolts on: `productId` and the singular `image`. Model the mapper's input type as:

```ts
type RecentlyViewedProduct = ShopperProductsTypes.Product & {
  /** Set by use-einstein.js's fetchRecProductDetails to rec.id. Guaranteed present and equal to
   *  Product.id for every entry that function produces (it already filters out any rec with no
   *  matching product before this shape exists at all) — read this rather than `.id` only
   *  because it's the field the real runtime hook explicitly produces this way. */
  productId: string;
  /** Same function's own quick single-reference image (Einstein's own rec.imageUrl/rec.productName),
   *  distinct from the full product's own `imageGroups` array below — used as a fallback only
   *  when imageGroups filtering comes up empty (see the mapper's own image-selection logic). */
  image?: { disBaseLink?: string; alt?: string };
};
```

## Image selection — a specific, verified decision, not a guess

Prefer `filterImageGroups(product.imageGroups, {viewType: 'medium', variationValues: {}})` (real signature confirmed in `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/product-utils.js` — `(imageGroups = [], filters) => ...`, filters by `viewType` and optionally one `variationValues` attribute/value pair; pass an empty `variationValues` object since a Recently Viewed rec is already one specific product, not a search hit needing a variant pick like the demo mapper's `resolveDemoVariant` — do not port that variant-picking logic, it doesn't apply here) — take `[0]?.images` from the filtered result. **Fall back to the top-level `image: {disBaseLink, alt}` field** (built via a synthetic single-entry array) only if `imageGroups` filtering produces nothing usable. This reconciles the plan's two seemingly-different instructions (reuse `filterImageGroups`, *and* the input includes a flat `image` field) — the flat field is Einstein's own convenience shape and the correct fallback, not the primary source, per `AGENTS.md`'s image-sizing guidance (never serve a full-resolution/arbitrary-sized image at thumbnail size — `filterImageGroups` with `viewType: 'medium'` gets a properly-sized image; Einstein's raw `imageUrl` might be sized for anything).

Per SFCC-83 AC 3 ("the product's index image" — singular), only ever return **one** image (`primaryImage`), never `hoverImage`/`images` — those two fields should always be `undefined`/omitted from this mapper's return shape entirely (not just empty). Don't port the demo mapper's multi-image/hover-image logic; it doesn't apply here at all.

`ZimmProductCardMediaImage.alt` (imported type) is required and must be non-empty. Mirror the demo mapper's own fallback exactly: `img.alt?.trim() || product.name` (no colour suffix needed here — this variation doesn't render an attributes line anyway, and there's no confirmed colour/variant context for this specific product the way the demo mapper had one).

## href — verified against the already-shipping precedent, not guessed

`overrides/app/components/product-tile/index.jsx` (wait — check the REAL base file, not an override: `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-tile/index.jsx`) — confirmed it builds its own PDP link via bare `productUrlBuilder({id: productId})` (`app/utils/url`), with **no manual site-prefixing of its own**. This is the exact same context (a product tile inside a recommendation rail) already shipping correctly in production across the other five/six unrelated rails today. Match this precedent exactly: `productUrlBuilder({id: product.productId})`, no site-prefix logic of your own to invent.

## Price — deliberately narrow scope, state it as a decision not an omission

Map `currentPrice` only (via the injected `formatPrice(product.price, product.currency)`, skipping formatting entirely — returning `undefined` — when either is missing/not a number, matching `productInfo.ts`'s own "no hardcoded fallback currency" comment). **Do not attempt was/now sale-price detection** (no `originalPrice`) — that requires `getPriceData`-style pricebook logic `productInfo.ts` sources from a separate, more elaborate utility this merged Einstein shape doesn't have available; the plan's own A3 pass criteria never asks for it, only for "price without currency" handling. State this as a deliberate scope decision in the module's own docblock (one sentence, matching this file's established documentation culture — see `productInfo.ts` for the tone), not a silent gap.

## `name` — required, and it matters even though A2's variation never visually shows it

Return `null` for the whole mapping when `product.name` is missing (same "no productName, no usable card" gate the demo mapper uses, just off the real SDK field name — it's `name`, not `productName`; `rec.productName` is Einstein's own separate, likely-redundant copy and should NOT be preferred over the SDK's own authoritative field — the upstream hook's own filter step already guarantees a real matched product exists for every surviving rec, so `product.name` should always be populated in practice, but guard for it anyway per this mapper's own null-safety contract). /**
 * Maps one Recently Viewed recommendation onto the subset of `ZimmProductCard` props the
 * `recentlyViewed` variation (SFCC-83) actually renders.
 * ...
 */
import type { ShopperProductsTypes } from 'commerce-sdk-isomorphic';
import { filterImageGroups } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/product-utils';
import { productUrlBuilder } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/url';
import type { ZimmProductCardBaseProps, ZimmProductCardImage } from '../components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard';

export type RecentlyViewedProduct = ShopperProductsTypes.Product & {
  productId: string;
  image?: { disBaseLink?: string; alt?: string };
};

export type FormatPrice = (amount: number, currency: string) => string;

export type RecentlyViewedCard = Pick<
  ZimmProductCardBaseProps,
  'id' | 'href' | 'name' | 'primaryImage' | 'currentPrice'
>;

const MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE = 'medium';

const selectPrimaryImage = (product: RecentlyViewedProduct, productName: string): ZimmProductCardImage | null => {
  const filteredGroups = filterImageGroups(product.imageGroups ?? [], {
    viewType: MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE,
    variationValues: {},
  }) as ShopperProductsTypes.ImageGroup[];
  const [groupImage] = filteredGroups[0]?.images ?? [];

  const src = groupImage ? groupImage.disBaseLink || groupImage.link : product.image?.disBaseLink;
  if (!src) return null;

  const alt = (groupImage ? groupImage.alt : product.image?.alt)?.trim() || productName;
  return { src, alt };
};

export const selectRecentlyViewedCard = (
  product: RecentlyViewedProduct | undefined | null,
  formatPrice: FormatPrice,
): RecentlyViewedCard | null => {
  if (!product?.name) return null;

  const primaryImage = selectPrimaryImage(product, product.name);
  if (!primaryImage) return null;

  return {
    id: product.productId,
    href: productUrlBuilder({ id: product.productId }),
    name: product.name,
    primaryImage,
    currentPrice:
      typeof product.price === 'number' && product.currency ? formatPrice(product.price, product.currency) : undefined,
  };
};
```

name: feedback_build_pace_overtesting
description: Marcel corrected excessive per-step Tester/Scorer agent overhead during zimmerMANNBuild loop execution — verify directly, don't ritually spin up exhaustive sub-agent audits
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

During `zimmerMANNBuild` (or any similar multi-agent implement→test→score loop), don't treat "this step gets the full loop" as license to dispatch a maximally exhaustive Tester agent every time — especially not one that itself spins up 4+ of its own sub-agents and runs 20-30 minutes per step. Verify the plan's own stated pass criteria directly first (tsc/test/lint/grep/read the diff — usually 5-10 concrete, fast checks). Only dispatch a separate Tester/Scorer agent for a piece of logic with real, specific ambiguity or risk — not as a blanket per-step ritual just because the plan's loop-configuration table says "full loop."

**Why:** Marcel said mid-build (SFCC-83/84, 2026-09-07): *"the build is taking too long... we have 20+ mins running tests, and this is not even the full implementation/feature test... can't we just run the actual tests that we need, not overthink, and do more building than testing?"* This was a direct correction after A1/A2 each burned through multiple full agent rounds (implementer → tester → rework → scorer, sometimes with the tester itself fanning out 4 parallel sub-agents) totaling well over an hour combined for what the plan itself explicitly scoped as a "mid-size build" of ~22 files. The skill's own instructions already say *"Scale to the work... over-scaled machinery is a defect, not thoroughness"* — I wasn't actually honoring that in practice, even though I was technically following the plan's textual "full loop" assignment per step. "Full loop" describes which roles are involved, not a mandate that the Tester role itself be maximally thorough every single time regardless of actual risk.

**How to apply:** Default to self-verification against the plan's stated pass criteria. Reserve a dedicated Tester/Scorer dispatch for genuinely high-risk or subtle logic the implementer itself flagged as uncertain — not as an automatic step. When about to dispatch a verification agent, ask first: "is this the actual test we need, or padding?" Applies to `zimmerMANNBuild` specifically, but the principle (verification effort should scale to real risk, not to a rote process checklist) generalizes to any multi-agent build/review loop on this project.

1	# SFCC-236: fix two live-testing regressions in ZimmProductCard
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	While testing PR #85 (`feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component`) live, Marcel found two
6	real bugs in the shared `ZimmProductCard` family:
7	
8	**(a) A recent hover-reveal fix broke keyboard nav and VoiceOver.** The most recent fix on this
9	branch (`983bddf`) replaced `:focus-within` with `:has(:focus-visible)` across five hover-reveal
10	sites, specifically to stop the carousel arrows (and everything else gated the same way) from
11	staying visible after a mouse click even once the mouse moved away — a real, correctly-diagnosed
12	bug, and that part of the fix is not being reverted. The regression is elsewhere: every one of
13	those five reveals uses `display: 'none'` as its "hidden" state, gated behind an *interaction*
14	heuristic (`:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)`). `display: none` unconditionally strips an element
15	from the accessibility tree — it answers "is this painted," not "does this exist for assistive
16	tech," and this recipe has been using it to answer both questions at once. `:focus-visible` is
17	itself a browser heuristic for "does this focus event look keyboard-like," and VoiceOver-driven
18	focus (VO+Arrow, rotor, swipe) is not guaranteed to satisfy it in every engine — a real, documented
19	mismatch, and *not* a touch-only concern: `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` is true on any Mac
20	trackpad, so a VoiceOver user on ordinary MacBook hardware is exactly the population this gate
21	applies to. If that heuristic never matches for a given user, all five reveals (carousel arrows,
22	Home's price reveal, PLP/Wishlist's price↔size-selector swap, notify-me) stay invisible to them
23	for the entire session, no matter how they navigate. A secondary, lower-severity effect confirmed
24	alongside it: because these controls only exist as Tab stops *while* the interaction condition is
25	currently true, Shift+Tab entry into the card from something after it lands on the last
26	unconditionally-visible stop (the bag button) — the user has already tabbed past controls that,
27	at that instant, didn't exist yet, and must reverse direction to reach them. (Forward-Tab is fine:
28	landing on the always-present scroll container triggers the reveal before reaching the arrows.)
29	
30	**(b) Multi-image cards don't respond to touch swipe on mobile.** The slide indicator renders
31	correctly (so the image data and gallery logic are fine), but swiping the image doesn't page
32	through it at all. Root cause: the organism's whole-card stretched-link overlay
33	(`[data-card-slot="content"] a::after`, `position: absolute; inset: 0`) resolves its containing
34	block to the organism root — because `ZimmProductCardContent` never sets `position` anywhere —
35	so it's sized to the *entire* card, image included, not just the name-link row. That overlay
36	carries no `z-index`, and the recipe already lifts exactly three things above it (`close`,
37	`carousel`, buttons inside `content`) — the media/gallery scroll region was never added to that
38	list. A touch swipe on the image actually starts on the invisible overlay `<a>`, so the browser's
39	native swipe-scroll gesture never engages the real scroll container at all.
40	
41	Both root causes were confirmed via direct investigation of this exact code (file/line citations
42	below) before any fix was designed, and both fixes reuse patterns already shipped elsewhere in
43	this same codebase rather than inventing anything new — `ZimmColourSwatchGroup`'s already-tested
44	off-page-swatch technique for (a), and this recipe's own existing z-index-lift pattern for (b).
45	
46	## Fix (b) — swipe blocked by the stretched-link overlay
47	
48	**File:** `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/zimmProductCard.css.ts`
49	
50	- Add a fourth lift entry alongside the existing three (currently lines 240-253):
51	  ```
52	  [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.media}"]`]: { zIndex: 1 },
53	  ```
54	  `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own root is already `position: 'relative'` (its own recipe), so only
55	  `zIndex` is needed here — identical in shape to the existing `close`/`carousel` entries.
56	- Extend docblock point 2 (the "lifting every interactive control" explanation, ~lines 62-101)
57	  with a new dated fix note, continuing this file's own Fix 1/Fix 3/Fix H lettered convention,
58	  explaining the media/gallery region needed the same lift the click targets already got, and
59	  that this was missed because clicking `close`/`carousel`/content-buttons was checked live but
60	  swiping the image itself never was.
61	- Extend `index.test.tsx`'s existing z-index-lift describe block (or add a sibling one) to assert
62	  the new entry's object shape, matching that file's own established idiom for these proofs.
63	
64	**Verification:** jsdom cannot prove this (no stacking-context resolution — this file's own
65	"KNOWN LIMITATION" docblock already says so). Needs a real touch check: Playwright's
66	`mobile-chrome` project with a real drag/swipe gesture on the image, or Marcel's own device,
67	confirming the gallery pages and the indicator updates.
68	
69	## Fix (a) — hover-reveal content invisible to VoiceOver / skipped on Shift+Tab
70	
71	**Files:** `zimmProductCard.css.ts` (all 5 reveal sites) and
72	`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`
73	(carousel's own base state)
74	
75	**Recommended fix** — keep every one of the five reveal targets permanently present in the DOM,
76	focusable, and in the accessibility tree at all times. Stop using `display` to express "hidden";
77	use the exact technique `ZimmColourSwatchGroup` already ships for its own off-page swatches
78	(confirmed real, `molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx:215`:
79	`{ position: 'absolute', clipPath: 'inset(50%)' }`):
80	
81	- **Hidden (default) state:** `position: 'absolute'`, `clipPath: 'inset(50%)'` instead of
82	  `display: 'none'` — out of flow (no layout gap, same as today), paints nothing, but stays in
83	  the DOM/tab order/accessibility tree.
84	- **Revealed state** (same `&:hover [...]` / `&:has(:focus-visible) [...]` selectors, byte-for-byte
85	  unchanged): `position: 'static'`, `clipPath: 'none'` instead of `display: 'block'/'flex'`.
86	- Applies at all 5 sites in `zimmProductCard.css.ts`: Home price reveal (~293-297, 323-325),
87	  PLP/Wishlist price hide (~330-332, 338-340), PLP/Wishlist size-selector reveal (~344-346,
88	  348-350), notify-me reveal (~359-362, 364-366), carousel arrow reveal (~379-384).
89	- `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s `carousel` part: its own unconditional base `display: 'none'`
90	  becomes the same clip-path equivalent (already `position: 'absolute'` unconditionally, so only
91	  the hidden-state property changes).
92	- **Carousel-specific addition:** the wrapper deliberately sets `pointerEvents: 'none'` with each
93	  `arrowButton` individually re-enabling `pointerEvents: 'auto'` (so clicks in the empty centre
94	  pass through to the image). Once the wrapper is no longer `display:none`, add an explicit
95	  belt-and-braces rule in the organism recipe — `[data-card-slot="carousel"] button` gets
96	  `pointerEvents: 'none'` by default and `'auto'` only in the two revealed selectors — rather than
97	  relying on clip-path's hit-testing suppression alone. (Price/size-selector/notify-me need no
98	  equivalent — none of them sets `pointerEvents` at all today.)
99	
100	**Why this is the recommended path, not one of several open options** (a JS-tracked hover/focus
101	state was considered and rejected): there is no signal exposed to page-level JavaScript, any more
102	than to CSS, that says "this focus event was AT-originated." A hand-rolled heuristic (e.g.
103	flagging `focusin` as non-keyboard when preceded by `pointerdown`) has exactly the same blind spot
104	as the native `:focus-visible` heuristic it would be reimplementing. It would also break this
105	organism's own stated design principle ("CSS alone decides what is visible... no JS-tracked reveal
106	state," `index.tsx` ~349-350) and introduce real SSR/hydration-mismatch risk pure CSS structurally
107	can't have, for no correctness gain.
108	
109	**Why this doesn't reintroduce the `983bddf` stuck-open bug:** that bug was entirely about *when*
110	`:has(:focus-visible)` matches (a click-focused button not un-matching on mouseout until focus
111	moved elsewhere) — a selector-matching-timing question, completely orthogonal to which property
112	the matched rule sets. The trigger selectors aren't touched at all; only the property values
113	inside the already-existing blocks change.
114	
115	**Docblock updates:** extend/rewrite docblock points 3 and 6 and the "Fix H" note with a new dated
116	fix note (continuing the lettered sequence), stating explicitly that Fix H's `:focus-within` →
117	`:has(:focus-visible)` swap was and remains correct for the paint-timing question it solved, and
118	that the actual defect was using `display` (an AT-tree-removal property) to answer a different
119	question than the one it should answer. Explicitly out of scope, left as `display:none`: the
120	permanent, non-hover-capable-pointer hides (`sizeSelectorUnavailable`'s unconditional size-chip
121	hide, the PLP-mobile bag-icon hide) — separate, correct, Figma-confirmed, non-regressed decisions,
122	since nothing about them is gated behind an interaction heuristic.
123	
124	**Test updates:** the existing `.matches()`-based selector-proof describe block in
125	`index.test.tsx` needs no change (it doesn't depend on which property the matched rule sets). Any
126	structural/object-shape assertions elsewhere in the same file checking the recipe's declared
127	`display` values for these 5 sites need updating to the new property values — identify the exact
128	assertions at implementation time against the real current file, don't guess line numbers here.
129	
130	**New real-browser verification** (jsdom can't prove any of this): this repo already has
131	scaffolded-but-empty Playwright a11y projects (`playwright.config.js`'s `a11y-desktop` →
132	`e2e/tests/a11y/desktop`, `a11y-mobile` → `e2e/tests/a11y/mobile`; both Chromium-only, no WebKit
133	project configured — not touching `playwright.config.js` itself, only adding specs inside the
134	already-existing target directories). Add specs for:
135	
136	1. **Accessibility-tree presence** — load a card in its default (non-hovered, non-focused) state
137	   and assert, via a real Chromium accessibility-tree snapshot, that the size-chip radiogroup,
138	   notify-me button, and carousel arrow buttons are present with correct role/name — proving
139	   AT-tree presence no longer depends on any hover/focus-visible condition having matched.
140	2. **Tab-order parity** — forward-Tab from before the card and Shift+Tab from after it, asserting
141	   the stop set/sequence is now identical in both directions (today Shift+Tab skips the
142	   reveal-gated controls entirely).
143	3. **No regression on the original stuck-open bug** — real mouse click on an arrow button, move
144	   the mouse off the card, assert the control is no longer visually painted by reading
145	   `getComputedStyle(el).clipPath` directly (Playwright's default `toBeVisible()` is primarily a
146	   bounding-box/`visibility` check and may not reliably catch clip-path-based hiding).
147	
148	**Honest limitation, not skippable:** the actual disputed claim — does real VoiceOver announce and
149	activate these controls — can't be fully closed out by any automated check above. Chromium's
150	accessibility tree isn't the engine VoiceOver actually talks to (WebKit), no WebKit Playwright
151	project exists in this repo, and Playwright can't drive real VoiceOver at all. The automated specs
152	give strong, real regression-prevention signal (AT-tree presence + tab-order parity are both real,
153	previously-uncaught bugs), but final confirmation needs one manual pass from Marcel: navigate a
154	card via VO+Right-Arrow/rotor only (no mouse, no literal Tab keypress) on real macOS Safari +
155	VoiceOver, confirming price, the size-chip radiogroup, notify-me, and the carousel arrows are all
156	announced and activatable via VO+Space.
157	
158	## Verification (both fixes)
159	
160	1. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
161	2. Full local Storybook build + `test-storybook --ci` — same pattern used earlier on this branch
162	   for the axe-contrast fix; confirms no regression across the whole story set.
163	3. Updated/new Vitest assertions in both `index.test.tsx` files pass.
164	4. New Playwright a11y specs (AT-tree presence, tab-order parity, stuck-open non-regression) pass.
165	5. Real-device/manual checks, both required before calling this done:
166	   - Real touch swipe (device or Playwright mobile-chrome touch simulation) confirms gallery
167	     paging works.
168	   - Real VoiceOver + Safari pass (Marcel, one-time) confirms AT reachability/activation for all
169	     five previously-broken controls.
170	
171	## Files touched
172	
173	All within one protection tier — squad-owned `ui-kits` component recipes/tests, no Tier 1/2 file:
174	
175	- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/zimmProductCard.css.ts`
176	- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.test.tsx`

  explaining the media/gallery region needed the same lift the click targets already got, and
  that this was missed because clicking `close`/`carousel`/content-buttons was checked live but
  swiping the image itself never was.
- Extend `index.test.tsx`'s existing z-index-lift describe block (or add a sibling one) to assert
  the new entry's object shape, matching that file's own established idiom for these proofs.

**Verification:** jsdom cannot prove this (no stacking-context resolution — this file's own
"KNOWN LIMITATION" docblock already says so). Needs a real touch check: Playwright's
`mobile-chrome` project with a real drag/swipe gesture on the image, or Marcel's own device,
confirming the gallery pages and the indicator updates.

## Fix (a) — hover-reveal content invisible to VoiceOver / skipped on Shift+Tab

**Files:** `zimmProductCard.css.ts` (all 5 reveal sites) and
`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`
(carousel's own base state)

**Recommended fix** — keep every one of the five reveal targets permanently present in the DOM,
focusable, and in the accessibility tree at all times. Stop using `display` to express "hidden";
use the exact technique `ZimmColourSwatchGroup` already ships for its own off-page swatches
(confirmed real, `molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx:215`:
`{ position: 'absolute', clipPath: 'inset(50%)' }`):

- **Hidden (default) state:** `position: 'absolute'`, `clipPath: 'inset(50%)'` instead of
  `display: 'none'` — out of flow (no layout gap, same as today), paints nothing, but stays in
  the DOM/tab order/accessibility tree.
- **Revealed state** (same `&:hover [...]` / `&:has(:focus-visible) [...]` selectors, byte-for-byte
  unchanged): `position: 'static'`, `clipPath: 'none'` instead of `display: 'block'/'flex'`.
- Applies at all 5 sites in `zimmProductCard.css.ts`: Home price reveal (~293-297, 323-325),
  PLP/Wishlist price hide (~330-332, 338-340), PLP/Wishlist size-selector reveal (~344-346,
  348-350), notify-me reveal (~359-362, 364-366), carousel arrow reveal (~379-384).
- `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s `carousel` part: its own unconditional base `display: 'none'`
  becomes the same clip-path equivalent (already `position: 'absolute'` unconditionally, so only
  the hidden-state property changes).
- **Carousel-specific addition:** the wrapper deliberately sets `pointerEvents: 'none'` with each
  `arrowButton` individually re-enabling `pointerEvents: 'auto'` (so clicks in the empty centre
  pass through to the image). Once the wrapper is no longer `display:none`, add an explicit
  belt-and-braces rule in the organism recipe — `[data-card-slot="carousel"] button` gets
  `pointerEvents: 'none'` by default and `'auto'` only in the two revealed selectors — rather than
  relying on clip-path's hit-testing suppression alone. (Price/size-selector/notify-me need no
  equivalent — none of them sets `pointerEvents` at all today.)

**Why this is the recommended path, not one of several open options** (a JS-tracked hover/focus
state was considered and rejected): there is no signal exposed to page-level JavaScript, any more
than to CSS, that says "this focus event was AT-originated." A hand-rolled heuristic (e.g.
flagging `focusin` as non-keyboard when preceded by `pointerdown`) has exactly the same blind spot
as the native `:focus-visible` heuristic it would be reimplementing. It would also break this
organism's own stated design principle ("CSS alone decides what is visible... no JS-tracked reveal
state," `index.tsx` ~349-350) and introduce real SSR/hydration-mismatch risk pure CSS structurally
can't have, for no correctness gain.

**Why this doesn't reintroduce the `983bddf` stuck-open bug:** that bug was entirely about *when*
`:has(:focus-visible)` matches (a click-focused button not un-matching on mouseout until focus
moved elsewhere) — a selector-matching-timing question, completely orthogonal to which property
the matched rule sets. The trigger selectors aren't touched at all; only the property values
inside the already-existing blocks change.

**Docblock updates:** extend/rewrite docblock points 3 and 6 and the "Fix H" note with a new dated
fix note (continuing the lettered sequence), stating explicitly that Fix H's `:focus-within` →
`:has(:focus-visible)` swap was and remains correct for the paint-timing question it solved, and
that the actual defect was using `display` (an AT-tree-removal property) to answer a different
question than the one it should answer. Explicitly out of scope, left as `display:none`: the
permanent, non-hover-capable-pointer hides (`sizeSelectorUnavailable`'s unconditional size-chip
hide, the PLP-mobile bag-icon hide) — separate, correct, Figma-confirmed, non-regressed decisions,
since nothing about them is gated behind an interaction heuristic.

**Test updates:** the existing `.matches()`-based selector-proof describe block in
`index.test.tsx` needs no change (it doesn't depend on which property the matched rule sets). Any
structural/object-shape assertions elsewhere in the same file checking the recipe's declared
`display` values for these 5 sites need updating to the new property values — identify the exact
assertions at implementation time against the real current file, don't guess line numbers here.

**New real-browser verification** (jsdom can't prove any of this): this repo already has
scaffolded-but-empty Playwright a11y projects (`playwright.config.js`'s `a11y-desktop` →
`e2e/tests/a11y/desktop`, `a11y-mobile` → `e2e/tests/a11y/mobile`; both Chromium-only, no WebKit
project configured — not touching `playwright.config.js` itself, only adding specs inside the
already-existing target directories). Add specs for:

1. **Accessibility-tree presence** — load a card in its default (non-hovered, non-focused) state
   and assert, via a real Chromium accessibility-tree snapshot, that the size-chip radiogroup,
   notify-me button, and carousel arrow buttons are present with correct role/name — proving
   AT-tree presence no longer depends on any hover/focus-visible condition having matched.
2. **Tab-order parity** — forward-Tab from before the card and Shift+Tab from after it, asserting
   the stop set/sequence is now identical in both directions (today Shift+Tab skips the
   reveal-gated controls entirely).
3. **No regression on the original stuck-open bug** — real mouse click on an arrow button, move
   the mouse off the card, assert the control is no longer visually painted by reading
   `getComputedStyle(el).clipPath` directly (Playwright's default `toBeVisible()` is primarily a
   bounding-box/`visibility` check and may not reliably catch clip-path-based hiding).

**Honest limitation, not skippable:** the actual disputed claim — does real VoiceOver announce and
activate these controls — can't be fully closed out by any automated check above. Chromium's
accessibility tree isn't the engine VoiceOver actually talks to (WebKit), no WebKit Playwright
project exists in this repo, and Playwright can't drive real VoiceOver at all. The automated specs
give strong, real regression-prevention signal (AT-tree presence + tab-order parity are both real,
previously-uncaught bugs), but final confirmation needs one manual pass from Marcel: navigate a
card via VO+Right-Arrow/rotor only (no mouse, no literal Tab keypress) on real macOS Safari +
VoiceOver, confirming price, the size-chip radiogroup, notify-me, and the carousel arrows are all
announced and activatable via VO+Space.

2. Full local Storybook build + `test-storybook --ci` — same pattern used earlier on this branch
   for the axe-contrast fix; confirms no regression across the whole story set.
3. Updated/new Vitest assertions in both `index.test.tsx` files pass.
4. New Playwright a11y specs (AT-tree presence, tab-order parity, stuck-open non-regression) pass.
5. Real-device/manual checks, both required before calling this done:

     paging works.
   - Real VoiceOver + Safari pass (Marcel, one-time) confirms AT reachability/activation for all
     five previously-broken controls.

All within one protection tier — squad-owned `ui-kits` component recipes/tests, no Tier 1/2 file:

- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.test.tsx`

## Files to touch

- CREATE `overrides/app/hooks/useRecentlyViewedGate.ts`
- CREATE `overrides/app/hooks/useRecentlyViewedGate.test.ts`
- MODIFY `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` — **exactly two lines added, nothing else changes.** This file is Tier 3 (CODEOWNERS: `pwa-squad-b`); do not touch anything beyond the two lines specified below.

## Why this hook exists (context, don't re-derive it)

Einstein's `viewed-recently-einstein` recommender returns a persistent baseline for a visitor with zero real history, so `recs.length === 0` never fires — AC 8 (empty state: no rail when nothing's been viewed) can't be implemented from the API response alone. The gate is a local boolean, not a read of Einstein's own list: `hasRecentlyViewed = sessionFlagIsSet || isRegistered`.

## The hook's shape

```ts
export const useRecentlyViewedGate = (): boolean => { ... }
export const markProductViewed = (): void => { ... }
```

- `markProductViewed()`: writes a session-scoped flag (a fixed key — name it something like `zimm-recently-viewed`, exported as a named constant, not a magic string repeated in two places) to `sessionStorage`. Wrap in `try/catch` — Safari private-browsing mode throws on `sessionStorage` access. On throw, this function does nothing (no flag gets set) rather than throwing further.
- `useRecentlyViewedGate()`: returns `hasRecentlyViewed: boolean`.
  - `isRegistered` comes from `useCustomerType()`, imported from `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` — confirmed real, already used exactly this way at `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-einstein.js:449` (`const {isRegistered} = useCustomerType()`).
  - **SSR-safe, no hydration mismatch:** initial state must be `false`, resolved inside a `useEffect` — never read `sessionStorage` during render. The rail this gates doesn't exist on first paint and appears after hydration (it also sits inside `<Island hydrateOn='visible'>` on the PDP, so this is consistent with how that page already defers non-critical content).
  - Read the session flag inside the same `try/catch` guard as `markProductViewed` — a throw there also degrades to `false` (no rail), never an uncaught exception.
  - The effect should re-resolve when `isRegistered` changes (include it in the dependency array) — a shopper who logs in mid-session should immediately see `hasRecentlyViewed` flip to `true` without needing a fresh page load.
  - JSDoc with an explicit `@returns` description (`.claude/rules/components.md`'s hook convention).

## The PDP change — exactly two lines, nothing else moves

Read `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` around lines 772-802 yourself first — the existing Einstein `useEffect` is:

```tsx
useEffect(() => {
  if (product && product.type.set) {
    einstein.sendViewProduct(product);
    ... (unchanged, existing code)
  } else if (product) {
    einstein.sendViewProduct(product);
    ... (unchanged, existing code)
  }
}, [product]);
```

Add:
1. **One import line** near this file's existing hook imports (match its current import grouping/style — don't reorder or reformat anything else in the import block): `import { markProductViewed } from '../../hooks/useRecentlyViewedGate';` (confirm the exact relative path from this file's actual location).
2. **One call line**, as a *new, standalone* statement inside the existing `useEffect` body — either immediately before the existing `if (product && product.type.set) {` line or immediately after the closing `}` of the existing `else if (product) {...}` block (your choice, whichever reads more naturally, but do not merge it into either existing branch or restructure the if/else-if chain in any way): `if (product) markProductViewed();`

This fires once per real product view (set or plain — "a shopper viewed a product" is the same signal either way, whether it's a set with children or a single item), guarded by the exact same truthiness check the existing branches already use, without touching a single character of the existing branches themselves. Do not add braces/multi-line formatting to this new line if the file's existing style elsewhere uses single-line guarded statements without braces — match whatever's actually idiomatic in this specific file; if genuinely ambiguous, a single-line `if (product) markProductViewed();` with no braces is the safest minimal choice.

**Verify after:** `git diff overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` should show exactly 2 added lines (`+`) and zero removed/changed lines (`-`) anywhere in the file.

## Tests (`useRecentlyViewedGate.test.ts`)

Per the plan's own pass criteria, and make each fail on purpose first (flip/break the implementation locally, confirm the test fails with real output, then restore and confirm green — this project's standing bar, not optional):

- No flag set, guest (`isRegistered: false`) → `false`.
- Flag set (call `markProductViewed()` first, or seed `sessionStorage` directly), guest → `true`.
- No flag set, registered (`isRegistered: true`) → `true`.
- `sessionStorage` throwing (mock it to throw on `getItem`/`setItem`) → `false`, no uncaught exception.
- First render, before the effect has run → `false` (this is the SSR-safety proof — assert the hook's return value synchronously on initial render, before `act()`/effect flush).

You'll need to mock/stub `useCustomerType` from `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` (`vi.mock`) to control `isRegistered` per test case, and mock/stub or directly manipulate `window.sessionStorage` for the flag-state and throwing cases. Use `@testing-library/react`'s `renderHook` (already a dependency in this repo — confirm via existing hook test files for the exact import path/pattern this codebase already uses, e.g. `overrides/app/hooks/useCountryConfig.test.ts` or similar, don't guess).

## Pass criteria

- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
- `npm run test` green, including the new test file.
- `npm run lint` — check the baseline first (currently 26 problems / 5 errors / 21 warnings), confirm zero new after your changes.
- `git diff overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` shows exactly 2 added lines, 0 removed/changed.
- No `sessionStorage` access outside a `try/catch` or outside a `useEffect`.
- Every one of the 5 test cases was made to fail first, then fixed — report the real failure output for each, not just "it failed."

## Scope boundary

Only the three files named above. Do not touch anything else in `product-detail/index.tsx` beyond the two specified lines — if you find yourself wanting to change more, stop and report why instead. Do not stage or commit — the orchestrating skill handles that.

When done, report: final file contents, the exact PDP diff, and real command output for every pass criterion.

During `zimmerMANNBuild` (or any similar multi-agent implement→test→score loop), don't treat "this step gets the full loop" as license to dispatch a maximally exhaustive Tester agent every time — especially not one that itself spins up 4+ of its own sub-agents and runs 20-30 minutes per step. Verify the plan's own stated pass criteria directly first (tsc/test/lint/grep/read the diff — usually 5-10 concrete, fast checks). Only dispatch a separate Tester/Scorer agent for a piece of logic with real, specific ambiguity or risk — not as a blanket per-step ritual just because the plan's loop-configuration table says "full loop."

**Why:** Marcel said mid-build (SFCC-83/84, 2026-09-07): *"the build is taking too long... we have 20+ mins running tests, and this is not even the full implementation/feature test... can't we just run the actual tests that we need, not overthink, and do more building than testing?"* This was a direct correction after A1/A2 each burned through multiple full agent rounds (implementer → tester → rework → scorer, sometimes with the tester itself fanning out 4 parallel sub-agents) totaling well over an hour combined for what the plan itself explicitly scoped as a "mid-size build" of ~22 files. The skill's own instructions already say *"Scale to the work... over-scaled machinery is a defect, not thoroughness"* — I wasn't actually honoring that in practice, even though I was technically following the plan's textual "full loop" assignment per step. "Full loop" describes which roles are involved, not a mandate that the Tester role itself be maximally thorough every single time regardless of actual risk.

**How to apply:** Default to self-verification against the plan's stated pass criteria. Reserve a dedicated Tester/Scorer dispatch for genuinely high-risk or subtle logic the implementer itself flagged as uncertain — not as an automatic step. When about to dispatch a verification agent, ask first: "is this the actual test we need, or padding?" Applies to `zimmerMANNBuild` specifically, but the principle (verification effort should scale to real risk, not to a rote process checklist) generalizes to any multi-agent build/review loop on this project.

# SFCC-236: fix two live-testing regressions in ZimmProductCard

## Context

While testing PR #85 (`feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component`) live, Marcel found two
real bugs in the shared `ZimmProductCard` family:

**(a) A recent hover-reveal fix broke keyboard nav and VoiceOver.** The most recent fix on this
branch (`983bddf`) replaced `:focus-within` with `:has(:focus-visible)` across five hover-reveal
sites, specifically to stop the carousel arrows (and everything else gated the same way) from
staying visible after a mouse click even once the mouse moved away — a real, correctly-diagnosed
bug, and that part of the fix is not being reverted. The regression is elsewhere: every one of
those five reveals uses `display: 'none'` as its "hidden" state, gated behind an *interaction*
heuristic (`:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)`). `display: none` unconditionally strips an element
from the accessibility tree — it answers "is this painted," not "does this exist for assistive
tech," and this recipe has been using it to answer both questions at once. `:focus-visible` is
itself a browser heuristic for "does this focus event look keyboard-like," and VoiceOver-driven
focus (VO+Arrow, rotor, swipe) is not guaranteed to satisfy it in every engine — a real, documented
mismatch, and *not* a touch-only concern: `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` is true on any Mac
trackpad, so a VoiceOver user on ordinary MacBook hardware is exactly the population this gate
applies to. If that heuristic never matches for a given user, all five reveals (carousel arrows,
Home's price reveal, PLP/Wishlist's price↔size-selector swap, notify-me) stay invisible to them
for the entire session, no matter how they navigate. A secondary, lower-severity effect confirmed
alongside it: because these controls only exist as Tab stops *while* the interaction condition is
currently true, Shift+Tab entry into the card from something after it lands on the last
unconditionally-visible stop (the bag button) — the user has already tabbed past controls that,
at that instant, didn't exist yet, and must reverse direction to reach them. (Forward-Tab is fine:
landing on the always-present scroll container triggers the reveal before reaching the arrows.)

**(b) Multi-image cards don't respond to touch swipe on mobile.** The slide indicator renders
correctly (so the image data and gallery logic are fine), but swiping the image doesn't page
through it at all. Root cause: the organism's whole-card stretched-link overlay
(`[data-card-slot="content"] a::after`, `position: absolute; inset: 0`) resolves its containing
block to the organism root — because `ZimmProductCardContent` never sets `position` anywhere —
so it's sized to the *entire* card, image included, not just the name-link row. That overlay
carries no `z-index`, and the recipe already lifts exactly three things above it (`close`,
`carousel`, buttons inside `content`) — the media/gallery scroll region was never added to that
list. A touch swipe on the image actually starts on the invisible overlay `<a>`, so the browser's
native swipe-scroll gesture never engages the real scroll container at all.

Both root causes were confirmed via direct investigation of this exact code (file/line citations
below) before any fix was designed, and both fixes reuse patterns already shipped elsewhere in
this same codebase rather than inventing anything new — `ZimmColourSwatchGroup`'s already-tested
off-page-swatch technique for (a), and this recipe's own existing z-index-lift pattern for (b).

## Fix (b) — swipe blocked by the stretched-link overlay

**File:** `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/zimmProductCard.css.ts`

- Add a fourth lift entry alongside the existing three (currently lines 240-253):
  ```
  [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.media}"]`]: { zIndex: 1 },
  ```
  `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own root is already `position: 'relative'` (its own recipe), so only
  `zIndex` is needed here — identical in shape to the existing `close`/`carousel` entries.
- Extend docblock point 2 (the "lifting every interactive control" explanation, ~lines 62-101)
  with a new dated fix note, continuing this file's own Fix 1/Fix 3/Fix H lettered convention,
  explaining the media/gallery region needed the same lift the click targets already got, and
  that this was missed because clicking `close`/`carousel`/content-buttons was checked live but
  swiping the image itself never was.
- Extend `index.test.tsx`'s existing z-index-lift describe block (or add a sibling one) to assert
  the new entry's object shape, matching that file's own established idiom for these proofs.

**Verification:** jsdom cannot prove this (no stacking-context resolution — this file's own
"KNOWN LIMITATION" docblock already says so). Needs a real touch check: Playwright's
`mobile-chrome` project with a real drag/swipe gesture on the image, or Marcel's own device,
confirming the gallery pages and the indicator updates.

## Fix (a) — hover-reveal content invisible to VoiceOver / skipped on Shift+Tab

**Files:** `zimmProductCard.css.ts` (all 5 reveal sites) and
`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`
(carousel's own base state)

**Recommended fix** — keep every one of the five reveal targets permanently present in the DOM,
focusable, and in the accessibility tree at all times. Stop using `display` to express "hidden";
use the exact technique `ZimmColourSwatchGroup` already ships for its own off-page swatches
(confirmed real, `molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx:215`:
`{ position: 'absolute', clipPath: 'inset(50%)' }`):

- **Hidden (default) state:** `position: 'absolute'`, `clipPath: 'inset(50%)'` instead of
  `display: 'none'` — out of flow (no layout gap, same as today), paints nothing, but stays in
  the DOM/tab order/accessibility tree.
- **Revealed state** (same `&:hover [...]` / `&:has(:focus-visible) [...]` selectors, byte-for-byte
  unchanged): `position: 'static'`, `clipPath: 'none'` instead of `display: 'block'/'flex'`.
- Applies at all 5 sites in `zimmProductCard.css.ts`: Home price reveal (~293-297, 323-325),
  PLP/Wishlist price hide (~330-332, 338-340), PLP/Wishlist size-selector reveal (~344-346,
  348-350), notify-me reveal (~359-362, 364-366), carousel arrow reveal (~379-384).
- `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s `carousel` part: its own unconditional base `display: 'none'`
  becomes the same clip-path equivalent (already `position: 'absolute'` unconditionally, so only
  the hidden-state property changes).
- **Carousel-specific addition:** the wrapper deliberately sets `pointerEvents: 'none'` with each
  `arrowButton` individually re-enabling `pointerEvents: 'auto'` (so clicks in the empty centre
  pass through to the image). Once the wrapper is no longer `display:none`, add an explicit
  belt-and-braces rule in the organism recipe — `[data-card-slot="carousel"] button` gets
  `pointerEvents: 'none'` by default and `'auto'` only in the two revealed selectors — rather than
  relying on clip-path's hit-testing suppression alone. (Price/size-selector/notify-me need no
  equivalent — none of them sets `pointerEvents` at all today.)

**Why this is the recommended path, not one of several open options** (a JS-tracked hover/focus
state was considered and rejected): there is no signal exposed to page-level JavaScript, any more
than to CSS, that says "this focus event was AT-originated." A hand-rolled heuristic (e.g.
flagging `focusin` as non-keyboard when preceded by `pointerdown`) has exactly the same blind spot
as the native `:focus-visible` heuristic it would be reimplementing. It would also break this
organism's own stated design principle ("CSS alone decides what is visible... no JS-tracked reveal
state," `index.tsx` ~349-350) and introduce real SSR/hydration-mismatch risk pure CSS structurally
can't have, for no correctness gain.

**Why this doesn't reintroduce the `983bddf` stuck-open bug:** that bug was entirely about *when*
`:has(:focus-visible)` matches (a click-focused button not un-matching on mouseout until focus
moved elsewhere) — a selector-matching-timing question, completely orthogonal to which property
the matched rule sets. The trigger selectors aren't touched at all; only the property values
inside the already-existing blocks change.

**Docblock updates:** extend/rewrite docblock points 3 and 6 and the "Fix H" note with a new dated
fix note (continuing the lettered sequence), stating explicitly that Fix H's `:focus-within` →
`:has(:focus-visible)` swap was and remains correct for the paint-timing question it solved, and
that the actual defect was using `display` (an AT-tree-removal property) to answer a different
question than the one it should answer. Explicitly out of scope, left as `display:none`: the
permanent, non-hover-capable-pointer hides (`sizeSelectorUnavailable`'s unconditional size-chip
hide, the PLP-mobile bag-icon hide) — separate, correct, Figma-confirmed, non-regressed decisions,
since nothing about them is gated behind an interaction heuristic.

**Test updates:** the existing `.matches()`-based selector-proof describe block in
`index.test.tsx` needs no change (it doesn't depend on which property the matched rule sets). Any
structural/object-shape assertions elsewhere in the same file checking the recipe's declared
`display` values for these 5 sites need updating to the new property values — identify the exact
assertions at implementation time against the real current file, don't guess line numbers here.

**New real-browser verification** (jsdom can't prove any of this): this repo already has
scaffolded-but-empty Playwright a11y projects (`playwright.config.js`'s `a11y-desktop` →
`e2e/tests/a11y/desktop`, `a11y-mobile` → `e2e/tests/a11y/mobile`; both Chromium-only, no WebKit
project configured — not touching `playwright.config.js` itself, only adding specs inside the
already-existing target directories). Add specs for:

1. **Accessibility-tree presence** — load a card in its default (non-hovered, non-focused) state
   and assert, via a real Chromium accessibility-tree snapshot, that the size-chip radiogroup,
   notify-me button, and carousel arrow buttons are present with correct role/name — proving
   AT-tree presence no longer depends on any hover/focus-visible condition having matched.
2. **Tab-order parity** — forward-Tab from before the card and Shift+Tab from after it, asserting
   the stop set/sequence is now identical in both directions (today Shift+Tab skips the
   reveal-gated controls entirely).
3. **No regression on the original stuck-open bug** — real mouse click on an arrow button, move
   the mouse off the card, assert the control is no longer visually painted by reading
   `getComputedStyle(el).clipPath` directly (Playwright's default `toBeVisible()` is primarily a
   bounding-box/`visibility` check and may not reliably catch clip-path-based hiding).

**Honest limitation, not skippable:** the actual disputed claim — does real VoiceOver announce and
activate these controls — can't be fully closed out by any automated check above. Chromium's
accessibility tree isn't the engine VoiceOver actually talks to (WebKit), no WebKit Playwright
project exists in this repo, and Playwright can't drive real VoiceOver at all. The automated specs
give strong, real regression-prevention signal (AT-tree presence + tab-order parity are both real,
previously-uncaught bugs), but final confirmation needs one manual pass from Marcel: navigate a
card via VO+Right-Arrow/rotor only (no mouse, no literal Tab keypress) on real macOS Safari +
VoiceOver, confirming price, the size-chip radiogroup, notify-me, and the carousel arrows are all
announced and activatable via VO+Space.

## Verification (both fixes)

1. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
2. Full local Storybook build + `test-storybook --ci` — same pattern used earlier on this branch
   for the axe-contrast fix; confirms no regression across the whole story set.
3. Updated/new Vitest assertions in both `index.test.tsx` files pass.
4. New Playwright a11y specs (AT-tree presence, tab-order parity, stuck-open non-regression) pass.
5. Real-device/manual checks, both required before calling this done:
   - Real touch swipe (device or Playwright mobile-chrome touch simulation) confirms gallery
     paging works.
   - Real VoiceOver + Safari pass (Marcel, one-time) confirms AT reachability/activation for all
     five previously-broken controls.

## Files touched

All within one protection tier — squad-owned `ui-kits` component recipes/tests, no Tier 1/2 file:

- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/zimmProductCard.css.ts`
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.test.tsx`
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/index.test.tsx` (only if the
  carousel base-state change needs an assertion update there too — confirm at implementation time)
- New: `e2e/tests/a11y/desktop/*.spec.ts`, `e2e/tests/a11y/mobile/*.spec.ts` (exact filenames
  follow this repo's existing spec-naming convention, decided at implementation time)

# SFCC-236: fix two live-testing regressions in ZimmProductCard

## Context

While testing PR #85 (`feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component`) live, Marcel found two
real bugs in the shared `ZimmProductCard` family:

**(a) A recent hover-reveal fix broke keyboard nav and VoiceOver.** The most recent fix on this
branch (`983bddf`) replaced `:focus-within` with `:has(:focus-visible)` across five hover-reveal
sites, specifically to stop the carousel arrows (and everything else gated the same way) from
staying visible after a mouse click even once the mouse moved away — a real, correctly-diagnosed
bug, and that part of the fix is not being reverted. The regression is elsewhere: every one of
those five reveals uses `display: 'none'` as its "hidden" state, gated behind an *interaction*
heuristic (`:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)`). `display: none` unconditionally strips an element
from the accessibility tree — it answers "is this painted," not "does this exist for assistive
tech," and this recipe has been using it to answer both questions at once. `:focus-visible` is
itself a browser heuristic for "does this focus event look keyboard-like," and VoiceOver-driven
focus (VO+Arrow, rotor, swipe) is not guaranteed to satisfy it in every engine — a real, documented
mismatch, and *not* a touch-only concern: `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` is true on any Mac
trackpad, so a VoiceOver user on ordinary MacBook hardware is exactly the population this gate
applies to. If that heuristic never matches for a given user, all five reveals (carousel arrows,
Home's price reveal, PLP/Wishlist's price↔size-selector swap, notify-me) stay invisible to them
for the entire session, no matter how they navigate. A secondary, lower-severity effect confirmed
alongside it: because these controls only exist as Tab stops *while* the interaction condition is
currently true, Shift+Tab entry into the card from something after it lands on the last
unconditionally-visible stop (the bag button) — the user has already tabbed past controls that,
at that instant, didn't exist yet, and must reverse direction to reach them. (Forward-Tab is fine:
landing on the always-present scroll container triggers the reveal before reaching the arrows.)

**(b) Multi-image cards don't respond to touch swipe on mobile.** The slide indicator renders
correctly (so the image data and gallery logic are fine), but swiping the image doesn't page
through it at all. Root cause: the organism's whole-card stretched-link overlay
(`[data-card-slot="content"] a::after`, `position: absolute; inset: 0`) resolves its containing
block to the organism root — because `ZimmProductCardContent` never sets `position` anywhere —
so it's sized to the *entire* card, image included, not just the name-link row. That overlay
carries no `z-index`, and the recipe already lifts exactly three things above it (`close`,
`carousel`, buttons inside `content`) — the media/gallery scroll region was never added to that
list. A touch swipe on the image actually starts on the invisible overlay `<a>`, so the browser's
native swipe-scroll gesture never engages the real scroll container at all.

Both root causes were confirmed via direct investigation of this exact code (file/line citations
below) before any fix was designed, and both fixes reuse patterns already shipped elsewhere in
this same codebase rather than inventing anything new — `ZimmColourSwatchGroup`'s already-tested
off-page-swatch technique for (a), and this recipe's own existing z-index-lift pattern for (b).

## Fix (b) — swipe blocked by the stretched-link overlay

**File:** `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/zimmProductCard.css.ts`

- Add a fourth lift entry alongside the existing three (currently lines 240-253):
  ```
  [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.media}"]`]: { zIndex: 1 },
  ```
  `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own root is already `position: 'relative'` (its own recipe), so only
  `zIndex` is needed here — identical in shape to the existing `close`/`carousel` entries.
- Extend docblock point 2 (the "lifting every interactive control" explanation, ~lines 62-101)
  with a new dated fix note, continuing this file's own Fix 1/Fix 3/Fix H lettered convention,
  explaining the media/gallery region needed the same lift the click targets already got, and
  that this was missed because clicking `close`/`carousel`/content-buttons was checked live but
  swiping the image itself never was.
- Extend `index.test.tsx`'s existing z-index-lift describe block (or add a sibling one) to assert
  the new entry's object shape, matching that file's own established idiom for these proofs.

**Verification:** jsdom cannot prove this (no stacking-context resolution — this file's own
"KNOWN LIMITATION" docblock already says so). Needs a real touch check: Playwright's
`mobile-chrome` project with a real drag/swipe gesture on the image, or Marcel's own device,
confirming the gallery pages and the indicator updates.

## Fix (a) — hover-reveal content invisible to VoiceOver / skipped on Shift+Tab

**Files:** `zimmProductCard.css.ts` (all 5 reveal sites) and
`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`
(carousel's own base state)

**Recommended fix** — keep every one of the five reveal targets permanently present in the DOM,
focusable, and in the accessibility tree at all times. Stop using `display` to express "hidden";
use the exact technique `ZimmColourSwatchGroup` already ships for its own off-page swatches
(confirmed real, `molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx:215`:
`{ position: 'absolute', clipPath: 'inset(50%)' }`):

- **Hidden (default) state:** `position: 'absolute'`, `clipPath: 'inset(50%)'` instead of
  `display: 'none'` — out of flow (no layout gap, same as today), paints nothing, but stays in
  the DOM/tab order/accessibility tree.
- **Revealed state** (same `&:hover [...]` / `&:has(:focus-visible) [...]` selectors, byte-for-byte
  unchanged): `position: 'static'`, `clipPath: 'none'` instead of `display: 'block'/'flex'`.
- Applies at all 5 sites in `zimmProductCard.css.ts`: Home price reveal (~293-297, 323-325),
  PLP/Wishlist price hide (~330-332, 338-340), PLP/Wishlist size-selector reveal (~344-346,
  348-350), notify-me reveal (~359-362, 364-366), carousel arrow reveal (~379-384).
- `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s `carousel` part: its own unconditional base `display: 'none'`
  becomes the same clip-path equivalent (already `position: 'absolute'` unconditionally, so only
  the hidden-state property changes).
- **Carousel-specific addition:** the wrapper deliberately sets `pointerEvents: 'none'` with each
  `arrowButton` individually re-enabling `pointerEvents: 'auto'` (so clicks in the empty centre
  pass through to the image). Once the wrapper is no longer `display:none`, add an explicit
  belt-and-braces rule in the organism recipe — `[data-card-slot="carousel"] button` gets
  `pointerEvents: 'none'` by default and `'auto'` only in the two revealed selectors — rather than
  relying on clip-path's hit-testing suppression alone. (Price/size-selector/notify-me need no
  equivalent — none of them sets `pointerEvents` at all today.)

**Why this is the recommended path, not one of several open options** (a JS-tracked hover/focus
state was considered and rejected): there is no signal exposed to page-level JavaScript, any more
than to CSS, that says "this focus event was AT-originated." A hand-rolled heuristic (e.g.
flagging `focusin` as non-keyboard when preceded by `pointerdown`) has exactly the same blind spot
as the native `:focus-visible` heuristic it would be reimplementing. It would also break this
organism's own stated design principle ("CSS alone decides what is visible... no JS-tracked reveal
state," `index.tsx` ~349-350) and introduce real SSR/hydration-mismatch risk pure CSS structurally
can't have, for no correctness gain.

**Why this doesn't reintroduce the `983bddf` stuck-open bug:** that bug was entirely about *when*
`:has(:focus-visible)` matches (a click-focused button not un-matching on mouseout until focus
moved elsewhere) — a selector-matching-timing question, completely orthogonal to which property
the matched rule sets. The trigger selectors aren't touched at all; only the property values
inside the already-existing blocks change.

**Docblock updates:** extend/rewrite docblock points 3 and 6 and the "Fix H" note with a new dated
fix note (continuing the lettered sequence), stating explicitly that Fix H's `:focus-within` →
`:has(:focus-visible)` swap was and remains correct for the paint-timing question it solved, and
that the actual defect was using `display` (an AT-tree-removal property) to answer a different
question than the one it should answer. Explicitly out of scope, left as `display:none`: the
permanent, non-hover-capable-pointer hides (`sizeSelectorUnavailable`'s unconditional size-chip
hide, the PLP-mobile bag-icon hide) — separate, correct, Figma-confirmed, non-regressed decisions,
since nothing about them is gated behind an interaction heuristic.

**Test updates:** the existing `.matches()`-based selector-proof describe block in
`index.test.tsx` needs no change (it doesn't depend on which property the matched rule sets). Any
structural/object-shape assertions elsewhere in the same file checking the recipe's declared
`display` values for these 5 sites need updating to the new property values — identify the exact
assertions at implementation time against the real current file, don't guess line numbers here.

**New real-browser verification** (jsdom can't prove any of this): this repo already has
scaffolded-but-empty Playwright a11y projects (`playwright.config.js`'s `a11y-desktop` →
`e2e/tests/a11y/desktop`, `a11y-mobile` → `e2e/tests/a11y/mobile`; both Chromium-only, no WebKit
project configured — not touching `playwright.config.js` itself, only adding specs inside the
already-existing target directories). Add specs for:

1. **Accessibility-tree presence** — load a card in its default (non-hovered, non-focused) state
   and assert, via a real Chromium accessibility-tree snapshot, that the size-chip radiogroup,
   notify-me button, and carousel arrow buttons are present with correct role/name — proving
   AT-tree presence no longer depends on any hover/focus-visible condition having matched.
2. **Tab-order parity** — forward-Tab from before the card and Shift+Tab from after it, asserting
   the stop set/sequence is now identical in both directions (today Shift+Tab skips the
   reveal-gated controls entirely).
3. **No regression on the original stuck-open bug** — real mouse click on an arrow button, move
   the mouse off the card, assert the control is no longer visually painted by reading
   `getComputedStyle(el).clipPath` directly (Playwright's default `toBeVisible()` is primarily a
   bounding-box/`visibility` check and may not reliably catch clip-path-based hiding).

**Honest limitation, not skippable:** the actual disputed claim — does real VoiceOver announce and
activate these controls — can't be fully closed out by any automated check above. Chromium's
accessibility tree isn't the engine VoiceOver actually talks to (WebKit), no WebKit Playwright
project exists in this repo, and Playwright can't drive real VoiceOver at all. The automated specs
give strong, real regression-prevention signal (AT-tree presence + tab-order parity are both real,
previously-uncaught bugs), but final confirmation needs one manual pass from Marcel: navigate a
card via VO+Right-Arrow/rotor only (no mouse, no literal Tab keypress) on real macOS Safari +
VoiceOver, confirming price, the size-chip radiogroup, notify-me, and the carousel arrows are all
announced and activatable via VO+Space.

## Verification (both fixes)

1. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
2. Full local Storybook build + `test-storybook --ci` — same pattern used earlier on this branch
   for the axe-contrast fix; confirms no regression across the whole story set.
3. Updated/new Vitest assertions in both `index.test.tsx` files pass.
4. New Playwright a11y specs (AT-tree presence, tab-order parity, stuck-open non-regression) pass.
5. Real-device/manual checks, both required before calling this done:
   - Real touch swipe (device or Playwright mobile-chrome touch simulation) confirms gallery
     paging works.
   - Real VoiceOver + Safari pass (Marcel, one-time) confirms AT reachability/activation for all
     five previously-broken controls.

## Files touched

All within one protection tier — squad-owned `ui-kits` component recipes/tests, no Tier 1/2 file:

- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/zimmProductCard.css.ts`
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.test.tsx`
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/index.test.tsx` (only if the
  carousel base-state change needs an assertion update there too — confirm at implementation time)
- New: `e2e/tests/a11y/desktop/*.spec.ts`, `e2e/tests/a11y/mobile/*.spec.ts` (exact filenames
  follow this repo's existing spec-naming convention, decided at implementation time)

This agent should be used proactively after writing or modifying code, especially before committing changes or creating pull requests. It will check for style violations, potential issues, and ensure code follows the established patterns in CLAUDE.md. Also the agent needs to know which files to focus on for the review. In most cases this will be recently completed work which is unstaged in git (can be retrieved by running git diff). However there can be cases where this is different, make sure to specify this as the agent input when calling the agent. Typical triggers include the user asking for a review of a feature they just implemented, the assistant proactively reviewing its own newly-written code before declaring a task done, and a final pre-PR check before opening a pull request. user: "Fix the null pointer exception in the data processor"
assistant: "I've added the necessary null checks to prevent the exception:"
<function call omitted for brevity>

</commentary>
assistant: "Let me refine this bug fix using the code-simplifier agent to ensure it follows our best practices"
</example>

<function call omitted for brevity>

See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

This agent should be invoked proactively after completing a logical chunk of work that involves error handling, catch blocks, fallback logic, or any code that could potentially suppress errors. Examples:

- **`0abe8d0`** — Made our own editable copy of the base "recommended products" component (converted to TypeScript). No new behaviour yet, just a copy we're now allowed to change.
- **`dff3ea1`** — Taught the shared product card a new look: image-only, no price, no add-to-bag button — the stripped-down style Recently Viewed needs.
- **`fe73abc`** — Wrote a small translator that takes the raw data Einstein (the recommendation engine) hands back and reshapes it into exactly what the product card expects.
- **`2449e9f`** — Added the "should we even show this rail?" logic (hide it from a visitor who hasn't viewed anything yet) and the "mark this product as viewed" trigger on the product page.

## 2. The foundation we're standing on — the shared Product Card (~45 commits, SFCC-236)

Before Recently Viewed could exist, someone had to build the reusable card component itself — a separate, earlier piece of work:
- Built it piece by piece: the image/slideshow part, the price/text part, size chips, a "New"/"Sale" badge — then assembled them into one shared `ZimmProductCard` other pages plug into.
- Then a long tail of polish: keyboard and screen-reader accessibility fixes, fixing swipe-to-browse-photos on mobile, price wrapping on small screens, and test/Storybook cleanup.

We're not touching this directly — we're building on top of it, so it rides along with the branch.

## 3. Fixes that came along for the ride (~15 commits)

Other people's already-finished, already-merged work, picked up when this branch synced with `develop`. Nothing to do with Recently Viewed:
- **CI fixes** — cleaning up abandoned preview environments, a gate script fix, a new P0 test gate.
- **Header fixes** — cart/wishlist icon states, mobile drawer closing on resize, a divider colour tweak.
- **PDP drawer fixes** — sizing, alignment, tabs, animation on the product page's drawer (SFCC-898).
- A couple of one-offs — a mega-menu click fix, removing a placeholder modal.

Nothing here needs our review — it was already done and merged before we synced.

410	### A5 — `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` organism + recipe
411	
412	Create `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmRecentlyViewedRail/` (`index.tsx`,
413	`zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts`, `index.stories.tsx`, `index.test.tsx`); register
414	`ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` in `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts`.
415	
416	**Purely presentational — data as props.** Props: `title: ReactNode`, `cards: readonly
417	ZimmProductCardProps[]`, `seeAllHref?: string`, `seeAllLabel?: string`. No `useEinstein`, no
418	`useIntl` — the container owns the copy. (An `IntlProvider` wrapper is still needed in the test
419	because `ZimmProductCard` itself calls `useIntl`; follow `zimmProductCard/index.test.tsx`'s wrapper.)
420	
421	Structure mirrors Figma: a `title-and-link` row (title left, See-Full-History link right) above a
422	horizontally scrollable `group` of `ZimmProductCard`s at `variation: 'recentlyViewed'`.
423	
424	**No rail-level arrow buttons.** Desktop `40000307:12444` decomposes into exactly two children —
425	`title-and-link` (1440×96) and `group` (1440×432) — with no arrow layer. `ZimmProductCard` already
426	carries its own intra-card arrows; rail arrows would collide. Native scroll with scroll-snap only.
427	
428	**Three explicit media queries** off `breakpoints` imported from `app/theme/foundation`, never Chakra's
429	array shorthand (it fails `recipeGuards.test.ts`). Real geometry, read from the nodes 2026-09-06:
430	
431	| Viewport | Rail node | Card | Cards across |
432	|---|---|---|---|
433	| Mobile (base, 402) | `40000538:25030` — 402×355.82 | **201×299.82** | **2** (201×2 = 402, exactly full-bleed) |
434	| Tablet (`breakpoints.md`, 768) | `40000730:13363` — 768×437.85 | **256×381.85** | **3** |
435	| Desktop (`breakpoints.xl`) | `40000307:12444` — 1440×528 | **288×432** | **5** |
436	
437	All three cards are 2:3, matching `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s existing `aspectRatio: '2 / 3'` — so card
438	width is the only thing that varies per breakpoint; height follows. Header (`title-and-link`) is
439	**h96** on Desktop (`40000538:20306`) and **h56** on Mobile (`40000538:25031`); the link is present on
440	both, so it is never hidden by viewport.
441	
442	**Pass criteria**
443	- **Every value is `textStyle`, `var(--zimm-*)`, or a named constant with a `provisional`/`pending`
444	  comment.** Zero raw hex/px/rem/em, zero bare Chakra token strings. `npm run audit:tokens` reports no
445	  new finding here; `recipeGuards.test.ts` passes (namespacing + bare-token guards).
446	- Recipe key namespaced `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` — an unnamespaced key deep-merges with any same-named
447	  SFCC base recipe.
448	- `ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts` passes — declared `parts` cover every part read off
449	  `useMultiStyleConfig`.
450	- **Cap is client-side.** At most `RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_MAX_ITEMS` (5, matching the Desktop
451	  composition) regardless of input length. Finding 29: the API ignores `limit`, so the cap cannot live
452	  in the request. Named constant, never a literal.
453	- **Order preserved verbatim** — renders `cards` in received order, most-recent-first, left to right
454	  (AC 2). Test with an input whose correct and incorrect orderings are distinguishable (**not** a list
455	  already order-independent — that is exactly the encoded-bug trap). Make it fail by reversing.
456	- Renders `null` when `cards` is empty — a second guard behind A4's gate.
457	- **See-Full-History link states — RESOLVED FROM REGISTERED TOKENS 2026-09-06, not from the
458	  `zimmNavItem` fallback (which is now known to be wrong for this link).** The Figma default state
459	  (`40000138:469`, *"State=default, Size=Large"*) is `Default/Link-lg`, uppercase, **underlined at
460	  rest**, colour `--alias/color/link/default` `#191919`. The old plan borrowed `zimmNavItem`'s
461	  "underline appears on hover" — impossible on a link that is already underlined.
462	
463	  Every piece is already registered in this repo's Tier 1 foundation, so nothing is invented:
464	
465	  | State | Treatment | Token |
466	  |---|---|---|
467	  | default | `textStyle="linkLg"` — **already encodes `textTransform: uppercase` + `textDecoration: underline`**, so it matches the node exactly | `typography.ts:152` |
468	  | | colour | `var(--zimm-color-link-default)` (= `grey[900]`, matches `#191919`) |
469	  | hover | colour shift only — underline persists | `var(--zimm-color-link-hover)` (= `grey[500]`) |
470	  | focus-visible | `outline: var(--zimm-focus-ring)`, `outlineOffset: var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)` | `zimmTokens.ts:68-69` |
471	  | active | no distinct token exists — inherit hover, with a comment saying so | — |
472	  | disabled | N/A — the link is absent below the threshold, never disabled | — |
473	
474	  **Honest caveat to carry in a code comment:** no Figma hover/focus/active *variant* was located
475	  (the symbol name implies a `State` axis, but only `State=default` exists in the supplied nodes and
