`ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` in `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts`.

**Purely presentational — data as props.** Props: `title: ReactNode`, `cards: readonly
ZimmProductCardProps[]`, `seeAllHref?: string`, `seeAllLabel?: string`. No `useEinstein`, no
`useIntl` — the container owns the copy. (An `IntlProvider` wrapper is still needed in the test
because `ZimmProductCard` itself calls `useIntl`; follow `zimmProductCard/index.test.tsx`'s wrapper.)

Structure mirrors Figma: a `title-and-link` row (title left, See-Full-History link right) above a
horizontally scrollable `group` of `ZimmProductCard`s at `variation: 'recentlyViewed'`.

**No rail-level arrow buttons.** Desktop `40000307:12444` decomposes into exactly two children —
`title-and-link` (1440×96) and `group` (1440×432) — with no arrow layer. `ZimmProductCard` already
carries its own intra-card arrows; rail arrows would collide. Native scroll with scroll-snap only.

**Three explicit media queries** off `breakpoints` imported from `app/theme/foundation`, never Chakra's
array shorthand (it fails `recipeGuards.test.ts`). Real geometry, read from the nodes 2026-09-06:

| Viewport | Rail node | Card | Cards across |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mobile (base, 402) | `40000538:25030` — 402×355.82 | **201×299.82** | **2** (201×2 = 402, exactly full-bleed) |
| Tablet (`breakpoints.md`, 768) | `40000730:13363` — 768×437.85 | **256×381.85** | **3** |
| Desktop (`breakpoints.xl`) | `40000307:12444` — 1440×528 | **288×432** | **5** |

All three cards are 2:3, matching `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s existing `aspectRatio: '2 / 3'` — so card
width is the only thing that varies per breakpoint; height follows. Header (`title-and-link`) is
**h96** on Desktop (`40000538:20306`) and **h56** on Mobile (`40000538:25031`); the link is present on
both, so it is never hidden by viewport.

**Pass criteria**
- **Every value is `textStyle`, `var(--zimm-*)`, or a named constant with a `provisional`/`pending`
  comment.** Zero raw hex/px/rem/em, zero bare Chakra token strings. `npm run audit:tokens` reports no
  new finding here; `recipeGuards.test.ts` passes (namespacing + bare-token guards).
- Recipe key namespaced `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` — an unnamespaced key deep-merges with any same-named
  SFCC base recipe.
- `ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts` passes — declared `parts` cover every part read off
  `useMultiStyleConfig`.
- **Cap is client-side.** At most `RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_MAX_ITEMS` (5, matching the Desktop
  composition) regardless of input length. Finding 29: the API ignores `limit`, so the cap cannot live
  in the request. Named constant, never a literal.
- **Order preserved verbatim** — renders `cards` in received order, most-recent-first, left to right
  (AC 2). Test with an input whose correct and incorrect orderings are distinguishable (**not** a list
  already order-independent — that is exactly the encoded-bug trap). Make it fail by reversing.
- Renders `null` when `cards` is empty — a second guard behind A4's gate.
- **See-Full-History link states — RESOLVED FROM REGISTERED TOKENS 2026-09-06, not from the
  `zimmNavItem` fallback (which is now known to be wrong for this link).** The Figma default state
  (`40000138:469`, *"State=default, Size=Large"*) is `Default/Link-lg`, uppercase, **underlined at
  rest**, colour `--alias/color/link/default` `#191919`. The old plan borrowed `zimmNavItem`'s
  "underline appears on hover" — impossible on a link that is already underlined.

  Every piece is already registered in this repo's Tier 1 foundation, so nothing is invented:

  | State | Treatment | Token |
  |---|---|---|
  | default | `textStyle="linkLg"` — **already encodes `textTransform: uppercase` + `textDecoration: underline`**, so it matches the node exactly | `typography.ts:152` |
  | | colour | `var(--zimm-color-link-default)` (= `grey[900]`, matches `#191919`) |
  | hover | colour shift only — underline persists | `var(--zimm-color-link-hover)` (= `grey[500]`) |
  | focus-visible | `outline: var(--zimm-focus-ring)`, `outlineOffset: var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)` | `zimmTokens.ts:68-69` |
  | active | no distinct token exists — inherit hover, with a comment saying so | — |
  | disabled | N/A — the link is absent below the threshold, never disabled | — |

  **Honest caveat to carry in a code comment:** no Figma hover/focus/active *variant* was located
  (the symbol name implies a `State` axis, but only `State=default` exists in the supplied nodes and
  `search_design_system` finds no "Link" component set). `colors.link.hover` exists in the
  designer-owned foundation for exactly one purpose and is the only link-hover colour in the system,
  so deriving hover from it is defensible — but it is a derivation, not a node reading.
- **If any hover-reveal is added, its trigger is `:hover, :has(:focus-visible)` — never
  `:focus-within`**, which stays matched after a click until focus leaves the subtree entirely and has
  already caused a stuck-open regression here (`zimmProductCard.css.ts` Fix H/J).

  `Default` (5 cards), `WithSeeAllLink`, `SingleCard`, `OverCap` (8 in, 5 rendered). A `play` on
  `WithSeeAllLink` asserting the link is keyboard-reachable with the right accessible name.
- `index.test.tsx` asserts this component's own contract only — cap, order, empty-null,
  link-shown-when-href-present. Do not re-prove `ZimmProductCard`'s internals (`testing.md`).

content.text:
Settling it: **keep B1 narrow, exactly as planned — no shared grid abstraction with PLP.**

Reasoning:

- **The actual reusable part is already shared, at the right layer.** B1 already renders cards at `variation: 'plp'` (badge on, hover-swap on) — same as the quick-test. The card itself, the part with real behavior, is already common. What's left is just the *layout shell* around it (title bar + column grid) — and that's a much thinner thing to duplicate than a whole card.
- **B1's shell source is provisional; PLP doesn't have a shell spec at all yet.** B1's grid layout comes from `3332:35655`, explicitly flagged in the plan as a non-final placeholder pending real design. The PLP quick-test didn't design a grid organism — it just dropped `ZimmProductCard` into the page's existing raw layout. Building a shared abstraction now means generalizing across two unconfirmed shapes at once, not one real one and one hypothetical.
- **The plan already made this exact call once, one section up.** It explicitly declined to share a title row between A5's rail and B1's grid — different Figma sources, so forcing a shared component would be "a wrong DRY call." Same logic applies here, one level higher: Recently-Viewed's grid shell and PLP's future grid shell are different consumers with no confirmed shared source yet.
- **Cheap to fix later, expensive to guess now.** Once PLP gets a real grid design, extracting a shared shell out of two already-shipped, already-similar components is a mechanical refactor. Guessing at a shared shape now — against a provisional source on our side and nothing at all on PLP's — risks shipping the wrong abstraction and unwinding it later, which is worse than the small duplication.

One related FYI while we're here, not blocking: B1's cards will inherit the same known gap the quick-test flagged — `plp` variation has no wishlist-toggle affordance. Worth a quick confirm later whether that's acceptable for SFCC-84's full-history page or needs its own tracked gap, but doesn't affect B1's build.

Build B1 per the plan as-is. Let me know if you want it any other way — otherwise this is settled and I'll proceed with it when we get there.

content.text:
Think of it like two different pages both wanting the same kind of thing: a grid of product cards. Right now:

- **The plan (B1)** says: build a grid ONLY for the Recently-Viewed "See Full History" page. Call it `ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid`. Narrow, simple, done.
- **The PLP quick-test's docblock** flagged that PLP *also* wants a grid like this eventually, and doesn't have one yet.

**Why I'm not just recommending "build the shared version now":**
- Nobody has actually scoped what PLP's real grid needs to do (pagination? infinite scroll? PLP-specific loading skeletons?) — building "generic" for a need nobody's defined yet means guessing, and guesses that turn out wrong get thrown away or awkwardly bent later.
- A shared component also drags in a real ownership/tier question (who approves changes to it, which CODEOWNERS rule covers it) that hasn't been decided and isn't part of either ticket.
- This repo's own written rule is literally "don't build the shared version until two real things need it" — resist designing for a hypothetical future requirement.

**Why punting is safe, not lazy:** building it narrow now doesn't waste anything. When PLP's grid becomes a real, scoped ticket, whoever picks it up can look at `ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid`'s working code and pull the shared bits out *then*, once we actually know what PLP's version needs to do differently. Extracting shared code after two real examples exist is easy; guessing it before the second example exists is how you end up with the wrong abstraction baked in.

Verified against the actual code rather than just the plan — here's the honest picture: **nothing user-facing exists yet.** All four phases are foundation work; the first thing an actual shopper could see doesn't land until A5+A6.

## Actually running in the app today

- **A1 — Cart's product recommendations now render through our own TypeScript copy**, not the original SFCC file. Byte-identical behavior (it was a straight port), so nobody would notice — but it's genuinely live, confirmed via the resolver redirect. PDP doesn't get this yet (that's A6's import-path fix).
- **A4's write-side — every real PDP visit now sets a `sessionStorage` flag.** Open any product page on this branch and check devtools → Application → Session Storage → `zimm-recently-viewed`. This is live and working right now.

## Built, tested, proven — but not connected to anything real yet

- **A2 — the `recentlyViewed` card style exists and works**, provable in Storybook (`Commerce/ZimmProductCard` → `RecentlyViewed` story) and fully unit-tested — but zero real pages pass `variation: 'recentlyViewed'` yet. Confirmed by grep: the only places that string appears are the card's own type file, stories, and tests.
- **A3 — the Einstein-rec-to-card translator function exists and is tested** against real edge cases, but nothing calls it outside its own test file. It's a finished tool sitting on the shelf.
- **A4's read-side — `useRecentlyViewedGate()` (the "should we show the rail?" hook) is written and tested**, but nothing calls it yet either. Only its sibling `markProductViewed()` is wired in.

## One housekeeping note

`recommended-products/index.tsx` still has its `console.log('[overrides] ...')` copy-first marker in it — left in deliberately, gets removed as part of A6.

**In short:** A1-A4 built the gate, the translator, and the visual style — three separate, independently-proven pieces. A5 (running now) builds the component that assembles them into an actual rail. A6 is what plugs that rail into PDP and Cart so a real shopper sees it.

content.text:
Since B1-B3 (the See Full History page) haven't landed yet, what's testable right now is the rail itself on PDP and Cart. Here's a practical checklist for your running dev server:

## 1. The empty-state gate (the trickiest part to get right)

- **Fresh incognito window, guest, go straight to Cart** (don't visit any PDP first). Expect: **no Recently Viewed section at all** — not even a skeleton. (The skeleton you saw earlier should be gone now that PDP's import actually reaches our code.)
- **Same session, now visit 2-3 different PDPs**, then go to Cart. Expect: the rail now appears, showing those products, **most-recently-viewed first** (the last one you looked at should be leftmost).
- **Log in as a registered customer in a session where you haven't viewed anything.** Expect: the rail shows immediately — registered status alone satisfies the gate. (Known, accepted gap: if that customer has *genuinely* never viewed anything, Einstein's own 2-product baseline recommendation shows instead of true emptiness — that's a parked, documented issue, not a new bug.)
- Check devtools → Application → Session Storage for a `zimm-recently-viewed` key set to `true` after step 2 — confirms the write side is firing.

## 2. Visual/style check

- Recently Viewed cards should be **image-only**: no price, no add-to-bag button, no wishlist heart, no "New"/"Sale" badge. Just the image.
- Tab through the cards on keyboard — each should be **one** reachable stop with a visible focus ring, not several.

## 3. Cap and geometry

- View more than 5 distinct products in one session — the rail should cap at exactly **5**, most-recent-first.
- **Worth a specific look on mobile width** (resize or devtools device toolbar): cards should reach the true screen edges with no side gap. This is the one thing I fixed today without being able to visually confirm it myself (the `mx` bleed-prop forwarding) — if you see a gap on the sides on mobile/tablet, that's the thing to flag back to me.

## 4. Regression check — everything else should look untouched

content.text:
Two quick things to rule out first, then the likely real cause:

## Quick checks (30 seconds)

1. **Hard refresh** (or restart the dev server if it's been running a while) — a lot changed across A5/A6, and a stale HMR bundle is the cheapest thing to rule out.
2. **Browser console** — any red errors on the PDP/Cart page? A silent render exception in the new branch would make the section just vanish rather than show a fallback.

## The likely real cause: Einstein isn't pointed at Zimmermann's own catalog

Checked `config/default.js`:
```js
einsteinAPI: {
  einsteinId: '1ea06c6e-c936-4324-bcf0-fada93f83bb1',
  siteId: process.env.EINSTEIN_API_SITE_ID,   // = 'aaij-MobileFirst' in .env.sample
}
```
`aaij-MobileFirst` is Salesforce's own unmodified SDK demo/boilerplate site ID — not a real Zimmermann Einstein instance. This is a known, already-tracked gap (SFCC-112, "In Refinement"), not something introduced by this build.

**Why this produces exactly your symptom:** the gate (session flag / registered check) is a separate, purely local mechanism — it likely *is* passing correctly. But the rail's actual content comes from Einstein returning recommended product IDs, which then get looked up against Zimmermann's real Shopper Products API (`use-einstein.js`'s own `fetchRecProductDetails`, already filtered to "only recs with a real matched product"). If Einstein is querying the wrong demo catalog, the IDs it returns don't exist in Zimmermann's real catalog — the follow-up lookup finds nothing for any of them, every card gets filtered out, and you end up with zero usable cards. `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` correctly renders nothing when `cards` is empty (that's by design, AC-compliant) — so this would look identical to "the gate is broken," even though it's actually "there's nothing real to show."

**Fastest way to confirm:** open devtools → Network tab, filter for `cquotient.com` (Einstein's API host), reload PDP. Look at the recommendations response — if the returned product IDs don't look like real Zimmermann SKUs, or a follow-up Shopper Products call for those IDs 404s, that confirms it.

I can't fix this myself even if confirmed — `config/default.js` is Tier 1 (Runtime & Integration Config), owned by Integration/SI Partner, and this is exactly the SFCC-112 gap already tracked separately from this build. Let me know what the Network tab shows and we can confirm which of these three it actually is.

content.text: `viewed-recently-einstein` came back 200 with a real 871-byte payload — so Einstein itself is responding with actual data, which narrows things down. But that's not the whole chain: `useEinstein()` does a *second* lookup afterward, resolving those recommended product IDs into full product details against Zimmermann's real Shopper Products API (a completely different host, not `cquotient.com`) — and only recs that resolve to a real product survive. Let me check that logic directly before asking you to dig further.

input.description: Find the secondary product-lookup call inside useEinstein

content.text:
That secondary lookup is the key. Reading `use-einstein.js`'s actual logic (lines 465-519):

1. It takes the IDs Einstein just returned and calls `api.shopperProducts.getProducts({ids: ...})` against Zimmermann's **real** commerce API (a different host than `cquotient.com` — won't show up in that filter).
2. It keeps only recs where that call actually finds a matching product (`products?.data?.find(...)`) — anything that doesn't match gets silently dropped.
3. **If that call throws entirely**, it's caught, logged via `logger.error('Error fetching product details for recommendations', ...)`, and the function falls back to returning the raw, unprocessed Einstein response — where each rec is missing the `productId` field our own mapper requires.

Either path — zero matches, or an outright throw — ends the same way: nothing usable reaches our code, regardless of whether the gate passed. This lines up exactly with the demo-siteId theory: if Einstein (via `aaij-MobileFirst`) is recommending product IDs that don't exist in Zimmermann's real catalog, this is precisely where they'd get filtered out.

Two things to check, cheapest first:

1. **Browser console** — look for `"Error fetching product details for recommendations"`. If it's there, the call threw outright — confirms the failure point immediately.
2. **If no console error**, check the Network tab for a call to the Shopper Products API (different host than `cquotient.com` — look for a request with `ids=` in its query string, likely alongside your other normal product/category calls). Check its status and whether `data` actually contains matching products for the IDs Einstein recommended.

Either result would confirm this is the pre-existing Einstein/catalog mismatch (SFCC-112), not a defect in A1-A6.

content.text:
Good news buried in that noise — most of it is unrelated (Home page icon-import warnings, Contentful source-map noise, missing-translation warnings, a swatch-group duplicate-key warning, DataCloud send failures). None of that touches Recently Viewed. The one thing that actually matters here is what's **not** there.

**Confirmed: the `fetchRecProductDetails` error never fired.** I can see `getRecommendations @ use-einstein.js:600` in one of the stack traces, called from `index.tsx:189`, completing normally and dispatching new state (`dispatchSetState @ use-einstein.js:592`) — no exception, no `"Error fetching product details for recommendations"` log anywhere in what you pasted. That rules out the "the API call threw" branch of my theory.

**That leaves the other branch, and it now looks like the actual cause:** `api.shopperProducts.getProducts()` succeeded, but **none of the product IDs Einstein recommended matched anything in Zimmermann's real catalog** — so `use-einstein.js`'s own filter (`recs.filter(rec => products?.data?.find(product => product.id === rec.id))`) silently reduced the list to zero. This produces no error at all — from the code's own point of view, "the recommended IDs don't exist here" isn't exceptional, it's just an empty result. That's exactly consistent with Einstein pointing at `aaij-MobileFirst` (Salesforce's demo catalog) instead of Zimmermann's real one.

Given this, I'm confident the gate and A6's branch logic are both working correctly — an empty `cards` array correctly renders nothing, by design. There's nothing left in our own code to suspect.

**If you want it airtight rather than just well-evidenced:** open that `viewed-recently-einstein` request in the Network tab and look at its response body — the product IDs in there almost certainly won't look like real Zimmermann SKUs (check one against Business Manager or a real PDP URL).

This is the SFCC-112 gap, not something A1-A6 got wrong, and not something I can fix — `config/default.js` is Tier 1, owned by Integration/SI Partner. Once Einstein is pointed at a real Zimmermann instance, this should start working without any code change on our side.

15:EINSTEIN_API_SITE_ID=aaij-MobileFirst
---
75-| `/checkout/shopper-orders/v1/*`    | POST, GET                | Order placement and lookup (SFCC-owned checkouts only)                                                                                          |
76-| `/customer/shopper-customers/v1/*` | GET, POST, PATCH         | Profile, addresses, saved-payment references                                                                                                    |
77-| `/pricing/shopper-promotions/v1/*` | GET                      | Active promotions, coupon validation                                                                                                            |
78:| Einstein recommendations endpoints | GET                      | Personalised recommendations slot. Consent-gated (Didomi purpose TBC) — falls back to a static SFCC merchandising group if consent is not given |
79-
80-Every request carries the site ID, organisation ID, locale, currency, and SLAS bearer token. PII travels over TLS only. PCI scope is Adyen's — SFCC holds token references only.
81-
82-## 5. reCAPTCHA on register and login (CRM-008)
83-
84-- The storefront loads the reCAPTCHA v3 script on register and login forms only — not on any other page — and only after the customer first touches the form, so the script never blocks first paint.
85-- On submit, the reCAPTCHA token is sent alongside the form data to the MRT layer. The MRT layer verifies the token against Google's `siteverify` endpoint (using the secret key held as the `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` MRT environment variable) before forwarding the request to SCAPI. The secret key never reaches the browser.
86-- The site key is set per environment as `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` (MRT environment variable, public). The secret key is held as `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` (MRT environment variable, server-only).
87-- reCAPTCHA loads on form interaction regardless of consent. **Exception: EU and UK** — in those regions it only loads after Didomi consent, which means a visitor who declines gets no bot protection there.
88-
--
122-| SCAPI catalogue 5xx                           | TanStack Query retries three times with exponential backoff. On final failure, show the last cached payload if available; otherwise show an error state with a "Try again" CTA. |
123-| SCAPI basket 5xx during add-to-cart           | Inline error toast. The user's intent stays in client state so a retry resends the same request.                                                                                |
124-| Order placement 5xx after Adyen authorisation | Hard error — the order cannot fail silently. The customer sees an explicit error with a contact reference and ops is alerted.                                                   |
125:| Einstein recommendations 5xx                  | Hide the slot or fall back to a static merchandising group.                                                                                                                     |
126-| SLAS token refresh fails                      | Force re-login. The basket is preserved on the guest token until the customer completes checkout.                                                                               |
127-| TSOB 409 (rapid storefront switch)            | Retry after 3 seconds. Do not re-login the customer — the existing session is still valid on the origin channel.                                                                |
128-| reCAPTCHA fails to load or token rejected     | Block the register/login submit, show a "please retry" message, and offer a contact-support path after two failures.                                                            |
129-
130-## 9. Security and privacy
131-
132-- All traffic is TLS 1.2+ over HTTPS.
133-- SLAS private-client flow — the authorisation code exchange is proxied through MRT so the client secret never reaches the browser.
134-- Refresh tokens are held in `httpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Strict` cookies — never in browser JavaScript.
135-- PCI scope is Adyen's — the browser sends payment data directly to Adyen. SFCC holds token references only.

84-- The storefront loads the reCAPTCHA v3 script on register and login forms only — not on any other page — and only after the customer first touches the form, so the script never blocks first paint.
85-- On submit, the reCAPTCHA token is sent alongside the form data to the MRT layer. The MRT layer verifies the token against Google's `siteverify` endpoint (using the secret key held as the `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` MRT environment variable) before forwarding the request to SCAPI. The secret key never reaches the browser.
86-- The site key is set per environment as `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` (MRT environment variable, public). The secret key is held as `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` (MRT environment variable, server-only).
87-- reCAPTCHA loads on form interaction regardless of consent. **Exception: EU and UK** — in those regions it only loads after Didomi consent, which means a visitor who declines gets no bot protection there.
88-
--
122-| SCAPI catalogue 5xx                           | TanStack Query retries three times with exponential backoff. On final failure, show the last cached payload if available; otherwise show an error state with a "Try again" CTA. |
123-| SCAPI basket 5xx during add-to-cart           | Inline error toast. The user's intent stays in client state so a retry resends the same request.                                                                                |
124-| Order placement 5xx after Adyen authorisation | Hard error — the order cannot fail silently. The customer sees an explicit error with a contact reference and ops is alerted.                                                   |
125:| Einstein recommendations 5xx                  | Hide the slot or fall back to a static merchandising group.                                                                                                                     |
126-| SLAS token refresh fails                      | Force re-login. The basket is preserved on the guest token until the customer completes checkout.                                                                               |
127-| TSOB 409 (rapid storefront switch)            | Retry after 3 seconds. Do not re-login the customer — the existing session is still valid on the origin channel.                                                                |
128-| reCAPTCHA fails to load or token rejected     | Block the register/login submit, show a "please retry" message, and offer a contact-support path after two failures.                                                            |
129-
130-## 9. Security and privacy
131-
132-- All traffic is TLS 1.2+ over HTTPS.
133-- SLAS private-client flow — the authorisation code exchange is proxied through MRT so the client secret never reaches the browser.
134-- Refresh tokens are held in `httpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Strict` cookies — never in browser JavaScript.
135-- PCI scope is Adyen's — the browser sends payment data directly to Adyen. SFCC holds token references only.

content.text:
Found the exact mechanism — this is a real, reproducible gap in the tooling, not something you did wrong.

**Confirmed from the actual script (`scripts/switchEnv.mjs`):**
- `npm run env -- init` unconditionally calls `pullFromGitHubEnvironments()` (line 257) — even for tier files that already exist and get skipped from scaffolding (line 235-236). It's not gated behind "only for freshly-created files."
- That pull calls `upsertKeys(filePath, updates, true)` — and critically, it doesn't pass the `fillOnly` flag, so it defaults to `false`. Looking at `upsertKeys`'s own logic (line 461): when `fillOnly` is `false`, it **overwrites an existing non-blank local value whenever it differs from what's stored on GitHub** — this isn't a "fill in blanks only" operation, it's overwrite-on-mismatch.
- `switchTo()` (plain `npm run env -- dev`) does **not** call the pull step at all — only `init` does.

**What this means concretely:** at some point you ran `npm run env -- init`. Your local `.env.dev` already had a real, working `EINSTEIN_API_SITE_ID` (the one that showed you `/product/25519318M`). The `dev` GitHub Environment's centrally-stored copy of that same variable is apparently still `aaij-MobileFirst` (the placeholder from `.env.sample`) — nobody's corrected it there. The `init` pull silently overwrote your correct local value with that wrong central one, with no warning that a value was being replaced rather than filled.

This is also a shared-impact problem, not just yours: anyone else who runs `init` against the `dev` GitHub Environment right now would get the same broken value.

**What I can't do:** recover the original correct site ID myself — it's not in git history (`.env.dev` is gitignored) and the GitHub Environment's own stored copy is already the wrong one, so there's no remaining copy of the real value anywhere I have access to.

Do you remember the actual site ID (or where it'd be recorded — Business Manager's Einstein settings, a Slack thread, a note from whoever set it up)? Once you have it, since you're a tier-1-approver, `npm run env -- push dev` after fixing your local `.env.dev` would also correct it centrally so this doesn't happen to anyone else next time they `init`.

That's useful — it rules out "the demo key can never return real products," so my theory was wrong as stated. Since that exact key produced a real result before, the key itself isn't structurally broken.

That shifts suspicion elsewhere. Two things stay true regardless of your correction:
- Einstein's `viewed-recently-einstein` call is currently returning a real, non-trivial 871-byte payload (confirmed from your Network tab).
- Nothing then reaches our own rail, because `use-einstein.js`'s own follow-up `getProducts()` lookup against Zimmermann's real catalog is what actually determines whether any of Einstein's recommended IDs turn into renderable cards.

Given the key itself isn't the problem, the more likely explanation now is that whatever Einstein is recommending in *today's* session simply isn't resolving against the catalog right now — which could still be an env/config mismatch (just not the Einstein site ID specifically — e.g. `COMMERCE_API_ORGANIZATION_ID`, currently `f_ecom_bkzk_002` in your `.env.dev`), or could be something more mundane like Einstein's personalization state for this particular guest session not having anything real logged yet and even its 2-product fallback baseline not matching this catalog for some other reason.

This is exactly why the response body itself is the decisive piece of evidence, more so now than before: open that 871-byte `viewed-recently-einstein` response in the Network tab and look at the actual `recs` array — what do the `id` values look like? If they resemble real Zimmermann SKUs (like `25519318M`'s shape), the break is downstream in the `getProducts()` resolution step. content.text:
Yes, exactly right. The OOTB PWA Kit already has a "Recently Viewed" feature — it's not something invented from scratch. It's the same base `<RecommendedProducts recommender={EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED}>` / `CART_RECENTLY_VIEWED` wiring that already existed on PDP and Cart before we touched anything, rendering via base `ProductScroller` + base `ProductTile`.

**What SFCC-83/84 actually overrides:**
- **The visual/component layer** — A5 built a Zimmermann-branded `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` (image-only cards, no price/bag/wishlist) to replace the generic OOTB `ProductScroller`/`ProductTile` styling, but *only* for this one recommender.
- **The empty-state behaviour** — A4's `useRecentlyViewedGate` is genuinely new logic that doesn't exist OOTB at all. Base SFCC just shows whatever Einstein returns, including its 2-product fallback baseline for a brand-new visitor. We added a real "don't show anything until this visitor has actually viewed something (or is registered)" gate on top.
- **The wiring** — A6 added one conditional branch inside the same shared `recommended-products` component: our recommender gets the new rail, every other recommender (Complete-the-Set, Might-Also-Like, Cart May-Also-Like, add-to-cart-modal, both PLP empty-search rails) still hits the exact same untouched OOTB path.

**What's explicitly NOT overridden:** Einstein itself — the API, the site ID config, the `viewed-recently-einstein` recommender's own logic for deciding what to recommend, and the `use-einstein.js` hook's own product-resolution mechanism (`getRecommendations` → `fetchRecProductDetails` → `api.shopperProducts.getProducts`). All of that is the same base SFCC code the OOTB feature already depended on, completely unmodified by this build.

That last point matters for what we've been debugging: if the base, unmodified OOTB Recently Viewed scroller were still active right now with nothing from this build wired in, it would hit the exact same Einstein/catalog resolution chain and show the exact same "nothing renders" symptom under whatever's currently misconfigured. So the empty rail isn't a regression this build introduced — it's an OOTB dependency that was already fragile, just newly visible because A6 finally made this recommender reachable at all.

content.text:
Good instinct — capture this before restarting, since a restart will reset whatever session/cache state made it work. Here's what's most valuable, in priority order:

## 1. Highest value: do you still have the earlier failing attempt in the same Network tab?

If you haven't cleared it, scroll back and find the **earlier** `viewed-recently-einstein` request (from when it wasn't working) sitting alongside this new successful one. Having both lets us directly diff them instead of theorizing. For each one, grab:
- The full request URL (right-click → Copy → Copy as cURL, or just expand it)
- The full response body (click the request → Response tab — not just the size, the actual JSON)

## 2. The Shopper Products lookup that happens right after

This is the one I flagged earlier as the actual resolution point — a call to Zimmermann's real commerce API (**not** `cquotient.com`), with `ids=` in its query string, going out right after `viewed-recently-einstein` returns. Filter Network for `shopper-products` or `qmyt7hks` (your short code) instead of `cquotient`. Grab:
- Full request URL
- Response status
- Response body (does it contain `25519318M`?)

## 3. What did you actually do differently, if anything?

Just reload the same page? Visit a different product first? Log in/out? Wait a while? Even "nothing, I just refreshed" is useful — it tells us whether this is session-state-dependent or genuinely random.

## 4. Any console errors, scrolled further back

Specifically anything mentioning `shopperProducts`, a 401/403/404, or CORS — even ones that appeared once and didn't repeat.

If you've got #1 (both requests side by side), that alone would probably tell us more than everything else combined — a real diff beats guesswork. Grab what you can before restarting.

Let me check something more specific to our own code: whether `RecommendedProducts` actually re-fetches when you navigate between two different PDPs, since React Router can keep the same component instance mounted across `/product/:id` route changes.

Found the mechanism, and it rules out our code as the cause too.

Look at line 1197-1210 — this is **pre-existing base SFCC code, untouched by anything we built**:
```tsx
// The Recently Viewed recommender doesn't use `products`, so instead we
// provide a key to update the recommendations on navigation.
key={location.key}
```
The base template already anticipated exactly this problem: since the Recently Viewed rail has no `products` prop to naturally change per page (unlike "Might Also Like", which passes `products={[product]}`), it forces a full remount on every navigation via React Router's `location.key` — which changes on every route change, including client-side transitions between different `/product/:id` values. A fresh mount means `RecommendedProducts`' data-fetching effect runs from scratch every time, with no stale dependency-array to skip it.

Combined with what we just confirmed — `einstein.sendViewProduct(product)` **is** being called on every real PDP visit (lines 792/797/809) — this means both halves of the pipeline are correct on our end: every view gets reported to Einstein, and the rail re-fetches fresh on every navigation. There's nothing left in our own code to suspect.

That leaves Einstein's own server-side behavior as the explanation, and it's consistent with what you're seeing: real recommendation engines commonly process view events with some delay before they show up in a "recently viewed" response, rather than instantly — and/or this test environment's Einstein instance may have limited real session data to personalize against yet, falling back toward the same result.

**One way to test this theory directly:** view a new product, then wait 30-60 seconds before checking Cart/PDP again (rather than checking immediately) — if the rail eventually picks up the new product after a delay, that confirms propagation lag rather than a bug. If it never changes no matter how long you wait, that's a different, more specific finding worth digging into further on the Einstein-config side.

- **Gate logic** — correct (AC-8 passing is why anything renders at all).
- **Mapper/branch/wiring logic** — verified against real data, matches the exact real product.

- **No client-side caching** — `useEinstein()` uses plain `useState`, no query cache; and the response sizes you saw actually differ between checks (871B → 530B), so these aren't cached/replayed responses — Einstein is computing something fresh each time, it's just not incorporating your new views into this slot.

That last point is the key one: Einstein is responding dynamically, but not with *your session's own recently-viewed history*. Nothing left on our side explains that — the write side and the read side are both wired correctly and firing.

content.text:
Let me go through these one at a time — a few of these don't match what's built or planned, and one I genuinely can't confirm.

**"Going to PLP, PDP, and CART"** — Same correction as before: PLP isn't in scope anywhere for this rail. No `PLP_RECENTLY_VIEWED`-type recommender exists in the base SFCC constants, and nothing in the plan's file manifest touches a PLP file or route for SFCC-83. It's PDP + Cart only, per both what's built and what A6 was scoped against.

**"No consent gating as the JIRA card prescribes"** — I genuinely can't confirm this either way. I haven't seen a Didomi/consent discussion anywhere in this build's plan or code for Recently Viewed specifically. If the ticket states no consent gating is required, that's plausible (Einstein recommendations are often treated as first-party personalization rather than a third-party marketing script), but I haven't verified it against `.docs/prd/regional.md` or the Einstein integration doc. Want me to check those before we treat this as settled?

**"Temporary storage for guests, persistent for auth'd users"** — This doesn't match what got built, and it's worth being precise about why. What we actually have:
- `sessionStorage` is used identically for *everyone*, guest or registered — and it's not a product list at all, just a single boolean-ish gate signal ("has this session viewed anything").
- The actual *content* (which products) never gets stored by our own code at all — it's fetched fresh from Einstein's own server-side history every time, for both guests and registered shoppers alike.

So there's no dual-persistence architecture in this build — no session-scoped-for-guests-vs-persistent-for-registered storage of viewed products. If the JIRA card specifies that as a real requirement, that's missing scope, not a detail we got slightly wrong — it would mean our own code needs to actually persist a product-ID list somewhere (e.g., against the customer record) rather than relying entirely on Einstein's own tracking, which we've just spent considerable effort establishing is unreliable in this environment anyway.

**"View at least 1 and recently viewed is activated"** — This matches AC-8's gate logic, yes (session flag set on one real view, OR registered, activates the gate).

**"See Full History when exceeded — 5 desktop / 3 tablet / 2 mobile"** — This conflates two different things that happen to share the same numbers. 2/3/5 are correct as *how many cards are visible at once* per breakpoint (mobile/tablet/desktop) — that's real, confirmed layout math. But the *CTA trigger threshold* is a single flat number, not per-breakpoint: the plan's closed decision is "link shown when available cards exceed 5" — one number, regardless of viewport, with `No ResizeObserver` explicitly called out as a deliberate choice not to make it viewport-aware. A genuinely per-breakpoint trigger (different overflow thresholds at each screen size) isn't built and isn't what was decided — it would need real rework (including the ResizeObserver the plan deliberately ruled out) if that's actually what the ticket requires.

Do you have a specific AC citing either the consent-gating point or a per-breakpoint CTA threshold? Both would be real, not-yet-built scope if so, worth pinning down before B3.

content.text:
This is a genuinely important set of source documents — thank you for pulling the real ACs. Going through them against what's built and what I told you, I need to walk back two of my own corrections, and there are several real gaps that aren't in the current plan.

## Where I was wrong

**PLP is real, confirmed scope — I was wrong twice.** The ticket states it plainly: "Confirmed surfaces are PLP, PDP, and Cart." My evidence (no base `PLP_RECENTLY_VIEWED` recommender constant, manifest doesn't touch PLP) was true about what's *built*, not about what's *required*. It's real, missing scope — PLP needs its own call site added, using the same `'viewed-recently-einstein'` recommender string (same value as `PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED`/`CART_RECENTLY_VIEWED`) and the same `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail`. Not built anywhere yet.

**The "See Full History" trigger is viewport-relative, not a flat 5.** Both tickets use identical language: *"the number of recently viewed products exceeds the **visible rail width**"* — not "exceeds 5." That's inherently per-breakpoint (2 visible on mobile, 3 tablet, 5 desktop, per A5's own geometry). The plan's closed Open Question #1 ("link shown when available cards exceed 5," explicitly "No ResizeObserver") misread this AC. This needs a real design decision — either a lightweight visibility check we'd been trying to avoid, or a pure-CSS overflow-detection approach — not the flat threshold currently planned for B3.

## Where I was right, now confirmed

**No consent gating belongs in 83/84.** Confirmed directly: Jasmijn's dependency note says "move the consent acceptance criteria to separate user story," and the comment log shows it was removed into SFCC-106 (a separate, blocked ticket). Correct as built — nothing to add here.

## A gap I need to correct myself on

I told you two messages ago that "temporary for guests, persistent for auth'd users" was missing frontend architecture. Rereading the ticket's own Assumptions: **"The storage of Recently Viewed is handled by SFCC."** That means the ticket itself doesn't expect our frontend to build persistence — it expects Einstein/SFCC to handle it transparently. So this isn't missing frontend scope; it's the *same* Einstein/SFCC-112 configuration gap we already spent a long investigation on (the "stuck on one product" bug). The architecture we built (delegate entirely to Einstein, no local product-list storage) is actually correct per the ticket's own stated assumption — the gap is entirely on the Einstein-config side, already tracked.

## New gaps from Jasmijn's latest comment (SFCC-84, 6 hours ago)

This one's dense and introduces real card-behavior requirements B1 doesn't currently cover:

- **Was/now pricing required** ("price (incl. was/now)") — A3's mapper (`selectRecentlyViewedCard`) deliberately produces `currentPrice` only, no `originalPrice`, per its own docblock. B2 is currently planned to reuse A3's mapper — that won't satisfy this AC. Needs either an extended mapper or a second one.
- **Multi-image hover-carousel required** ("arrows appear... click through the product images") — A3's mapper only ever selects one primary image, and the rail's own variation deliberately suppresses gallery mode entirely. The full-history page needs real multi-image support that nothing we've built provides yet.
- Desktop hover (size-selector reveal, price-hide, image swap), mobile (no size-selector), and out-of-stock (greyed cart + notify-me) are all likely already covered by the existing `plp` variation from SFCC-236 — worth confirming, not re-building, but I haven't independently verified each one against this specific card yet.

**One more loose end:** AC-84 says item count displays "in the top right of the page" — a specific position B1's spec doesn't currently capture (it just has an abstract `itemCountLabel` prop). And the comment references "SFCC-80" for canonical PLP tile behavior — a ticket I haven't seen; worth checking whether it has anything beyond SFCC-236.

---

Given the number of real gaps here (PLP surface, the CTA trigger mechanism, was/now pricing, multi-image support), do you want me to update the plan file with all of this first so it's the accurate source of truth, or work through these one at a time starting with whichever you think is most blocking?

36	 * — not hand-rolled), plus the two fields `fetchRecProductDetails` bolts on that have no SDK
37	 * equivalent:
38	 */
39	export type RecentlyViewedProduct = ShopperProductsTypes.Product & {
40	  /** Set by `fetchRecProductDetails` to `rec.id`. Guaranteed present and equal to `Product.id`
41	   *  for every entry that function produces (it already filters out any rec with no matching
42	   *  product before this shape exists at all) — read this rather than `.id` only because it's
43	   *  the field the real runtime hook explicitly produces this way. */
44	  productId: string;
45	  /** The same function's own quick single-reference image (Einstein's own `rec.imageUrl`/
46	   *  `rec.productName`), distinct from the full product's own `imageGroups` array below — used
47	   *  as a fallback only when `imageGroups` filtering comes up empty. See `selectPrimaryImage`. */
48	  image?: { disBaseLink?: string; alt?: string };
49	};
50	
51	/** Formats a bare amount for the storefront. Injected so this module stays free of react-intl,
52	 *  mirroring `productInfo.ts`'s own `FormatPrice` shape. */
53	export type FormatPrice = (amount: number, currency: string) => string;
54	
55	/**
56	 * The subset of `ZimmProductCardBaseProps` this mapper populates. Deliberately excludes
57	 * `headingLevel` and `variation` — both are render-context decisions belonging to the container
58	 * step that maps recs through this mapper and renders the rail (SFCC-83's A6 step), which supplies
59	 * `headingLevel` uniformly for every card and adds `variation: 'recentlyViewed'` itself when
60	 * spreading this output into `<ZimmProductCard>` — the rail organism itself (A5) takes already-full
61	 * `ZimmProductCardProps` objects, so variation must already be set before it sees them. A pure data
62	 * mapper choosing a heading level would conflate a data concern with a layout one. Also excludes `hoverImage`/`images` — this
63	 * mapper only ever returns one image (`primaryImage`); see `selectPrimaryImage`'s own docblock
64	 * for why.
65	 */
66	export type RecentlyViewedCard = Pick<
67	  ZimmProductCardBaseProps,
68	  'id' | 'href' | 'name' | 'primaryImage' | 'currentPrice'
69	>;
70	
71	/** The correctly-sized product image view, per AGENTS.md's image-sizing guidance: never serve an
72	 *  arbitrary-sized image at thumbnail size. Named rather than inlined per conventions.md's
73	 *  no-magic-strings rule — this is a real, semantic SFCC image `viewType` key. */
74	const MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE = 'medium';
75	
76	/**
77	 * Resolves the one image this mapper ever returns. `hoverImage`/`images` are never populated —
78	 * SFCC-83 AC 3 asks for "the product's index image" (singular), and the `recentlyViewed`
79	 * variation renders neither a hover-swap nor a gallery (see `zimmProductCard/index.tsx`'s
80	 * `recentlyViewed` row: `showHoverImageSwap: false`, and its render branch never forwards
81	 * `images` at all).
82	 *
83	 * Prefers `filterImageGroups` at `viewType: 'medium'` (a real, correctly-sized product image) —
84	 * `variationValues` is deliberately empty: a Recently Viewed rec is already one specific product,
85	 * not a search hit needing a variant pick the way `liveProductCardDemoMapper.ts`'s own
86	 * `resolveDemoVariant` handles, so that logic does not apply here. Falls back to Einstein's own
87	 * flat `image` field only when that filtering produces nothing usable — see
88	 * `RecentlyViewedProduct.image`'s own comment for what that field is.
89	 *
90	 * @returns `null` when neither source has a usable `src`. `ZimmProductCardMediaImage.alt` is
91	 *   required and non-empty, so there is no safe placeholder card to build without a real image —
92	 *   a card with an invented placeholder `src` would need an asset this codebase has no confirmed
93	 *   token or precedent for, so "no usable image" is treated the same as "no usable name" in
94	 *   `selectRecentlyViewedCard` below: a hard gate that yields no card at all. Returning `null`
95	 *   here is the only option that structurally cannot violate the non-empty-`alt` contract, since
96	 *   there is no returned object for `alt` to be empty on.
97	 */
98	const selectPrimaryImage = (product: RecentlyViewedProduct, productName: string): ZimmProductCardImage | null => {
99	  const filteredGroups = filterImageGroups(product.imageGroups ?? [], {
100	    viewType: MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE,
101	    variationValues: {},
102	  }) as ShopperProductsTypes.ImageGroup[];
103	  const [groupImage] = filteredGroups[0]?.images ?? [];
104	
105	  const src = groupImage ? groupImage.disBaseLink || groupImage.link : product.image?.disBaseLink;
106	  if (!src) return null;
107	
108	  // ZimmProductCardMediaImage.alt is required and non-empty (unlike base ProductTile's
109	  // decorative alt: '' convention) — mirrors liveProductCardDemoMapper.ts's own fallback exactly.
110	  const alt = (groupImage ? groupImage.alt : product.image?.alt)?.trim() || productName;
111	  return { src, alt };
112	};
113	
114	/**
115	 * @param product - The merged Einstein rec + Commerce API product `fetchRecProductDetails`
116	 *   produces, or `undefined`/`null` while that data is not yet available.
117	 * @param formatPrice - Currency formatter, normally `intl.formatNumber`.
118	 * @returns Props for the `recentlyViewed` `ZimmProductCard` variation, or `null` when the rec has
119	 *   no usable name or no usable image — never a broken card, never a throw.
120	 */
121	export const selectRecentlyViewedCard = (
122	  product: RecentlyViewedProduct | undefined | null,
123	  formatPrice: FormatPrice,
124	): RecentlyViewedCard | null => {
125	  if (!product?.name) return null;
126	
127	  const primaryImage = selectPrimaryImage(product, product.name);
128	  if (!primaryImage) return null;
129	
130	  return {
131	    // Reads productId, not the SDK Product's own `id` — see RecentlyViewedProduct.productId's
132	    // own comment for why (guaranteed equal in practice, but productId is the field the real
133	    // runtime hook explicitly produces this way).
134	    id: product.productId,
135	    href: productUrlBuilder({ id: product.productId }),
136	    name: product.name,
137	    primaryImage,
138	    // No hardcoded fallback currency — if either is absent, skip formatting rather than guess,
139	    // matching productInfo.ts's own "no hardcoded fallback currency" comment.
140	    currentPrice:
141	      typeof product.price === 'number' && product.currency ? formatPrice(product.price, product.currency) : undefined,
142	  };
143	};
144

Multi-image, yes — fully agreed, and now directly confirmed: PLP's own mapper (`productListCardMapper.ts`) already builds a real multi-image array (`selectGalleryImages`), proving the `plp` variation genuinely renders the hover-carousel today. - PLP's own mapper, separately: `originalPrice: undefined` — with its own comment saying the same thing: *"a real 'Was' price needs pricebook-level discount detection this integration doesn't attempt."*

So it's not that A3 is missing something the `plp` variant already solved elsewhere — **neither mapper in this codebase currently does real was/now detection.** The component can render it (confirmed via SFCC-236's own `f2842ac` was/now-price fix), but the actual pricebook-discount logic to *populate* `originalPrice` correctly hasn't been built anywhere yet, on either surface. That's a genuinely separate, harder piece of work than reusing an existing pattern — worth deciding whether it's in scope for B2 now, or another documented gap for the PR body, same treatment as Finding 28.

# SFCC-236: fix two live-testing regressions in ZimmProductCard

## Context

While testing PR #85 (`feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component`) live, Marcel found two
real bugs in the shared `ZimmProductCard` family:

**(a) A recent hover-reveal fix broke keyboard nav and VoiceOver.** The most recent fix on this
branch (`983bddf`) replaced `:focus-within` with `:has(:focus-visible)` across five hover-reveal
sites, specifically to stop the carousel arrows (and everything else gated the same way) from
staying visible after a mouse click even once the mouse moved away — a real, correctly-diagnosed
bug, and that part of the fix is not being reverted. The regression is elsewhere: every one of
those five reveals uses `display: 'none'` as its "hidden" state, gated behind an *interaction*
heuristic (`:hover`/`:has(:focus-visible)`). `display: none` unconditionally strips an element
from the accessibility tree — it answers "is this painted," not "does this exist for assistive
tech," and this recipe has been using it to answer both questions at once. `:focus-visible` is
itself a browser heuristic for "does this focus event look keyboard-like," and VoiceOver-driven
focus (VO+Arrow, rotor, swipe) is not guaranteed to satisfy it in every engine — a real, documented
mismatch, and *not* a touch-only concern: `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` is true on any Mac
trackpad, so a VoiceOver user on ordinary MacBook hardware is exactly the population this gate
applies to. If that heuristic never matches for a given user, all five reveals (carousel arrows,
Home's price reveal, PLP/Wishlist's price↔size-selector swap, notify-me) stay invisible to them
for the entire session, no matter how they navigate. A secondary, lower-severity effect confirmed
alongside it: because these controls only exist as Tab stops *while* the interaction condition is
currently true, Shift+Tab entry into the card from something after it lands on the last
unconditionally-visible stop (the bag button) — the user has already tabbed past controls that,
at that instant, didn't exist yet, and must reverse direction to reach them. (Forward-Tab is fine:
landing on the always-present scroll container triggers the reveal before reaching the arrows.)

**(b) Multi-image cards don't respond to touch swipe on mobile.** The slide indicator renders
correctly (so the image data and gallery logic are fine), but swiping the image doesn't page
through it at all. Root cause: the organism's whole-card stretched-link overlay
(`[data-card-slot="content"] a::after`, `position: absolute; inset: 0`) resolves its containing
block to the organism root — because `ZimmProductCardContent` never sets `position` anywhere —
so it's sized to the *entire* card, image included, not just the name-link row. That overlay
carries no `z-index`, and the recipe already lifts exactly three things above it (`close`,
`carousel`, buttons inside `content`) — the media/gallery scroll region was never added to that
list. A touch swipe on the image actually starts on the invisible overlay `<a>`, so the browser's
native swipe-scroll gesture never engages the real scroll container at all.

Both root causes were confirmed via direct investigation of this exact code (file/line citations
below) before any fix was designed, and both fixes reuse patterns already shipped elsewhere in
this same codebase rather than inventing anything new — `ZimmColourSwatchGroup`'s already-tested
off-page-swatch technique for (a), and this recipe's own existing z-index-lift pattern for (b).

## Fix (b) — swipe blocked by the stretched-link overlay

**File:** `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/zimmProductCard.css.ts`

- Add a fourth lift entry alongside the existing three (currently lines 240-253):
  ```
  [`[data-card-slot="${CARD_SLOT.media}"]`]: { zIndex: 1 },
  ```
  `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own root is already `position: 'relative'` (its own recipe), so only
  `zIndex` is needed here — identical in shape to the existing `close`/`carousel` entries.
- Extend docblock point 2 (the "lifting every interactive control" explanation, ~lines 62-101)
  with a new dated fix note, continuing this file's own Fix 1/Fix 3/Fix H lettered convention,
  explaining the media/gallery region needed the same lift the click targets already got, and
  that this was missed because clicking `close`/`carousel`/content-buttons was checked live but
  swiping the image itself never was.
- Extend `index.test.tsx`'s existing z-index-lift describe block (or add a sibling one) to assert
  the new entry's object shape, matching that file's own established idiom for these proofs.

**Verification:** jsdom cannot prove this (no stacking-context resolution — this file's own
"KNOWN LIMITATION" docblock already says so). Needs a real touch check: Playwright's
`mobile-chrome` project with a real drag/swipe gesture on the image, or Marcel's own device,
confirming the gallery pages and the indicator updates.

## Fix (a) — hover-reveal content invisible to VoiceOver / skipped on Shift+Tab

**Files:** `zimmProductCard.css.ts` (all 5 reveal sites) and
`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`
(carousel's own base state)

**Recommended fix** — keep every one of the five reveal targets permanently present in the DOM,
focusable, and in the accessibility tree at all times. Stop using `display` to express "hidden";
use the exact technique `ZimmColourSwatchGroup` already ships for its own off-page swatches
(confirmed real, `molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx:215`:
`{ position: 'absolute', clipPath: 'inset(50%)' }`):

- **Hidden (default) state:** `position: 'absolute'`, `clipPath: 'inset(50%)'` instead of
  `display: 'none'` — out of flow (no layout gap, same as today), paints nothing, but stays in
  the DOM/tab order/accessibility tree.
- **Revealed state** (same `&:hover [...]` / `&:has(:focus-visible) [...]` selectors, byte-for-byte
  unchanged): `position: 'static'`, `clipPath: 'none'` instead of `display: 'block'/'flex'`.
- Applies at all 5 sites in `zimmProductCard.css.ts`: Home price reveal (~293-297, 323-325),
  PLP/Wishlist price hide (~330-332, 338-340), PLP/Wishlist size-selector reveal (~344-346,
  348-350), notify-me reveal (~359-362, 364-366), carousel arrow reveal (~379-384).
- `zimmProductCardMedia.css.ts`'s `carousel` part: its own unconditional base `display: 'none'`
  becomes the same clip-path equivalent (already `position: 'absolute'` unconditionally, so only
  the hidden-state property changes).
- **Carousel-specific addition:** the wrapper deliberately sets `pointerEvents: 'none'` with each
  `arrowButton` individually re-enabling `pointerEvents: 'auto'` (so clicks in the empty centre
  pass through to the image). Once the wrapper is no longer `display:none`, add an explicit
  belt-and-braces rule in the organism recipe — `[data-card-slot="carousel"] button` gets
  `pointerEvents: 'none'` by default and `'auto'` only in the two revealed selectors — rather than
  relying on clip-path's hit-testing suppression alone. (Price/size-selector/notify-me need no
  equivalent — none of them sets `pointerEvents` at all today.)

**Why this is the recommended path, not one of several open options** (a JS-tracked hover/focus
state was considered and rejected): there is no signal exposed to page-level JavaScript, any more
than to CSS, that says "this focus event was AT-originated." A hand-rolled heuristic (e.g.
flagging `focusin` as non-keyboard when preceded by `pointerdown`) has exactly the same blind spot
as the native `:focus-visible` heuristic it would be reimplementing. It would also break this
organism's own stated design principle ("CSS alone decides what is visible... no JS-tracked reveal
state," `index.tsx` ~349-350) and introduce real SSR/hydration-mismatch risk pure CSS structurally
can't have, for no correctness gain.

**Why this doesn't reintroduce the `983bddf` stuck-open bug:** that bug was entirely about *when*
`:has(:focus-visible)` matches (a click-focused button not un-matching on mouseout until focus
moved elsewhere) — a selector-matching-timing question, completely orthogonal to which property
the matched rule sets. The trigger selectors aren't touched at all; only the property values
inside the already-existing blocks change.

**Docblock updates:** extend/rewrite docblock points 3 and 6 and the "Fix H" note with a new dated
fix note (continuing the lettered sequence), stating explicitly that Fix H's `:focus-within` →
`:has(:focus-visible)` swap was and remains correct for the paint-timing question it solved, and
that the actual defect was using `display` (an AT-tree-removal property) to answer a different
question than the one it should answer. Explicitly out of scope, left as `display:none`: the
permanent, non-hover-capable-pointer hides (`sizeSelectorUnavailable`'s unconditional size-chip
hide, the PLP-mobile bag-icon hide) — separate, correct, Figma-confirmed, non-regressed decisions,
since nothing about them is gated behind an interaction heuristic.

**Test updates:** the existing `.matches()`-based selector-proof describe block in
`index.test.tsx` needs no change (it doesn't depend on which property the matched rule sets). Any
structural/object-shape assertions elsewhere in the same file checking the recipe's declared
`display` values for these 5 sites need updating to the new property values — identify the exact
assertions at implementation time against the real current file, don't guess line numbers here.

**New real-browser verification** (jsdom can't prove any of this): this repo already has
scaffolded-but-empty Playwright a11y projects (`playwright.config.js`'s `a11y-desktop` →
`e2e/tests/a11y/desktop`, `a11y-mobile` → `e2e/tests/a11y/mobile`; both Chromium-only, no WebKit
project configured — not touching `playwright.config.js` itself, only adding specs inside the
already-existing target directories). Add specs for:

1. **Accessibility-tree presence** — load a card in its default (non-hovered, non-focused) state
   and assert, via a real Chromium accessibility-tree snapshot, that the size-chip radiogroup,
   notify-me button, and carousel arrow buttons are present with correct role/name — proving
   AT-tree presence no longer depends on any hover/focus-visible condition having matched.
2. **Tab-order parity** — forward-Tab from before the card and Shift+Tab from after it, asserting
   the stop set/sequence is now identical in both directions (today Shift+Tab skips the
   reveal-gated controls entirely).
3. **No regression on the original stuck-open bug** — real mouse click on an arrow button, move
   the mouse off the card, assert the control is no longer visually painted by reading
   `getComputedStyle(el).clipPath` directly (Playwright's default `toBeVisible()` is primarily a
   bounding-box/`visibility` check and may not reliably catch clip-path-based hiding).

**Honest limitation, not skippable:** the actual disputed claim — does real VoiceOver announce and
activate these controls — can't be fully closed out by any automated check above. Chromium's
accessibility tree isn't the engine VoiceOver actually talks to (WebKit), no WebKit Playwright
project exists in this repo, and Playwright can't drive real VoiceOver at all. The automated specs
give strong, real regression-prevention signal (AT-tree presence + tab-order parity are both real,
previously-uncaught bugs), but final confirmation needs one manual pass from Marcel: navigate a
card via VO+Right-Arrow/rotor only (no mouse, no literal Tab keypress) on real macOS Safari +
VoiceOver, confirming price, the size-chip radiogroup, notify-me, and the carousel arrows are all
announced and activatable via VO+Space.

## Verification (both fixes)

1. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
2. Full local Storybook build + `test-storybook --ci` — same pattern used earlier on this branch
   for the axe-contrast fix; confirms no regression across the whole story set.
3. Updated/new Vitest assertions in both `index.test.tsx` files pass.
4. New Playwright a11y specs (AT-tree presence, tab-order parity, stuck-open non-regression) pass.
5. Real-device/manual checks, both required before calling this done:
   - Real touch swipe (device or Playwright mobile-chrome touch simulation) confirms gallery
     paging works.
   - Real VoiceOver + Safari pass (Marcel, one-time) confirms AT reachability/activation for all

1	# SFCC-83 + SFCC-84 — Build Plan
2	
3	**Produced:** 2026-09-06 · **Gate:** `findings.md` (four passes, cleared at the 2026-09-06 adjudication)
4	**Base branch:** `feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component` (PR #85, open, unmerged)
5	
6	## 1. Goal statement
7	
8	Build the Recently Viewed rail and its full-history page per **SFCC-83** and **SFCC-84** (ACs in Jira
9	`customfield_10231`), designed in **`Zimmermann_Design_System_2026` component set `40000587:38471`**
10	(Desktop `40000307:12444`, Tablet `40000730:13363`, Mobile `40000538:25030` — all authoritative,
11	corroborated by PDP-template instances `7998:13508` / `8272:28947`), with SFCC-84's page from the
12	**provisional** `Zimmermann_Designs` `3332:35655` — following `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`
13	(token hierarchy) and `.claude/rules/components.md` (container/presentational split), and extending
14	**PR #85 / SFCC-236's** `ZimmProductCard` family via a **new `VARIATION_CONFIG` entry** (not a new
15	card), a **copy-first override of `recommended-products/`**, and **co-located `<name>.css.ts`**
16	recipes registered in `theme/components/index.ts`.
17	
18	Scope follows `.docs/prd/search.md` §7.4 (PDP + Cart). **PLP is out**; SFCC-83 AC 9 knowingly not met.
19	**No consent gating** (development-phase carve-out, Marcel 2026-09-06) — must be stated in both PR
20	bodies; must not reach production.
21	
22	## 2. Scale call
23	
24	### Architecture fork — resolved: override `recommended-products/`, which removes the Cart port
25	
26	Verified directly at `node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev/configs/webpack/overrides-plugin.js`.
27	`isFromExtends` returns true when the request names `@salesforce/retail-react-app` **and the issuing
28	file is not itself inside `overrides/`**. The plugin's own comment (lines 116–127): *"This will return
29	true if the issuer is a file in a base template... This allow the base template to import from
30	overrides."* Implementation: `this.extends.includes(pkgName) && !filepath.includes(issuerPath)`.
31	
32	Base Cart imports at `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/cart/index.jsx:36`:
33	`import RecommendedProducts from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/recommended-products'`
34	— a package-path import issued from a base file, so it **is** redirected once our override exists.
35	Base Cart is itself loaded by base `routes.jsx` via a relative `import('./pages/cart')`, which is not
36	redirected — so base Cart keeps rendering and picks up our override for free.
37	
38	**Consequence: the ~2,460-line Cart copy-first (`index.jsx` 1515 + 8 real partials ≈ 948) is not
39	required.** This departed from adjudication item #10 ("we only have to copy-first for cart"), in the
40	direction of *less* work. **APPROVED by Marcel, 2026-09-06**, on the evidence that this is already the
41	dominant pattern in this repo: nine component overrides shadow base paths and are reached purely by
42	the resolver (`icons` at 64 base import sites — and mandated by AGENTS.md — `responsive` 12,
43	`product-view` 6, `drawer-menu`/`list-menu` 2 each, `header`/`footer` 1 each). The single page port
44	(`product-detail`) exists only because base `routes.jsx` loads pages by *relative* import, which the
45	resolver never redirects — a constraint that does not apply to components. Open Question 5 is closed.
46	
47	**Caveat:** this is a *build-time webpack* resolver. It runs in the dev server and production build
48	only — **not** Storybook (`.storybook/main.js` aliases straight to `node_modules`) and **not** Vitest.
49	So the Cart behaviour cannot be proven by any automated test in this repo; it must be checked in the
50	running app. That is why A1's pause is a hard gate.
51	
52	Cost of this choice: the override module loads at **four base import sites serving eight rails**, not
53	five as an earlier draft of this plan stated:
54	
55	| Base import site | Rails | Takes the new branch? |
56	|---|---|---|
57	| `app/pages/cart/index.jsx:36` | Cart Recently Viewed, Cart May-Also-Like | **Yes** (1 of 2) |
58	| `app/pages/product-detail/index.jsx:40` | *(shadowed by our own PDP override — 3 rails)* | **Yes** (1 of 3) |
59	| `app/hooks/use-add-to-cart-modal.js:30` | add-to-cart modal (`pdp-similar-items`) | No |
60	| `app/pages/product-list/partials/empty-results.jsx:20` | PLP empty-search top-sellers, most-viewed | No |
61	
62	It is therefore a **faithful port plus exactly one branch**, keyed off
63	`EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED` (`'viewed-recently-einstein'` — the same string as
64	`CART_RECENTLY_VIEWED`, `constants.js:156,160`). **Two rails take the new branch; the other six must
65	render identically before and after** — a hard pass criterion.
66	
67	**🔴 Correction, 2026-09-06 — the PDP row above is misleading, verified directly against
68	`overrides-plugin.js`'s actual source, not just this plan's earlier paraphrase of it.** The
69	table's "Yes (1 of 3)" for `product-detail/index.jsx:40` describes the **base** file's import —
70	but that file is shadowed by our own PDP override page and never loads. What actually matters is
71	*our own* `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx`'s import of `RecommendedProducts`, and
72	`isFromExtends` (`overrides-plugin.js:128-146`) returns **false** whenever the issuing file is
73	itself inside `overrides/` — its own doc comment says so plainly: *"This will return false if the
74	issuer is a file in the overrides dir."* Our PDP page's current package-path import
75	(`product-detail/index.tsx:59`) is therefore **not** redirected to our override, at all, regardless
76	of `Island`, scroll position, or Einstein data — none of which were ever the actual blocker.
77	Discovered live during A1's mandatory Cart/PDP verification (Marcel: zero marker fires on PDP even
78	after a full scroll to the bottom, while Cart fired correctly and repeatedly).
79	
80	**Consequence, and why this isn't just a testing nuisance:** as originally planned, PDP's Recently
81	Viewed rail would never render even after A6 lands the branch — Cart would work, PDP would
82	silently not, and SFCC-83's PDP requirement would ship broken with no test catching it (no PR-time
83	E2E on this path either, per the Loop depth section below). **Fix, folded into A6 (Marcel,
84	2026-09-06):** change `product-detail/index.tsx:59`'s `RecommendedProducts` import from the base
85	package path to a relative path pointing at our own override, per
86	`.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`'s existing "Importing an already-overridden component from a
87	new component" rule — the exact same doctrine
88	A6 already applies to `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` below, just missed for `RecommendedProducts` itself
89	in the original draft of this plan. See A6's updated step and pass criteria.
90	
91	Two of those six are on **PLP**, explicitly descoped at adjudication #2. The override *loads* there
92	but its branch never fires (those rails use `EMPTY_SEARCH_RESULTS_*` recommenders), so **no Recently
93	Viewed rail appears on PLP**. State this in the PR body so a reviewer does not read the override's
94	presence on PLP as scope creep.
95	
96	Rejected alternative — re-homing the fetch into a new Zimmermann container: still needs a per-surface
97	caller, and Cart is a base page we cannot pass props to without the 2,460-line port. Buys nothing,
98	costs the port.
99	
100	### Branch: ONE, single PR (Marcel, 2026-09-06)
101	
102	**`feature/SFCC-83-84_recently-viewed`**, cut from `feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component`.
103	
104	An earlier draft proposed two stacked branches. **Marcel chose a single branch / single PR to
105	maintain**, which is now the plan. Step IDs keep their `A*`/`B*` prefixes (they read as "rail work"
106	and "page work") but execute as one sequence on one branch:
107	
108	> A1 → A2 → A3 → A4 → A5 → A6 → B1 → B2 → B3 → GATES
109	
110	**What this buys:**
111	- **The AC 5 / AC 84-1 split disappears.** Those two ACs are the *same* requirement. On two branches
112	  the rail would have shipped with an unsupplied `seeAllHref` and SFCC-83 could not be marked Done
113	  until the second PR merged. On one branch the link and its destination land together — no
114	  interim state where the link points at a 404, and both stories close on one merge.
115	- One review conversation, one CI run, one changelog entry.
116	
117	**What it costs, stated plainly:**
118	- **The four-team CODEOWNERS fan-out on `overrides/app/routes.tsx` (`CODEOWNERS:94`) now applies to
119	  the whole PR**, not just the page half. Every reviewer group sees the full diff.
120	- **The provisional-design page now gates the confirmed-design rail.** SFCC-83's rail is authoritative
121	  at all three viewports and corroborated twice; SFCC-84's page comes entirely from a provisional
122	  source. If the page's design is challenged in review, the rail — which re-skins two live surfaces
123	  and has no such doubt — waits with it. Accepted deliberately; flag it in the PR body so a reviewer
124	  knows the rail can be split back out if the page stalls.
125	
126	### Loop depth
127	
128	Two stories, ~22 files, one 236-line copy-first file. Mid-size build.
129	
130	- **Full implementer → tester → scorer** on A2, A3, A4, A5, B1, B3 — where a silent wrong answer
131	  ships (a variation flag misread from Figma; an ordering/cap bug of exactly the shape the FED
132	  handbook's finding 18 warns encodes itself into a passing test; an AC-8 gate that never fires).
133	- **Implementer + scorer only** on A1, A6, B2, A7, B4 — their gate is mechanical (`tsc`, `npm run
134	  test`, a diff read); a tester pass adds a round-trip without adding a check.
135	
136	**Deliberately dropped, with reasons:**
137	- **No Playwright/E2E.** Adding an allow-list group to `.github/workflows/qa.yml` is Tier 1 CI config
138	  (`CODEOWNERS:65`) — out of scope. Without it these paths resolve to `e2e_scope: skip` and there is
139	  no PR-time E2E run either way (`.claude/rules/testing.md` > Change-scoped E2E). State this in both
140	  PR bodies rather than implying coverage exists.
141	- **No page-level Storybook story.** No page in this repo has one; the presentational organisms carry
142	  the stories, matching `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/*.stories.tsx`.
143	- **No new `theme/components/*Shared.ts`.** Both recipes derive media queries from `breakpoints`
144	  imported from `app/theme/foundation` — one source, two importers, no copied literal.
145	- **No visual-regression tooling.** None exists; Figma parity is checked by eye against named nodes.
146	
147	## 3. File manifest
148	
149	Tiers from `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md`, `.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md`, `CODEOWNERS` — **never**
150	`.claude/registry/*.md`. **No Tier 1 file is touched. Nothing is BLOCKED.**
151	
152	### Rail work (SFCC-83)
153
