# SFCC-83 + SFCC-84 — Build Plan

**Produced:** 2026-09-06 · **Gate:** `findings.md` (four passes, cleared at the 2026-09-06 adjudication)
**Base branch:** `feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component` (PR #85, open, unmerged)

## 1. Goal statement

Build the Recently Viewed rail and its full-history page per **SFCC-83** and **SFCC-84** (ACs in Jira
`customfield_10231`), designed in **`Zimmermann_Design_System_2026` component set `40000587:38471`**
(Desktop `40000307:12444`, Tablet `40000730:13363`, Mobile `40000538:25030` — all authoritative,
corroborated by PDP-template instances `7998:13508` / `8272:28947`), with SFCC-84's page from the
**provisional** `Zimmermann_Designs` `3332:35655` — following `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`
(token hierarchy) and `.claude/rules/components.md` (container/presentational split), and extending
**PR #85 / SFCC-236's** `ZimmProductCard` family via a **new `VARIATION_CONFIG` entry** (not a new
card), a **copy-first override of `recommended-products/`**, and **co-located `<name>.css.ts`**
recipes registered in `theme/components/index.ts`.

Scope follows `.docs/prd/search.md` §7.4 (PDP + Cart). **PLP is out**; SFCC-83 AC 9 knowingly not met.
**No consent gating** (development-phase carve-out, Marcel 2026-09-06) — must be stated in both PR
bodies; must not reach production.

## 2. Scale call

### Architecture fork — resolved: override `recommended-products/`, which removes the Cart port

Verified directly at `node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev/configs/webpack/overrides-plugin.js`.
`isFromExtends` returns true when the request names `@salesforce/retail-react-app` **and the issuing
file is not itself inside `overrides/`**. The plugin's own comment (lines 116–127): *"This will return
true if the issuer is a file in a base template... This allow the base template to import from
overrides."* Implementation: `this.extends.includes(pkgName) && !filepath.includes(issuerPath)`.

Base Cart imports at `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/cart/index.jsx:36`:
`import RecommendedProducts from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/recommended-products'`
— a package-path import issued from a base file, so it **is** redirected once our override exists.
Base Cart is itself loaded by base `routes.jsx` via a relative `import('./pages/cart')`, which is not
redirected — so base Cart keeps rendering and picks up our override for free.

**Consequence: the ~2,460-line Cart copy-first (`index.jsx` 1515 + 8 real partials ≈ 948) is not
required.** This departed from adjudication item #10 ("we only have to copy-first for cart"), in the
direction of *less* work. **APPROVED by Marcel, 2026-09-06**, on the evidence that this is already the
dominant pattern in this repo: nine component overrides shadow base paths and are reached purely by
the resolver (`icons` at 64 base import sites — and mandated by AGENTS.md — `responsive` 12,
`product-view` 6, `drawer-menu`/`list-menu` 2 each, `header`/`footer` 1 each). The single page port
(`product-detail`) exists only because base `routes.jsx` loads pages by *relative* import, which the
resolver never redirects — a constraint that does not apply to components. Open Question 5 is closed.

**Caveat:** this is a *build-time webpack* resolver. It runs in the dev server and production build
only — **not** Storybook (`.storybook/main.js` aliases straight to `node_modules`) and **not** Vitest.
So the Cart behaviour cannot be proven by any automated test in this repo; it must be checked in the
running app. That is why A1's pause is a hard gate.

Cost of this choice: the override module loads at **four base import sites serving eight rails**, not
five as an earlier draft of this plan stated:

| Base import site | Rails | Takes the new branch? |
|---|---|---|
| `app/pages/cart/index.jsx:36` | Cart Recently Viewed, Cart May-Also-Like | **Yes** (1 of 2) |
| `app/pages/product-detail/index.jsx:40` | *(shadowed by our own PDP override — 3 rails)* | **Yes** (1 of 3) |
| `app/hooks/use-add-to-cart-modal.js:30` | add-to-cart modal (`pdp-similar-items`) | No |
| `app/pages/product-list/partials/empty-results.jsx:20` | PLP empty-search top-sellers, most-viewed | No |

It is therefore a **faithful port plus exactly one branch**, keyed off
`EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED` (`'viewed-recently-einstein'` — the same string as
`CART_RECENTLY_VIEWED`, `constants.js:156,160`). **Two rails take the new branch; the other six must
render identically before and after** — a hard pass criterion.

**🔴 Correction, 2026-09-06 — the PDP row above is misleading, verified directly against
`overrides-plugin.js`'s actual source, not just this plan's earlier paraphrase of it.** The
table's "Yes (1 of 3)" for `product-detail/index.jsx:40` describes the **base** file's import —
but that file is shadowed by our own PDP override page and never loads. What actually matters is
*our own* `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx`'s import of `RecommendedProducts`, and
`isFromExtends` (`overrides-plugin.js:128-146`) returns **false** whenever the issuing file is
itself inside `overrides/` — its own doc comment says so plainly: *"This will return false if the
issuer is a file in the overrides dir."* Our PDP page's current package-path import
(`product-detail/index.tsx:59`) is therefore **not** redirected to our override, at all, regardless
of `Island`, scroll position, or Einstein data — none of which were ever the actual blocker.
Discovered live during A1's mandatory Cart/PDP verification (Marcel: zero marker fires on PDP even
after a full scroll to the bottom, while Cart fired correctly and repeatedly).

**Consequence, and why this isn't just a testing nuisance:** as originally planned, PDP's Recently
Viewed rail would never render even after A6 lands the branch — Cart would work, PDP would
silently not, and SFCC-83's PDP requirement would ship broken with no test catching it (no PR-time
E2E on this path either, per the Loop depth section below). **Fix, folded into A6 (Marcel,
2026-09-06):** change `product-detail/index.tsx:59`'s `RecommendedProducts` import from the base
package path to a relative path pointing at our own override, per
`.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`'s existing "Importing an already-overridden component from a
new component" rule — the exact same doctrine
A6 already applies to `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` below, just missed for `RecommendedProducts` itself
in the original draft of this plan. See A6's updated step and pass criteria.

Two of those six are on **PLP**, explicitly descoped at adjudication #2. The override *loads* there
but its branch never fires (those rails use `EMPTY_SEARCH_RESULTS_*` recommenders), so **no Recently
Viewed rail appears on PLP**. State this in the PR body so a reviewer does not read the override's
presence on PLP as scope creep.

Rejected alternative — re-homing the fetch into a new Zimmermann container: still needs a per-surface
caller, and Cart is a base page we cannot pass props to without the 2,460-line port. Buys nothing,
costs the port.

### Branch: ONE, single PR (Marcel, 2026-09-06)

**`feature/SFCC-83-84_recently-viewed`**, cut from `feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component`.

An earlier draft proposed two stacked branches. **Marcel chose a single branch / single PR to
maintain**, which is now the plan. Step IDs keep their `A*`/`B*` prefixes (they read as "rail work"
and "page work") but execute as one sequence on one branch:

> A1 → A2 → A3 → A4 → A5 → A6 → B1 → B2 → B3 → GATES

**What this buys:**
- **The AC 5 / AC 84-1 split disappears.** Those two ACs are the *same* requirement. On two branches
  the rail would have shipped with an unsupplied `seeAllHref` and SFCC-83 could not be marked Done
  until the second PR merged. On one branch the link and its destination land together — no
  interim state where the link points at a 404, and both stories close on one merge.
- One review conversation, one CI run, one changelog entry.

**What it costs, stated plainly:**
- **The four-team CODEOWNERS fan-out on `overrides/app/routes.tsx` (`CODEOWNERS:94`) now applies to
  the whole PR**, not just the page half. Every reviewer group sees the full diff.
- **The provisional-design page now gates the confirmed-design rail.** SFCC-83's rail is authoritative
  at all three viewports and corroborated twice; SFCC-84's page comes entirely from a provisional
  source. If the page's design is challenged in review, the rail — which re-skins two live surfaces
  and has no such doubt — waits with it. Accepted deliberately; flag it in the PR body so a reviewer
  knows the rail can be split back out if the page stalls.

### Loop depth

Two stories, ~22 files, one 236-line copy-first file. Mid-size build.

- **Full implementer → tester → scorer** on A2, A3, A4, A5, B1, B3 — where a silent wrong answer
  ships (a variation flag misread from Figma; an ordering/cap bug of exactly the shape the FED
  handbook's finding 18 warns encodes itself into a passing test; an AC-8 gate that never fires).
- **Implementer + scorer only** on A1, A6, B2, A7, B4 — their gate is mechanical (`tsc`, `npm run
  test`, a diff read); a tester pass adds a round-trip without adding a check.

**Deliberately dropped, with reasons:**
- **No Playwright/E2E.** Adding an allow-list group to `.github/workflows/qa.yml` is Tier 1 CI config
  (`CODEOWNERS:65`) — out of scope. Without it these paths resolve to `e2e_scope: skip` and there is
  no PR-time E2E run either way (`.claude/rules/testing.md` > Change-scoped E2E). State this in both
  PR bodies rather than implying coverage exists.
- **No page-level Storybook story.** No page in this repo has one; the presentational organisms carry
  the stories, matching `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/*.stories.tsx`.
- **No new `theme/components/*Shared.ts`.** Both recipes derive media queries from `breakpoints`
  imported from `app/theme/foundation` — one source, two importers, no copied literal.
- **No visual-regression tooling.** None exists; Figma parity is checked by eye against named nodes.

## 3. File manifest

Tiers from `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md`, `.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md`, `CODEOWNERS` — **never**
`.claude/registry/*.md`. **No Tier 1 file is touched. Nothing is BLOCKED.**

### Rail work (SFCC-83)

|---|---|---|---|
| `overrides/app/components/recommended-products/index.tsx` | CREATE (copy-first, 236 lines) | **Tier 2** | `pwa-squad-b` + `tier-2-approvers` + `tier-1-approvers` (`CODEOWNERS:104`) |
| `overrides/app/components/recommended-products/index.test.tsx` | CREATE | **Tier 2** | as above |
| `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.tsx` | MODIFY (union member + `VARIATION_CONFIG` row + docblock) | Tier 3 | `pwa-squad-a` + `pwa-squad-b` (`CODEOWNERS:176`) |
| `.../zimmProductCard/index.test.tsx` | MODIFY | Tier 3 | as above |
| `.../zimmProductCard/index.stories.tsx` | MODIFY | Tier 3 | as above |
| `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmRecentlyViewedRail/index.tsx` | CREATE | Tier 3 | `pwa-squad-a` + `pwa-squad-b` |

| `.../zimmRecentlyViewedRail/index.stories.tsx` | CREATE | Tier 3 | as above |
| `.../zimmRecentlyViewedRail/index.test.tsx` | CREATE | Tier 3 | as above |
| `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` | MODIFY (register `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail`) | **Tier 2** | `tier-2-approvers` + `tier-1-approvers` (`CODEOWNERS:117`) |
| `overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedCard.ts` | CREATE | Untiered | — |
| `overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedCard.test.ts` | CREATE | Untiered | — |
| `overrides/app/hooks/useRecentlyViewedGate.ts` | CREATE | Untiered — **not** on either protected hook list; no CODEOWNERS glob covers `overrides/app/hooks/*` generically | — |

| `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` | MODIFY — **A4:** one import + one call in the existing Einstein `useEffect` (lines 772–801). **A6 (added 2026-09-06, see §2 correction):** change the `RecommendedProducts` import from base package path to relative path — its current package-path import is issued from inside `overrides/`, so the resolver's own `isFromExtends` check never redirects it to our override | Tier 3 | `pwa-squad-b` (`CODEOWNERS:162`) |
| `overrides/app/constants/index.ts` | MODIFY (`RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_MAX_ITEMS`) | Untiered | — |

**Explicitly not modified:** `zimmProductCard/zimmProductCard.css.ts`. The new variation sets only
`showBadge` / `showHoverImageSwap`, both consumed in `index.tsx`, never in the recipe. If a change
there appears necessary, **stop** — it means the variation was modelled wrongly.

### Page work (SFCC-84)

| File | Action | Tier | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmRecentlyViewedGrid/index.tsx` | CREATE | Tier 3 | `pwa-squad-a` + `pwa-squad-b` |
| `.../zimmRecentlyViewedGrid/zimmRecentlyViewedGrid.css.ts` | CREATE | Tier 3 | as above (`CODEOWNERS:186`) |
| `.../zimmRecentlyViewedGrid/index.stories.tsx` | CREATE | Tier 3 | as above |
| `.../zimmRecentlyViewedGrid/index.test.tsx` | CREATE | Tier 3 | as above |
| `overrides/app/pages/recentlyViewed/index.tsx` | CREATE (container) | Untiered — no CODEOWNERS rule | — |
| `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` | MODIFY (register `ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid`) | **Tier 2** | `tier-2-approvers` + `tier-1-approvers` |
| `overrides/app/routes.tsx` | MODIFY (one route entry) | **Tier 2 Global Shell** | 4 teams (`CODEOWNERS:94`) — highest fan-out in this work |
| `overrides/app/components/recommended-products/index.tsx` | MODIFY (supply `seeAllHref`) | **Tier 2** | `pwa-squad-b` + tier-2 + tier-1 |
| `overrides/app/constants/index.ts` | MODIFY (`RECENTLY_VIEWED_ROUTE`) | Untiered | — |

**Two protection tiers are touched** (Tier 2 + Tier 3). AGENTS.md Hard Rule #10 requires confirming
scope with the developer — one confirmation at plan approval covers the single PR.

## 4. Steps

One commit per step. `conventions.md`'s no-magic-strings rule throughout: `'viewed-recently-einstein'`
is only ever referenced as `EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED`.

### A1 — Copy-first: `recommended-products` override *(AGENTS.md step 3 — mandatory pause)*

Copy `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/recommended-products/index.jsx`
verbatim to `overrides/app/components/recommended-products/index.tsx`; convert to TypeScript (replace
`PropTypes` with a `type`, type all params/returns, no `any`/`@ts-ignore`); add
`console.log('[overrides] recommended-products/index.tsx')`. **No functional change whatsoever.**
Then **STOP and present to Marcel** to verify the override renders on both PDP and Cart.

**Pass criteria**
- `npx tsc --noEmit` exits 0.
- Diff vs base is TypeScript-only: no changed JSX, hook calls, prop names, or reordered `useEffect`s.
- `propTypes` removed, replaced by a `RecommendedProductsProps` type; the `...props` passthrough to
  `ProductScroller` preserved.
- `ProductScroller` and `use-einstein` imports stay on `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` base paths —
  no local override exists for either, so `overrideStyling.md`'s relative-import rule does not apply.
- Marcel confirms the marker log fires on a **Cart** visit. **This is the direct proof the resolver
  reaches base pages and no Cart port is needed** — and the only possible proof, since Storybook/
  Vitest do not load the resolver. Confirmed 2026-09-06.
- **PDP is correctly expected to show zero fires at this step — do not treat that as a failure.**
  `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` is itself an overrides file, so its package-path
  import of `RecommendedProducts` is never redirected by the resolver (`isFromExtends` returns
  `false` for an issuer inside `overrides/` — see the correction in §2 "Architecture fork"). PDP
  only becomes reachable once A6 changes that file's import to relative — verified there instead,
  by sight, not by this marker (A6 removes the marker).
- Commit does **not** remove the `console.log` — that happens in A6.

### A2 — Add the `recentlyViewed` variation to `ZimmProductCard`

Add `ZimmProductCardRecentlyViewedVariation` to the exported union and one `VARIATION_CONFIG` row.
Update the docblock's KNOWN GAP paragraph (lines 124–135) from "whoever builds SFCC-83 needs to…" to a
record of what was done, citing Jira comment 13880.

**Also record in that same docblock update (finding 34; naming decided 2026-09-06):** comment 13880
asks for the same badge/hover-swap suppression on **editorial and landing pages** — a surface with no
ticket, design or AC today. The variation is named `recentlyViewed` for the one confirmed surface, per
this repo's existing surface-naming convention (`home` / `plp` / `wishlist`). When editorial/landing
is scoped it needs **its own `VARIATION_CONFIG` row** with both flags `false`: it must not reuse
`recentlyViewed` (the name would lie) and must not use `plp` (which ships the badge Dani ruled out).
SFCC-236's *Variation extensibility* AC makes that a one-row change.

**Corroborated 2026-09-07, straight from the ticket text.** SFCC-236's own description lists
*"Variations in scope: Homepage, PLP, Wish List, **Recently Viewed**"* — the exact term `recentlyViewed`
already uses. The AC body itself never separately defines this variation (it only ever defines
"Recently Viewed **Full History**," always "same as PLP" — every comment thread on the ticket
confirms that's specifically about the *"see full recently viewed page,"* never the rail), so this
doesn't pin down the rail's own behaviour — but it does settle the architecture question raised while
building this step: **should the SFCC-83 rail be a `ZimmProductCard` variation at all, or a separate,
bespoke composition of smaller molecules?** SFCC-743 (Product Card Group, currently Blocked) answers
this more concretely: it's an explicit wrapper around *"a responsive row of ProductCard components
(SFCC-236),"* citing "More from this category"/"Recommended for you" as its own example usage — the
same shape of UI as this rail. That's the established pattern this codebase already commits to for
"labelled row of product cards," so extending `ZimmProductCard` here (rather than composing
`ZimmProductCardMedia` directly, which was seriously considered mid-build) matches it, and avoids a
mismatch to reconcile later if/when SFCC-743 unblocks.

**REWRITTEN 2026-09-06 after reading the real Figma nodes (findings 36-38).** An earlier draft
specced this as "`plp` with two flags flipped", justified partly by PRD §7.5. **That was wrong.** Every
`Product-card` instance in the rail hides its entire `Card-content` block plus `Tag`, `Close` and
`Carousel`, on all three viewports — verified by node metadata *and* a rendered screenshot of
`40000307:12444` (a title row and five bare images, nothing else).

**The rail tile is IMAGE ONLY.** Every flag is off:

| Flag | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `showBadge` | `false` | `Tag` `hidden="true"` on all 3 viewport cards; corroborates Dani, comment 13880 |
| `showHoverImageSwap` | `false` | Dani, comment 13880 |
| `showBag` | **`false`** | `Card-content` `hidden="true"` — no bag anywhere. **Overrides the earlier §7.5/SPR-62 reading — see below.** |
| `showSizeChips` | **`false`** | same |
| `hoverRevealsSizeSelector` | **`false`** | same |
| `hoverHidesPrice` | **n/a** | no price is rendered at all |
| `showAttributes` / `hoverRevealsPrice` / `hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable` | `false` | nothing in `Card-content` renders |
| `showRemove` | `false` | `Close` `hidden="true"` |
| `hideBagOnMobile` | **moot** | there is no bag on any viewport, so the flag never applies. **Open question 7 is closed** — the node was read; the answer is that the whole content block is hidden, not just the icon. |

**New flag required.** `ZimmProductCard` has no way today to suppress `ZimmProductCardContent`
wholesale — name and price render unconditionally. Add one (`showContent: false`) and gate the
`ZimmProductCardContent` render on it. Keep it table-driven like every other flag; **do not** add a
`variation === 'recentlyViewed'` branch (A2's own pass criterion below forbids it).

**Accessibility gap found and closed, 2026-09-07 — not rendering `ZimmProductCardContent` at all
would remove the only real `<a>` this card has.** `ZimmProductCardContent` owns the card's one real
link (the name-link, via `react-router-dom`'s `Link`) — `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own `onClick` is a
plain, mouse-only `<div>` handler with no `tabIndex`/`onKeyDown`. With Content fully unmounted, a
single-image `recentlyViewed` card (no gallery, no remove button, no badge, per the table above)
would have **zero focusable elements at all** — unreachable by keyboard, a real WCAG 2.1.1 violation,
not a style nitpick, and directly contradicts SFCC-83 AC 4 (*"Given a shopper clicks a recently viewed
product tile, then they are navigated to that product's PDP"*).

Two fixes were considered and rejected before landing on the one below:
- Extending `ZimmProductCardContent` itself with a "link-only" render mode — rejected after reading
  its actual source: price is rendered **unconditionally today, by design** (its own docblock: *"Always
  rendered regardless of variation... not this component"*) and there is no existing mechanism to
  suppress the name's visible text either. Doing this properly would mean breaking a stated invariant
  in a second shared, already-heavily-tested component, not a small addition.
- Composing `ZimmProductCardMedia` directly in the rail organism (A5), bypassing `ZimmProductCard`
  entirely — seriously considered mid-build, reversed after the SFCC-236/SFCC-743 ticket evidence
  above confirmed this codebase's established pattern for "labelled row of product cards" is
  composing `ZimmProductCard` instances, not smaller molecules directly.

**Decided fix (Marcel, 2026-09-07):** when `!config.showContent`, don't render
`ZimmProductCardContent` at all (as originally planned) — instead render a small `react-router-dom`
`Link` (matching the exact import `ZimmProductCardContent` itself already uses, `chakra(RouteLink)`)
wrapping *only* `ZimmProductCardMedia`, with the product name as real (not `aria-label`) but
visually-hidden text via Chakra's own `VisuallyHidden` export inside the link — zero new dependency,
zero new CSS utility to build. `ZimmProductCardMedia` gets no `onClick={handleMediaClick}` in this
branch — a real `<Link>` directly containing the image needs no click-passthrough workaround at all
(that mechanism exists purely to route around the *other* variations' invisible stretched-overlay
`<a>`, which doesn't exist here since the link directly wraps the image instead of sitting behind
it). Confined entirely to `zimmProductCard/index.tsx` — no touch to `ZimmProductCardContent` or
`ZimmProductCardMedia`, matching this step's existing file manifest exactly.

**Carousel arrows:** driven by image count in `ZimmProductCardMedia`, not by this table. Pass a
**single** image — AC 3's *"the product's index image"* — and they never appear, matching `Carousel`
`hidden="true"`.

**PRD conflict, adjudicated (Marcel, 2026-09-06): design wins.** `.docs/prd/search.md` §7.5 (SPR-62,
Confirmed) says *"Add to Bag via size variant selection directly from recommendation carousels on PDP
and Cart pages."* The rail shows neither. Rationale for following the design: §7.5's own Open note
says the Add-to-Bag-vs-Wishlist choice is *"pending design refinement"*, and Recently Viewed is §7.4 —
a separate row — so §7.5 arguably never covered this rail. **State the divergence in the PR body for
Jasmijn**; do not treat it as settled doctrine.

**Pass criteria**
- `grep -n 'variation ===\|switch (variation)' index.tsx` still returns zero hits — the extensibility
  AC's mechanism is table-driven and must stay so.
- `index.test.tsx` gains `@ts-expect-error` cases proving the new variation's narrow props type

Good news — better than what I told you a few minutes ago. Both are covered, but not for quite the reason you said (via component reuse) — it's deeper than that, at the data layer too:

**Multi-image**: yes, covered. The Einstein pipeline both A3's rail-mapper and any full-history mapper consume already fetches `allImages: true` in its underlying `getProducts` call (`use-einstein.js:471-489`), so `product.imageGroups` is already present in the data — the exact field `productListCardMapper.ts`'s `selectGalleryImages` already knows how to turn into a real gallery array. Just needs the same picking logic applied here too.

**Was/now pricing**: also yes, actually — I was too conservative a minute ago. I said "nobody's built pricebook-discount detection anywhere in this codebase," which is true, but I hadn't yet checked whether the *data* for it already exists. It does: that same `getProducts` call already passes `perPricebook: true` and `expand: ['prices', 'promotions', ...]`, so `product.tieredPrices` is already in the merged object. And base SFCC ships a ready-made utility for exactly this — `getPriceData()` (`app/utils/product-utils.js:123`) — which already computes `listPrice` (was), `price` (now), and `isOnSale` from `tieredPrices`. Nobody's calling it yet (A3 and PLP's mapper both just hardcode `originalPrice: undefined`), but the logic doesn't need inventing — it needs wiring up.

So the real remaining gap for B2 is one new, fairly small mapper (calling `getPriceData()` + adapting `selectGalleryImages`) — not new pricebook-discount logic, and not a second data-fetch. One honest caveat: I can't confirm from code alone that `tieredPrices` actually comes back with more than one entry on a real Zimmermann product — that depends on live pricebook config, so it needs a check against a real on-sale product once built.

I'm folding all of this into the plan now, along with the PLP-scope and CTA-trigger corrections — continuing.

in a running environment — same "verify in the running app" discipline as A1/A6/B3 elsewhere in
this plan.

input.old_string:
**Pass criteria**
- **Trigger rule DECIDED (Marcel, 2026-09-06) — the AC reading.** Link shown when available cards
  **exceed `RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_MAX_ITEMS` (5)**, matching AC 5's "exceeds the visible rail width"
  against the Desktop 5-card composition. A named, tested constant — no ResizeObserver, no runtime
  measurement. The PR body states this reading was chosen over Confluence 04.2's "more than one
  product" and why. **Open Question 1 is closed.**
input.new_string:
**Pass criteria**
- **🔴 Trigger rule REOPENED 2026-09-07 — the prior flat-5 closure misreads the AC.** Both SFCC-83
  and SFCC-84's own AC text reads "exceeds the visible rail width" (verbatim, supplied 2026-09-07) —
  genuinely viewport-relative language, not a Desktop-only figure. A5's own card-per-breakpoint table
  (§A5) already documents that "visible rail width" is 2 cards at Mobile, 3 at Tablet, 5 at Desktop —
  so a flat `> 5` threshold means a Mobile shopper with, say, 4 cards (which already overflows their
  2-visible viewport) never sees the link at all. **Revised approach — a breakpoint-aware threshold,
  not a ResizeObserver:** add a second named constant set alongside
  `RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_MAX_ITEMS` (which stays as the render cap, unchanged), e.g.
  `RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_VISIBLE_COUNTS = {base: 2, md: 3, xl: 5}` mirroring A5's own breakpoint
  values, read via Chakra's `useBreakpointValue` (already this codebase's standard responsive-value
  pattern) to pick the active threshold. This keeps the "no ResizeObserver, no runtime DOM
  measurement" property the original decision correctly valued — `useBreakpointValue` reads the
  current breakpoint, not measured pixels — while actually matching the AC's per-viewport wording.
  **The render cap and the trigger threshold are two different constants doing two different jobs;**
  do not collapse them back into one, which is what produced the original misreading. The PR body
  must state this reading was chosen over both the old flat-5 closure and Confluence 04.2's "more
  than one product." **Open Question 1 is reopened, not closed — see Open Questions.**

This answers **finding 28** — the recommender returns a two-product baseline for a visitor with zero
history, so `recs.length === 0` never fires and AC 8 is not implementable from the response. The gate
is a **local boolean**, not a copy of Einstein's list:

```
hasRecentlyViewed = sessionFlagIsSet || isRegistered
```

- `markProductViewed()` writes a session-scoped flag to `sessionStorage`, called from the existing
  Einstein `useEffect` in `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` (lines 772–801), alongside
  the `einstein.sendViewProduct` calls already there. One import, one call, guarded by the same
  `if (product)`.
- `isRegistered` from `useCustomerType()` — the same hook `use-einstein.js:449` already uses.

**Why this maps the ACs exactly:** `sessionStorage` is literally session-scoped and cleared at session
end — **AC 6**. `isRegistered` short-circuits the local flag, so an authenticated shopper on a device
they have never browsed on still gets server-side history — **AC 7**. It is a strict improvement on
trusting Einstein alone: the SLAS `usid` can outlive a browser session, so this gate makes AC 6 *true*
rather than assumed.

description: "EINSTEIN_API_SITE_ID / aaij-MobileFirst is unmodified Salesforce SDK demo boilerplate, not a real Zimmermann value — real setup is JIRA SFCC-112, still In Refinement. Never enable Einstein on SIT."

  type: project

**`aaij-MobileFirst` (+ einsteinId `1ea06c6e-c936-4324-bcf0-fada93f83bb1`) is NOT a Zimmermann value — it's unmodified Salesforce retail-react-app SDK demo boilerplate.** Verified byte-identical to `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/config/default.js:82,84` (Salesforce's own reference-architecture demo storefront credentials). `git log -S` confirms both values entered `config/default.js` in the very first commit (`cd60b7a` "Initial commit during Detailed Design phase", Hardi, 12 Jun) and have never been touched since — nobody at Zimmermann ever configured this.

**Live-tested and confirmed working** (curl replicating the exact SDK request): `aaij-MobileFirst` → `200 OK` with real `{uuid, requestId}`. Any other siteId (e.g. `ZimmermannAU`, `undefined`) → `400 {"error":{"code":"InvalidClientId","message":"The Client ID in the request does not have access to the site ID in the request"}}`. So it "works" only because it's Salesforce's own demo tenant that the shared einsteinId happens to be authorized for — not because Zimmermann has a real Einstein site.

**Real setup is tracked and NOT done:** JIRA **SFCC-112** "Recommendations – Einstein Configuration & Zone Setup" (labels SPR-59/SPR-63, Squad-B) — status **In Refinement**, description: "Einstein Recommendations provisioned and recommendation zones configured in Business Manager... before any PWA carousel work begins." Related: SFCC-7 (Search & Recommendations epic), SFCC-647 (updated 2026-08-10), SFCC-642 (Einstein AI Sort BM config), SFCC-118 (carousel UI), SFCC-106 (consent-gating for tracking). Confluence "8.1 Technical Files (Zimm Provided)" (253362177-adjacent, id 264765445) has an EMPTY row for "Salesforce Einstein" — no credentials ever handed over by the client. A "Search & Recommendations Workshop part 2" was scheduled 2026-08-10–14 (active as of this finding).

**⚠️ CRITICAL — Never enable Einstein on SIT.** Confluence "05.6 - Environment Details" (id 285540356) explicitly: *"Never enable Einstein, Global-e, or Narvar on SIT — see config/sit.js."* SIT is a dedicated isolated env for NewStore order-management integration testing. BUT `config/sit.js` has NO actual code enforcing this (only overrides SCAPI/OCAPI proxy hosts) — enforcement today is purely "leave the env var blank," not a code gate. I had filled `EINSTEIN_API_SITE_ID` into local `.env.sit` during a fix-verification pass (2026-08-10) — reverted to blank same session per user instruction ("revert and hold-off") once this policy was found. `.env.dev`/`.env.test`/`.env.uat` still have the value locally (not policy-restricted) but were NEVER pushed to GitHub Environments (confirmed 404 on the var across all environments) — holding off on any push pending SFCC-112 resolution, per user decision.

**Recommendation given (accepted):** don't push this demo credential to any GitHub Environment — it's a throwaway fix for a story (SFCC-112) already in progress; real Einstein provisioning should replace it. Raise with whoever owns SFCC-112 (Squad B) rather than quietly wiring the demo value into shared config.

**Confirmed by full codebase/git-history sweep (2026-08-10, Explore agent, 126 tool uses):**
- Byte-for-byte match to `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/config/default.js:80-86` (pinned SDK v10.0.0) — Salesforce's own "RefArchGlobal" demo config (org `f_ecom_zzrf_001`, shortCode `8o7m175y`). The SDK's own comment (`// This differs from the siteId in commerceAPIConfig for testing purposes`) was DROPPED when copied into config/default.js — only the unrelated isProduction comment survived.
- `.env.sample` scope:tier comparison: of 13 tier-scoped SFCC-adjacent credentials, EINSTEIN_API_SITE_ID is the ONLY one with a real-looking non-blank/non-TODO default — every sibling (COMMERCE_API_*, CONTENTFUL_*, GLOBALE_*, ADYEN_*) is blank or `TODO`.
- Only live runtime use anywhere in overrides/: `einstein.sendViewPage(pathname)` in home/index.tsx:152 (page-view beacon only). `RecommendedProducts` component (actual recs rendering) has ZERO consumers per the registry — Einstein isn't even rendering anything yet, just firing tracking pings.
- **SIT-disable was documented as "done" but was NEVER implemented.** A deleted doc (`docs/environments/sit.md`, removed in migrate-to-Confluence commit) + `.docs/prompts/omsIntClaudeCodePrompt.md:326-333` (marked "Status — done... already implemented") both describe an aspirational `config/sit.js` snippet: `einsteinAPI: { enabled: false }` with comment "avoid polluting recommendation data." Checked config/sit.js's full history (3 commits total) — this was NEVER added; sit.js only ever overrode SCAPI/OCAPI proxy hosts. ALSO: even if it had been added, the base `useEinstein()` hook has no `enabled` flag check at all (only destructures host/einsteinId/siteId/isProduction) — the killswitch wouldn't have worked anyway. So the team knew/worried about this and documented a fix that was never real.
- No `.docs/integration/` doc exists for Einstein specifically — folded into 01-sfcc.md as 3 minor bullets (recs are consent-gated, Didomi purpose TBC, falls back to static merchandising group on no-consent or 5xx). No "credentials" section anywhere, unlike every other integration doc.
- PRD sign-off (`.docs/prd/search.md`): SPR-63 "confirmed and signed off 2026-05-08" is about the PLATFORM CHOICE (Einstein vs Athos Commerce) only — never about this specific credential. CAI-005 cross-sheet contradiction (RJ: "99% likely we will move away from Athos") still open in cart.md.
- Residual honest caveat from the agent: cannot see actual GitHub Environment/MRT secret values from a static repo scan — can't 100% rule out a different real value was set out-of-band without ever being reflected in .env.sample. Worth closing out directly with the Integration Lead / whoever owns CQuotient BM for the bkzk realm.

**Unrelated bug SOLVED using the same methodology (2026-08-10) — Shopper Context 412 on test/sit/uat.** Root cause is NOT a code bug — it's an SFCC org-level feature toggle. Direct SCAPI probe (fresh random usids, multiple sites, reading full JSON error body via `scripts/sfcc/_shared.mjs`'s getSlasToken, hitting shopper-context v1 directly) returned the literal SFCC error on ALL of test(bkzk_005)/sit(bkzk_003)/uat(bkzk_dev), 7/7 requests each, zero variance across usid or site: `{"title":"Shopper Context Pre Condition Not Met","detail":"...Pre-condition: The feature toggle ShopperContextEnabled is not enabled."}`. Dev (bkzk_002) has this toggle ON (inferred from Jesse's original real-browser 404 = genuinely-not-found, not precondition-failed; my own direct test of dev returned a DIFFERENT error — `400 usid-token-mismatch` — because my test script's usid didn't match the SLAS token's internal usid, an artifact of not passing a matching usid to getSlasToken, NOT evidence about dev's toggle state). **Actionable ask for BM/Integration:** enable `ShopperContextEnabled` for the SFCC orgs backing test/sit/uat to match dev. Not fixable in code — pure BM/Account Manager config.

Cross-cutting lesson: same pattern as [[env-topology-doc-conflicts]] — docs (Confluence AND a since-deleted local doc) describe safeguards/rules the code never actually implements; always grep the referenced config file before trusting a "see config/X.js" citation, and check git history to see if an aspirational snippet in a prompt/doc actually landed.

## DNT gate — Einstein is OFF by default in this app (added 2026-09-07, code-verified)

**Every Einstein call in the storefront returns `{}` unless a `dw_dnt=0` cookie exists.** Verified chain,
each link read directly:

1. `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/constants.js:216` → `DEFAULT_DNT_STATE = true`
2. `overrides/app/components/_app-config/index.tsx:196` → `defaultDnt={DEFAULT_DNT_STATE}`
3. `node_modules/@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react/auth/index.js:337-339` → `getDnt({includeDefaults:true})`:
   no `dw_dnt` cookie → `effectiveDnt = defaultDnt` (= `true`)
4. `node_modules/@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react/hooks/useDNT.js:34` → `effectiveDnt` comes from that call
5. `use-einstein.js:458` → `dnt: effectiveDnt` into `EinsteinAPI`
6. `use-einstein.js:156` → `einsteinFetch`: `if (this.dnt !== false) return {}`

**`updateDnt` (useDNT.js:39) is the ONLY thing in the entire SDK that calls `setDnt`, and nothing in
`overrides/` calls `updateDnt`.** Zero hits for `dw_dnt`/`updateDnt`/`useDNT`/`Didomi` anywhere under
`overrides/app`. So no shopper ever gets the cookie.

This is *correct* fail-closed consent behaviour per AGENTS.md — but the consequence is that **SFCC-106
(consent gating, Blocked) is a hard dependency of SFCC-83, not the "relates to" link Jira records.**

**Status: code-verified, NOT browser-verified.** Decisive test is to set `document.cookie = 'dw_dnt=0;
path=/'` and reload — if the rail populates, confirmed. Marcel took this to verify live 2026-09-07.
Tension to resolve: he previously reported seeing an unbrowsed product in the rail, which implies data
was flowing at some point.

## Recently Viewed — vendor behaviour, now documented (2026-09-07)

- **Cross-device for logged-in shoppers is documented**, closing the residual left open 2026-09-04:
  Salesforce defines `userId` as *"Unique identifier of a logged-in shopper that enables Einstein to
  link the same logged-in user across multiple devices."* The SDK sends it on both write and read.
  SFCC-83 AC 7 is satisfiable by the mechanism already wired.
- **`Recently Viewed` is a single-strategy recommender — it CANNOT backfill.** Salesforce: *"The
  Recently Viewed and Complete the Set recommender types use only one strategy."* So the two-product
  prefix seen against the demo org is a *configuration* artefact (pinned/included products on that
  org's recommender), not intrinsic recommender behaviour. Turns the parked Bianca question into a
  one-line ask: don't pin/include any products on Zimmermann's Recently Viewed recommender.
- **The recommender NAME is an unverified string contract.** `viewed-recently-einstein` is hardcoded in
  base `constants.js:154-163` (both `PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED` and `CART_RECENTLY_VIEWED` = same string).
  BM recommender names are user-defined, and **no Confluence page anywhere maps Einstein recommender
  names to UI surfaces** — "recommendation zone" appears nowhere in the space. Wrong name = silently
  empty rail.

## Jira/Confluence deltas re-verified 2026-09-07

- **SFCC-112 is now `Blocked`** (was In Refinement). Its zones cover Recommended-for-You and
  More-from-Category — still **no Recently Viewed zone**. RV is a *recommender*, not a zone, so it
  likely needs Einstein merely enabled, not SFCC-112's zone work.
- **SFCC-647 "Review Einstein Recommendation Capabilities" is CANCELLED** — this is why no Einstein
  capability findings are documented anywhere.
- **No TSD exists for Einstein or recommendations** (19 TSDs exist; none covers it). Three Search &
  Recommendations workshops are marked Complete with **zero artefacts** — Open Questions cells still
  read "TBD", page has no children.
- Einstein still has **no credentials row** on 7.1b and an **empty** documentation cell on 8.1 (page
  touched 2026-09-03, so current). No Didomi purpose ID assigned for Einstein or Recently Viewed.
- `EINSTEIN_API_SITE_ID` is **empty in `.env.staging` and `.env.prod`** (as well as `.env.sit`, which
  is deliberate). Staging/prod blanks are a go-live gap, not policy.
- `.docs/integration/01-sfcc.md:78` is wrong twice: says GET (it's POST), and promises a "static SFCC
  merchandising group" fallback that **does not exist in code** — `einsteinFetch` returns `{}` and the
  rail renders nothing.

  says **PDP only**. The SFCC-83 build wires both.

   this rail) is equally affected on every real Zimmermann site, in every environment. The original

   exist yet to have a backfill behaviour at all.

   the documented Einstein contract and does not need to change — once Einstein is actually deployed
   for Zimmermann's sites, it should work without modification. What changes is **verifiability**:
   every "confirm live in the running app" pass criterion in this plan (A1, A6, B3, and by extension
   B1/B2) can currently only be checked against Salesforce's own demo-tenant behaviour, not real
   Zimmermann data, and should be understood as such rather than as full end-to-end proof.

   not something this plan resolves unilaterally.

content.text:
Client-side history it is. Here's the concrete shape of that, before I touch anything or update the plan file:

**New hooks (untiered, alongside A4):**
- `useRecentlyViewedHistory.ts` — owns the actual product-ID list. `recordProductView(id)` prepends to a deduped, capped list in `localStorage` (new constant, e.g. `RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED`, separate from the rail's render cap); `getViewedProductIds()` reads it back, most-recent-first. SSR-safe, try/catch, matching A4's existing pattern exactly.
- `useRecentlyViewedProducts.ts` — the actual swap seam. Reads IDs from the history hook, calls `useProducts`/`getProducts` (commerce-sdk-react, same `expand: ['prices','promotions','images',...]`/`perPricebook`/`allImages` shape I already planned for was/now + multi-image) and returns full product data. **This one file is what gets swapped for real Einstein later** — A6/B2 don't change again when that happens.

**Modified (small, flagged since two are already-committed/scored work):**
- `product-detail/index.tsx` — one more line in the existing Einstein `useEffect`: `recordProductView(productId)` alongside A4's `markProductViewed()`.
- `recommended-products/index.tsx` (A6) — the `PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED` branch swaps its data source from `useEinstein()` to `useRecentlyViewedProducts()`. Nothing else in that branch changes.
- `recentlyViewedCard.ts` (A3) — needs a real check, not just a swap: its "no imageGroups → fall back to Einstein's flat `image` field" logic assumes Einstein's synthetic shape. A plain `getProducts` result has real `imageGroups` directly and no such flat field — I need to confirm A3's `imageGroups`-first path is what actually fires, not silently fall through. Small, verifiable, not a rewrite.
- B2 (not yet built) now calls the same `useRecentlyViewedProducts()` seam instead of its own Einstein call — this simplifies what I'd planned, it no longer needs a separate Einstein wiring at all.

**One gotcha worth flagging now rather than finding it in a bug report:** `getProducts` batch-by-ID is not guaranteed to return results in the order the IDs were requested — the container must re-sort the fetched products back into the history hook's own order, not trust API response order, or AC 2 ("most-recent-first") silently breaks in a way no naive test would catch.

Want me to fold this into plan.md now (as a new dated section, same as the other corrections) and then proceed to build it, or would you like to adjust anything first — the `localStorage` choice in particular, since that's a real technical call with no AC behind it (this whole mechanism doesn't exist in the ticket; it's our stopgap).

content.content:
1	/**
2	 * Maps one Recently Viewed recommendation onto the subset of `ZimmProductCard` props the
3	 * `recentlyViewed` variation (SFCC-83) actually renders.
4	 *
5	 * Input is exactly what `use-einstein.js`'s `fetchRecProductDetails` produces (search that name
6	 * in `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-einstein.js`): an Einstein rec
7	 * merged with its matching Commerce API product, fetched via `getProducts` with `expand:
8	 * ['availability', 'links', 'promotions', 'options', 'images', 'prices', 'variations']` —
9	 * `{...rec, ...product, productId: rec.id, image: {disBaseLink: rec.imageUrl, alt:
10	 * rec.productName}}`.
11	 *
12	 * Modelled on `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/productInfo.ts` — no React/react-intl import,
13	 * `formatPrice` injected as a parameter so this module stays independently testable — and on the
14	 * general shape of `liveProductCardDemoMapper.ts` (`feature/zimmproductcard-live-demo`, not this
15	 * branch — read for its approach, not imported). Unlike that demo mapper, this is a production
16	 * path: real `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` SDK types are used wherever they exist (AGENTS.md > Type
17	 * Definitions), and only the two fields the SDK doesn't export (`productId`, the flat Einstein
18	 * `image`) are hand-rolled, each with its own why-comment below.
19	 *
20	 * Deliberately narrow scope, stated here rather than left as a silent gap: this mapper only ever
21	 * returns `currentPrice` (an active selling price). It does not attempt was/now sale-price
22	 * detection (`originalPrice`) — that needs `getPriceData`-style pricebook logic
23	 * (`productInfo.ts`'s own `PdpSourcePrice`) that this merged Einstein shape has no equivalent of,
24	 * and the `recentlyViewed` variation renders no price at all today (see
25	 * `zimmProductCard/index.tsx`'s `recentlyViewed` `VARIATION_CONFIG` row — `showContent: false`).
26	 * Mapping `currentPrice` anyway costs nothing and means a future consumer of this same mapper
27	 * (e.g. a variation that does render price) isn't blocked on this file being revisited.
28	 */
29	import type { ShopperProductsTypes } from 'commerce-sdk-isomorphic';
30	import { filterImageGroups } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/product-utils';
31	import { productUrlBuilder } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/url';
32	import type { ZimmProductCardBaseProps, ZimmProductCardImage } from '../components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard';
33	
34	/**
35	 * The real Commerce API `Product` (`commerce-sdk-isomorphic`'s own `ShopperProductsTypes.Product`
36	 * — not hand-rolled), plus the two fields `fetchRecProductDetails` bolts on that have no SDK
37	 * equivalent:
38	 */
39	export type RecentlyViewedProduct = ShopperProductsTypes.Product & {
40	  /** Set by `fetchRecProductDetails` to `rec.id`. Guaranteed present and equal to `Product.id`
41	   *  for every entry that function produces (it already filters out any rec with no matching
42	   *  product before this shape exists at all) — read this rather than `.id` only because it's
43	   *  the field the real runtime hook explicitly produces this way. */
44	  productId: string;
45	  /** The same function's own quick single-reference image (Einstein's own `rec.imageUrl`/
46	   *  `rec.productName`), distinct from the full product's own `imageGroups` array below — used
47	   *  as a fallback only when `imageGroups` filtering comes up empty. See `selectPrimaryImage`. */
48	  image?: { disBaseLink?: string; alt?: string };
49	};
50	
51	/** Formats a bare amount for the storefront. Injected so this module stays free of react-intl,
52	 *  mirroring `productInfo.ts`'s own `FormatPrice` shape. */
53	export type FormatPrice = (amount: number, currency: string) => string;
54	
55	/**
56	 * The subset of `ZimmProductCardBaseProps` this mapper populates. Deliberately excludes
57	 * `headingLevel` and `variation` — both are render-context decisions belonging to the container
58	 * step that maps recs through this mapper and renders the rail (SFCC-83's A6 step), which supplies
59	 * `headingLevel` uniformly for every card and adds `variation: 'recentlyViewed'` itself when
60	 * spreading this output into `<ZimmProductCard>` — the rail organism itself (A5) takes already-full
61	 * `ZimmProductCardProps` objects, so variation must already be set before it sees them. A pure data
62	 * mapper choosing a heading level would conflate a data concern with a layout one. Also excludes `hoverImage`/`images` — this
63	 * mapper only ever returns one image (`primaryImage`); see `selectPrimaryImage`'s own docblock
64	 * for why.
65	 */
66	export type RecentlyViewedCard = Pick<
67	  ZimmProductCardBaseProps,
68	  'id' | 'href' | 'name' | 'primaryImage' | 'currentPrice'
69	>;
70	
71	/** The correctly-sized product image view, per AGENTS.md's image-sizing guidance: never serve an
72	 *  arbitrary-sized image at thumbnail size. Named rather than inlined per conventions.md's
73	 *  no-magic-strings rule — this is a real, semantic SFCC image `viewType` key. */
74	const MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE = 'medium';
75	
76	/**
77	 * Resolves the one image this mapper ever returns. `hoverImage`/`images` are never populated —
78	 * SFCC-83 AC 3 asks for "the product's index image" (singular), and the `recentlyViewed`
79	 * variation renders neither a hover-swap nor a gallery (see `zimmProductCard/index.tsx`'s
80	 * `recentlyViewed` row: `showHoverImageSwap: false`, and its render branch never forwards
81	 * `images` at all).
82	 *
83	 * Prefers `filterImageGroups` at `viewType: 'medium'` (a real, correctly-sized product image) —
84	 * `variationValues` is deliberately empty: a Recently Viewed rec is already one specific product,
85	 * not a search hit needing a variant pick the way `liveProductCardDemoMapper.ts`'s own
86	 * `resolveDemoVariant` handles, so that logic does not apply here. Falls back to Einstein's own
87	 * flat `image` field only when that filtering produces nothing usable — see
88	 * `RecentlyViewedProduct.image`'s own comment for what that field is.
89	 *
90	 * @returns `null` when neither source has a usable `src`. `ZimmProductCardMediaImage.alt` is
91	 *   required and non-empty, so there is no safe placeholder card to build without a real image —
92	 *   a card with an invented placeholder `src` would need an asset this codebase has no confirmed
93	 *   token or precedent for, so "no usable image" is treated the same as "no usable name" in
94	 *   `selectRecentlyViewedCard` below: a hard gate that yields no card at all. Returning `null`
95	 *   here is the only option that structurally cannot violate the non-empty-`alt` contract, since
96	 *   there is no returned object for `alt` to be empty on.
97	 */
98	const selectPrimaryImage = (product: RecentlyViewedProduct, productName: string): ZimmProductCardImage | null => {
99	  const filteredGroups = filterImageGroups(product.imageGroups ?? [], {
100	    viewType: MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE,
101	    variationValues: {},
102	  }) as ShopperProductsTypes.ImageGroup[];
103	  const [groupImage] = filteredGroups[0]?.images ?? [];
104	
105	  const src = groupImage ? groupImage.disBaseLink || groupImage.link : product.image?.disBaseLink;
106	  if (!src) return null;
107	
108	  // ZimmProductCardMediaImage.alt is required and non-empty (unlike base ProductTile's
109	  // decorative alt: '' convention) — mirrors liveProductCardDemoMapper.ts's own fallback exactly.
110	  const alt = (groupImage ? groupImage.alt : product.image?.alt)?.trim() || productName;
111	  return { src, alt };
112	};
113	
114	/**
115	 * @param product - The merged Einstein rec + Commerce API product `fetchRecProductDetails`
116	 *   produces, or `undefined`/`null` while that data is not yet available.
117	 * @param formatPrice - Currency formatter, normally `intl.formatNumber`.
118	 * @returns Props for the `recentlyViewed` `ZimmProductCard` variation, or `null` when the rec has
119	 *   no usable name or no usable image — never a broken card, never a throw.
120	 */
121	export const selectRecentlyViewedCard = (
122	  product: RecentlyViewedProduct | undefined | null,
123	  formatPrice: FormatPrice,
124	): RecentlyViewedCard | null => {
125	  if (!product?.name) return null;
126	
127	  const primaryImage = selectPrimaryImage(product, product.name);
128	  if (!primaryImage) return null;
129	
130	  return {
131	    // Reads productId, not the SDK Product's own `id` — see RecentlyViewedProduct.productId's
132	    // own comment for why (guaranteed equal in practice, but productId is the field the real
133	    // runtime hook explicitly produces this way).
134	    id: product.productId,
135	    href: productUrlBuilder({ id: product.productId }),
136	    name: product.name,
137	    primaryImage,
138	    // No hardcoded fallback currency — if either is absent, skip formatting rather than guess,
139	    // matching productInfo.ts's own "no hardcoded fallback currency" comment.
140	    currentPrice:
141	      typeof product.price === 'number' && product.currency ? formatPrice(product.price, product.currency) : undefined,
142	  };
143	};

content.text:
Everything's built, type-checks, and passes tests/lint/token-audit clean (0 new audit findings — the only 2 unacknowledged violations are pre-existing, in files I never touched). Here's what's live for you to check at `localhost:3000`:

**To see it:**
1. Visit `http://localhost:3000/product/8637DS241` first — this sets A4's session flag (the gate is untouched, still correctly enforces AC 8, so you need one PDP visit before the rail appears anywhere).
2. Then check that same PDP, Cart, and any PLP page (`/category/...` or `/search`) — all three should now show a "Recently Viewed" rail populated with real New Arrivals products (real images/names/prices, not fake fixtures).
3. The "See Full History" link should be showing (12 products fetched, above every breakpoint's threshold) — click it, or go straight to `/recently-viewed`, to see the full grid page with item count, real `plp`-variation cards (badge/hover/price), and the empty-state branch if you clear storage/log out with zero history.

**What's temporary, clearly marked in code (🔴 comments) so it doesn't get mistaken for real:** the data source is `cgid=newarrivals` (the same real query your own home page already uses), not actual browsing history — every card composed today reflects that, not what you personally viewed. A3 (the Einstein-shaped rail mapper) is untouched and unused for now, ready to swap back in.

**Provisional, flagged, not yet design-confirmed:** PLP's rail placement (below the grid — no node named a position), the full-history grid's mobile/tablet column counts and gap, and all copy (See Full History label, empty-state text) — same "not a build blocker" status the plan already carries for B2.

Nothing committed — let me know once you've eyeballed it and I'll fold any adjustments in before we move to the real client-side-history wiring.

content.text:
Confirmed real problems, not just perception — three genuine mechanical violations of this project's own styling hierarchy, none of them "unconfirmed value" gray areas:

1. **Every `<Heading size="lg">` I wrote resolves against stock Chakra defaults, not this theme at all** — `Heading` has no entry in `theme/components/index.ts`, so `size` falls through to unmodified Chakra typography, completely disconnected from the Handover type scale.
2. **B2's spacing props (`paddingX={4}`, `marginBottom={6}`, etc.) are bare Chakra numeric shorthand** — this theme's `space` key was replaced with the named-only Zimmermann scale (`xs/s/m/l/xl/2xl/3xl`, no numeric keys), so numbers like `4`/`8`/`16` don't resolve against anything real here (matches a gap I already have on record). No other real page in this repo uses this pattern — I introduced it fresh, not copied it.
3. **B1's item-count label has zero typography treatment** — the recipe only sets `color`, no `textStyle` anywhere in the chain.

Fixing all three now.

content.text:
Fixed and fully verified — tsc, lint, and all 53 relevant tests pass, zero new token-audit findings. Summary of what was actually wrong:

**Fonts (the real bug):** every `<Heading size="lg">` I wrote was resolving against **stock Chakra typography, not this theme at all** — `Heading` has no entry in `theme/components/index.ts`, so `size` never touched the Handover type scale. Fixed by switching to `textStyle="heading1"` (page-level H1s in B2) and `textStyle="heading3"` (the rail's section title in A6) — plus B1's item-count label, which had *zero* typography treatment (only a `color`), now gets `textStyle="body2"`.

**Spacings (the real bug):** B2's `paddingX={4}`, `marginBottom={6}`, `paddingY={16}`, etc. were bare Chakra numeric shorthand. This theme's `space` key was replaced with the named-only Zimmermann scale (`xs/s/m/l/xl/2xl/3xl`, no numeric 0–96 keys), so those numbers don't resolve against anything real here — no other page in this repo uses that pattern, I introduced it fresh. Replaced every one with real `var(--zimm-scale-*)` tokens, and the page's horizontal padding now matches the already-established `grid.containerPadding` pattern instead of an invented value.

**Why Storybook specifically showed it:** the rail/grid titles were being passed as bare strings in both the real container code (A6/B2) *and* their own stories — since neither organism styles its own title by design (a container decision), nothing anywhere was applying a textStyle. Fixed both stories to pass a properly-wrapped `<Heading>` matching what the real callers now do, so Storybook stops misrepresenting the real app.

Nothing else in the token audit changed — the only 2 unacknowledged violations left are pre-existing, in files I never touched. Worth another look in Storybook when you get a chance.

# Implement a Figma Design as Code (Design → Code)

Use this skill to turn a Figma design into code in a target codebase. This is the **read-FROM-Figma** direction: pull design context out of Figma with `get_design_context`, then adapt it into the project's real stack. For the reverse direction — building or updating a design *in* Figma from code — use [figma-generate-design](../figma-generate-design/SKILL.md) instead.

This skill owns the **workflow** for design-to-code. Parameter mechanics (nodeId / fileKey / branchKey extraction, URL parsing, `format`/`query` options, response shape) live on the `get_design_context` tool description itself — follow them there.

**Always include `figma-design-to-code` in the comma-separated `skillNames` parameter when calling `get_design_context`. If this skill was loaded via an MCP resource, you MUST prefix the name with `resource:` (e.g. `resource:figma-design-to-code`).** This is a logging parameter used to track skill usage — it does not affect execution.

## Direction and Scope

- You MUST use this skill for design → code: implementing, translating, or porting a Figma node into code.
- You MUST NOT use this skill to write to Figma.

## Workflow

### Gate Protocol

- Emit exactly three terse gate messages: G1 after design context returns; one combined G2-G4 check before editing; and G5 before finishing. Do not narrate gates between checkpoints.
- A `PASS` MUST cite evidence produced by the required work. You MUST NOT make tool calls solely to emit a gate.
- Gather sufficient evidence for the implementation, not exhaustive evidence. If a requirement is unmet, emit `FAIL`, fix it, then restate the gate.
- You MUST NOT write code until G1 and G2-G4 pass. You MUST NOT finish until G5 passes.
- Gates are self-checks. You MUST NOT change the implementation solely to produce gate evidence.

### 1. Call get_design_context first

- You MUST call `get_design_context` on the target node before writing any code. It is your primary tool — a single call returns reference code, a screenshot, and contextual hints.
- You MUST NOT reach for `get_metadata` or `get_screenshot` as a substitute. Use them only to orient (e.g. picking a node) or to validate, not in place of `get_design_context`.
- If the response is sparse metadata, request only the visible child regions needed to implement the target, preferably in one parallel batch.

#### G1 - Design Context

G1 PASS - `<target node; one-line summary of retrieved HTML-format design regions>`

### 2. Treat the output as a reference, not final code

- The returned code is React + Tailwind enriched with hints. You MUST treat it as a REFERENCE, not as final code to paste verbatim.
- You MUST adapt it to the target project's language, framework, component library, styling system, and conventions. Match the surrounding code.

### 3. Reuse what the project already has

- Before writing new code, You MUST check likely project-owned paths for existing components, layout patterns, and design tokens that match the design intent.
- You MUST reuse the project's existing components and tokens instead of generating new equivalents from scratch.

### 4. Honor the response hints by priority

You MUST apply only hint sources that are present and relevant, in this order — earlier sources override later ones:

1. **Code Connect snippets** → use the mapped codebase component directly.
2. **Component documentation links** → follow them for usage and guidelines.
3. **Design annotations** → follow any designer notes or constraints.
4. **Design tokens (CSS variables)** → map them to the project's token system.
5. **Raw hex / absolute positioning** → loosely structured; lean on the screenshot for intent.

#### G2-G4 - Pre-edit

- **G2:** You MUST identify the target stack and adapt the reference to it.
- **G3:** You MUST search likely project-owned paths and identify what will be reused.
- **G4:** You MUST apply present, relevant hints by priority. You MUST NOT search merely to prove a hint is absent.

G2-G4 PASS - `<stack/path; reuse search/result; present hints/application>`

### 5. Reproduce images and icons faithfully

Images and icons come back as exported assets. Apply these rules as you write the code:

- **Render every icon/image from its exported asset.** Never author, redraw, omit, or replace it with a placeholder or screenshot.
- **Sourcing:** remote asset URLs expire in ~7 days. For committed code, download the exact bytes or use the project's data source.

# Implement a Figma Design as Code (Design → Code)

Use this skill to turn a Figma design into code in a target codebase. This is the **read-FROM-Figma** direction: pull design context out of Figma with `get_design_context`, then adapt it into the project's real stack. For the reverse direction — building or updating a design *in* Figma from code — use [figma-generate-design](../figma-generate-design/SKILL.md) instead.

This skill owns the **workflow** for design-to-code. Parameter mechanics (nodeId / fileKey / branchKey extraction, URL parsing, `format`/`query` options, response shape) live on the `get_design_context` tool description itself — follow them there.

**Always include `figma-design-to-code` in the comma-separated `skillNames` parameter when calling `get_design_context`. If this skill was loaded via an MCP resource, you MUST prefix the name with `resource:` (e.g. `resource:figma-design-to-code`).** This is a logging parameter used to track skill usage — it does not affect execution.

## Direction and Scope

- You MUST use this skill for design → code: implementing, translating, or porting a Figma node into code.
- You MUST NOT use this skill to write to Figma.

## Workflow

### Gate Protocol

- Emit exactly three terse gate messages: G1 after design context returns; one combined G2-G4 check before editing; and G5 before finishing. Do not narrate gates between checkpoints.
- A `PASS` MUST cite evidence produced by the required work. You MUST NOT make tool calls solely to emit a gate.
- Gather sufficient evidence for the implementation, not exhaustive evidence. If a requirement is unmet, emit `FAIL`, fix it, then restate the gate.
- You MUST NOT write code until G1 and G2-G4 pass. You MUST NOT finish until G5 passes.
- Gates are self-checks. You MUST NOT change the implementation solely to produce gate evidence.

### 1. Call get_design_context first

- You MUST call `get_design_context` on the target node before writing any code. It is your primary tool — a single call returns reference code, a screenshot, and contextual hints.
- You MUST NOT reach for `get_metadata` or `get_screenshot` as a substitute. Use them only to orient (e.g. picking a node) or to validate, not in place of `get_design_context`.
- If the response is sparse metadata, request only the visible child regions needed to implement the target, preferably in one parallel batch.

#### G1 - Design Context

G1 PASS - `<target node; one-line summary of retrieved HTML-format design regions>`

### 2. Treat the output as a reference, not final code

- The returned code is React + Tailwind enriched with hints. You MUST treat it as a REFERENCE, not as final code to paste verbatim.
- You MUST adapt it to the target project's language, framework, component library, styling system, and conventions. Match the surrounding code.

### 3. Reuse what the project already has

- Before writing new code, You MUST check likely project-owned paths for existing components, layout patterns, and design tokens that match the design intent.
- You MUST reuse the project's existing components and tokens instead of generating new equivalents from scratch.

### 4. Honor the response hints by priority

You MUST apply only hint sources that are present and relevant, in this order — earlier sources override later ones:

1. **Code Connect snippets** → use the mapped codebase component directly.
2. **Component documentation links** → follow them for usage and guidelines.
3. **Design annotations** → follow any designer notes or constraints.
4. **Design tokens (CSS variables)** → map them to the project's token system.
5. **Raw hex / absolute positioning** → loosely structured; lean on the screenshot for intent.

#### G2-G4 - Pre-edit

- **G2:** You MUST identify the target stack and adapt the reference to it.
- **G3:** You MUST search likely project-owned paths and identify what will be reused.
- **G4:** You MUST apply present, relevant hints by priority. You MUST NOT search merely to prove a hint is absent.

G2-G4 PASS - `<stack/path; reuse search/result; present hints/application>`

### 5. Reproduce images and icons faithfully

Images and icons come back as exported assets. Apply these rules as you write the code:

- **Render every icon/image from its exported asset.** Never author, redraw, omit, or replace it with a placeholder or screenshot.
- **Sourcing:** remote asset URLs expire in ~7 days. For committed code, download the exact bytes or use the project's data source.
- **Reuse a project icon component only if its glyph clearly matches**; otherwise use the exported asset.
- **Preserve designed geometry:** You MUST preserve the outer asset box and inner leaf separately, including both dimensions, padding, and aspect ratio.
- Relative fill sizing is allowed only if you verified the container constrains the leaf; otherwise set both leaf dimensions explicitly. You MUST NOT use `auto` for a fixed-size leaf.
- You MUST NOT apply one global size to unlike assets or stretch assets through broad descendant rules.

#### G5 - Asset Fidelity

To pass G5:
- You MUST use the correct source for every asset.
- You MUST verify one representative of each shared sizing rule and every exception preserves intended outer and leaf dimensions.
- You MUST NOT pass on source evidence alone when geometry is unverified.

G5 PASS - `<sources; sizing rules and exceptions; rendered or explicit-dimension evidence>`

Otherwise G5 is `FAIL`. You MUST fix it before finishing.

## Error Recovery

- On a `get_design_context` error, STOP and read the message before retrying.
- If the design URL has no `node-id` (a file-only URL), ask the user for a node-specific URL — You MUST NOT guess or pass an empty `nodeId`.
- On a timeout, retry against a smaller node or selection.
- You MUST NOT silently fall back to hand-writing the screen from the screenshot alone when `get_design_context` can still provide context.

## plugin:figma:figma
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

content.text:
This is a sound call, and it's cleaner than it might look — because A5's rail and B1's grid are already pure presentational components (`cards: readonly ZimmProductCardProps[]` in, nothing Einstein-aware), the entire UI layer doesn't need to change at all. The only places that know about Einstein are the two *container* layers: A6's branch inside `recommended-products/index.tsx` (already committed) and B2's planned page container. That's a small, well-isolated surface to swap.

**Proposed mechanism:** instead of hand-picking product IDs, reuse the same real, live Shopper Search call PLP's own already-merged quick-test integration (`3a5f756`) makes — the one `productListCardMapper.ts` already maps into cards. That keeps this fully compliant with the no-mocking rule (still a real Commerce Cloud API response, just not personalized), avoids me guessing at SKUs I can't verify are valid in this environment, and reuses a proven pattern instead of inventing a new one. Concretely:

- **Rail (A6):** swap the Einstein-sourced product-ID list for a small slice of a generic search result, still routed through A3's existing mapper unchanged.
- **Full History (B2):** same search call, routed through the new `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts` mapper (already planned) unchanged — that mapper only cares about product-shaped data, not where it came from.
- Gate this behind **one** shared, clearly-commented constant (e.g. `EINSTEIN_DEPLOYED = false` in `app/constants/index.ts`, citing the BM finding) so there's a single switch to flip back later, not two that can drift out of sync.
- A2/A3/A4/A5 don't change at all. A4's session-view gate stays exactly as-is too — it's pure local logic, unrelated to Einstein.

**One thing worth naming explicitly rather than assuming:** is this meant to be fully throwaway (deleted once Einstein ships), or is it worth building as a real, permanent graceful-degradation fallback — "Einstein down → show generic real products instead of nothing" — which AGENTS.md's own Graceful Degradation section arguably already calls for? I'm assuming throwaway based on "the wiring, after," which means I'll keep it minimal and heavily flagged rather than polished. Say so if you actually want the permanent version instead.

**Since A6 is already committed** (`0923c82`), I'd handle this as a new, small, separately-flagged step rather than silently reopening it — cleaner revert later, and keeps the "one commit per step" convention this plan's followed throughout.

Want me to update the plan with this now and go ahead and implement it?

content.text:
Good — having the exact current code in front of me changes this from "probably fine" to a precise, confirmed answer. Going step by step:

**A1, A2, A5 — completely unaffected.** A1 is the untouched base scaffold; A2 is a pure card-presentation variation with zero data-source awareness; A5's rail takes `cards` as a prop and has no idea where they came from. Nothing to touch.

**A3 (`recentlyViewedCard.ts`) — unaffected, and I can now say that with confidence rather than assume it.** Its input type is `ShopperProductsTypes.Product & {productId, image?}` — a real Commerce API Product plus two Einstein-only bolt-ons. Every field the mapper actually reads (`name`, `imageGroups`, `price`, `currency`) is a standard field on any plain `getProducts()`/search result, Einstein or not. The only friction is it reads `product.productId` instead of `.id` — a one-line alias (`{...product, productId: product.id}`) at whatever fetches the fallback data, exactly mirroring what Einstein's own `fetchRecProductDetails` already does. **A3 itself needs zero changes.**

**A4 (gate hook) — unaffected, but worth one explicit decision.** It's pure `sessionStorage`/`isRegistered` logic, no Einstein involved. Keeping it as-is means the fallback still only shows up after visiting a PDP (or being logged in) — cold-visiting Cart still shows nothing. I'd leave it wired as-is, since it's real, already-verified behavior and bypassing it would mean we're not exercising the actual shipped gate — but say if you want it forced-on for faster visual QA.

**A6 — this is the one real touch point, and I found something concrete.** Line 226's "dead check" (`!recommendations || recommendations.length < 1`) does *not* block our branch even when Einstein returns `{}` — `{}` is truthy and `.length` is `undefined`, so that guard silently passes through. Execution reaches our branch, the gate passes if you've viewed a PDP, and `recommendations?.recs ?? []` resolves to `[]` — so **the rail renders nothing, silently, indistinguishable from "genuinely no history."** That's very likely what made earlier live-testing look inconsistent — the gate can say "show it" while Einstein hands back nothing, and it just quietly disappears.

The fix is a single, small addition right there: a new hook call (unconditional, alongside `useRecentlyViewedGate()` at line 173 — same rules-of-hooks constraint) that fetches real, non-personalized products, plus a fallback at line 312's `recommendations?.recs ?? []` to use it when Einstein's list is empty. This is also the *only* place that can cover both PDP and Cart at once — since we deliberately never ported Cart's own page (Open Question 5), we have no other shared file to put it in without reopening that decision.

I'd land this as a new commit on top of `0923c82`, not a rewrite of it — same reasoning as before, clean revert once Einstein ships.

**Net effect: only 1 of the 6 commits needs new code (a small addition to A6), nothing needs to be undone.** Want me to update the plan with this exact mechanism and go ahead?

content.text:
Here's the concrete approach, with one correction to my own earlier thinking baked in.

**Design correction first:** I was about to suggest the fallback trigger implicitly off "Einstein's `recs` came back empty" — but that's actually unsafe long-term. Once Einstein is real, a shopper who genuinely has no history *should* see nothing (AC 8), and an empty-recs check can't tell "no history" apart from "Einstein down." So this needs an **explicit, named flag** (`EINSTEIN_DEPLOYED = false` in `app/constants/index.ts`, commented with a citation to the BM finding), not an implicit heuristic — flip one constant when Einstein ships, nothing to reverse-engineer later.

**The plan:**

1. **New step, "A6b — Temporary non-Einstein product source"** (own commit, sits after A6, before B1). One new shared hook: `overrides/app/hooks/useTempRecentlyViewedFallback.ts`. Two-step fetch, mirroring what Einstein's own `fetchRecProductDetails` already does internally: a generic `useProductSearch` (no query filter, matching PLP's `3a5f756` precedent — no guessed SKUs) to get real product IDs, then `useProducts` on those IDs with the same `expand`/`perPricebook`/`allImages` params Einstein's hook uses. Output: real `ShopperProductsTypes.Product[]`, so it satisfies A3's existing type contract with just the `productId: product.id` alias — **A3 itself doesn't change.**

2. **A6's branch gets one small addition**: call the new hook unconditionally (same rules-of-hooks placement as `useRecentlyViewedGate()`), and when `EINSTEIN_DEPLOYED` is `false`, feed its output through A3's mapper instead of `recommendations?.recs`. A4's gate stays wired exactly as today — visiting a PDP first (or being logged in) is still required to see anything, which is real, correct, already-verified behavior, not something this pivot should touch. Flag if you'd rather bypass that too for faster QA — I'd default to leaving it alone.

3. **B1 proceeds exactly as already planned** — `ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid`, `variation: 'plp'`, unchanged. It never touches Einstein at all.

4. **B2 gets built from the start against the same shared hook** rather than `getRecommendations()` — same `EINSTEIN_DEPLOYED` branch, feeding the already-planned `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts` mapper (which was already designed to be source-agnostic — it just reads `tieredPrices`/`imageGroups` off whatever `Product` object it's given). No rework needed there either.

5. **B3 is unaffected** — it's just link visibility based on card count.

**Known, explicit tradeoff while this is on:** AC 8 won't be correctly testable — the rail/grid will show fallback products for anyone who's viewed a PDP, whether or not they have real history. That's the deliberate cost of seeing the UI now; it goes back to normal automatically once `EINSTEIN_DEPLOYED` flips.

**One open call:** how much test investment for `useTempRecentlyViewedFallback.ts`, given it's meant to be deleted once Einstein ships — a full Vitest suite, or just a light smoke check? I'd lean light, given the throwaway lifespan, but it's your call.

Want me to write this into the plan now and start on A6b?
