content.text:
Here's where things stand, in plain terms:

**What we're building**
Two connected things for the Zimmermann site:
1. A "Recently Viewed" row of products — shows up on the product page, the cart, and (we just found out) the product listing page too.
2. A "See Full History" page — click a link on that row and see *everything* you've recently looked at, not just the handful that fit in the row.

**What's actually done**
The row itself (#1) is built and working, code-wise — for the product page and cart. The Full History page (#2) is still just a plan, nothing built yet.

**The plot twist we found**
This whole feature is supposed to pull real, personalized "you looked at this" data from Salesforce's recommendation engine (think "customers who viewed this also viewed" on Amazon). Marcel checked and discovered that engine has actually never been switched on for Zimmermann's real store — on any of it, in any environment. So even though our code is built correctly, right now it has nothing real to show. This isn't just our problem either — it affects every "recommended products" feature on the whole site, not just this one. That's been flagged for whoever owns the Salesforce relationship to sort out; not something we can fix from the code side.

**The workaround**
Rather than sit and wait, we're building the actual UI now using real products that already exist in the store (just not personalized to each shopper) as a stand-in. Once the real recommendation engine gets switched on, we swap the data source — the UI itself won't need to be rebuilt.

**What we just nailed down**
Before building the Full History page, we checked what pieces it needs:
- The product tile/box style it needs — turns out it's identical to one we've already built and tested elsewhere. Free win, no new work.
- The little title bar at the top ("Recently Viewed" / "16 Items") — confirmed exactly what it should look like, and it uses styles we already have.
- The overall grid layout (rows of 4 products) — confirmed.
- A couple of the design links Marcel sent turned out to be dead ends on Figma's side, but it didn't matter — we got the answer another way.
- One small loose end: the exact spacing between product cards needs one more quick check.

**What's next**
Speccing is basically done. Next step is actually building the Full History page.

content.text:
Picture it from a shopper's point of view:

**The Rail — on the product page, cart, and product listing page**

A horizontal row of product photos — just photos, no name or price, nothing else — showing whatever you've recently looked at, most recent first. You can only click a photo; there's no size picker or "add to bag" here, this row is a teaser.

- On phone you see 2 at a time, tablet 3, desktop 5 — swipe/scroll sideways to see the rest (up to a maximum of 5 held in the row itself).
- If your device can't fit everything the row is holding, a "See Full History" link appears next to the row's title — take a phone with 4 recently-viewed items: that's more than the 2 you can see at once, so the link shows up even though a desktop user with the same 4 items wouldn't need it (5 fit fine there).
- Click a photo → straight to that product's page.
- Never looked at anything yet? The row simply doesn't exist on the page at all — no empty box, no placeholder.

**The Full History page — what "See Full History" leads to**

A dedicated page titled "Recently Viewed" with a live count in the top right ("16 Items"). Below that, a grid of *everything* you've viewed (not capped at 5 like the row), using the exact same product-tile style as the product listing page — so this time each tile has photo, name, price (crossed-out "was" price if it's on sale), and a cart button. Hover on desktop and it swaps to a model photo, reveals a size picker; if a product's sold out, the cart button greys out and offers "notify me" instead.

Nothing in your history? You still get a real page — a friendly "nothing here yet" message, a button to go shopping, and a sign-in nudge if you're a guest — never a blank screen.

**The thing under the hood, briefly**

Both pieces are wired to pull from "whatever's recently viewed" as an interchangeable data source. Today that source is real store products (since the actual personalization engine isn't switched on yet); later it becomes true per-shopper history without either of these two pieces needing to be rebuilt.

content.text:
Good question — the answer is: most of the ACs can genuinely pass right now, not just "look like" they pass. A few structurally can't, and those need to be called out explicitly rather than faked. Here's the breakdown:

**The key idea: track real views ourselves, fetch real product data — don't fake anything**

Instead of just sprinkling in arbitrary published products, the better version of the workaround is: when a shopper visits a product page, we record *that real product's ID* ourselves (client-side, in the browser). Then the rail/full-history page fetch *real* product data for those *real* IDs directly from Commerce Cloud — same live API, same product-detail depth (images, price, stock) we already need for was/now pricing and the multi-image gallery. Nothing is mocked or hardcoded; it's real catalog data, just sourced by "what did this browser actually look at" instead of "what did Einstein say to recommend."

This is a small extension of something already built, not new architecture: the gate hook (A4) already writes a session flag when you view a product — this just has it remember *which* product too, not just *that* one happened.

**AC by AC, what actually passes vs. what can't**

Passes for real, fully testable, no caveats:
- Rail shows on PDP/Cart/PLP
- Order is genuinely most-recent-first (it's real browser history now, not simulated)
- Click a tile → real PDP
- View 1+ products → rail appears; view none → it doesn't
- "See Full History" appears/hides based on how many you've actually viewed
- Full History page's item count, was/now pricing, multi-image, hover states, out-of-stock treatment — all real, since we're rendering genuine catalog products that happen to have those real states
- Empty states on both rail and full-history page
- Session-only for guests (sessionStorage genuinely clears at session end)

Structurally can't pass without real Einstein, and shouldn't be faked:
- **Cross-device / cross-session continuity for registered shoppers.** "View something on your phone, see it on your laptop" needs server-side storage — that's the one piece only a real backend can do. A client-side stand-in is device-local by nature, full stop.

For that one, the honest move is to state it plainly as a known, temporary, accepted gap in the PR and to whoever signs off testing — not quietly skip it and hope nobody checks. We could optionally extend the local tracking to `localStorage` for registered users too, so it at least survives a browser session close (better than nothing), but it still won't cross devices — worth being upfront that this is a partial mitigation, not a fix.

**Why this isn't wasted work once Einstein lands**

The only thing that changes later is "where does the list of product IDs come from" — swap our local tracker for Einstein's response. Everything downstream (the real-product-data fetch, the was/now/multi-image mapping, the rail, the full-history grid) stays exactly as built. That downstream part is work we need either way, not a throwaway.

Want me to fold this into the plan as the concrete interim data-source design before we start building B1?

### Interim data source — Einstein unavailable, ship against real browser-tracked history (Marcel, 2026-09-08)

**Why this exists.** Einstein is confirmed "Not Deployed" on every real Zimmermann site (see Open
Question 6) — not a data-quality nuance, a total absence of any engine to call. Rather than block
the whole build on a platform-provisioning timeline outside this team's control, Marcel directed:
ship the UI now against **real, live Commerce Cloud product data**, sourced by **this browser's own
actual view history**, tracked client-side — not Einstein, and not any hardcoded/mocked fixture
(AGENTS.md's "no mocking" rule is fully respected: every product shown is real and live-fetched,
only the *list of which IDs to fetch* is sourced differently). A follow-up ticket (not yet created)
swaps that one seam for real Einstein once SFCC-112 unblocks; everything else in this build is
intended to survive that swap unchanged.

**The seam, precisely — this is what makes the later swap small.** Two independent concerns, today
both interim, only one of which changes later:
1. **"Which product IDs has this shopper recently viewed?"** — today: read from browser storage,
   written by this shopper's own PDP visits. Later: Einstein's `getRecommendations` response. **This
   is the only piece the Einstein follow-up ticket touches.**
2. **"Given those IDs, fetch real product data and turn it into cards"** — a live Shopper Products
   `getProducts` call (`allImages: true`, `perPricebook: true`, `expand: [...]` — the same
   three-flag combination already confirmed correct three independent times this session: Einstein's
   own `fetchRecProductDetails`, the PLP quick-test mapper, and the `zimmproductcard-live-demo`
   branch) plus a mapper. **This is real, permanent work regardless of data source** — it's the same
   was/now-pricing (`getPriceData`) and multi-image (`imageGroups`) work B2 already needed (Open
   Question 16), not thrown away when Einstein arrives.

**What this revises (already-committed steps, not just new B1/B2 work):**
- **A4** — `useRecentlyViewedGate.ts` is renamed to `useRecentlyViewedHistory.ts` and extended: it
  already writes a session flag on PDP view; it now also **records the viewed product's ID**, not
  just a boolean. Not a protected/shared hook (not on either hook-protection list, single consumer
  today), so the rename costs nothing structurally — see A4's rewrite below. This is the one file
  where "browser/local it is" is literally implemented.
- **A3** — the mapper's input shape changes from Einstein's merged rec+product object to a plain
  Shopper Product from our own `getProducts` call. Its output contract and its own scope decision
  (image-only, no price, no gallery — A2's `recentlyViewed` variation is unchanged) do **not**
  change; only where the input object comes from does.
- **A6** — the `recommender === EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED` branch trigger is
  unchanged (the base pages still pass that same recommender prop regardless of what we do with
  it) — what changes is that inside the branch, `recommendations.recs` (Einstein's response) is
  never read; the new history hook + a real `getProducts` call are used instead.
- **B2** — same swap: the page container calls the new history hook instead of
  `getRecommendations`, and feeds the *full, uncapped* ID list (not the rail's 5-item slice) into
  the richer was/now/multi-image mapper already planned.

**Storage mechanics, per "browser/local it is":**
- **Guests:** `sessionStorage` — unchanged from A4's existing design, still correctly satisfies AC 6
  (session-scoped, cleared at session end).
- **Registered shoppers:** `localStorage` — a genuine, explicit, temporary deviation from both AC 7
  ("available on login from any device") and the ticket's own Assumption ("storage... handled by
  SFCC"). `localStorage` survives closing the browser (better than nothing, testable), but is still
  **device-local** — it cannot and will not satisfy cross-device continuity. This is not a
  workaround for that AC, it's an explicit, stated non-fix pending the Einstein follow-up — must be
  called out plainly in the PR body and to whoever signs off testing, not discovered by a confused
  reviewer. AC 7 should be marked N/A-pending-follow-up for this PR, not silently tested against a
  single device and called passing.
- **De-duplication / ordering:** viewing a product already in history moves it to the front rather
  than creating a duplicate entry — required for AC 2's "most-recent-first" to hold up under repeat
  views, and needs its own explicit test (view A, B, A again → order must be `[A, B]`, not `[A, B, A]`
  or `[B, A]` misordered).
- **Stored-history cap:** a new named constant, distinct from `RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_MAX_ITEMS` (which
  only ever governs the rail's *display* slice) — proposed `RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED = 50`
  as a sane ceiling against unbounded growth, not a UX-confirmed number. **Owner: Marcel/Jasmijn to
  confirm the real number** — not a build blocker, ship the proposed default and revise if told
  otherwise.

**What stays exactly as planned, unaffected by this whole section:** A2 (variation config), A5 (rail
UI), B1 (grid UI) — all purely presentational, receive cards as props, and have never cared where
those props came from. This is the container/presentational split (`components.md`) paying off
exactly as designed.

**To verify at implementation time, not guessed here:** the exact `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`
hook name for a batch product-detail fetch (likely `useProducts`, plural, alongside the already-used
singular `useProduct` — confirm against `node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/dist/` per AGENTS.md's
own Gotchas note before trusting the name).

**Not a scope decision for this PR:** what the Einstein follow-up ticket looks like in detail (does
it reuse the `getProducts`-and-map layer, or fully replace it with `fetchRecProductDetails`'s own
internal enrichment?). Left for that ticket, once it exists — this section only needs to ship a
clean, honest interim, not pre-solve the migration.

### A4 — AC-8 gate hook, plus the PDP write

Create `overrides/app/hooks/useRecentlyViewedGate.ts`.

This answers **finding 28** — the recommender returns a two-product baseline for a visitor with zero
history, so `recs.length === 0` never fires and AC 8 is not implementable from the response. The gate
is a **local boolean**, not a copy of Einstein's list:

```
hasRecentlyViewed = sessionFlagIsSet || isRegistered
```

- `markProductViewed()` writes a session-scoped flag to `sessionStorage`, called from the existing
  Einstein `useEffect` in `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` (lines 772–801), alongside
  the `einstein.sendViewProduct` calls already there. One import, one call, guarded by the same
  `if (product)`.
- `isRegistered` from `useCustomerType()` — the same hook `use-einstein.js:449` already uses.

**Why this maps the ACs exactly:** `sessionStorage` is literally session-scoped and cleared at session
end — **AC 6**. `isRegistered` short-circuits the local flag, so an authenticated shopper on a device
they have never browsed on still gets server-side history — **AC 7**. It is a strict improvement on
trusting Einstein alone: the SLAS `usid` can outlive a browser session, so this gate makes AC 6 *true*
rather than assumed.

**Confirmed 2026-09-07, not a frontend gap.** SFCC-83's own Assumptions section states *"the storage
of Recently Viewed is handled by SFCC."* This hook's design already matches that: it holds no product
list of its own, only a local boolean answering "should the rail be visible," while the actual
recently-viewed history stays entirely server/Einstein-side. Recorded here because an earlier
conversation-level claim (before this plan was checked against the real AC text) treated the
temporary-guest/persistent-registered storage split as unbuilt frontend scope — it isn't; it's this
already-correct delegation, with the one real residual being finding 28/Open Question 6
(Einstein's own backfill behaviour), not anything this hook needs to change.

**Stated assumption (must appear in the PR body):** a *registered* shopper who has genuinely never
viewed anything still sees the two-product baseline. That residual is owned by Open Question 6. Do not
paper over it with a heuristic.

**Pass criteria**
- SSR-safe: initial state `false`, resolved in `useEffect`. No `sessionStorage` access during render.
  No hydration mismatch — the rail does not exist on first paint and appears after hydration. (Also
  good for LCP; the PDP rail is inside `<Island hydrateOn='visible'>` anyway.)
- Wrapped in `try/catch` — Safari private mode throws on `sessionStorage`. Failure degrades to `false`
  (no rail), never an exception.
- JSDoc with `@returns` (`components.md` > Hooks).
- Vitest: no flag + guest → `false`; flag + guest → `true`; no flag + registered → `true`;
  `sessionStorage` throwing → `false`; first render before effect → `false`.
- **Make each fail on purpose first.** The FED handbook's finding 18 trap is a test that passes
  because it was written against the only arrangement already correct.
- The PDP change is exactly two lines. Nothing else in `product-detail/index.tsx` moves (AGENTS.md
  Hard Rule #5 — no refactoring upward).

### A4 — Recently-viewed history hook, plus the PDP write

**🔴 REVISED 2026-09-08 — renamed and re-designed, per "Interim data source" in §2. Read this whole
step before implementing; the original boolean logic below is no longer correct and would ship a
real bug if built as originally specced.**

Create `overrides/app/hooks/useRecentlyViewedHistory.ts` (was `useRecentlyViewedGate.ts`).

This still answers **finding 28** — the *original* concern was that Einstein's recommender returns a
two-product baseline for a visitor with zero history, so `recs.length === 0` never fires and AC 8
isn't implementable from the response. With Einstein out of the picture for this build, that specific
failure mode can't happen either way (there is no Einstein response to leak a baseline from) — but
the fix is still needed, now for a more basic reason: something has to track what "recently viewed"
even means without Einstein.

**The boolean logic changes, not just the storage mechanism — this is the one real gotcha in this
revision.** The original design was:

```
hasRecentlyViewed = sessionFlagIsSet || isRegistered
```

`isRegistered` was a deliberate short-circuit: trust that a logged-in shopper has *some* server-side
Einstein history even on a fresh device. **That assumption breaks entirely once Einstein is out of
the loop** — there is no server-side history to trust anymore. Built as originally specced, every
registered shopper would show `hasRecentlyViewed = true` unconditionally, including one who has
never viewed anything in this interim system on any device — gating the rail *open* with zero real
cards behind it. That's a real, shippable bug, not a hypothetical; it must not be carried into the
interim build. **Corrected logic:**

```
hasRecentlyViewed = recentlyViewedIds.length > 0
```

— true for both guests and registered shoppers alike, based purely on this interim system's own
tracked history. `isRegistered` still matters, just for a different purpose now: it selects *which*
storage to read/write (see below), not whether to bypass the check.

**New return shape:** `{hasRecentlyViewed: boolean, recentlyViewedIds: readonly string[],
markProductViewed: (productId: string) => void}` — the boolean is now derived from the ID list, not
tracked independently, so the two can never disagree.

- `markProductViewed(productId)` writes to `sessionStorage` (guest) or `localStorage` (registered,
  via `isRegistered` from `useCustomerType()` — the same hook `use-einstein.js:449` already uses) —
  called from the existing Einstein `useEffect` in
  `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` (lines 772–801), alongside the
  `einstein.sendViewProduct` calls already there (left untouched — that call is unrelated real
  analytics, not this build's concern). One import, one call, guarded by the same `if (product)`.
- **De-duplication / move-to-front:** if `productId` is already in the stored list, remove the old
  entry before prepending — never a duplicate, and a re-view correctly becomes "most recent" again.
- **Cap the stored list** at `RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED` (proposed 50 — see §2) — trim from
  the tail, oldest-first, on write.

**AC mapping, restated for the interim system:** `sessionStorage` is session-scoped and cleared at
session end — **AC 6**, unchanged. **AC 7 (cross-device for registered shoppers) is explicitly
*not* satisfied by this interim design** — `localStorage` is still device-local. This must be stated
plainly in the PR body and marked N/A-pending-the-Einstein-follow-up for this specific AC, not tested
against a single device and reported as passing. See §2's "Interim data source" for the full
reasoning — this is a stated, accepted gap, not an oversight.

**Confirmed 2026-09-07, not a frontend gap** (pre-dates and is unaffected by this revision — restated
for continuity): SFCC-83's own Assumptions section states *"the storage of Recently Viewed is
handled by SFCC."* The interim system above is a **temporary, explicit stand-in** for that
assumption while Einstein is unavailable, not a rejection of it — once the Einstein follow-up lands,
this hook's job reverts to a thin boolean/gate again and the real history moves back server-side, per
the original design intent this section used to describe.

**Superseded by the above, not applicable to the interim build:** the old "stated assumption" about
a registered shopper with genuinely zero Einstein history still seeing a two-product baseline
(Open Question 6's original framing) — that residual was specific to trusting Einstein's own
baseline behaviour, which the interim system never calls, so it cannot leak through here. It returns
once the Einstein follow-up is built, at which point Open Question 6's original text applies again.

**Pass criteria**
- SSR-safe: initial state `{hasRecentlyViewed: false, recentlyViewedIds: []}`, resolved in
  `useEffect`. No storage access during render. No hydration mismatch — the rail does not exist on
  first paint and appears after hydration. (Also good for LCP; the PDP rail is inside
  `<Island hydrateOn='visible'>` anyway.)
- Wrapped in `try/catch` — Safari private mode throws on both `sessionStorage` and `localStorage`.
  Failure degrades to `{hasRecentlyViewed: false, recentlyViewedIds: []}`, never an exception.
- JSDoc with `@returns` (`components.md` > Hooks).
- Vitest: empty storage + guest → `false`/`[]`; one ID + guest → `true`/`[id]`; empty storage +
  **registered** → `false`/`[]` (**the corrected case — must be tested explicitly, since this is
  exactly where the old short-circuit bug would have shipped silently**); re-viewing an existing ID
  moves it to front with no duplicate; writing past the cap trims the oldest entry; storage throwing
  → safe empty default; first render before effect → safe empty default.
- **Make each fail on purpose first.** The FED handbook's finding 18 trap is a test that passes
  because it was written against the only arrangement already correct — this applies doubly to the
  registered-with-zero-history case above, since that's precisely the case the old logic got wrong.
- The PDP change is exactly two lines (now passing `product.id` into `markProductViewed`, not a
  no-arg call). Nothing else in `product-detail/index.tsx` moves (AGENTS.md Hard Rule #5 — no
  refactoring upward).

content.content:
1	/**
2	 * Maps one Recently Viewed recommendation onto the subset of `ZimmProductCard` props the
3	 * `recentlyViewed` variation (SFCC-83) actually renders.
4	 *
5	 * Input is exactly what `use-einstein.js`'s `fetchRecProductDetails` produces (search that name
6	 * in `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-einstein.js`): an Einstein rec
7	 * merged with its matching Commerce API product, fetched via `getProducts` with `expand:
8	 * ['availability', 'links', 'promotions', 'options', 'images', 'prices', 'variations']` —
9	 * `{...rec, ...product, productId: rec.id, image: {disBaseLink: rec.imageUrl, alt:
10	 * rec.productName}}`.
11	 *
12	 * Modelled on `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/productInfo.ts` — no React/react-intl import,
13	 * `formatPrice` injected as a parameter so this module stays independently testable — and on the
14	 * general shape of `liveProductCardDemoMapper.ts` (`feature/zimmproductcard-live-demo`, not this
15	 * branch — read for its approach, not imported). Unlike that demo mapper, this is a production
16	 * path: real `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` SDK types are used wherever they exist (AGENTS.md > Type
17	 * Definitions), and only the two fields the SDK doesn't export (`productId`, the flat Einstein
18	 * `image`) are hand-rolled, each with its own why-comment below.
19	 *
20	 * Deliberately narrow scope, stated here rather than left as a silent gap: this mapper only ever
21	 * returns `currentPrice` (an active selling price). It does not attempt was/now sale-price
22	 * detection (`originalPrice`) — that needs `getPriceData`-style pricebook logic
23	 * (`productInfo.ts`'s own `PdpSourcePrice`) that this merged Einstein shape has no equivalent of,
24	 * and the `recentlyViewed` variation renders no price at all today (see
25	 * `zimmProductCard/index.tsx`'s `recentlyViewed` `VARIATION_CONFIG` row — `showContent: false`).
26	 * Mapping `currentPrice` anyway costs nothing and means a future consumer of this same mapper
27	 * (e.g. a variation that does render price) isn't blocked on this file being revisited.
28	 */
29	import type { ShopperProductsTypes } from 'commerce-sdk-isomorphic';
30	import { filterImageGroups } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/product-utils';
31	import { productUrlBuilder } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/url';
32	import type { ZimmProductCardBaseProps, ZimmProductCardImage } from '../components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard';
33	
34	/**
35	 * The real Commerce API `Product` (`commerce-sdk-isomorphic`'s own `ShopperProductsTypes.Product`
36	 * — not hand-rolled), plus the two fields `fetchRecProductDetails` bolts on that have no SDK
37	 * equivalent:
38	 */
39	export type RecentlyViewedProduct = ShopperProductsTypes.Product & {
40	  /** Set by `fetchRecProductDetails` to `rec.id`. Guaranteed present and equal to `Product.id`
41	   *  for every entry that function produces (it already filters out any rec with no matching
42	   *  product before this shape exists at all) — read this rather than `.id` only because it's
43	   *  the field the real runtime hook explicitly produces this way. */
44	  productId: string;
45	  /** The same function's own quick single-reference image (Einstein's own `rec.imageUrl`/
46	   *  `rec.productName`), distinct from the full product's own `imageGroups` array below — used
47	   *  as a fallback only when `imageGroups` filtering comes up empty. See `selectPrimaryImage`. */
48	  image?: { disBaseLink?: string; alt?: string };
49	};
50	
51	/** Formats a bare amount for the storefront. Injected so this module stays free of react-intl,
52	 *  mirroring `productInfo.ts`'s own `FormatPrice` shape. */
53	export type FormatPrice = (amount: number, currency: string) => string;
54	
55	/**

/*

import React from 'react'
import PropTypes from 'prop-types'
import {FormattedMessage} from 'react-intl'
import {
    Box,
    Button,
    Stack,
    Center,
    Text
} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui'
import {AccountIcon, BasketIcon} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/icons'
import Link from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/link'

const EmptyCart = ({isRegistered}) => {
    return (
        <Box data-testid="sf-cart-empty" flex="1" minWidth="100%" width="full" background="gray.50">
            <Center>
                <Stack spacing={6} width={['343px', '444px']} marginTop="20%" marginBottom="20%">
                    <Box align="center">
                        <BasketIcon boxSize={[8, 10]} />
                    </Box>
                    <Stack spacing={8}>
                        <Stack spacing={2}>
                            <Text
                                lineHeight={1}
                                align="center"
                                fontSize={['18px', '2xl']}
                                fontWeight="bold"
                            >
                                <FormattedMessage
                                    defaultMessage="Your cart is empty."
                                    id="empty_cart.description.empty_cart"
                                />
                            </Text>

                            <Text align="center" fontSize="md" color="gray.700">
                                {isRegistered ? (
                                    <FormattedMessage
                                        defaultMessage="Continue shopping to add items to your cart."
                                        id="empty_cart.message.continue_shopping"
                                    />
                                ) : (
                                    <FormattedMessage
                                        defaultMessage="Sign in to retrieve your saved items or continue shopping."
                                        id="empty_cart.message.sign_in_or_continue_shopping"
                                    />
                                )}
                            </Text>
                        </Stack>
                        <Stack justify="center" direction={['column', 'row']} spacing={4}>
                            <Button
                                as={Link}
                                href={'/'}
                                width={['343px', '220px']}
                                variant={isRegistered ? 'solid' : 'outline'}
                                color={isRegistered ? 'white' : 'blue.600'}
                            >
                                <FormattedMessage
                                    defaultMessage="Continue Shopping"
                                    id="empty_cart.link.continue_shopping"
                                />
                            </Button>
                            {!isRegistered && (
                                <Button
                                    as={Link}
                                    href="/account"
                                    width={['343px', '220px']}
                                    rightIcon={<AccountIcon />}
                                    variant="solid"
                                >
                                    <FormattedMessage
                                        defaultMessage="Sign In"
                                        id="empty_cart.link.sign_in"
                                    />
                                </Button>
                            )}
                        </Stack>
                    </Stack>
                </Stack>
            </Center>
        </Box>
    )
}
EmptyCart.propTypes = {isRegistered: PropTypes.bool}

export default EmptyCart

 * file being revisited — extending it to also call `getPriceData` at that point would be a small,
 * well-precedented addition, not new pricebook work.
 */

input.new_string:
- **Stored-history cap — RESOLVED 2026-09-08 (Marcel: "how would this be treated if Einstein were
  available? do the same as that").** Real Einstein has no client-supplied "how far back to
  remember" parameter at all — `getRecommendations` never tells Einstein how much history to keep;
  the recommender's own BM configuration governs how many it *returns* per call, and the frontend
  never owns or enforces a storage limit of its own. Mirroring that: **this is not a product/UX
  decision needing Jasmijn's sign-off, and the earlier "50, propose a number" framing was the wrong
  shape of answer.** The stored list should accumulate real history unbounded from a UX standpoint,
  same as Einstein never truncates for UX reasons — the only cap needed is a generous **engineering
  safety ceiling** against pathological unbounded growth (a multi-year shopper with thousands of
  entries), which is an implementation detail, not a business rule. `RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED
  = 500` — high enough that normal usage never approaches it, low enough to bound worst-case storage
  (a product ID is ~15-20 chars; 500 of them is a few KB, nowhere near `localStorage`'s ~5-10MB
  origin limit). **Open Question 17 is closed** — no further confirmation needed.

content.text:
Ran the checks. Good news first, then one real problem the feasibility pass was built to catch.

**Confirmed clean (no plan changes needed):**
- Baseline test suite: **165/165 passing** across the existing recently-viewed + zimmProductCard suites — solid foundation.
- `routes.tsx`'s real structure matches the plan's placement claim exactly — `/preview` sits right where "after `..._routes`, before `/:slug`" describes; `/recently-viewed` goes beside it.
- No icon in this project's icon barrel fits an empty-state "recently viewed" illustration — confirms "omit the icon" was the right call, not just a hedge.
- `useRecentlyViewedGate`'s only real consumers are exactly what the plan assumed (PDP, `recommended-products`, its own test) — the rename is safe.
- No naming collision for the new constants.
- Checked zimmTokens.ts's *entire* numeric scale this time (not a subset) — confirms, exhaustively, that 96px genuinely has no token anywhere in it.

**Real problem found:** `getProducts` (the endpoint both `useProducts` and Einstein's own `fetchRecProductDetails` call) has a **hard limit of 24 product IDs per request** — it's in the SDK's own doc comment, not something either of us anticipated. This directly collides with B2's "fetch the full, uncapped history" design: any shopper with more than 24 recently-viewed items can't be fetched in one call. `useProducts` is a React Query hook, so it can't just be called in a loop to batch — that would need dropping to the imperative `client.shopperProducts.getProducts()` pattern (which is what Einstein's own code actually does, not coincidentally).

Two ways to resolve it:
- **Cap the Full History page's fetch/display at 24** — simplest, matches the API's natural ceiling, and is a perfectly normal "recently viewed" page size industry-wide.
- **Batch in groups of 24** via the imperative pattern — more correct for a genuinely heavy history, more code.

I'd default to capping at 24 rather than building batching for a case that's unlikely to matter in practice — but this is a real scope call, your take?

Smaller correction found alongside it: `getPriceData`'s `currentPrice` comes from its own internal `findLowestPrice()`, not a flat `product.price` field — so B2's new mapper needs to pull *both* `currentPrice` and `originalPrice` from the same `getPriceData()` call, not mix that with a separately-read `product.price`, or the two could disagree on a multi-variant product. No decision needed there, just noting it so I don't miss it at implementation time.

1	import React from 'react';
2	import type { ReactNode } from 'react';
3	import { chakra, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
4	import { Link as RouteLink } from 'react-router-dom';
5	import { RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_MAX_ITEMS } from 'app/constants';
6	import { ZimmProductCard } from '../zimmProductCard';
7	import type { ZimmProductCardProps } from '../zimmProductCard';
8	
9	// Same `chakra(RouteLink)` wrap this component family already establishes for its own internal
10	// links (zimmProductCard/index.tsx's `MediaOnlyCardLink`, zimmProductCardContent/index.tsx's
11	// `ProductNameLink`) — used here for the See-Full-History link, which navigates to the SFCC-84
12	// Recently Viewed Full History page, an internal route, not an external URL.
13	const SeeAllLink = chakra(RouteLink);
14	
15	export type ZimmRecentlyViewedRailProps = {
16	  /**
17	   * Rendered as-is, with no textStyle imposed by this component. Typed as `ReactNode`, not
18	   * `string`, deliberately: this component owns no copy/intl (the container, A6, does), and this
19	   * step's own brief gives no confirmed Figma text-style reading for the title itself (only the
20	   * header row's overall height) — so rather than guess at one, this component only lays the
21	   * title out, leaving whatever styling it already carries (e.g. a caller-supplied `Heading`)
22	   * untouched.
23	   */
24	  title: ReactNode;
25	  /**
26	   * Rendered in the exact order received (AC 2: most-recent-first, left to right) — no sorting or
27	   * reordering happens here. Capped to `RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_MAX_ITEMS` regardless of length; see
28	   * that constant's own comment (app/constants/index.ts) for why the cap has to live here rather
29	   * than in the request that produced this array.
30	   */
31	  cards: readonly ZimmProductCardProps[];
32	  /** Href to the SFCC-84 Recently Viewed Full History page. The See-Full-History link only
33	   *  renders when this is provided — see the render body below. */
34	  seeAllHref?: string;
35	  /**
36	   * No default/fallback text is supplied when this is omitted while `seeAllHref` is provided —
37	   * this component owns no copy or intl (see the module docblock), so inventing an English
38	   * fallback here would risk shipping untranslated text on non-English storefronts. In real usage
39	   * the container (A6) is expected to always supply this alongside `seeAllHref`.
40	   */
41	  seeAllLabel?: string;
42	};
43	
44	const ZIMM_RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_RECIPE = 'ZimmRecentlyViewedRail';
45	
46	/**
47	 * SFCC-83 — the Recently Viewed rail organism (build plan section A5). Purely presentational:
48	 * data arrives as props, no data-fetching, no `useEinstein`, no `useIntl` — see
49	 * .claude/rules/components.md's container/presentational split. The container (A6) is
50	 * responsible for building `cards` (via A3's Einstein-rec-to-card mapper), gating this
51	 * component's visibility (A4's `hasRecentlyViewed`), and supplying `title`/`seeAllLabel` copy.
52	 *
53	 * Structure mirrors Figma exactly: a `header` row (title left, the See-Full-History link right)
54	 * above a horizontally scrollable `group` of `ZimmProductCard`s. No rail-level arrow buttons —
55	 * `ZimmProductCardMedia` already carries its own intra-card carousel arrows, and a second set at
56	 * the rail level would collide with them (see zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts's own docblock for
57	 * the Figma node evidence). Paging is native horizontal scroll with CSS scroll-snap only.
58	 *
59	 * `cards` is typed as the full `ZimmProductCardProps` union, matching this step's own given
60	 * component contract verbatim — this component therefore spreads each entry straight into
61	 * `ZimmProductCard` (`<ZimmProductCard {...card} />`) rather than forcing
62	 * `variation: 'recentlyViewed'` onto every card itself. In real usage every entry already carries
63	 * that variation by construction (A3's mapper produces `recentlyViewed`-shaped cards, matching
64	 * `variation: 'recentlyViewed'` in the type union — see zimmProductCard/index.tsx's
65	 * `ZimmProductCardRecentlyViewedVariation`) — this component trusts that contract rather than
66	 * re-asserting it, consistent with staying purely presentational.
67	 *
68	 * `data-testid="product-card"` / `data-product-id` on each rendered card come from
69	 * `ZimmProductCard`'s own root (zimmProductCard/index.tsx: "a DOM hook for QA automation/
70	 * analytics") — this component adds no additional per-card test hook of its own.
71	 */
72	export const ZimmRecentlyViewedRail = ({ title, cards, seeAllHref, seeAllLabel }: ZimmRecentlyViewedRailProps) => {
73	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_RECIPE, {});
74	
75	  // Cap is enforced here, client-side, regardless of how many cards were passed in — see
76	  // RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_MAX_ITEMS's own comment (app/constants/index.ts): the Einstein API this
77	  // data ultimately comes from does not itself honour a requested limit. A slice, never a sort —
78	  // order is otherwise untouched (AC 2).
79	  const visibleCards = cards.slice(0, RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_MAX_ITEMS);
80	
81	  // Second guard behind A4's own visibility gate, which lives in the container, not here — an
82	  // empty rail renders nothing at all, not an empty shell.
83	  if (visibleCards.length === 0) {
84	    return null;
85	  }
86	
87	  return (
88	    <chakra.div __css={styles.container} data-testid="recently-viewed-rail">
89	      <chakra.div __css={styles.header}>
90	        {title}
91	        {seeAllHref && (
92	          <SeeAllLink to={seeAllHref} textStyle="linkLg" __css={styles.seeAllLink}>
93	            {seeAllLabel}
94	          </SeeAllLink>
95	        )}
96	      </chakra.div>
97	      <chakra.div __css={styles.group} data-testid="recently-viewed-rail-group">
98	        {visibleCards.map((card) => (
99	          <chakra.div key={card.id} __css={styles.card}>
100	            <ZimmProductCard {...card} />
101	          </chakra.div>
102	        ))}
103	      </chakra.div>
104	    </chakra.div>
105	  );
106	};

Read all three of those files in full first — they are your ground truth for the real shapes involved, more reliable than any paraphrase below.

Read the plan at `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-83+84/plan.md` next — specifically the "Interim data source" subsection in §2, and step A6 (marked "🔴 REVISED 2026-09-08").

**Your one file to fix:** `overrides/app/components/recommended-products/index.tsx`, plus its test `overrides/app/components/recommended-products/index.test.tsx`. Right now `npx tsc --noEmit` fails on this exact file (`Cannot find module '../../hooks/useRecentlyViewedGate'`) — that's the expected, known state Phase 1 left behind for you to fix, not a mistake.

Read the current file in full before touching it — it has an extensive docblock explaining its own structure, most of which is still accurate and should be preserved/updated in place, not rewritten wholesale.

**What needs to change, and why — read this carefully, it's more than a rename:**

1. Line ~105: `import { useRecentlyViewedGate } from '../../hooks/useRecentlyViewedGate';` → `import { useRecentlyViewedHistory } from '../../hooks/useRecentlyViewedHistory';`. Line ~173: `const hasRecentlyViewed = useRecentlyViewedGate();` → destructure whatever Phase 1's hook actually returns (read it to get the exact shape — don't guess).

2. **A real bug I found reading this file directly, not yet fixed by anyone — you must fix it, it's in scope for this step:** look at the `useEffect` around lines 175-192. It unconditionally calls `getRecommendations(recommender, _products)` for *every* recommender, including Recently-Viewed, before the render-time branch (`if (recommender === EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED)`, around line 302) ever runs. Once this branch stops needing Einstein's response at all (per the plan's "Interim data source" section — the whole point of this phase), that effect must skip firing `getRecommendations`/`getZoneRecommendations` specifically when `recommender === EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED` — otherwise it's a real network call fetching data nothing will ever read.

/**
 * Data-URI SVG at ZimmProductCardMedia's own 2:3 aspect ratio — no network needed, keeps stories
 * deterministic in CI. Same no-network precedent as zimmProductCard/index.stories.tsx's own
 * PRIMARY_IMAGE.
 *
 * **Bordered + numbered, not a flat fill (fixed 2026-09-08 — flagged via live Storybook
 * testing).** An earlier version of this used one identical flat `fill='#f6f4f1'` rect for every
 * card, with no border. That's indistinguishable from broken/missing images to a human eyeballing
 * the story — worse, `zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts`'s `group` part has a deliberate zero gap
 * between cards (matching the real Figma spec), so five identical, borderless, flush-together
 * rectangles visually merge into what looks like one giant block rather than five cards. The
 * component itself was never broken (`OverCap`'s own `play` function below already asserts
 * exactly 5 `data-testid="product-card"` elements render) — only this story's own placeholder
 * failed to make that visible. Fix: a visible border plus the card's own position number baked
 * into the SVG, so each card's boundary and identity are both genuinely legible at a glance, and
 * the rendered left-to-right order (AC 2) is visually self-checkable too.
 *
 * The literal `alt` text here is overridden to `''` internally by ZimmProductCard's own
 * `recentlyViewed` render branch regardless of what is supplied (see zimmProductCard/index.tsx's
 * own docblock), so its exact wording doesn't matter — kept descriptive anyway for readability.
 */

### What the mapper does

`selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard(product, formatPrice)` maps a plain Commerce API `Product` (`ShopperProductsTypes.Product`, the exact shape `recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts` produces) to `ZimmProductCardBaseProps & ZimmProductCardPlpVariation` — badge, size chips, was/now pricing, multi-image gallery, with `headingLevel: 'h3'` and `variation: 'plp'` baked in directly (confirmed types by reading `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.tsx` directly). It is a pure module — no React/react-intl import, `formatPrice` injected as a parameter, same as `recentlyViewedCard.ts`.

- **Price fix (the core ask):** `selectPriceFields` calls base `getPriceData(product)` once (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/product-utils.js:123-170`, read directly) and derives both `currentPrice` and `originalPrice` from that single call's `currentPrice`/`listPrice`/`isOnSale`. `originalPrice` is only set when `isOnSale` is true. Neither field ever reads a flat `product.price` separately.
- **Multi-image:** `selectGalleryImages` is a near-verbatim port of `productListCardMapper.ts`'s function (same "largest group wins, viewpoint-agnostic" heuristic), re-pointed at `product.imageGroups` directly.
- **Primary image:** not ported from `productListCardMapper.ts` (that reads a Search-hit-only flat `image` field that doesn't exist on plain `Product`). Confirmed by reading `commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.esm.d.ts:59783-59835` directly (the block backing `ShopperProductsTypes.Product`): **there is no typed `c_productBadges` field on the plain `Product` type** — only a generic `{[key: string]: any}` index signature, which would let `product.c_productBadges` compile without error but proves nothing about whether it's actually populated. `c_productBadges` is confirmed real only on `ShopperSearchTypes.ProductSearchHit` (the Search-index endpoint `productListCardMapper.ts` reads it from). import type { SystemStyleObject } from '@chakra-ui/react';
import { breakpoints } from 'app/theme/foundation';

/**
 * Recipe for the Recently Viewed Full History grid organism (SFCC-84), build plan section B1.
 * Design source: `Zimmermann_Designs` file, `3332:35655` → `Container` → `PLP Bar desktop`
 * (`3332:37131`, 1440×75, title left / item-count right) + `Sidebar` (`3332:35664`, four stacked
 * `Products Module Desktop` instances, each 1440×606, containing `Products S Desktop` cards at
 * 288×542, x = 0/384/768/1152 — a `plp`-shaped `ZimmProductCard`, not a new card; see index.tsx's
 * own `cards` JSDoc for the `variation: 'plp'` citation). **This source is provisional per
 * Marcel's 2026-09-04 precedence rule** (it is not a PDP/Recently Viewed node in the authoritative
 * `Zimmermann_Design_System_2026` file `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail`'s own recipe uses) — that ranking
 * is unaffected by the "confirmed" values below; see index.tsx's own module docblock for why both
 * things are true at once.
 *
 * Parts: `container`, `header`, `grid` — reconciled against index.tsx's own `useMultiStyleConfig`
 * reads by `ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts`. No `card` part (contrast
 * `zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts`'s own `card` part): the rail fixes a per-breakpoint PIXEL width
 * on each item because it lays out a horizontally-scrolling flex row with no requirement to fill
 * the viewport exactly. This is a real grid, not a scroller — `grid` below uses fractional
 * (`1fr`) column tracks instead, so each card's rendered width falls out of the container width
 * divided across the current column count with nothing extra to style per card; `ZimmProductCard`
 * itself still has no width/height opinion of its own (`zimmProductCard.css.ts`), same precedent
 * the rail's own docblock already establishes.
 *
 * HORIZONTAL GAP — 96px, GENUINELY UN-TOKENISED (not a search gap). Checked at two independent
 * Figma sources per Marcel's own steer (build plan §B1, "RESOLVED 2026-09-08, checked twice"): the
 * page-level instance (`3332:35655`) and, separately, the master "Product Card Group" component
 * (`40000301:11694`, `Size=Desktop, Display=4`, node `40000307:12446`) — both give identical
 * geometry (x 0/384/768/1152, 288px cards → 96px gaps, zero edge padding at the group's own frame
 * boundary). `get_variable_defs` at both scopes surfaces real spacing variables
 * (`alias/space/100` through `alias/space/2000`, i.e. 4 through 80px, plus 160/180) but none equal
 * 96. Independently re-checked here directly against this repo's own registered scale
 * (`foundation/spacing.ts`, read in full, not assumed from a comment): the named scale's own
 * nearest neighbours are `5xl` = 80px and `6xl` = 128px, and the numeric-alias scale
 * (`zimmTokens.ts`) jumps straight from `--zimm-scale-1600` (64px) to `--zimm-scale-3500` (140px)
 * — nothing at 96 on either scale. Treated exactly like `zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts`'s own
 * `CARD_WIDTH_MOBILE`/`TABLET`/`DESKTOP` precedent: a named constant carrying an explicit
 * pending-token comment, per `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`'s "Never" note — not a hardcoded
 * literal in the ordinary sense that rule targets. Expressed in rem, matching that same precedent
 * (a sizing/spacing dimension that should scale with root font-size/zoom, WCAG 1.4.4 — see
 * `overrideStyling.md`'s Units section).
 *
 * VERTICAL (ROW) GAP — 64px, and UNLIKE the horizontal gap above, this one has a real registered
 * token: `--zimm-scale-1600` (`zimmTokens.ts`), which resolves to `spacing['4xl']` —
 * independently verified directly against `foundation/spacing.ts` (`'4xl': '4rem'`, i.e. 64px),
 * not assumed from the build plan's own citation of it. Matches the real bound Figma variable
 * `section/4xl` (Designs file) / `alias/space/1600` (System file) per build plan §B1. Per this
 * step's own instruction, a REAL token is referenced directly (`var(--zimm-scale-1600)`) rather
 * than re-declared as a named constant — there is nothing to name here that isn't already named.
 *
 * COLUMN COUNT PER BREAKPOINT — two tiers, not three, and the smaller tier is a stated
 * placeholder, not a confirmed reading. The only Figma node supplied for this grid (unlike
 * `zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts`, which has a Mobile AND a Tablet AND a Desktop node) is the
 * Desktop one cited above — no Tablet/Mobile-specific card size or column count exists anywhere
 * in the provisional source for THIS grid. Per `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`'s "don't guess
 * design values" rule (also stated directly in the build plan's own B1 pass criteria: "If a
 * viewport's count cannot be read from the provisional mockup, leave it inherited and comment
 * why"), this recipe does not invent a specific Tablet/Mobile card size or column count. Instead:
 *   - A single sub-desktop tier (covering both Mobile and Tablet) at `GRID_COLUMNS_BASE` = 2 —
 *     the same "two states, not three" shape `zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts`'s own
 *     `HEADER_HEIGHT_MOBILE`/`HEADER_HEIGHT_DESKTOP` already uses for the identical situation (one
 *     node covering Mobile+Tablet, one separate Desktop node, no third reading to key a middle
 *     tier off).
 *   - `GRID_COLUMNS_BASE = 2` specifically (rather than some other placeholder number) matches an
 *     already-established "2-up on the smallest breakpoint" convention for a real product-card
 *     grid elsewhere in this exact codebase: `overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx`'s own
 *     search-results `SimpleGrid columns={[2, 2, 4, 5]}` — a different page, different card width
 *     (280px, per that file's own inline comment) and different breakpoint set (Chakra's default
 *     array breakpoints, not this recipe's explicit `breakpoints.xl` step), so the exact numbers
 *     are NOT reused wholesale from there — only the "start at 2-up, not some other count" shape.
 *   - `GRID_COLUMNS_DESKTOP = 4` is the one confirmed value (Desktop, cited above).
 *   - Flagged here for confirmation once this grid sits inside a real page (build plan §B2),
 *     exactly like `zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts`'s own flagged-but-unconfirmed title-row
 *     horizontal inset: getting the sub-desktop count wrong shows up as a real-world layout
 *     decision to revisit once a genuine Tablet/Mobile node exists, not a test failure — this
 *     organism has no assigned page context of its own.
 *
 * HEADER HEIGHT — deliberately UNSET (contrast `zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts`'s own
 * `HEADER_HEIGHT_MOBILE`/`DESKTOP`). The one Figma reading available (`3332:37131`, 75px,
 * Desktop-only) has no corroborating Mobile/Tablet reading to pair it with, and neither this
 * step's brief nor the build plan's own B1 pass criteria asks for a fixed header height at all —
 * unlike the rail, where two independent node heights (Mobile+Tablet-covering 56px, Desktop 96px)
 * were both explicitly supplied. Setting one anyway from a single, viewport-unconfirmed number
 * would be inventing a cross-viewport claim this session has no evidence for. `header` below sizes
 * itself from its own content instead (`display: flex`, vertically centred) — the same
 * "leave it simple, comment why" instruction this docblock's COLUMN COUNT section above follows
 * for the same underlying reason (one Desktop-only reading, no Tablet/Mobile counterpart).
 *
 * TITLE ROW HORIZONTAL INSET — also deliberately zero, for the same reason
 * `zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts`'s own `header` part gives its own title-and-link row: no
 * horizontal-inset measurement was supplied for this row either, and this organism has no
 * assigned page context (that is build plan §B2's job). Flagged for confirmation there, not
 * guessed here.
 */

// Horizontal card-to-card gap — see this file's own "HORIZONTAL GAP" docblock section above. rem,
// not px, matching zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts's CARD_WIDTH_MOBILE/TABLET/DESKTOP precedent for
// a sizing (non-hairline) dimension with no foundation token yet.
const GRID_CARD_GAP = '6rem'; // 96px — confirmed Figma value, checked at two independent sources (40000301:11694 "Product Card Group" master, Size=Desktop/Display=4, node 40000307:12446; and the page-level instance 3332:35655). No --zimm-scale-* equivalent (nearest neighbours: named scale 5xl=80px / 6xl=128px; numeric alias 1600=64px jumps straight to 3500=140px) — pending promotion to foundation/spacing.ts or sizes.ts by the UI designer.

// Column counts per breakpoint — see this file's own "COLUMN COUNT PER BREAKPOINT" docblock
// section above for the full reasoning (only Desktop is a confirmed Figma reading; the sub-desktop
// tier is a stated, flagged placeholder, not a guess presented as fact).
const GRID_COLUMNS_BASE = 2; // Mobile + Tablet (below breakpoints.xl) — UNCONFIRMED placeholder, see docblock.
const GRID_COLUMNS_DESKTOP = 4; // breakpoints.xl and up — confirmed (Figma nodes cited in the docblock above).

const DESKTOP_UP_QUERY = `@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.xl})`; // 1280px — same "Desktop" tier convention as zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts's identically-named constant; the confirmed 4-up/288px reading itself comes from a 1440px Figma frame, inside this tier.

export const ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid = {
  parts: ['container', 'header', 'grid'],

  baseStyle: (): Record<string, SystemStyleObject> => ({
    container: {
      width: '100%',
    },

    header: {
      display: 'flex',
      alignItems: 'center',
      justifyContent: 'space-between',
    },

    grid: {
      display: 'grid',
      width: '100%',
      gridTemplateColumns: `repeat(${GRID_COLUMNS_BASE}, 1fr)`,
      columnGap: GRID_CARD_GAP,
      // Real registered token, referenced directly — see this file's own "VERTICAL (ROW) GAP"
      // docblock section above for why this one is NOT a named constant, unlike GRID_CARD_GAP.
      rowGap: 'var(--zimm-scale-1600)', // 64px
      [DESKTOP_UP_QUERY]: {
        gridTemplateColumns: `repeat(${GRID_COLUMNS_DESKTOP}, 1fr)`,
      },
    },
  }),
};

10	   * `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail`'s own `title` prop documents for itself (build plan §A5/§B1). Styled

18	   * Medium, size 16 / line-height 18 / letterSpacing -1 — cross-checked against
19	   * `theme/foundation/typography.ts`'s own registered `heading3` (`fontSizes.xs` 16px /

25	  /**
26	   * A pre-formatted, already-pluralized node (e.g. "16 Items" / "1 Item") — this component does
27	   * not own copy/intl, matching `title` above and `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail`'s own container/
28	   * presentational split (`.claude/rules/components.md`). Build plan §B1: the item count is
29	   * mechanical ICU-plural-selector copy ("go for it" — Marcel, 2026-09-08), which is the calling
30	   * container's job (SFCC-84's Full History page container, not built by this step), not this
31	   * organism's. **Rendered exactly as received — never recomputed from `cards.length` here.** A
32	   * caller is expected to derive this from the same `cards` array it passes below; see this
33	   * component's own stories/tests for the "the two stay in sync when a real caller wires them
34	   * together correctly" proof this step's brief asked for — that proof lives at the call site
35	   * (story/test), not as internal recomputation, precisely so a future divergence between what a
36	   * caller *says* the count is and what actually rendered stays visible instead of being silently
37	   * papered over by this component re-deriving its own "correct" answer.
38	   *
39	   * Same `textStyle="heading3"` / colour treatment as `title` above — confirmed via the same
40	   * `3332:37131` screenshot, which renders "RECENTLY VIEWED" (left) and "16 ITEMS" (right) in the
41	   * same text style.
42	   */
43	  itemCountLabel: ReactNode;
44	  /**
45	   * Rendered in the exact order received — no sorting or reordering happens here, and (unlike
46	   * `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail`) no cap/slice either: SFCC-84's Full History page has no ordering AC
47	   * of its own, but per build plan §B1 "the page is the rail's overflow — same order or it reads
48	   * as broken", and the page container (not this component) is already responsible for capping
49	   * its fetch at `RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED` (24, `app/constants/index.ts`) before this

52	   * (build plan §A5) rather than a variation-narrowed type, so this component spreads each entry
53	   * straight into `ZimmProductCard` rather than forcing a variation onto every card itself. In
54	   * real usage every entry already carries `variation: 'plp'` by construction — SFCC-84 AC 2 /
55	   * SFCC-236's own "Recently Viewed Full History variation (same behavior as PLP card)" AC block,
56	   * corroborated 2026-09-07/08 against the `feature/zimmproductcard-live-demo` branch's own
57	   * "Recently Viewed (Full History)" section, which renders `variation: 'plp'` cards with zero
58	   * different props from its own PLP demo cards (see this component's own recipe file for the
59	   * full citation). Nothing new was needed on `ZimmProductCard` itself for this — see that
60	   * component's own module docblock: *"'Recently Viewed Full History' is not a fourth

64	};

67	
68	/**

70	 * presentational: data arrives as props, no data-fetching, no `useEinstein`, no `useIntl` — the
71	 * same container/presentational split `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` (SFCC-83, build plan §A5) already
72	 * establishes, adapted here from a horizontally-scrolling rail to a 4-up desktop grid. The
73	 * container (build plan §B2, not built by this step) is responsible for reading the shopper's
74	 * tracked view history, fetching real product data for it, mapping the result to `plp`-shaped
75	 * `ZimmProductCardProps` (a new mapper, `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts` — NOT
76	 * `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail`'s own `recentlyViewedCard.ts`, whose narrower image-only output cannot
77	 * feed this grid's fuller `plp` card), and supplying `title`/`itemCountLabel` copy.
78	 *
79	 * **Design source, stated plainly per build plan §B1: this grid's layout comes from a
80	 * PROVISIONAL design source** (`Zimmermann_Designs` file, node `3332:35655` — not a PDP/Recently
81	 * Viewed node in the authoritative `Zimmermann_Design_System_2026` file the rail sibling uses;
82	 * see Marcel's 2026-09-04 precedence rule, restated verbatim in the build plan). That ranking is
83	 * unchanged by anything below. What DID change, this session (2026-09-07/08): the specific

85	 * on the provisional source's word alone —
86	 *   - **Layout** confirmed via live Figma metadata AND a real screenshot of `3332:37131` ("PLP
87	 *     Bar desktop", 1440×75), which renders "RECENTLY VIEWED" (left) / "16 ITEMS" (right) —
88	 *     confirming both the title-left/count-right layout and the title bar's own content in one
89	 *     node, not inferred from layer names alone (which the build plan notes were misleading here).
90	 *   - **The `Sidebar` (`3332:35664`) child holds four stacked `Products Module Desktop` instances**
91	 *     (`35665`/`35666`/`35668`/`35669`, each 1440×606) — two of which were checked directly and are
92	 *     structurally identical (four `Products S Desktop` instances each, 288×542, at
93	 *     x=0/384/768/1152): confirmed as 4 repeated example rows of real content, not 4 different
94	 *     states to design against.
95	 *   - **The `variation: 'plp'` decision** (see `cards`' own JSDoc above) is independently
96	 *     corroborated by a real, interactive prior-art branch, not just an AC-text reading — see this
97	 *     recipe file's own docblock for the full citation.
98	 *   - **The 96px horizontal card gap** (this recipe's own `GRID_CARD_GAP`) was checked at two
99	 *     independent Figma sources specifically because it does NOT resolve to any bound variable —
100	 *     see this recipe's own docblock for the full "RESOLVED... checked twice, genuinely
101	 *     un-tokenised" citation.
102	 * So: provisional design *source*, independently confirmed design *values* — both things are true
103	 * at once, and this docblock states both rather than letting the provisional-source caveat imply
104	 * the specific numbers below are unverified guesses, or letting the confirmed-values framing imply
105	 * the source ranking has changed.
106	 *
107	 * **This grid does NOT share its title row with `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail`'s own `title-and-link`**
108	 * (a deliberate build-plan call, not an oversight): the rail's header is Figma node
109	 * `40000538:20306` (h96/h56); this grid's is `3332:37131` (h75, one Desktop reading only, no
110	 * separate Tablet/Mobile node). Different components in Figma, so sharing would be a wrong DRY
111	 * call — see this recipe's own docblock for why no fixed header height is set here at all (unlike
112	 * the rail's own two-tier `HEADER_HEIGHT_MOBILE`/`DESKTOP`).
113	 *
114	 * Renders `null` for an empty `cards` array — the same defensive-leaf-component default
115	 * `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` uses (its own container owns the actual "should this exist at all"
116	 * decision; SFCC-84's Full History page has its own separate empty-state design, per build plan
117	 * §B2, which does not involve mounting this component with zero cards at all).
118	 */
119	export const ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid = ({ title, itemCountLabel, cards }: ZimmRecentlyViewedGridProps) => {
120	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_RECENTLY_VIEWED_GRID_RECIPE, {});
121	
122	  if (cards.length === 0) {
123	    return null;
124	  }
125	
126	  return (
127	    <chakra.div __css={styles.container} data-testid="recently-viewed-grid">
128	      <chakra.div __css={styles.header}>
129	        <chakra.span textStyle="heading3" color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)">

import React from 'react';
import type { ReactNode } from 'react';
import { chakra, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
import { ZimmProductCard } from '../zimmProductCard';
import type { ZimmProductCardProps } from '../zimmProductCard';

export type ZimmRecentlyViewedGridProps = {
  /**
   * Typed as `ReactNode`, not `string` — this component owns no copy/intl, the same discipline
   * `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail`'s own `title` prop documents for itself (build plan §A5/§B1). Styled
   * with `textStyle="heading3"` directly below, applied from the start rather than left for a
   * caller to pre-style — the rail's own `title` shipped once *without* this and had to be fixed
   * after live Storybook testing caught it rendering in the ambient body weight instead of the
   * intended one (see `zimmRecentlyViewedRail/index.tsx`'s own docblock, "Styling resolved
   * 2026-09-08"). That token is independently confirmed correct for THIS component's own title
   * bar too, not just carried over from the rail: build plan §B1's `get_variable_defs` read on
   * Figma node `3332:37131` ("PLP Bar desktop") returns "Default/Heading 3" — Futura Round
   * Medium, size 16 / line-height 18 / letterSpacing -1 — cross-checked against
   * `theme/foundation/typography.ts`'s own registered `heading3` (`fontSizes.xs` 16px /
   * `lineHeights['2xs']` 18px / `letterSpacings.xs` -0.12px, the same documented sub-pixel
   * rounding `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`'s Units section already carries elsewhere /
   * `textTransform: uppercase` already baked in) and found to match exactly.
   */
  title: ReactNode;
  /**
   * A pre-formatted, already-pluralized node (e.g. "16 Items" / "1 Item") — this component does
   * not own copy/intl, matching `title` above and `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail`'s own container/
   * presentational split (`.claude/rules/components.md`). Build plan §B1: the item count is
   * mechanical ICU-plural-selector copy ("go for it" — Marcel, 2026-09-08), which is the calling
   * container's job (SFCC-84's Full History page container, not built by this step), not this
   * organism's. **Rendered exactly as received — never recomputed from `cards.length` here.** A
   * caller is expected to derive this from the same `cards` array it passes below; see this
   * component's own stories/tests for the "the two stay in sync when a real caller wires them
   * together correctly" proof this step's brief asked for — that proof lives at the call site
   * (story/test), not as internal recomputation, precisely so a future divergence between what a
   * caller *says* the count is and what actually rendered stays visible instead of being silently
   * papered over by this component re-deriving its own "correct" answer.
   *
   * Same `textStyle="heading3"` / colour treatment as `title` above — confirmed via the same
   * `3332:37131` screenshot, which renders "RECENTLY VIEWED" (left) and "16 ITEMS" (right) in the
   * same text style.
   */
  itemCountLabel: ReactNode;
  /**
   * Rendered in the exact order received — no sorting or reordering happens here, and (unlike
   * `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail`) no cap/slice either: SFCC-84's Full History page has no ordering AC
   * of its own, but per build plan §B1 "the page is the rail's overflow — same order or it reads
   * as broken", and the page container (not this component) is already responsible for capping
   * its fetch at `RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED` (24, `app/constants/index.ts`) before this
   * component ever sees `cards` — see the build plan's B2 step. Typed as the full
   * `ZimmProductCardProps` union, matching `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail`'s own contract verbatim
   * (build plan §A5) rather than a variation-narrowed type, so this component spreads each entry
   * straight into `ZimmProductCard` rather than forcing a variation onto every card itself. In
   * real usage every entry already carries `variation: 'plp'` by construction — SFCC-84 AC 2 /
   * SFCC-236's own "Recently Viewed Full History variation (same behavior as PLP card)" AC block,
   * corroborated 2026-09-07/08 against the `feature/zimmproductcard-live-demo` branch's own
   * "Recently Viewed (Full History)" section, which renders `variation: 'plp'` cards with zero
   * different props from its own PLP demo cards (see this component's own recipe file for the
   * full citation). Nothing new was needed on `ZimmProductCard` itself for this — see that
   * component's own module docblock: *"'Recently Viewed Full History' is not a fourth
   * variation... callers pass `variation: 'plp'` for it."*
   */
  cards: readonly ZimmProductCardProps[];
};

const ZIMM_RECENTLY_VIEWED_GRID_RECIPE = 'ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid';

/**
 * SFCC-84 — the Recently Viewed Full History grid organism (build plan section B1). Purely
 * presentational: data arrives as props, no data-fetching, no `useEinstein`, no `useIntl` — the
 * same container/presentational split `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` (SFCC-83, build plan §A5) already
 * establishes, adapted here from a horizontally-scrolling rail to a 4-up desktop grid. The
 * container (build plan §B2, not built by this step) is responsible for reading the shopper's
 * tracked view history, fetching real product data for it, mapping the result to `plp`-shaped
 * `ZimmProductCardProps` (a new mapper, `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts` — NOT
 * `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail`'s own `recentlyViewedCard.ts`, whose narrower image-only output cannot
 * feed this grid's fuller `plp` card), and supplying `title`/`itemCountLabel` copy.
 *
 * **Design source, stated plainly per build plan §B1: this grid's layout comes from a
 * PROVISIONAL design source** (`Zimmermann_Designs` file, node `3332:35655` — not a PDP/Recently
 * Viewed node in the authoritative `Zimmermann_Design_System_2026` file the rail sibling uses;
 * see Marcel's 2026-09-04 precedence rule, restated verbatim in the build plan). That ranking is
 * unchanged by anything below. What DID change, this session (2026-09-07/08): the specific
 * geometry/typography/variation values actually used here were independently verified, not taken
 * on the provisional source's word alone —
 *   - **Layout** confirmed via live Figma metadata AND a real screenshot of `3332:37131` ("PLP
 *     Bar desktop", 1440×75), which renders "RECENTLY VIEWED" (left) / "16 ITEMS" (right) —
 *     confirming both the title-left/count-right layout and the title bar's own content in one
 *     node, not inferred from layer names alone (which the build plan notes were misleading here).
 *   - **The `Sidebar` (`3332:35664`) child holds four stacked `Products Module Desktop` instances**
 *     (`35665`/`35666`/`35668`/`35669`, each 1440×606) — two of which were checked directly and are
 *     structurally identical (four `Products S Desktop` instances each, 288×542, at
 *     x=0/384/768/1152): confirmed as 4 repeated example rows of real content, not 4 different
 *     states to design against.
 *   - **The `variation: 'plp'` decision** (see `cards`' own JSDoc above) is independently
 *     corroborated by a real, interactive prior-art branch, not just an AC-text reading — see this
 *     recipe file's own docblock for the full citation.
 *   - **The 96px horizontal card gap** (this recipe's own `GRID_CARD_GAP`) was checked at two
 *     independent Figma sources specifically because it does NOT resolve to any bound variable —
 *     see this recipe's own docblock for the full "RESOLVED... checked twice, genuinely
 *     un-tokenised" citation.
 * So: provisional design *source*, independently confirmed design *values* — both things are true
 * at once, and this docblock states both rather than letting the provisional-source caveat imply
 * the specific numbers below are unverified guesses, or letting the confirmed-values framing imply
 * the source ranking has changed.
 *
 * **This grid does NOT share its title row with `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail`'s own `title-and-link`**
 * (a deliberate build-plan call, not an oversight): the rail's header is Figma node
 * `40000538:20306` (h96/h56); this grid's is `3332:37131` (h75, one Desktop reading only, no
 * separate Tablet/Mobile node). Different components in Figma, so sharing would be a wrong DRY
 * call — see this recipe's own docblock for why no fixed header height is set here at all (unlike
 * the rail's own two-tier `HEADER_HEIGHT_MOBILE`/`DESKTOP`).
 *
 * Renders `null` for an empty `cards` array — the same defensive-leaf-component default
 * `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` uses (its own container owns the actual "should this exist at all"
 * decision; SFCC-84's Full History page has its own separate empty-state design, per build plan
 * §B2, which does not involve mounting this component with zero cards at all).
 */
export const ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid = ({ title, itemCountLabel, cards }: ZimmRecentlyViewedGridProps) => {
  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_RECENTLY_VIEWED_GRID_RECIPE, {});

  if (cards.length === 0) {
    return null;
  }

  return (
    <chakra.div __css={styles.container} data-testid="recently-viewed-grid">
      <chakra.div __css={styles.header}>
        <chakra.span textStyle="heading3" color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)">
          {title}
        </chakra.span>
        <chakra.span
          textStyle="heading3"
          color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)"
          data-testid="recently-viewed-grid-count"
        >
          {itemCountLabel}
        </chakra.span>
      </chakra.div>
      <chakra.div __css={styles.grid} data-testid="recently-viewed-grid-group">
        {cards.map((card) => (
          <ZimmProductCard key={card.id} {...card} />
        ))}
      </chakra.div>
    </chakra.div>
  );
};

Homepage/PLP SSR HTML don't embed product links directly, so I found real product IDs via `/search?q=dress` (the same query the `zimmproductcard-live-demo` branch used against this sandbox): `8637DS241`, `ZWNEWPRD03`, `ZWNEWPRD04`. Curled `http://localhost:3000/product/8637DS241`:

content.text:
Yes — fully possible and fully reversible, with one important caveat about *how* to do it safely: right now, ALL of Phases 1–6's work is uncommitted (sitting only in the working directory). A merge needs something safe to "snap back to" afterward, and the naive way to discard a merge (`git reset --hard`) wipes out uncommitted changes too — which would take our actual work down with it.

The safe way:
1. **Checkpoint commit** — commit the current state as-is, clearly labeled as a temporary local checkpoint (never pushed, not the real feature commit history — we'd still commit "for real" later, separately, whenever you actually ask for that).
2. **Merge PR #81's branch** on top of that checkpoint.
3. **You test** — using the same already-running dev server/Storybook, no restart needed unless the merge touches something that requires one.
4. **Discard cleanly** — `git reset --hard` back to the checkpoint commit. This removes PR #81's changes entirely and returns exactly to our current state, with nothing lost.

The only thing this requires that I'd normally stop and confirm separately: an actual `git commit`, even though it's just a local safety checkpoint. Given you're asking for this specific workflow directly, I'll treat that as your go-ahead for step 1 specifically — flag me if you'd rather I hold off and ask each time.

Alternative if you'd prefer zero contact with this branch at all: a separate git worktree with its own temporary branch and its own dev server on different ports — fully isolated, nothing to reset afterward, just delete the worktree when done. More setup, but the main branch is never touched even transiently. I'd lean toward the checkpoint approach above since it lets you keep using the servers you're already looking at, but let me know if you'd rather have the isolation instead.

Either way — still waiting on Phase 6 before touching anything, since merging into a tree another agent is actively writing to is the one thing I don't want to risk.

content.text:
That's a lot of noise, but let me triage it properly rather than react to raw volume. None of the 59 errors reference any of our own recently-viewed files by name — that's a real, checkable fact, not an assumption. Most are pre-existing/environmental (DataCloud/Einstein failures — already-documented from earlier this session; a third-party CSP block from "measmerize.com"; generic PageDesigner warnings). A few look like they could be PR #81's own gallery work surfacing issues unrelated to us (a Suspense-hydration error, an "Element type is invalid" error, and a duplicate-React-key warning specifically inside `ZimmColourSwatchGroup` — a file PR #81 itself modified). Worth flagging those to you separately, but not mine to fix.

content.text:
Here's the full picture across all three surfaces, now that PR #81's real page context is merged in:

**Cart — works correctly.** My own test showed "0 rails" but that was because my test cart was empty, and Cart's empty-state correctly never renders recommendation rails at all (matches base `EmptyCart`'s real structure). Your screenshot with an actual item confirms the rail renders fine there.

**PDP — data pipeline works, but width is wrong.** Real product images render correctly (not placeholders), cards are ordered correctly, cap/gate logic all correct. But the rail is confined to roughly the gallery column's width instead of spanning the full page — all my earlier fixes made the rail internally self-consistent (header aligned with its own card group), but I never verified what width its *parent* hands it inside a real PDP, and PR #81 restructured that page's layout. This needs code investigation into how `RecommendedProducts` is now nested relative to PR #81's new gallery structure.

**PLP — inconclusive, need to redo.** My automated test found the rail present in the DOM but it didn't show up in my own screenshot — could be a genuine visibility bug or just a timing race in my test (the product-fetch hadn't resolved when I captured it). Not confirmed either way yet — I don't want to report this as a bug until I've actually pinned it down.

**Real bug, all three surfaces — broken images for at least some products.** Confirmed precisely: for product `4673TS251`, our rail resolves an image URL using an `en/v{version}` locale-catalog path that doesn't load, while that exact product's own real gallery uses a `default/dw{hash}` path that works fine. This is in our own `filterImageGroups({viewType: 'medium'})` call landing on the wrong `imageGroups` entry for at least this product — a real bug in our mapper's image selection, not a missing-data problem, and not something that disappears when we revert PR #81.

**Separately, not ours:** a handful of the 59 console errors look like genuine issues in PR #81's own new code (a Suspense-hydration error, an "Element type is invalid" error, and a duplicate-React-key warning specifically inside `ZimmColourSwatchGroup`, which PR #81 itself modified) — worth flagging to whoever owns that PR, not something for us to fix.

Want me to go fix the PDP-width and broken-image bugs now, or finish nailing down PLP first?
